coveredGames.title: Nukige VN where you spend the summer with 3 hot sisters in the countryside. A simple story, great art and 21 uncensored still sex scenes with lewd JP VA. Good fap material but need a patch. 7.5⭐

coveredGames.name: Labyronia RPG
coveredGames.title: Labyronia RPG is a visually pleasant game that despite using some assets from RPG Maker as well as several new ones, also manages to provide us with an original and entertaining story.

coveredGames.name: Strategy & Tactics: Wargame Collection
coveredGames.title: You’re supposed to stare at a map and plan ahead. The 2D unit icons have sufficient diversity and the hundreds of regions , seem accurate as far as I can tell from my hefty experience with such games.

coveredGames.name: Velvet Assassin
coveredGames.title: Velvet Assassin is a terribly underrated game which certainly deserved more attention, patches and a sequel.

coveredGames.name: GALAK-Z
coveredGames.title: GALAK-Z is an arcade rogue-like hybrid which features randomly generated levels. Words cannot describe how difficult the first few missions truly are. Yet it is fully worth it!

coveredGames.name: Rooks Keep
coveredGames.title: A clever new perspective into one of the oldest board games in history. Chess need occasional refreshes and Rooks Keep certainly won't disappoint in that regard. It can be enjoyed by chess vets too!

coveredGames.name: The Hat Man: Shadow Ward
coveredGames.title: Indie horror games aren’t a novelty yet most try to stand out from the crowd and fail. Not this title though.

coveredGames.name: Red Faction Guerrilla Re-Mars-tered
coveredGames.title: Few series managed to showcase sheer environmental destruction coupled with a captivating SciFi storyline. Well, Red Faction should be on your radar. Currently dormant, but perhaps rebooted one day...

coveredGames.name: Mandate Order
coveredGames.title: There is something satisfying about watching carts carry resources through a settlement you designed yourself.

coveredGames.name: Mosaique Neko Waifus 6
coveredGames.title: The gradual power scaling keeps frustration at zero, making it an ideal title for kicking back and enjoying some neko shenanigans.

coveredGames.name: Escape from Vlogger: Runaway
coveredGames.title: There is something wonderfull and unsettling about turning a familiar creator’s home into a trap.

coveredGames.name: Bruisers 2D Boxing
coveredGames.title: Balancing workouts, meals, recovery and work creates an engaging concept that extends well beyond simply winning the next fight.

coveredGames.name: Under Canopies
coveredGames.title: Growing plants, collecting ingredients and preparing meals makes daily life in the forest feel rewarding and surprisingly immersive.

coveredGames.name: Space Savory
coveredGames.title: Customer conversations, difficult decisions and unexpected visitors give its diner an appealing sense of unpredictability, making the setting sound lively and full of character.

coveredGames.name: The Merlies
coveredGames.title: The Merlies combines platforming with rewarding exploration in a beautifully illustrated world. Its relaxed pace, secret routes and evolving squad abilities provide a satisfying sense of progress.

coveredGames.name: Tasty Chef
coveredGames.title: Conveyor service and different cooking routines encourage a fresh layout and an entirely new management strategy.

coveredGames.name: Rooster
coveredGames.title: Characters in Rooster are lovable. Each zodiac animal has distinctive traits, funny reactions, and meaningful moments, making the journey feel like a collection of charming stories connected by friend

coveredGames.name: Curve Fever Pro
coveredGames.title: Curve Fever Pro is approachable enough for newcomers yet demanding enough for competitive players. Playing against opponents fills each arena with constant tension.

coveredGames.name: Breathedge 2
coveredGames.title: Humor gives Breathedge 2 a personality few survival games can match. Absurd situations, bizarre items, and playful writing keep the bleakness of deep space entertaining.

coveredGames.name: Frontier: Path of Shadows
coveredGames.title: The journey offers mystery, strategic challenge and meaningful choices while maintaining an inviting sense of exploration from beginning.

coveredGames.name: Nicotine Merchant Simulator™
coveredGames.title: Different layouts, priorities, and automation choices make the sandbox feel flexible, replayable, and welcoming to creative management styles. I like how the game encourages players.

coveredGames.name: Echoes of Mystralia
coveredGames.title: The flexible crafting system supports creativity, making experimentation feel just as important as reflexes during combat.

coveredGames.name: SWAT Commander
coveredGames.title: Mission structure keeps players engaged. Each operation feels like a tactical puzzle, with different risks, routes, and decisions shaping the final outcome.

coveredGames.name: The Dream Office
coveredGames.title: Fans of workplace simulations may find The Dream Office especially inviting.

coveredGames.name: Last Drop
coveredGames.title: The blend of driving, exploration, survival mechanics, and intense one-on-one fighting gives Last Drop an appealing variety.

coveredGames.name: Wild West Miner Simulator
coveredGames.title: Expanding your town, upgrading equipment, and defending against raiders creates a compelling rhythm that makes every session feel rewarding and strategic.

coveredGames.name: Laundering Simulator - Clean Cash and Laundry
coveredGames.title: Laundering Simulator - Clean Cash and Laundry is perfect if you want a management game that is not too serious. It is funny, quirky, and surprisingly satisfying.

coveredGames.name: Stellar Warfare
coveredGames.title: Designing fleets beforehand is enjoyable, but adapting production, defenses, and attack routes during combat is equally important and satisfying.

coveredGames.name: Not Monday Cafe
coveredGames.title: Growing ingredients, unlocking recipes, and building a tiny cafe at the on your screen makes every session feel calm, charming, and productive.

coveredGames.name: Escape from Umbra
coveredGames.title: Escape from Umbra is creepy in all the right ways. A strong choice for fans of dark, puzzle-focused horror.

coveredGames.name: Neko Station
coveredGames.title: The idle gameplay is comfortable, and the decorations make each carriage feel unique.

coveredGames.name: Looking For Fael
coveredGames.title: The connected apartments, odd mechanisms, and dreamy visual ideas make Looking For Fael feel like exploring someone’s brilliant, chaotic imagination.

coveredGames.name: V.A.U.L.T. PROTOCOL
coveredGames.title: The AI surveillance, abandoned facilities, and escalating danger create a constant sense of pressure and curiosity.

coveredGames.name: Kingdom Loop
coveredGames.title: Kingdom Loop features excellent progression systems. Unlocking new cards and upgrades for my kingdom feels incredibly satisfying.

coveredGames.name: Quarantine Zone: The Last Check
coveredGames.title: The military aspects are handled with care, and the base management adds a nice layer of progression to the frantic daily inspections.

coveredGames.name: Beauties and the Stranded
coveredGames.title: Beauties and the Stranded provides a fresh take on the FMV genre. The acting is convincing, and the survival elements add a layer of urgency.

coveredGames.name: Little Witch in the Woods
coveredGames.title: The visuals are a pastel dream, and the sound design adds gentle, magical atmosphere. It’s easy to lose hours helping villagers and discovering new areas.

coveredGames.name: BAD BOY BROTHER
coveredGames.title: BAD BOY BROTHER - solid japanese beat'em'up with epic showdowns, amazing character design and absolute peak voice acting. Feel free to try.

coveredGames.name: Contraband Police
coveredGames.title: An incredible and engaging management Sim, packed with action, intrigue, and a deep plot amongst a political regime. Mechanically smart and unique, an absolute gem of a video-game. A blast of fun!

coveredGames.name: The Gold River Project
coveredGames.title: The Gold River Project rewards curiosity and cooperative play. It’s a refreshing take on survival that’s hard to put down.

coveredGames.name: MEMOLITH: Forsaken by Light
coveredGames.title: Combat is challenging but fair, with clear telegraphs and satisfying feedback. You plan, execute, and watch your strategies unfold with cinematic precision.

coveredGames.name: Lugh World
coveredGames.title: Following Manú’s story while unlocking Lugh histories adds depth beyond typical quests, enriching the exploration and battles.

coveredGames.name: HUNTDOWN: OVERTIME
coveredGames.title: HUNTDOWN: OVERTIME - amazing experience for all retro fans both from visual and gameplay perspectives.

coveredGames.name: Dread Neighbor
coveredGames.title: Cool, well-crafted psychological thriller that sticks with you long after you finish. The tension here is pretty good.

coveredGames.name: CarX Drift Racing Online 2
coveredGames.title: CarX Drift Racing Online 2 is pretty fun. New players can enjoy relaxed free-drive, while veterans chase rankings and duels.

coveredGames.name: Racer Overdrive
coveredGames.title: Neon-lit circuits, smooth framerates and a satisfying boost system create a legible, intense core loop that begs you to chase better times.

coveredGames.name: MyRobot
coveredGames.title: The combo of lighthearted gameplay with thoughtful conversation creates a refreshing, immersive vibe that keeps me returning for more tinkering and chats.

coveredGames.name: Real Estate Simulator 2
coveredGames.title: You design spaces, manage purchases, and optimize profits in a lively, semi-open world that rewards thoughtful decisions and bold renovations.

coveredGames.name: Gothic 1 Classic
coveredGames.title: A timeless RPG classic. Gothic’s gritty world, atmosphere, freedom, and memorable characters still shine today. Rough around the edges, but absolutely worth playing.

coveredGames.name: Pie in the Sky
coveredGames.title: Your bicycle helmet with googly eyes and cable ties won't save you. GET SWOOPED, MAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAATE.

coveredGames.name: R.E.P.O.
coveredGames.title: Playing R.E.P.O. with friends is a blast! Explore creepy houses, recover stuff, and try to survive together. The co-op adds so much to the experience. Perfect for some eerie teamwork fun!

coveredGames.name: LEGO® The Hobbit™
coveredGames.title: Lego Hobbit on the Steam Deck. Good times.

coveredGames.name: HELLDIVERS™ 2
coveredGames.title: Satire and fun. It's Starship Troopers. FAO Americans: This is how the rest of the world sees you.

coveredGames.name: LEGO® Batman™ 2: DC Super Heroes
coveredGames.title: Pick up and play fun, ideal on steam deck... even better on the couch playing co-op.

coveredGames.name: Twin Breaker: A Sacred Symbols Adventure
coveredGames.title: Classic puzzle game concept with a slightly new twist. Works well on Steam Deck. Worth picking up in a sale.

coveredGames.name: Anodyne
coveredGames.title: Pick up and play 1990s Zelda Clone. Cheap, fun and cheerful. Idea for long Steam Deck sessions.

coveredGames.name: Diablo® IV
coveredGames.title: Diablo 4 looks great and feels gritty, but repetitive endgame and monetization issues dull the excitement.

coveredGames.name: Seance
coveredGames.title: Test review for debugging

coveredGames.name: The Séance of Blake Manor
coveredGames.title: Manga-style whodunits where Mia literally talks to the dead to crack cases. 2D RPG vibes, banger soundtrack, and genuinely funny dialogue make this a solid little mystery romp.

coveredGames.name: Hearts of the Dungeon List
coveredGames.title: Lovable heroines and satisfying RPG loops make this a cozy, number-crunching treat. It's a bit short and simple for the price, but the charm and constant updates keep it engaging.

coveredGames.name: Trinoline Genesis
coveredGames.title: Fans of Sara and the main heroines get welcome closure here, plus two fresh routes to dive into. It's short and sweet, perfect for returning to your favorite girls.

coveredGames.name: Homura Hime
coveredGames.title: Combat that genuinely rivals DMC and Bayonetta — fast, stylish combos with bullet hell flair. The anime art and character design are gorgeous. Just wish it'd let you fight more between cutscenes.

coveredGames.name: Princess Maker 2 Regeneration
coveredGames.title: A classic father-daughter raising sim with tons of personality and surprising depth for its era. Expect to spend countless hours debating whether to send your girl to fencing class or etiquette sch...

coveredGames.name: Cursed Lands
coveredGames.title: A solid RPG/dating sim with 10 romance options (including a Naga!) and a mature story that links to *Loren the Amazon Princess*.

coveredGames.name: Edengrall
coveredGames.title: Charming 3D farming sim with Harvest Moon vibes and a cozy town to explore. Adorable villagers to befriend and enough content for a solid 20 hours, though it's still very early in development.

coveredGames.name: Bear's Restaurant
coveredGames.title: A short, beautifully melancholic adventure about a bear who cooks meals for the recently deceased to help them pass on. The pixel art is charming and the stories will absolutely wreck you emotionally.

coveredGames.name: Hell Blasters
coveredGames.title: Retro art with tight, addictive bullet hell mechanics and a killer soundtrack. It’s a great shmup for learning or chasing high scores.

coveredGames.name: Yurukill: The Calumniation Games
coveredGames.title: The courtroom-meets-shmup premise is wild, and at this price it's a fun enough ride for fans of chaos and bullet-hell.

coveredGames.name: The seven days i spent with you
coveredGames.title: Looks like a yandere prison scenario but it's actually mutual pure love — old-school galgame energy. Art and music land well for the price, though the plot gets messy in the second half.

coveredGames.name: Kamikaze Lassplanes
coveredGames.title: A steampunk magical girl story with solid shmup combat and cute Lassplanes to romance? Yes, the demo’s promise holds up in the full game, blending VN charm with exciting action.

coveredGames.name: Detective School Club
coveredGames.title: Cute art and a light-hearted mystery club vibe make this a charming little VN for fans of cozy anime stories.

coveredGames.name: Trials of Proelium
coveredGames.title: Letha and Yoni's dynamic is adorable, and swapping gear mid-combat for new skills keeps battles fresh—just brace for some clunky translation.

coveredGames.name: Aeterna Noctis
coveredGames.title: The hand-drawn art is gorgeous in a dark fantasy way, but heads up — this isn't really anime-styled, more gothic crown king vibes.

coveredGames.name: Swordbreaker: Origins
coveredGames.title: A CYOA-style prequel with solid art and branching paths, though the punishing 3-life system without saves will frustrate fans of exploring all routes.

coveredGames.name: InfiniteCorp: Cyberpunk Cards
coveredGames.title: Swipe through cyberpunk dilemmas in this Reigns-like card game where balancing corporate factions keeps you hooked—though outcomes can feel random. Perfect for quick, stylish dystopia sessions.

coveredGames.name: If only I could go home early
coveredGames.title: A short, emotionally charged puzzle game with charming pixel art that starts quirky but dives deep into the toll of work-life imbalance.

coveredGames.name: DEEP 8
coveredGames.title: Gritty 90s JRPG vibes with a character-driven sci-fi war story. The mod-based combat is deep and strategic, perfect for fans who love tactical battles and personal narratives.

coveredGames.name: Winning Love by Daylight [Ep 1+2]
coveredGames.title: Magical girls + high school drama with killer character writing and a soundtrack that slaps. The humor and wholesome vibes are pure comfort food for anime fans.

coveredGames.name: Seventh Lair
coveredGames.title: A chill parallel universe side story for Fata Morgana fans, letting you hang out with the beloved cast in a lighthearted school setting. The new soundtrack slaps, especially "Land of Nowhere.

coveredGames.name: MECHANICA: A Ballad of the Rabbit and Mercury
coveredGames.title: The cyberpunk Mercury setting with its neon-drenched visuals is a vibe, and the music-based exploration mechanic is a cool twist that anime fans should dig.

coveredGames.name: After I met that catgirl, my questlist got too long!
coveredGames.title: A charming yuri RPG/VN hybrid with surprisingly fun combat, excellent voice acting, and characters that actually grow on you. Vera's journey to build a guild is genuinely engaging.

coveredGames.name: Guardian of the future
coveredGames.title: Guardian of the Future lets you step into Miyuri's shoes as she navigates destiny with her clan's martial arts legacy. The anime-style art and gripping story blend romance and suspense perfectly.

coveredGames.name: Miraculo Island
coveredGames.title: Cheesy anime island mystery with charismatic characters and multiple endings that actually deliver. Horror twists kept me guessing, and the waifus have real personality.

coveredGames.name: Nonogram Animals
coveredGames.title: The pixel art is cute and the puzzles are satisfying for quick sessions, though it's more of a casual time-killer than a deep dive.

coveredGames.name: sunny-place
coveredGames.title: Racing through literal hell tracks with cute anime girls while customizing your apartment between races? Sign me up! The vibe is surprisingly cozy chaos.

coveredGames.name: Twilight Memoria
coveredGames.title: Cute art and a surprisingly deep alchemy system make this a cozy JRPG, but the active-time battles are super tough without a controller.

coveredGames.name: Trap Genesis
coveredGames.title: Adorable trap waifus, a playful harem romance, and character designs that hit just right — this 10-year trilogy finale knows exactly what its fans want. Pure fanservice with heart.

coveredGames.name: Tropicalia: a Brazilian Game
coveredGames.title: Explore a unique RPG rooted in Tupi-Guarani mythology – a first for bRPGs! Anime fans will dig the deep lore and free-spirited characters, even if it's tough at times.

coveredGames.name: De'Vine: Heavenly Acres
coveredGames.title: Farm by day, collect & fuse monsters by night—with charming anime-style visuals and romance options that make the grind worth it.

coveredGames.name: Hope's Journey: A Therapeutic Experience
coveredGames.title: A charming RPG about confronting your inner demons, though some therapists warn its CBT lessons might oversimplify mental health.

coveredGames.name: Frail Hearts: Versicorae Domlion
coveredGames.title: The monster designs and dark atmosphere are top-notch, but the story gets lost in its own cryptic, edgy plot. Art and music carry a flawed JRPG journey.

coveredGames.name: Doki Doki Ragnarok
coveredGames.title: Viking raid as a date with a sentient village? The absurd premise and quirky humor are the main draw here, but the comedy's hit-or-miss and it's over pretty quick.

coveredGames.name: Kunado Chronicles
coveredGames.title: A post-apocalyptic world where humanity rebuilds after killing a dragon, and the focus is on deep character drama and a unique mythic sci-fi setting? Yes, please.

coveredGames.name: Terrain of Magical Expertise
coveredGames.title: A hacker-themed RPG with slick turn-based combat and a fully voiced cast? Yes please! The non-linear story and unique enemy designs make this a must-play for VN and tactical RPG fans.

coveredGames.name: Infinity Project: PATTERNS
coveredGames.title: A post-apocalyptic city with void creatures and a mystery? This feels like a lost anime episode with solid indie RPG charm.

coveredGames.name: Hug Survivor
coveredGames.title: Cute characters and a surprisingly satisfying hugging mechanic make this shmup a joy, though the English translation is hilariously broken. The killer soundtrack is a huge plus.

coveredGames.name: Jester / King
coveredGames.title: A cursed kingdom mystery with a fun time-loop twist and charming characters—just don't expect polished art or deep romance routes.

coveredGames.name: Yukizuki no Seisou
coveredGames.title: This game turns a snowy holiday into a quietly unsettling mystery. Warm character art, Japanese voices and playful banter soften the dark opening. Settle in for reading, rumors and a strange dream.

coveredGames.name: Fuyukuru. - Winter winds, adieu? -
coveredGames.title: This game weaves a deeply enticing denpa mystery where immortal girls face a gruesome decapitation. The intoxicating blend of philosophical tension and surreal horror leaves a strong impression.

coveredGames.name: Shards Of Solitude
coveredGames.title: This game turns a lonely girl's invitation into a tense factory escape. Flashlight searches, watchful cameras, and Miyuki's shifting moods make every locked door feel like a decision worth fearing.

coveredGames.name: Memory of Memorie : A Chill Story
coveredGames.title: This game pairs a focus timer with a witch studying beside you. Story keys and a changing room give quiet work sessions a little magic, while familiar routines suit company more than constant action.

coveredGames.name: DevilConnection
coveredGames.title: This game makes mind-reading a temptation: two replies, expressive creatures, and endings to seek out. Its cute look hides darker themes, so come for curious choices rather than pure cozy comfort.

coveredGames.name: Warota: I Live Next to The Demon King's Castle LOL
coveredGames.title: This game makes a wooden bed feel like a win. You clear weeds, repair a house and finally have a place to sleep, across the water from an idol whose concerts send monsters running at your village.

coveredGames.name: Noa and the Bandits' Den
coveredGames.title: This game turns a feared mercenary into a prisoner who needs to read patrols and listen for clues. The guards' loose talk is a neat hook, though the long opening and uneven English slow the escape.

coveredGames.name: Chigusa's Diary
coveredGames.title: This game turns school days into a combat-free exploration RPG, with expressive portraits and a useful character memo. The guided opening suits patient readers, though its English can sound awkward.

coveredGames.name: Monster Girls Dice Board
coveredGames.title: https://youtu.be/UqB-UUN1tpQ

coveredGames.name: Taimanin Asagi 2
coveredGames.title: This game sends two ninja sisters into a city of demons and criminals. Their dry banter and ominous setting give this old-school visual novel its pull, with a slow, exposition-heavy opening to match.

coveredGames.name: UBAI Ending
coveredGames.title: This game makes a return to work feel like walking into a plan everyone else has read. A smiling CEO, a new recruit, and a meeting held without Ryousuke turn an ordinary office into an uneasy place.

coveredGames.name: TORAWASE: The Girl in the Mirror
coveredGames.title: This game turns a romantic promise into a supernatural identity crisis. Warm character art and unsettling doubles give its transformation premise an emotional hook, with choices and endings to come.

coveredGames.name: Monkeys!¡
coveredGames.title: This game turns a delinquent's school rescue into a riot of flying comic panels and suspiciously polite smiles. The bright cast and visual gags shine, while long conversations ask you to settle in.

coveredGames.name: Eternal Palace Sakura
coveredGames.title: This game turns a tower climb into a wager. Retla can cut through yokai with twin blades, but pushing into greater Mugen Depth stacks the odds against her. Even the loot screen feels like a breather.

coveredGames.name: False Myth 2
coveredGames.title: This game turns SP and guard breaks into satisfying combo chains, with expressive heroines and a fantasy mystery. Its talky opening suits patient JRPG fans more than anyone after nonstop action.

coveredGames.name: Seferia Matrix
coveredGames.title: This game turns spellcasting into a dice puzzle: lock and roll five dice to build the hand you want. Artifacts and Sigils push damage absurdly high, and failed runs still feed permanent upgrades.

coveredGames.name: Slotbound
coveredGames.title: This game turns every spin into a celebration, with jackpots, Prism units, and endless waves to crush. Its bright, dopamine-hit loop charms, though luck can swing a run from triumph to wipeout.

coveredGames.name: Dungeon Munchies 2
coveredGames.title: This game turns cosmic monsters into dinner and dinner into a combat build. Its expressive undead cast sells the absurdity, though the short Early Access story leaves plenty waiting to be served.

coveredGames.name: Mosaique Neko Waifus 6
coveredGames.title: This game turns catgirl chats into puzzle perks, pairing rotating picture blocks with quirky loot and growing skills. A cozy fit for collectors who enjoy watching their toolkit do more of the work.

coveredGames.name: ANOMALITH
coveredGames.title: This game turns a strange mall into a survival shooter where mutation lets you fight back. Eerie spaces and a missing friend give it a strong hook, though the talk-heavy opening takes some patience.

coveredGames.name: Ayako's Endeavors
coveredGames.title: This game follows a mother's search for hope through favors, curious neighbors, and a teasing shrine spirit. A combat-free RPG where listening to the heroine matters as much as listening to the town.

coveredGames.name: HAPPY PROPAGANDA
coveredGames.title: This game turns chat moderation into a tense choice between public anger and a rookie host's well-being. Its uneasy smiles and off-air talks make a tiny broadcast desk feel disturbingly personal.

coveredGames.name: AMPANIC
coveredGames.title: This game gives your aim a shopkeeping job: gather, process, mix, and serve. Cute pixel art hides a frantic juggling act where choosing the next task matters as much as landing the next click.

coveredGames.name: Princess Ilyana: Night of Falling Grace
coveredGames.title: This game turns a rescued princess into the start of a dark mystery. Twelve endings, expressive portraits, and clue-led exploration make its appeal clear, though route hunting may call for patience.

coveredGames.name: Stupid Never Dies
coveredGames.title: This game makes a zombie’s second chance a monster-powered makeover. Stolen forms, swap-in body parts, and a loud pop-punk cast give dungeon outings personality, though early players flag repetition.

coveredGames.name: Exorcism Agency
coveredGames.title: This game blends deckbuilding with a haunted match-three track. Chain clears and ghost companions give it a cheeky charm, though English wording has drawn complaints from players learning the rules.

coveredGames.name: Alice Nation
coveredGames.title: This game turns actions, items, and people into cards. Its inviting tabletop hides uneasy secrets, with crafting, conversations, and dice checks making curiosity more useful than a perfect attack.

coveredGames.name: Bladesmith Shop Simulator
coveredGames.title: This game links magical sword crafting with the bustle of running a shop. Its forge-to-counter loop looks inviting for makers and managers alike, with the full release ahead and details evolving.

coveredGames.name: Five Nights with Maids
coveredGames.title: This game makes a maid-filled mansion feel unsafe. Cameras, shutters and dwindling power turn a familiar night-watch routine into tense decisions, while scratchy monochrome art adds its own charm.

coveredGames.name: Idle Abyss Princesses
coveredGames.title: This game pairs charming heroines with idle loot hunting and flexible builds. It's a handy desktop distraction, but rewards stop when you close it: the princesses can idle, yet your PC stays on duty.

coveredGames.name: Alice's Gaze
coveredGames.title: This game turns a haunted mansion into an odd little engine of coins, upgrades, and dungeon runs. Come for Alice's eerie pixel art and steady growth; expect a lighter touch with puzzles and story.

coveredGames.name: Do Disciplinary Committee Members Dream of Succubi?
coveredGames.title: This game links campus duties with a demonic proxy war. Daytime preparation feeds nighttime RPG growth, while hidden rivals drive the mystery. Darker story beats and early bug reports deserve care.

coveredGames.name: Lord Liberty Quest II ~Pure White~
coveredGames.title: This game turns a priestess’s tower mission into an old-school RPG of clues, equipment, and healing. Curious explorers may enjoy its secrets, though loose guidance can make the next step unclear.

coveredGames.name: Magical Girl Yusya-chan and the Labyrinth of Lust
coveredGames.title: This game pairs an expressive Live2D heroine with turn-based dungeon crawling. Positioning, item choices, and equipment synthesis give its colorful maze more to offer than a cute first impression.

coveredGames.name: Cupid Parasite
coveredGames.title: This game gives Cupid five impossible clients and a promotion to chase. Its opening shines through workplace comedy, bold pop-art style, and a heroine whose matchmaking expertise meets human chaos.

coveredGames.name: Trap Yuri Tempest
coveredGames.title: This game pairs a prickly delinquent with a charming prince in a cross-dressing romance. Expressive art and sharp banter are the draw; familiar twists and a brief story may leave you wanting more.

coveredGames.name: Maid Cafe Simulator
coveredGames.title: This game pairs hands-on cafe chores with five lively maids, bond stories, and bursts of slapstick. The cast looks inviting; early reports of repetitive work make the free demo a sensible first stop.

coveredGames.name: Princess Maker: Children of Revelation
coveredGames.title: This game pairs a daughter's planned future with lessons, adventures, and little family memories. Lovely art draws you in, though player reports of repetitive routines deserve a closer look.

coveredGames.name: Sister Compass: Slow Life Loving with My Sisters on a Deserted Island
coveredGames.title: This game pairs a laid-back island home with expressive sisters and a gentle start. The farming promise is inviting, though awkward English can get in the way of its warm, dialogue-heavy opening.

coveredGames.name: Demon General Kirsten
coveredGames.title: This game turns a feared general’s setback into a character-led RPG opening. Battles, skill learning, and mysterious loot invite tinkering, while Aria brings warmth to Kirsten’s uneasy new start.

coveredGames.name: Card Survival: Fantasy Forest
coveredGames.title: An interesting card game. It has depth. it has replayability. It has RNG that can tank your run in a heartbeat. Still EA, so needs more work on balance and UI. It's a bit hard to parse at the moment.

coveredGames.name: Imperium
coveredGames.title: Do you remember Ascendancy from back in the mid 90's. Well, here is an A.I. assisted "spiritual successor". It runs well. It is improved. It is fun. What else can you ask for? Let's see how it grows.

coveredGames.name: Monarchs at Play
coveredGames.title: Wow this demo hooked us! Monarchs at Play does a great job at making bite-sized 4X games fun and interesting to play. We're excited for full release!

coveredGames.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn
coveredGames.title: A fun game (50% off at least). 4 different crashlanding scenarios on an alien world. A survival simulation with light to heavy combat depending on the start. Lots of potential with the workshop.

coveredGames.name: Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors
coveredGames.title: My oldest fell in-love with this game during recent trip when his auntie introduced it to him. He enjoyed it so much, that he even asked me to "lend" him my Steamdeck. Must be good, no more SD for me!

coveredGames.name: Cubic Annihilation
coveredGames.title: A voxel-cube Total Annihilation-like RTS game, that tries to catch the feel of it's inspirations. The demo feels a lot to be desired in terms of quality of life but it may be fun for a a few rounds.

coveredGames.name: Project Afterfall
coveredGames.title: MuHa does it again by bringing us what we wanted without even realizing we wanted it. A cyberpunk game set in a Slavic post-apocalyptic of Thea. TEA has ended and the game has grown... Great job MuHa!

coveredGames.name: Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous - Enhanced Edition
coveredGames.title: Did you enjoy the first game? Good because more of the same, but even better in my opinion. Lots of options. Lots of load-outs with even more options to get creative. A solid second try with results!

coveredGames.name: Pathfinder: Kingmaker — Enhanced Plus Edition
coveredGames.title: A fantastic RPG game with a party system that is robust. Territory management? Magic systems? Lots of combat? Yes. Solid lore and good DLC flesh the game out. Though combat and AI need work. Good buy!

coveredGames.name: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader
coveredGames.title: From the people that made Pathfinder, a WH40K twist on that engine and mechanic. Rich lore, solid game play and many branching paths. Is it good? Yea. Great? Maybe. Worth a buy? Certainly for me.

coveredGames.name: Disco Elysium - The Final Cut
coveredGames.title: A very smart narrative game set in some alternate type world. Interesting decisions, hard choices and diverse outcomes create a breathtaking narrative that can take the player to odd places. Enjoy!

coveredGames.name: ENDLESS Legend™ 2
coveredGames.title: The folks at Amplitude Studios are back in good form. They have taken all they've learned since the first game and brought it to its sequel. A stunning game musically and visually with improved play!

coveredGames.name: Let Them Trade
coveredGames.title: It's like Anno-lite with a really nice aesthetic from an indie developer. Could use some more keyboard shortcuts, a freeplay mode, and some other QOL stuff, but it's off to a great start.

coveredGames.name: Victoria 3
coveredGames.title: Worth the purchase. Fun, enjoyable, and something I can easily recommend.

coveredGames.name: Big Walk
coveredGames.title: Good gameplay, nice atmosphere, and plenty of fun. Glad I gave it a try.

coveredGames.name: Don't Starve Together
coveredGames.title: A really fun game that does what it needs to do. Definitely recommended.

coveredGames.name: Grim Dawn
coveredGames.title: Pleasantly surprised by this one. Enjoyable gameplay and a solid experience overall.

coveredGames.name: HITMAN World of Assassination
coveredGames.title: Fun from start to finish. Easy recommendation for anyone looking for a good game.

coveredGames.name: We Were Here Together

coveredGames.name: Assassin's Creed® Odyssey

coveredGames.name: Marvel’s Spider-Man Remastered

coveredGames.title: A solid game with a nice overall experience. Definitely worth playing.

coveredGames.name: The Sims™ 4
coveredGames.title: Really fun and enjoyable. I had a good time with it and would recommend giving it a try.

coveredGames.name: When Chests Rain Tons of Loot
coveredGames.title: Auto-battler incremental where you deploy heroes, grab flying loot, and fill a chest before it bursts. Each run powers a huge skill tree. Roguelite-flavored loop that escalates satisfyingly.

coveredGames.name: Cucumber
coveredGames.title: Press space. Collect cucumbers. Craft 100k across six rarity tiers to reach the top. Free collector with a surprising amount of depth hidden behind one very committed vegetable.

coveredGames.name: Astario
coveredGames.title: Build asteroid-hopping automated factories and ships where real orbital physics actually affect logistics. Barebones EA tutorial, but the foundation is satisfying automation in space.

coveredGames.name: Your party died again
coveredGames.title: Pick a party, sink into 225 skill nodes across 4 hero trees, and auto-shred demons while you hoard loot. Short but tightly built — a punchy incremental dungeon crawler worth the ask.

coveredGames.name: No Blink Allowed
coveredGames.title: Stop a deteriorating computer clock as close to zero as you can, collect shards, build a skill tree, and fight through glitching displays and hidden timers in this 1.5–2.5 hour sprint.

coveredGames.name: Fish It!: Sort the Aquarium Shop
coveredGames.title: 4,100 fish, zero order — sort every swimmer back to the right tank, unlock smart-throw and highlight abilities to pick up speed, and gradually turn the chaos into a tidy aquarium shop.

coveredGames.name: SHRED A BILLION
coveredGames.title: A billion dollars in a vault and one shredder — start with bare hands, upgrade to buckets, vacuums, and drones, dig five floors deep, and there's a secret at the bottom waiting.

coveredGames.name: 2.3 Billion
coveredGames.title: You start with one spark and 30 seconds. Dash, pull, trigger frenzy, then spend what you caught. Each reset flips a new perk. First goal: 2.3 billion. Find out what.

coveredGames.name: No Asteroids
coveredGames.title: One miner, a pickaxe, and 5 million cubic meters between Earth and oblivion. Pickaxe to missile swarm upgrade loop. Up to 8-player co-op. AI-generated music, SFX, and text disclosed.

coveredGames.name: Swift Cultivation
coveredGames.title: A text-based idle cultivation sim: set an action queue and let time run — breakthrough when full, eat when health drops, reincarnate stronger each death, across 50 realms toward ascension.

coveredGames.name: Guildlands
coveredGames.title: Free idle RPG that lives on your taskbar — your hero fights, mines and crafts while you work. Gear is drawn layer by layer onto your character. Shared world with a player-run economy and clans.

coveredGames.name: Depthforged
coveredGames.title: Forge gear at the anvil, slot it into grid packs where neighbours change each other's effects, and watch your party of four fight deeper through 500 dungeon levels. Releases in December.

coveredGames.name: Cornerwitch
coveredGames.title: Cozy desktop idler where a little witch lives in your screen's corner, leveling up spells and collecting cosmetics while you do other things. Casual, cute, and mostly mouse-only.

coveredGames.name: Örnöga: Idle & Loot
coveredGames.title: Idle mage RPG: grow from novice to archwizard through four spell schools, seven stats and loot that modifies your magic. Fully hands-off or hands-on; mercenaries back you up either way.

coveredGames.name: Internet Cafe 98
coveredGames.title: Build a 1998 internet cafe from one beige box to a global franchise. Assemble PCs part by part, serve customers, research tech, and play ten actual retro games while your regulars grind away.

coveredGames.name: Pest Protocol
coveredGames.title: Squash pests manually until your cursor handles the swinging, then start placing bombs, drones and a frog across a tactical grid — it scales from frantic clicking to full hands-off chaos.

coveredGames.name: Haoru: Desktop Chaos
coveredGames.title: She lives on your Windows desktop, keeps you company while you work, and smashes everything on screen with 27 weapons — nothing real is ever touched. Only pixels get hurt.

coveredGames.name: Undervein
coveredGames.title: Start with a pickaxe, hire dwarves, steam borers and quantum drills, and sink your tunnel through coal, gold and crystal toward an ancient portal. The old miners left their lanterns burning.

coveredGames.name: Hoard
coveredGames.title: Forge keys, open chests, dodge or slay the mimics, and hire goblin helpers who keep cracking chests while you're away. Six worlds of increasingly rare loot with a dragon at the end.

coveredGames.name: A Thousand Cloys
coveredGames.title: Harvest alien resources, deploy high-tech toasters (they're Cloys) to mine automatically, and explore a mysterious planet to unearth upgrade nodes. Fully active or fully idle — your pace.

coveredGames.name: DeepBreaker
coveredGames.title: Punch through stone blocks with bare hands, upgrade your gloves at the workbench, and carve a path deeper underground. Something is hiding beyond the walls — the mystery threads through every layer.

coveredGames.name: Token Club: AI Desktop Pet
coveredGames.title: An idle desktop pet for the vibe-coding era: it runs on stage to dance every time you prompt Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity, pocketing each prompt's API cost.

coveredGames.name: OVERDRIVE PINBALL
coveredGames.title: Neon pinball table meets full incremental automation. Upgrade bumpers, unlock auto-flippers, stack 120 skills for chain lightning and multiball madness. Manual or hands-off, it escalates.

coveredGames.name: Incraiders
coveredGames.title: Space invaders meets incremental progression. Shoot down waves of aliens, stack power upgrades, unlock the Mega Cannon, and warp to tougher dimensions. Retro arcade meets endless numbers.

coveredGames.name: Keep The Ammo Flowing
coveredGames.title: Mine ore, forge shells, lay track—your automated turret needs ammo, and the swarm never stops. 21 sectors of mobile rail-defense with upgrade paths, special ammo, and siege mode.

coveredGames.name: TCG Card Shop Simulator
coveredGames.title: Run your own card shop: stock booster packs, crack some to collect, set prices, hire staff, and host tournaments. The full addiction loop of TCGs in a satisfying management sim with absurd depth.

coveredGames.name: Slot Grind
coveredGames.title: Spin, bank the payout, buy machines and automate the lever into a money printer. The 77% hides a split — English reviews skew negative on two-hour depth, and one flags an NG+ reset wiping a save.

coveredGames.name: IDLE_DIRECTIVE
coveredGames.title: Idly gather and sort loot across a decaying world, automating repairs and trading with survivors — a grid-inventory idler. Very Positive and trending up, but timers gate hard and endgame thins out.

coveredGames.name: Sir, We Have an Orc Problem
coveredGames.title: Hold the line against orc hordes with a deep upgrade tree, strafing runs and orbital lasers — a crunchy tower-defense incremental. Very Positive and a blast, though short at ~12 levels and grindy.

coveredGames.name: Feed the Greed
coveredGames.title: Send skeletons to feed a hungry space rift for essence in this cheap, pretty pixel incremental. The 73% score hides it: English reviewers call it hollow and one-note, done in an hour.

coveredGames.name: Spiritstead
coveredGames.title: Raise a cozy magic village and coax out hidden spirits by doing the right things — gorgeous, gentle, idle-paced town-building. Very Positive, if short and light on strategy for the full price.

coveredGames.name: Hole Is Mine
coveredGames.title: Dive into a divine pit and fling your little Mini'Ohs to mine it clean — a charming incremental with a meaty skill tree and real polish. Very Positive, though the late-game grind wears thin.

coveredGames.name: Sandustry
coveredGames.title: Mine fully destructible pixel worlds where every grain of sand is a resource, then automate the whole messy supply chain — Factorio's depth minus the stress. Overwhelmingly Positive; wants more.

coveredGames.name: Fishing Inc
coveredGames.title: Inherited as a 'not recommended' pick — but 1,988 reviews say Very Positive. A cheap, relaxing fish-catch-and-upgrade incremental; just know the loop stays simple, so take it as cozy, not deep.

coveredGames.name: Suncraft
coveredGames.title: A cozy pixel adventure of gathering, crafting and automating to rebuild a village and its Sunspire. Very Positive — idle fans sink 12-30 hours in, though mid-game crafting waits divide people.

coveredGames.name: Alchemy Factory
coveredGames.title: A compact, co-op medieval automation game: belts, production lines, potions and relics with Factorio-level smarts in a cozier package. Very Positive; mid-game balance is the main gripe.

coveredGames.name: Maktala: Slime Lootfest
coveredGames.title: Grind slimes for loot up a skill tree. Its score is Positive, but nearly every English review is negative — scripted upgrades that don't scale together, no customization, no replay past ~4h.

coveredGames.name: Stellar Nursery
coveredGames.title: Click a cold star to life, buy nine empty worlds, watch Earth grow to billions and name its city. Offline ticking, 57 visual themes, a persistent narrator who waited a hundred thousand years for you.

coveredGames.name: AFKTower
coveredGames.title: Pixel-art idle RPG docked to screen's edge: hero climbs 10,000 floors solo, earning 12 loot rarities while you're away. Four classes, Paragon constellation, offline earning. AI art, hand-edited.

coveredGames.name: Summonforge: Idle RPG
coveredGames.title: Free-to-play idle RPG: collect 80 heroes, build a team of four, push through endless worlds and a leaderboard. Fuse dupes for star upgrades, collect loot with randomized affixes, progress offline.

coveredGames.name: Arctic Drive
coveredGames.title: A cooperative survival simulator set in the harsh Arctic. Drive vehicles with your friends, scavenge for supplies, repair your car on the go, and survive blizzards, hunger!

coveredGames.name: Desktop Wallet Heroes
coveredGames.title: "Desktop Wallet Heroes" offers a unique take on the genre—the game is built around resource management and tactics within a compact format.

coveredGames.name: Slotbound
coveredGames.title: Watching your army absorb weaker units to become an unstoppable force is so satisfying. Slotbound is an instant indie classic!

coveredGames.name: GloveUp!
coveredGames.title: Another fast-paced knockout! GloveUp! delivers incredible combat with intuitive controls and highly responsive punching mechanics. The intense gameplay and stellar sound design!

coveredGames.name: The Crust
coveredGames.title: This game is really cool. It will especially appeal to fans of building production lines and economic exploration sims-these aspects are implemented in great depth. I highly recommend checking it out.

coveredGames.name: Police Chief Simulator
coveredGames.title: The ultimate chief experience! Every choice matters, from budget cuts to tactical deployments. The crime heatmaps are a awesome feature. Can't stop playing this amazing game!

coveredGames.name: Quarantine Zone: The Last Check
coveredGames.title: This is a great game with a lot of potential. The story mode is short—you can complete the entire game in 3–4 hours. I really enjoyed spending time with it!

coveredGames.name: [HERROR] Gas Station Case
coveredGames.title: The plot was surprising, as it combines classic mystical stories with ones not typically found in horror games. I thoroughly enjoyed the game, searching for secrets, and enjoying the views!

coveredGames.name: Backyard Baseball '97
coveredGames.title: A true timeless masterpiece! An absolute classic of sports arcades! The game delivers pure nostalgia with its vibrant cartoon graphics and simple yet incredibly addictive gameplay.

coveredGames.name: Trees Inc
coveredGames.title: A meditative forestry business simulator: grow trees, build a timber harvesting and processing chain, upgrade equipment, and expand production.

coveredGames.name: Midnight Special
coveredGames.title: A retro horror game with a 1980s feel, featuring a dark 16-bit aesthetic and point-and-click gameplay. Explore a sinister mansion, solve puzzles, and survive terrifying mysteries!

coveredGames.name: Car Dealer Simulator
coveredGames.title: The game mechanics are polished, and the gameplay loop is addictive! It's fun to hunt, buy, repair, and flip cars while growing my dealership’s reputation.

coveredGames.name: CarX Drift Racing Online 2
coveredGames.title: The weight transfer physics are so intuitive, you can really feel the car biting into the corners. This is definitely one of the best games out there right now! Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: BIGFOOT
coveredGames.title: The game isn't very scary but cool. I love all games of this kind, but since in this game the enemy rarely attacks, I value it above others.I really like that game is constantly updated and refined.

coveredGames.name: Beer Manufacture Simulator
coveredGames.title: For each new beer variety, the recipe has to be purchased first, and you don't always automatically know which recipe is needed for the next beer you order. There's only one solution: Try it out!

coveredGames.name: Stellar Tactics
coveredGames.title: An RPG with elements of a full-fledged economic strategy. Explore the vastness of our universe - of course, you'll first need to arm your ship and assemble a loyal crew of professionals!

coveredGames.name: DuneCrawl
coveredGames.title: A great game for relaxing in co-op! There's a story, but it's not the main focus. You probably won't want to play it on purpose, but it's great to play with friends!

coveredGames.name: Chrono Gear: Warden of Time
coveredGames.title: The captivating adventures of virtual streaming stars. An inventive 2D platformer. An exemplary fan game that does everything it can to entice you!

coveredGames.name: Yunashi no Yume
coveredGames.title: In this unique role-playing game, you take on the role of a soul guide, guiding people into their new existence - a digital afterlife. The game is based on a deep narrative.

coveredGames.name: Desktop Heroes
coveredGames.title: Very nice standby mode. The fact that it doesn't take up the entire screen is exactly what I look for in a standby mode. The game floats smoothly underneath it while I work.

coveredGames.name: Deconstruction Simulator
coveredGames.title: A stress-relieving simulator where you can smash everything with incredible satisfaction and excellent physics!

coveredGames.name: Otherskin
coveredGames.title: Epic solo journey with alien morphs that provide variety and depth in combat and exploration. The AI guide enhances engagement and makes exploration seamless.

coveredGames.name: Gun Center Simulator
coveredGames.title: Immerse yourself in the atmosphere of an exciting simulator, where you take on the role of the owner and manager of your own gun shop.

coveredGames.name: Night Club Simulator
coveredGames.title: I've been waiting for this game for so long!! Oh my god, I never thought working in a club would be so difficult, but at the same time interesting, a very good game, I recommend it!

coveredGames.name: Animal Shelter 2
coveredGames.title: A very kind and heartfelt game! Animal Shelter 2 allows you to feel like a real savior for homeless animals. I like how well-thought-out the mechanics of caring for pets are!

coveredGames.name: Rooftops & Alleys: The Parkour Game
coveredGames.title: Very cool parkour game, if you understand the controls you can play with pleasure! Beautiful graphics and exciting game modes, you can play with friends!

coveredGames.name: Revenge of the Savage Planet
coveredGames.title: A good continuation of the first game. Large maps with a bunch of secrets, riddles and puzzles. Interesting storyline, new items and boosts, colorful biomes.

coveredGames.name: The Killing Antidote
coveredGames.title: The game is definitely worth attention for RE fans. I've played it several times, play additional modes including user modifications. I'm waiting for the continuation of the story.

coveredGames.name: Islets Defense
coveredGames.title: This is a great game for those who like a well-thought-out strategy, which requires not only attentiveness, but also the ability to adapt to a changing situation.

coveredGames.name: Heat Death: Survival Train
coveredGames.title: Solid early access with a clear path forward. The team’s openness and ongoing content adds confidence for long-term play.

coveredGames.name: MEMOLITH: Forsaken by Light
coveredGames.title: The pixel art atmosphere is haunting, while tight turn-based combat and clever memory-binding mechanics create satisfying, methodical progression that dont feel grindy.

coveredGames.name: The Hundred Line -Last Defense Academy-
coveredGames.title: The strategic combat system is both engaging and challenging, making every battle a thrilling experience. Great for fans of tactical RPGs.

coveredGames.name: Downward Spear
coveredGames.title: Playing as a human 'experiment' navigating a flooded world filled with grotesque monsters is both thrilling and terrifying

coveredGames.name: Dive The Depths
coveredGames.title: The variety of missions keeps me engagedmthere's always something new to strive for.

coveredGames.name: Rooftops & Alleys: The Parkour Game
coveredGames.title: Rooftops & Alleys: The Parkour Game maps are beautifully designed, offering unique challenges and aesthetic appeal. This game is a joy to traverse.

coveredGames.name: I Am Cat
coveredGames.title: A charming and immersive VR sandbox that nails the cat vibe. The house is full of secrets, the quests are engaging, and the mini-games provide a steady stream of lighthearted fun and laughter.

coveredGames.name: Maid of Salvation
coveredGames.title: Maid of Salvation delivers fast-paced combat and stylish sword-and-firearm combos. I’m impressed by the fluid combat system and the skill board progression.

coveredGames.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails through Daybreak
coveredGames.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails through Daybreak finally let it go from the traditional Cold Steel cast and prepare to meet entirely new teams and main characters. Calvard arc is really awesome.

coveredGames.name: Magicka
coveredGames.title: Lots of co-op fun. Combine elements to cast various types of spells, including combinations like making enemies wet and electrocuting them. Revenge for friendly fire will slow your pace in fun ways!

coveredGames.name: ENCODYA
coveredGames.title: ENCODYA - is cute and wholesome point-and-click adventure in cyberpunk dystopian setting. Main characters is instantly likeable, and a story about missing father is really touching.

coveredGames.name: The Banner Saga
coveredGames.title: A great looking unique tactical challenge alongside a story full of choices and surprise. Bleak landscapes and the depressing situations your characters find themselves in mean this isn't easy going.

coveredGames.name: Reverse Collapse: Code Name Bakery
coveredGames.title: Reverse Collapse: Code Name Bakery - this is a remaster and the original is pretty old (something around 2011), but the new version is really polished and add a ton of new content.

coveredGames.name: TOKOYO: The Tower of Perpetuity
coveredGames.title: TOKOYO is fantastic because of its easy pick-up and play appeal, as well as the fact that it provides an experience that actually renews itself each day.

coveredGames.name: Potato Flowers in Full Bloom
coveredGames.title: Potato Flowers in Full Bloom is separated into two modes: exploration, similar to a conventional dungeon crawler, and jrpg fights with cool moves and stuff, it's great.

coveredGames.name: Dragon Eclipse
coveredGames.title: Dragon Eclipse is another roguelike experience we have as a guest today and while it's a bit rough some edges, the overall experience is quite fun and satisfying.

coveredGames.name: Nancy Drew®: Mystery of the Seven Keys™
coveredGames.title: Nancy Drew®: Mystery of the Seven Keys - classic detective adventure with the usual point'n'click mechanics and sometimes challenging puzzles.

coveredGames.name: BREAK ARTS II
coveredGames.title: BREAK ARTS II is an absolutely insane and crazy fun mecha racing title, with a strong gameplay mechanics and good visuals.

coveredGames.name: Clonizer
coveredGames.title: The gameplay is approachable yet deep - perfect for casual players and strategy enthusiasts alike.

coveredGames.name: Touhou Luna Nights
coveredGames.title: Not only Touhou Luna Nights is one of the best games in Touhou series can offer, it's also a really great metroidvania by itself even if you don't know anything about characters.

coveredGames.name: Drago Noka
coveredGames.title: Given the quantity of decent to great farming and life sims on Steam, Drago Noka is a lot of fun and ranks high on the list of PC games.

coveredGames.name: Rauniot
coveredGames.title: Rauniot is around 6 hours long and the puzzles are bearable and interesting to do without guides and stuff. Great retro-inspired experience.

coveredGames.name: Croixleur Sigma - Deluxe Edition
coveredGames.title: Croixleur Sigma is surprisingly addictive, the gameplay loop is not that complex, but it will capture your heart and attention.

coveredGames.name: El Dorado: The Golden City Builder
coveredGames.title: A captivating city-building game in the Yucatan jungle. Manage resources, worship gods, and expand your empire. Despite minor UI flaws, the unique god system & gorgeous visuals make it worth playing!

coveredGames.name: Songs of Silence
coveredGames.title: Looking for a fresh strategy game? Songs of Silence delivers with innovative deckbuilding & epic battles. Lead your forces to glorious victory!

coveredGames.name: Project Hospital
coveredGames.title: Project Hospital dives deep into real illnesses, demanding complex workflows and meticulous hospital design. It's a challenging yet rewarding evolution for seasoned hospital tycoons.

coveredGames.name: Hookah Haze
coveredGames.title: The devs behind "Hookah Haze" already proved themselves with other games so we expected an original and fun game and they definitely delivered.

coveredGames.name: Oddsparks: An Automation Adventure
coveredGames.title: Oddsparks: An Automation Adventure - highly unique experience, and creating and commanding provides a lot of fun. Feel free to try this one.

coveredGames.name: Pan'orama

coveredGames.name: False Myth 2

coveredGames.name: Wielders of the Essence
