coveredGames.name: Tower Tactics II
coveredGames.title: A fantastic tower defense series & this installment is just as compelling as the original. There's plenty to do in Early Access w/ unlockable game modes, ascendance, workshop support, & deckbuilding.

coveredGames.name: Aarik And The Ruined Kingdom
coveredGames.title: Clearly inspired by Monument Valley, and that's good news for those of us with an appetite for more brain-bending puzzles. It's short and sweet, clocking in at about 2-4 hours.

coveredGames.name: Wispward
coveredGames.title: Reminiscent of a classic TD Flash game w/ added gathering. It's entertaining enough, but the short, folksy music loop will soon drive you mad. Easy to toggle it off & listen to Spotify. 120 levels.

coveredGames.name: WizKitty and the Tower of Doom, Gloom, and Other Bad Stuff
coveredGames.title: An odd little deckbuilder that really clicks once you get the hang of it. Nice to be introduced to a project that keeps calling us back to play another round. Addictive game loop.

coveredGames.name: Eslabong
coveredGames.title: There's a crazy amount of depth here, yet Eslabong is approachable to new players. It's ideal for short sessions or long binges, with plenty of features and upgrades to obsess over. Play solo or PvP.

coveredGames.name: Order Automatica
coveredGames.title: If you liked Throne of Bone, say goodbye to your loved ones, because this, right here, is digital crack. Rudimentary on the surface, strategies & synergies are constantly discovered. Also on mobile.

coveredGames.name: Whisper of the Swallows
coveredGames.title: Survive in a harsh world that wants you dead. Extreme weather hits hard & fast, so you better have plenty of firewood & shelter to bunker down & ride it out, wherever it finds you. Challenging & deep.

coveredGames.name: Magisterium: Fantasy Craft
coveredGames.title: Pleasantly surprised how much we're enjoying this W.I.P. medieval life sim that reminds of Gothic 1 & 2 with a survival-craft twist. It's refreshing to see a dev bring something new to the genre.

coveredGames.name: The Lantern of the Laughless Saint
coveredGames.title: Think of this as a work-in-progress, spiritual successor to Morrowind with an option for co-op. NerveLabs has nailed the immersive tone Bethesda created, with smart writing & sublime world-building.

coveredGames.name: Vonkelveld
coveredGames.title: A clever god sim that focuses on guidance: Tend, don't command. Shape land, weather, fortune & pressure while people remain free. Move from 1 life, a city, a civilization, a world, & the torus view.

coveredGames.name: Roots in the Sky - The Hand of Glory 2
coveredGames.title: This is a well-written, meaty adventure game in the vein of Broken Sword & Gabriel Knight. Travel the world as you unlock an intriguing mystery, investigating beautiful scenes & solving logic puzzles.

coveredGames.name: ASANA Visual Novel
coveredGames.title: A fully voiced, sci-fi dark comedy visual novel. Build stats, navigate branching paths, and argue with N.E.K.O., the ship’s godlike AI in cat form. Emanates moodiness, personality, and charm.

coveredGames.name: Circle Empires 2
coveredGames.title: Happy 8th B-day, Circle Empires! CE2 boasts endless RTS replayability w/ randomly generated worlds, new units, & custom units w/ single-player, co-op, & versus modes. Added content since release.

coveredGames.name: DiDiDiG
coveredGames.title: Mine ore on the Moon, send it back to Earth to earn money, & buy Skill Cores to upgrade your abilities. Use a variety of helpful equipment on your expedition.

coveredGames.name: Tormentum II
coveredGames.title: A dark, hand-drawn point & click adventure inspired by Giger & Beksiński. Challenges how far you will go to solve intriguing puzzles & machinations in a bleak world. Multiple, branching endings.

coveredGames.name: City States: Medieval
coveredGames.title: Grab your favorite snack & drink & dive into this deep grand strategy passion project by Reverie. A recent update has made HUGE QoL improvements, especially to the tutorial & mid-late game experience.

coveredGames.name: Human Host
coveredGames.title: A budget-friendly, open-world survival-craft alternative to 7 Days to Die. Create mobile forts, trap-mazes, tunnels, & destroy most anything...even skyscrapers. Frequent updates & Workshop support.

coveredGames.name: HOLD THE LINE
coveredGames.title: A short & sweet classic TD game that costs next to nothing. Eight maps with three difficulty modes to earn up to five stars per map. There's a good selection of towers and three special manual attacks

coveredGames.name: Deadhaus Sonata
coveredGames.title: DENIS DYACK IS BACK with a very early version of his spiritual successor to Blood Omen: Legacy of Kain. His method weaves deep narrative with fresh innovations that break through industry stagnation.

coveredGames.name: Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors
coveredGames.title: Dungeon Crawling mixed w/ card battling? YES PLEASE. The dev of Vampire Survivors is back w/ another smash hit & a new formula for building combos to battle waves of familiar sprites.

coveredGames.name: Invincible VS
coveredGames.title: Exactly what Invincible fans needed: an exciting & nimble arcade fighter stuffed w/ references to the comics & show. Very approachable for newcomers & veterans alike. Made by the Killer Instinct crew.

coveredGames.name: Voor De Kroon
coveredGames.title: It's like Mount & Blade & Total War gave birth to Voor De Kroon. Large open-field & castle siege campaign, highly-detailed army editor, & Workshop content. Dev grinds out regular updates.

coveredGames.name: Shards of the Realm
coveredGames.title: An absorbing hidden gem when you give it a chance. Manage your fortress & fight against the demonic siege in turn-based, directional combat w/ up to nine multi-class party members. 50+ hours of fun.

coveredGames.name: Skull Horde
coveredGames.title: Lovely presentation, thumpin' soundtrack, & stylish graphics grace surprisingly deep customization options & upgrades for your horde. Super smooth & plays great w/ a keyboard or controller.

coveredGames.name: Devil Spire Falls
coveredGames.title: Think of it as a sandbox 'King's Field' w/ a smattering of Asheron's Call. 18 weapon classes, 35 skills, true freedom, physics, shenanigans, & consequences for your actions in an unforgiving world.

coveredGames.name: Slay the Spire 2
coveredGames.title: Familiar faces return in another wonderfully weird spire of challenges that's easy to pick up & play, whether you're a new player or an old veteran of the series. Graphics & presentation are crisper.

coveredGames.name: Dungeon Warfare 3
coveredGames.title: DW3 has been a very enjoyable evolution in the series, especially after you get the hang of the new hex-grid mechanics. A recent, new roguelike mode is addictive as heck & offers even more ways play.

coveredGames.name: Deck Vs Doom
coveredGames.title: After over 100+ hrs, we can safely say that this is a phenomenal value for the nominal price tag. A plethora of decks, artifacts, achievements, unlockables, & powerful synergies to discover.

coveredGames.name: Super Battle Golf
coveredGames.title: Outstanding. A great way to release some stress after work, laughing your @ss off w/ friends. There's so many magic moments to be had here. 400k+ sold w/ new modes, maps, biomes, & workshop on the way

coveredGames.name: Aliosso
coveredGames.title: Combine tiles and run-changing cards to unleash power-packed combos and crush your enemies. A cool blending of Balatro and Slay the Spire mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Repel The Rifts
coveredGames.title: Even in Early Access, it's a pretty good value for the samoleans. There's currently four heroes, each w/ unique abilities to use actively (and passively), w/ their own special skill trees and loadouts

coveredGames.name: Pirates Outlaws 2: Heritage
coveredGames.title: A swashbuckling roguelike deckbuilder. Collect & fuse cards, gather powerful relics and adapt your strategy during each run.

coveredGames.name: Azmar Quest - Text Based RPG
coveredGames.title: Azmar Quest is a text-based RPG with turn-based battles and old-school vibes. Decide your path through dialogues with multiple choices.

coveredGames.name: BEYBLADE X EVOBATTLE
coveredGames.title: Three EVOLUTIONS have been unleashed in the "BEYBLADE ACTION" game that faithfully recreates the BEYBLADE X series.

coveredGames.name: Veterum
coveredGames.title: Turn-based tactical strategy with a detailed combat system and interactive environment. Explore the open world, complete quests, search for rare artifacts.

coveredGames.name: Command Deck
coveredGames.title: A sci-fi roguelike deckbuilder where you explore the galaxy, face hostile aliens, and upgrade your starship. It will take adaptability and strategic thinking to survive.

coveredGames.name: Marshals of Yore
coveredGames.title: Marshals of Yore is a hybrid of RTS and tower defense. It's easy to learn and play. Engage the enemy on 100+ stages. As you complete stages, you will unlock new and powerful items.

coveredGames.name: Oboro no Ichi
coveredGames.title: Another beautiful game from TheLaba, Oboro no Ichi is intuitive, relaxing, and fun to decorate and manage a vibey little night market for spirits, everything you need for a late night chill session <3

coveredGames.name: Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library!
coveredGames.title: The genesis of the insane sorting subgenre, it has all the vibes of a chill game while also managing to drive you crazy, worth every minute whether you're just relaxing or going completionist <3

coveredGames.name: Tidy Till Dawn
coveredGames.title: Tidy Till Dawn is a chill sorting game, taking a saturated subgenre and doing it better than most, though I also can't help but be a little biased towards the Japanese convenience store vibe <3

coveredGames.name: Monsters, Inn Order!
coveredGames.title: A cute little puzzle game where you have to make everyone in line happy. The concept is easy to grasp, and the puzzles make you think without stumping you, the perfect game to play while chilling <3

coveredGames.name: Loftia
coveredGames.title: Loftia is a vibey life sim where you can farm and decorate and chill with other players, creating a sense of community that you don't see in a lot of MMO's, can't wait to see more! <3

coveredGames.name: CooKing: Around the World
coveredGames.title: The gameplay itself is a fun experience of cooking trial and error, but it has a few bugs that prevent you from finishing the game. Once those are dealt with this would be an amazing puzzle game.

coveredGames.name: Cat Isle
coveredGames.title: Cat Isle is simplistic but satisfying, manage a little strip of shops for cute little cats, play a gatcha machine for decor, and expand and grow your cozy kitty isle <3 The sounds and music are a vibe

coveredGames.name: Pixel Pegz
coveredGames.title: This is such a satisfying arcade style game to play, simply made with plenty of games to pass some time in with or without friends <3

coveredGames.name: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered
coveredGames.title: Ok look, I know this one isn't cozy, but's it's my page and I'll put what I want on it, and I wanna put the Godzilla fighting game on it <3 (I swear this is the only time I'll do this, probably) <3

coveredGames.name: Witch's Cottage
coveredGames.title: The bones of this game are good, it just needs a bit more time to cook. As it is currently, it can feel a bit bare. If they continue updating this can absolutely turn into a little gem <3

coveredGames.name: Arcanum Idle
coveredGames.title: I not gonna lie, I'm not much of an idle clicker enjoyer, but for some reason this one quickly had me hooked! The art and gameplay is satisfying, the music is perfect, worth every bit of a try! <3

coveredGames.name: Character House -Desktop Companion-
coveredGames.title: Definitely one of the better, more freeing companion games! Tons of ways to customize your characters and interactions, cute art and smooth animations make this the perfection little companion game <3

coveredGames.name: Dressmaker
coveredGames.title: One of the best "crafting" games yet, loads of fabrics and details to choose from to let your creativity run wild. It is suuuper easy to spend hours making dresses without even realizing it <3

coveredGames.name: Aniimo
coveredGames.title: So far one of the coziest creature collector, and for free there's no reason not to give this a try. Tons of character customization, cute Aniimos, and solid gameplay await <3 just let them cook

coveredGames.name: Architecture & Design
coveredGames.title: One of the (way) better 'realistic' architecture games out there that will only get better as the community grows and adds to the workshop, nothing really limits you and I'm excited to see it develop!

coveredGames.name: Kemono Teatime
coveredGames.title: If you enjoyed Coffee Talk you'll love this little gem too! Brew tea, serve desserts, and find out little pieces of the world and the characters that makes you stop and think in the moment <3

coveredGames.name: Jammed
coveredGames.title: Ok, this one might be a little biased, but Jammed pairs a relaxed puzzler vibe with just enough transportation fidgeting to make the little Civ E major in me keep playing. Cozy nerd approved <3

coveredGames.name: Cozy Builder
coveredGames.title: Demo Review: A perfect building game to relax to. No combat, no hunger or stamina bar, and loads of building options to choose from. Collect materials and fix and build to your hearts content <3

coveredGames.name: lily's world XD
coveredGames.title: Demo Review: Lily's World is a cutesy "horror" game where you slowly uncover what happened to original owner of your PC, it balances cutey visuals with an overall eerie feeling beautifully <3

coveredGames.name: Moonfrost
coveredGames.title: Demo Review: Moonfrost takes a stylistic approach you don't see very often in this genre and it's absolutely beautiful for it. Build and farm in a game you can tell had love poured into every pixel <3

coveredGames.name: Moonlight Peaks
coveredGames.title: Demo Review: If Stardew and Animal Crossing had a spooky baby it would be Moonlight Peaks. It's game mechs you've (mostly) seen before but in a spooky wrapping that makes this lovely for alt gamers <3

coveredGames.name: 🌸 Lofi Mahjong 🌸
coveredGames.title: A timeless puzzle with cozy lofi vibes, perfect for late night idle discord chats where you just relax and match tiles until you have no more moves at 4 tiles left and start the whole vibe again <3

coveredGames.name: Midori no Kaori
coveredGames.title: A simple, soothing, *slow* experience. The content is simply decorating your little shop while serving customers. Don't go in expecting some end goal, just let your creativity flow <3

coveredGames.name: Cozy Cats Fit
coveredGames.title: Another solid vibey puzzle game from CozyPuzzleGames, soft sounds and art, simple gameplay, and relaxing music to idly solve some fitting puzzles <3

coveredGames.name: Planet of Lana II
coveredGames.title: Another game in the series that adds so much more to the story! The same beautiful art and music, but with quality of life additions and new ways to solve puzzles <3 just as fun as the last

coveredGames.name: Planet of Lana
coveredGames.title: A beautiful and (mostly) relaxing puzzle platformer with a deeper story. Puzzles are fun without being too difficult, making it the perfect relaxation platformer to spend a night chilling to <3

coveredGames.name: Hozy
coveredGames.title: Demo Review: Hozy offers loads of freedom in how you want to decorate and design your little spaces at the risk of losing track of time, can't wait to see the final result in the full release!

coveredGames.name: Glimvale : My Mini Overworld
coveredGames.title: A cute little city building idler. Nothing too complex or grindy, just a laid back little game where you build a village for your adventurers. Sweet and simple <3

coveredGames.name: Doodle Harmony Ghosts
coveredGames.title: A cute satisfying game. Something about the mouse and all the ghosties having names releases the dopamine in my brain, we love Nebula <3 The perfect game to play and replay when you have time to kill.

coveredGames.name: REANIMAL
coveredGames.title: Another absolute masterpiece from Tarsier <333 The atmosphere and music are darkly beautiful and finally you can play co-op with your friend! Another perfect "cozy" game for the slightly twisted <3

coveredGames.name: Virtual Cottage 2
coveredGames.title: Takes everything that made that made the first one a nice focusing game and made it even better, being able to design your cozy little space is *chefs kiss* and I can't wait to see the full release <3

coveredGames.name: Small Spaces
coveredGames.title: A nice decorating sim that allows loads of freedom in how you want to design your spaces, the vibes are nice and the lighting is better than a lot of games in this genre, 100% worth a try <3

coveredGames.name: ShantyTown
coveredGames.title: Demo Review: A beautifully simplistic game that gives you creative freedom without being too overwhelming. The art is lovely and the music is vibey, can't wait to see it on full release <3

coveredGames.name: Tiny Bookshop
coveredGames.title: A tiny bookshop with plenty of content! You can play slow and casual, or like a filthy sweat like I found myself doing. No matter how you end up playing, this is an amazing little gem to pick up! <3

coveredGames.name: Whisper of the House
coveredGames.title: A fun and detailed unpacking and design game that lets you explore the towns secrets and mysteries, the npc's are genuinely charming and the room designing is so satisfying <3

coveredGames.name: MakeRoom
coveredGames.title: A beautifully made room designer, the art is simplistic, there's plenty of options and abilities to make your own items, and the workshop community is wonderful and creative <3 they put me to shame

coveredGames.name: The August Before
coveredGames.title: A beautiful game that let's you pack up rooms while looking through little bread crumbs of a story between 3 girls, it's a simplistic but satisfying experience and the "story" had me taking sides :')

coveredGames.name: Little Corners
coveredGames.title: Demo Review: This little game takes those sticker books you see online and brings it to your PC, the levels are perfect to relax and vibe to and have loads of details to make it your perfect corner <3

coveredGames.name: Tailside: Cozy Cafe Sim
coveredGames.title: The perfect cafe sim that doesn't pressure you to go fast, it's simple and calming, the characters are cute and charming, and there's no reason not to give this little game a try <3

coveredGames.name: ISLANDERS: New Shores
coveredGames.title: A lovely little city builder with both strategy and relaxing sandbox modes, keeps your mind occupied but chill enough that it's the perfect game to play while watching your shows <3

coveredGames.name: Underkeep
coveredGames.title: Despite flaws, I consider Underkeep a modern—if casual—masterpiece and far superior to any other dungeon crawler to come out in recent memory.

coveredGames.name: The Sinking City 2
coveredGames.title: A Resident Evil-style survival horror shooter with great atmosphere and a romance-driven story. But if you want a deep Lovecraftian detective experience, look elsewhere. This isn't true Lovecraft.

coveredGames.name: Atomic Heart
coveredGames.title: If you’re interested in a shooter with a load of style and limited substance, and you have a high tolerance for modern, silly tones, then you might enjoy Atomic Heart. Otherwise, skip it.

coveredGames.name: Ground Zero
coveredGames.title: Ground Zero is an excellent successor to the classic Resident Evil style, offers a few nice quality-of-life changes of its own to the formula, and is well worth your time and money.

coveredGames.name: Mirage 7
coveredGames.title: Mirage 7 is a short yet fun puzzle adventure that mixes fantasy and sci-fi elements quite nicely. The straightforward gameplay was simple and enjoyable.

coveredGames.name: Xenonauts 2
coveredGames.title: Competently made & fun but its obsession with controlling the meta limits organic strategies and power fantasy. Xenonauts 2 is to X-COM what soymeat burgers are to a juicy steak.

coveredGames.name: Eye of the Commando
coveredGames.title: I want to make it clear that I really enjoyed Eye of the Commando. The game is a blast, and it does a great job with its concepts, but updates are sporadic and it's very short.

coveredGames.name: Devil Spire Falls
coveredGames.title: Devil Spire Falls obviously has a long way to go, but the game is already fun. Everything else hinges on Ithiro continuing to fill out the rest of the game.

coveredGames.name: The Necromancer's Tale
coveredGames.title: The game itself is decent, but contains woke elements that people may not want to deal with.

coveredGames.name: Hotel Galactic
coveredGames.title: I was dangerously close to being entertained when things weren’t breaking down, but I can’t comment on how long that would last since the gameplay loop was constantly disrupted by bugs.

coveredGames.name: Forever Skies
coveredGames.title: Forever Skies: Great airship building, poor pacing/story/endgame. Narrative blocks the fun gameplay. Wait for sale or pass unless you only want surface-level building.

coveredGames.name: Deadzone: Rogue
coveredGames.title: Deadzone offers decent fun for fans of repetitive "get stronger with each run" gameplay, though it's nothing special. Potential buyers should consider the studio's history and early access risks.

coveredGames.name: Denshattack!
coveredGames.title: this game is seriously so much fun with non-stop action, tricks, and flashy set pieces. ya can't go wrong with trainy hawk!

coveredGames.name: Wax Heads
coveredGames.title: a feel-good narrative game about recommending records and the power of music

coveredGames.name: LOVE ETERNAL
coveredGames.title: a short and weird precision platformer with tight gravity-flipping gameplay and a twisted story

coveredGames.name: Rayman® Origins
coveredGames.title: *must play* playing this on the 360 has been a life-altering experience and the music has been on repeat in my brain for days now. bonus points for couch co-op.

coveredGames.name: Phonopolis
coveredGames.title: Amanita Design has done it again! Another beautifully crafted world, another set of imaginative puzzles, and another cute protaganist. This may just be their best work yet...

coveredGames.name: Misericorde: Volume One
coveredGames.title: a slow burn at first (2/3 parts released so far) but i'm totally hooked on these VNs about a murder at a 15th century abbey. part murder mystery, part historical fiction, part... uh can't really say..

coveredGames.name: Creature Kitchen
coveredGames.title: a mysterious little cooking game where you befriend all sorts of creatures and feed them their favorite dishes. the perfect balance between creepy and cute.

coveredGames.name: Scarlet Hollow
coveredGames.title: *must play* a big mysterious/funny/dark/emotional choose your own adventure game with a seemingly impossible number of paths to go down. must.. romance... everybody...

coveredGames.name: Berry Bury Berry
coveredGames.title: a wonderfully addictive incremental game about throwing fruit into a hole in the ground

coveredGames.name: Cairn
coveredGames.title: *must play* an unforgettable journey about pushing through the pain and coming out on top... of the mountain.

coveredGames.name: Wobbledogs
coveredGames.title: weird as hell... i like it.

coveredGames.name: Skate Story
coveredGames.title: my favorite game of the year. vibrant, visceral, very, very chill. i'll be thinking about this one for a long time.

coveredGames.name: Hypogea
coveredGames.title: throwback 3d platformer with unique staff-based traversal mechanics. also, robots AND a megastructure.

coveredGames.name: Keeper
coveredGames.title: game took me to some very unexpected places... can't say more than that without spoiling anything, but this is one game ending i'll always remember

coveredGames.name: Metal Garden
coveredGames.title: a vibey little fps set inside an overgrown megastructure

coveredGames.name: Easy Delivery Co.
coveredGames.title: a spooky, snowy delivery game complete with energy drinks, minimum wage, and corporate conspiracy.

coveredGames.name: Strange Antiquities
coveredGames.title: a strange and spooky puzzle/investigation game that lets you get our your magnifying glass and search for clues. killer atmosphere and vibes.

coveredGames.name: Caput Mortum
coveredGames.title: a puzzle-heavy horror game with unconventional controls and a killer atmosphere. try the demo!

coveredGames.name: Strange Jigsaws
coveredGames.title: quite a strange (jigsaw) puzzle game with some really out of the box ideas. warning: you may need a walkthrough for this one. or maybe that's just me.. .

coveredGames.name: Öoo
coveredGames.title: *must play* a super tight puzzle platformer that uses its simplicity to continually blow your mind over the course of ~3 hours

coveredGames.name: FALLSTRUKTUR
coveredGames.title: *free* control your momentum as you fall through a dreamy, deconstructed megastructure. big vibes.

coveredGames.name: Supraworld
coveredGames.title: a fantastic early access start! extremely clever puzzles and a charming world to explore, just make sure your pc is up for running it

coveredGames.name: DOGWALK
coveredGames.title: *free* the cutest dog walking game everrr

coveredGames.name: Pseudoregalia
coveredGames.title: *must play* the 3d platformer/metroidvania GOAT (featuring a goat). the movement tech is so, so good it's unbelievable

coveredGames.name: The Lantern of the Laughless Saint
coveredGames.title: A densely packed, Elder Scrolls inspired first person RPG with superb world design & writing. There are Early Access issues, but an indie game of this scope deserves some leeway.

coveredGames.name: The Dream Of A Cockspur
coveredGames.title: A gripping, often unsettling adventure that toys with player expectations. The Dream Of A Cockspur is remarkably unique in it's art style, narrative and gameplay variety. Well worth the cost of entry.

coveredGames.name: The Incident at Galley House
coveredGames.title: An remarkable take on the detective genre, Galley House starts full of mystery and retains it throughout. While the captivating art and stellar voicework brings this seemingly static game to life.

coveredGames.name: HYPERBEAT
coveredGames.title: Hyperbeat's confident blend of Rez and OSU offers a well-paced campaign for players that just want to have a groovy weekend, while also having more than enough challenge for the rhythm game sickos.

coveredGames.name: Phonopolis
coveredGames.title: The latest gorgeously hand-crafted experience from Amanita Design is their best yet. Ending an oppressive regime with the power of your musical mind has never looked, sounded, or felt this good.

coveredGames.name: Map Map - A Game About Maps
coveredGames.title: Map Map is a bit like playing Geoguessr, but you are both Rainbolt AND the person with a GoPro constructing the Street View maps in realtime. A delightful puzzler!

coveredGames.name: Slay the Spire 2
coveredGames.title: Statistically speaking you're already playing this; you don't need a recommendation. But if you do, this is the best roguellike deckbuilder ever made. Yes it's better than the first one.

coveredGames.name: Funi Raccoon Game
coveredGames.title: Sure it's a 3D collectathon, yeah it's got good music, wow you can jump blah blah whatever - Funi Racoon Game is the highest-effort ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (complimentary) we've ever played.

coveredGames.name: Don't Stop, Girlypop!
coveredGames.title: Drenched in neon pinks and an e-girl aesthetic that makes the varied combat feel like it's being performed in a finely curated Tumblr page, Don't Stop, Girlypop! is hyperspeed FPS bubblegum goodness!

coveredGames.name: Berry Bury Berry
coveredGames.title: An incremental game that's more than simply Number Go Up. Multiple endings, a creepy vibe, and a play space that's waiting for you to break it open make Berry Bury Berry a great way to kill some time.

coveredGames.name: Perfect Tides: Station to Station
coveredGames.title: Station to Station has floated in on the same wave as Consume Me and Despelote to deliver a brutally honest examination of the blurry transition from teenage girl to adult woman in the early 2000s.

coveredGames.name: Cairn
coveredGames.title: The Game Bakers have crafted one of the greatest climbing games of all time. An experience that offers up an uncaring monolith of stone and leaves you to solve its geologically coincidental maze.

coveredGames.name: Angeline Era
coveredGames.title: Following in Analgesic's idiosynchratic stylings, Angeline Era revives bumpslashing to tell a story of religion & philosophy that's equal parts profound and hilarious. One of the best games of 2025!

coveredGames.name: BIRDCAGE
coveredGames.title: With bullet(and sword)-hell combat that's flanked on all sides by narrative beats that'd make Yoshiyuki Tomino blush and a soundtrack that'll set your soul on fire, BIRDCAGE is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic.

coveredGames.name: Detective Instinct: Farewell, My Beloved
coveredGames.title: Detective Instinct succeeds in pulling on every strand of DS era adventure game nostalgia while offering a story full of joy, intrigue and heartbreak. An incredibly charming debut title from Armonica!

coveredGames.name: Hypogea
coveredGames.title: Hypogea's technical (and forgiving) platforming, charming characters, and oppressive megastructure world combine to deliver an experience that's wonderfully joyful in spite of its dank environments.

coveredGames.name: Kingdoms of the Dump
coveredGames.title: A group of real-life janitors have done the seemingly impossible, creating a SNES-flavoured RPG that isn't simply mired in the trash heap of nostalgia, instead recycling the old to build anew.

coveredGames.name: Sektori
coveredGames.title: Fans of Geometry Wars rejoice, Sektori's the hot new twin stick shooter on the block from a Housemarque alumnus and it's here to blast your brain to bits with razor sharp visuals and thumping techno!

coveredGames.name: Mohrta
coveredGames.title: Much like the world and gameplay that this bizarre level-based FPS offers, Mohrta is equal parts familiar and totally fresh, pulling on similar strands of artistry as Morrowind and Doom.

coveredGames.name: Tavern Keeper 🍻
coveredGames.title: Even in its Early Access state, Tavern Keeper makes space at its joyful bar for every kind of player; from the number-crunching MBA graduate to interior decorators that lean Tolkien.

coveredGames.name: The Séance of Blake Manor
coveredGames.title: With puzzles and deductive intrigue that are as sharp as its presentation, The Seance of Blake Manor plays like a good book that you can't put down. One of 2025's best!

coveredGames.name: CARIMARA: Beneath the forlorn limbs
coveredGames.title: Carimara's pocket dimension of spooky delights rewards players for paying attention to its environmental oddities with an efficiently woven folk horror tale

coveredGames.name: Absolum
coveredGames.title: Taking the traditional beat-em-up formula of mastery through repetition, and giving it just enough of the roguelike twist to have some variety between runs, makes for an incredibly moreish action game

coveredGames.name: Baby Steps
coveredGames.title: Do not let the presentation fool you, while the initially absurd locomotion can result in a lot of frustration, Baby Steps is a deeply thoughtful game that challenges the very notions of difficulty.

coveredGames.name: Bloodthief
coveredGames.title: The sensation of reaching escape velocity in a low-poly Gothic Victorian setting using nothing more than the power of BLOOD makes for an eye-wateringly good time in Bloodthief.

coveredGames.name: Consume Me
coveredGames.title: Telling a story that's so brutally personal and affecting as the subject matter of Consume Me would imply, while being one of the cutest and funniest game of 2025, is nothing short of masterful.

coveredGames.name: PIGFACE
coveredGames.title: A perfectly grimy first-person action game out now in Early Access, evoking memories of the best in the FPS genre while offering modern refinements that will leave you desperate for the next update.

coveredGames.name: The Little Tomb: The Maholova Club and the Search for a Dead Body
coveredGames.title: On the hunt for a corpse to fill the void inside of your coffin shaped body, you'll meet a cast of characters eager to help flesh you out in this bizarrely charming coming-of-age adventure.

coveredGames.name: Hell Clock
coveredGames.title: While a solid distillation of the ARPG genre mixed with the trappings of a Hades-style roguelike, Hell Clock's greatest success is in the historical framing of its cyclical violence as retribution.

coveredGames.name: Mashina
coveredGames.title: The moulded clay and kitbashed plastic of Mashina's garbage world creates an atmosphere reminiscent of Saturday morning British television to keep you company as you dig deep in search of friendship

coveredGames.name: Caput Mortum
coveredGames.title: On top of this alchemy horror game's beautifully grimy visuals and grotesque monsters, Caput Mortum asks the question: "What is more terrifying than no longer being able to trust your own hands?"

coveredGames.name: Kaizen: A Factory Story
coveredGames.title: A new, free-form problem solver from a team of ex-Zachtronics alumni, Kaizen: A Factory Story is every bit as brain-steamingly challenging as its forebearers, while being much more approachable.

coveredGames.name: Wheel World
coveredGames.title: While a bit straightforward in its execution, Wheel World is a tightly wound arcade cycling racer that feels as good as its vibrant and lush environments look.

coveredGames.name: to a T
coveredGames.title: The latest from Keita Takahashi takes a more linear, narrative-first approach in contrast to his more sandbox-style projects of the past, but it's still full of the childlike wonder you'd expect.

coveredGames.name: Dune: Awakening
coveredGames.title: Set in an alternate reality version of Dune's Arrakis, this base-building online survival crafting game's masterful adaptation of Frank Herbert's world has lead to a game that's hard to put down.

coveredGames.name: Kokuhaku Confessional
coveredGames.title: A short visual novel about a guy trying to confess his feelings to the girl he truly loves while some gyarus try to tempt him. Features good artwork, partial voice acting, and Reverse NTR.

coveredGames.name: Modified Girl Eurie!
coveredGames.title: An H-RPG about a clumsy girl who dreams of becoming a hero in a city full of lustful men. Will she manage to succeed, or will she give in to them? Features excellent artwork and a bimbofication system

coveredGames.name: No One But You
coveredGames.title: Short romance/drama/supernatural VN featuring a male student in a modern Japanese setting (Has H-patch). It has 5 routes, 9 endings, good story, BGM, artwork.

coveredGames.name: TORAWASE: The Girl in the Mirror
coveredGames.title: Medium length visual novel with optional R18 Patch. Good story and art style, decent music, all girls are voiced. The story offer 3 different routes. A gallery and scenes review is available.

coveredGames.name: The Leisure of Grisaia
coveredGames.title: Short kinetic VN as a dramedy featuring the heroines of the Grisaia series. It has good artwork, BGM and VA.

coveredGames.name: Infiltrating Roudille
coveredGames.title: Classic turn-based H-RPG by RPG Maker: fantasy/adventure. Play as female MC (Isaria) investigating a criminal gang. Good artwork, free 18+ patch, easy gallery unlock.

coveredGames.name: AMANATSU+
coveredGames.title: A VN sequel to Amanatsu where you choose a girl to date and continue her story. Playing the prequel is recommended. Features high quality artwork, voice acting, and an 18+ patch with mosaics.

coveredGames.name: A Tragedy in Elvish
coveredGames.title: A classic HRPG by oneone1, about the elf Mari and her battle to save the only human who showed her kindness. Features good artwork, hardcore content, 18+ patch available with mosaics.

coveredGames.name: PUGAD
coveredGames.title: [DEMO] A wonderfully atmospheric take on fishing horror. Spearfishing, progression and the dread of diving deeper (and more) come together to make PUGAD a promising and distinctive experience.
[DEMO] 7 developers, 7 days, 7 visions of horror. An unnerving collaboration that captures the experimental nature of the genre in one captivating and unpredictable experience.

coveredGames.name: Mortal Shell II
coveredGames.title: A truly unique, bleak world that looks, feels, and sounds like an old, unheard black metal album. One that constantly puts you on edge, yet you can't stop listening to.

coveredGames.name: The Sinking City 2
coveredGames.title: A great survival horror game and an incredible achievement given the circumstances. Mechanically better than the original, but it lost something unique in its pivot to survival horror.

coveredGames.name: Flesh Made Fear
coveredGames.title: A proper love letter to retro survival horror. Flesh Made Fear blends fixed-camera goodness, grotesque atmosphere, and classic resource management into one unforgettable, beautiful nightmare.

coveredGames.name: Clown Is Hungry
coveredGames.title: HOLY PEPPERONI, a comedy horror game? In this day and age? This one was full of welcome surprises, twists and turns. Good stuff.

coveredGames.name: WORLD OF HORROR
coveredGames.title: A beautifully unsettling fusion of cosmic dread and retro charm, capturing the essence of Junji Ito and Lovecraft through its unsettling visuals, eerie atmosphere, and relentless sense of doom.

coveredGames.name: Iron Lung
coveredGames.title: Iron Lung is a claustrophobic, tension-drenched horror experience that proves you don’t need jump scares to be terrifying. Just a metal coffin, an ocean of blood, and the fear of the unknown.

coveredGames.name: Tormented Souls 2
coveredGames.title: Despite carrying over some of the same flaws as the first game, Tormented Souls II stands out as one of the finest modern interpretations of the classic survival horror formula.

coveredGames.name: Skinfreak
coveredGames.title: Skinfreak is a slow-burn descent into terror that grips you from the first moment and refuses to let go, blending a haunting narrative, suffocating atmosphere, and one unforgettable killer.

coveredGames.name: SILENT HILL f
coveredGames.title: Silent Hill f marks a chilling and triumphant return, expanding the series’ mythos with haunting visuals, gripping gameplay, and a promising new direction for this legendary horror franchise.

coveredGames.name: House of Necrosis
coveredGames.title: A thrilling mix of survival horror and mystery dungeon. Fast-paced, tactical, and full of surprises with risky situations. Perfect for fans of roguelites and tense survival horror.

coveredGames.name: Brotato
coveredGames.title: It's just you and some goofy weapons against hordes of slavering aliens, but the overwhelming wealth of classes and builds keeps Brotato from growing stale between runs.

coveredGames.name: Conquest Dark
coveredGames.title: An immensely satisfying dark fantasy survivorlike that leaves plenty of room for creativity as you swing your sword, staff, or schlong through hordes of juicy undead.

coveredGames.name: shapez 2 - Factory
coveredGames.title: This is true automation bliss boiled down to its purest form. What starts as cutting and painting single shapes ends with millions of machines across thousands of space platforms. Highly addictive!

coveredGames.name: Wanderburg
coveredGames.title: A ridiculously satisfying take on the Survivors genre, featuring over-the-top builds, creative foes, and a charming sense of humor

coveredGames.name: Dungeon Clawler
coveredGames.title: Not only can you make a roguelike out of anything, it turns out you can get a lot of strategic intrigue out of a claw machine full of weird objects and wild fluids.

coveredGames.name: All Hail the Orb
coveredGames.title: Need your clickers diverse, diabolical, and filled with ducks? All Hail the Orb will keep surprising you with new challenges and light management on your way to maximum pondering.

coveredGames.name: Cinderia
coveredGames.title: Many parts of this action roguelike may look familiar, but a surprising wealth of build options and some genuinely unique twists make Cinderia one with serious staying power.

coveredGames.name: Gambonanza
coveredGames.title: Another sterling example of the "Balatro but..." genre, this turns chess into a puzzling struggle against attrition with loads of gambits at your back to keep you flush with pieces and options.

coveredGames.name: Under Par Golf Architect
coveredGames.title: Simplistic design mechanics and challenges aside, this is an immensely charming sim in the Two Point vein that gives you plenty of creative freedom and the power to play your own courses.

coveredGames.name: Net.Attack() - Code or Die!
coveredGames.title: Survivorlikes need a strong hook to stand out, and the simplified visual coding for your weapons is just that, especially once you start understanding the wild implications of what you can do with it.

coveredGames.name: Fallout 3: Game of the Year Edition
coveredGames.title: As a fan of the original Fallouts, I've always found 3 to be an effective bridge between them and the modern era, as well as a fantastic game to simply wander and explore in.

coveredGames.name: Dice With Death
coveredGames.title: Cleverly pushing the mechanical possibilities of Yahtzee, this tight little title offers a wealth of dice and relic combinations to spice up your Death-defying rounds.

coveredGames.name: The Curse of Monkey Island
coveredGames.title: Truly one of all-time greatest point-and-click adventures, benefitting from gorgeous animation, hilarious voice acting, and a refinement of puzzles and game flow learned from the previous two entries.

coveredGames.name: Horripilant
coveredGames.title: A delightfully creepy clicker with more satisfying progression than most. The puzzle elements add some much-needed depth between bouts of resource management.

coveredGames.name: Texplore
coveredGames.title: A satisfying Motherlode-like with some potent meta-progression and even a few surprises.

coveredGames.name: StarRupture
coveredGames.title: Falling somewhere between Satisfactory and Subnautica, this mix of automation, exploration, and devastation has enough promise to stand on its own.

coveredGames.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder
coveredGames.title: Beautiful pixel art married to solid metroidvania mechanics makes Gestalt a compelling experience, even if the story can be a bit uneven at times.

coveredGames.name: Monkey Island™ 2 Special Edition: LeChuck’s Revenge™
coveredGames.title: It's bigger, zanier, and harder to follow than the first one, and it's absolutely worth experiencing with the special edition enhancements.

coveredGames.name: Roots Devour
coveredGames.title: Your path through this gruesome tale won't always be clear, but exploring and experimenting will reveal the clever design hidden here.

coveredGames.name: My Pet Femboy
coveredGames.title: It's definitely not my thing, but this weird mix of Tamagotchi and WarioWare will surely appeal to more twisted fans of the topic.

coveredGames.name: The Secret of Monkey Island: Special Edition
coveredGames.title: This zany point-and-click has aged like a fine wine, bolstered by the ability to swap at will between the modern, fully-voiced remake and the classic, pixel-perfect original.

coveredGames.name: Minishoot' Adventures
coveredGames.title: A mashup of Zelda and bullet hell is clever enough to get my attention, but the excellent controls, satisfying exploration, and wealth of content make this a truly special title.

coveredGames.name: Hell Clock
coveredGames.title: Despite the ever-present timer and blistering pace, this stylish roguelike offers satisfying challenges in balancing speed, power, and caution.

coveredGames.name: Neongarten
coveredGames.title: A tight, stylish score-attack puzzler with surprising depth as you unlock more components for your colorful dystopian megastructures.

coveredGames.name: Simogo Legacy Collection
coveredGames.title: Simogo's games are beautiful, striking experiences that are more accessible than ever with this charming collection.

coveredGames.name: Voids Vigil
coveredGames.title: If you like Boneraiser Minions, this feels like a darker, more streamlined version with faster runs and more creative weapons.

coveredGames.name: Lenrual
coveredGames.title: With a powerfully unique look and feel, Lenrual offers satisfying puzzles where half the challenge is figuring out what the expectations even are.

coveredGames.name: City of Gangsters
coveredGames.title: It's more of a slow-burn board game than you might be expecting of a kingpin sim, but building your backroom business to dominate the city is undeniably satisfying.

coveredGames.name: Zooika
coveredGames.title: Matching rotund animals with some goofy physics might remind you of another produce-based experience, but this is plenty entertaining for what it is.

coveredGames.name: Pocket Boss
coveredGames.title: A sharp little experience that mixes soul-sucking corporate culture with trippy Warioware-esque interludes in a surprisingly clever way.

coveredGames.name: Titan Quest II
coveredGames.title: I wouldn't recommend hardcore mode yet, but the Soulslike additions to the ARPG formula give Titan Quest II a promising start as a modern successor to the classic Diablolike.

coveredGames.name: United Penguin Kingdom
coveredGames.title: It's a slower, more linear builder than most, but the charming presentation and long road to penguin utopia makes it worth your time.

coveredGames.name: Atelier Ayesha: The Alchemist of Dusk DX
coveredGames.title: One of the coziest, most charming games I've ever played. Enjoyable characters, open-ended exploration, a fascinating world, and lovely slice-of-life antics to fill the spaces between.

coveredGames.name: Cat Quest II
coveredGames.title: It's more Cat Quest. Bigger world, smoother around the edges, and now with co-op, but it's the same cozy questing the first one did so well.

coveredGames.name: Automachef
coveredGames.title: Much more a puzzle game than a factory simulator, Automachef will scratch that itch for optimized solutions with its kitschy automat mechanics.

coveredGames.name: NAGAISAN
coveredGames.title: You'll have to trust me when I say the places that this creepy comedy go are totally worth your time.

coveredGames.name: Harold Rabbit - Finder of Lost Things
coveredGames.title: Clearly intended for younger audiences, Harold Rabbit is a fine little point-and-click that's big on charm and light on mystery.

coveredGames.name: The 5th Door
coveredGames.title: It's a pretty baseline find-the-difference game that will probably hand you a few repeat experiences before you beat it, but the fundamentals are solid and it's got some spooks to jump at.

coveredGames.name: EVERSPACE™ 2
coveredGames.title: This sprawling space epic gives you a wealth of combat, exploration, and upgrading to enjoy across dozens of hours. Solid story, gratifying gearing, and more than a few surprises here.

coveredGames.name: Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap
coveredGames.title: An antique metroidvania ahead of its time, revitalized with incredible modern visuals and sound, makes for a unique and enthralling experience now.

coveredGames.name: God Save Birmingham
coveredGames.title: Realistic SimCade: You want to be Scared? To be Permanently On Edge? Do You want Extreme Difficulty Survival mechanics & the ability to Craft Up & Take the Fight to the Enemy? Then this IS for YOU!

coveredGames.name: WARDOGS
coveredGames.title: (EA) Recommended — Excellent large-scale teamwork, atmosphere and gunplay, the learning curve & SOME poorly explained systems make the first hours confusing. Watch Review for Details.

coveredGames.name: Gallipoli
coveredGames.title: Recommended — Intense, addictive WW1 battles, but predictable attack routes and questionable hit registration hold it back. Watch Review for Details

coveredGames.name: Professional Ship Simulator
coveredGames.title: (EA) Recommended: Excellent maritime systems and immersion, but water physics and AI behaviour need work. Watch Review for Details

coveredGames.name: iRacing® Studios NASCAR 26

coveredGames.title: An excellent survival-horror experience that appears to take inspiration from '𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐄𝐯𝐢𝐥' and '𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐥', but the pricing is currently atrocious in regard to what it offers...

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE
coveredGames.title: They finally make a new '𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐅𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐬𝐲' game with turn-based combat, and it is very enjoyable. I am happy.

coveredGames.name: Terranigma
coveredGames.title: A classic from 1995, and it looks absolutely fantastic

coveredGames.name: Tulpa the Unseen Lover
coveredGames.title: It's advertised as a short VN, yet the concept, character designs, and its use of Blender by professionals who worked on '𝐀𝐜𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐫-𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐞' make it seem very charming.

coveredGames.name: ReStory: Chill Electronics Repairs
coveredGames.title: Freely getting to tinker with electronic hardware and learning how to do so seems fun. It's nice to see more relaxing games such as this out there in the wild

coveredGames.name: PATLABOR the Case Files
coveredGames.title: The gameplay looks charming in a retro way, kinda like playing a PS2 game. It unfortunately came out half-baked, but I'm still happy to see the series getting more attention these days.

coveredGames.name: MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls
coveredGames.title: The game is absolutely phenomenal when it plays well. Unfortunately, the PC port suffers from poor performance issues, requires PSN to log-in, and uses Easy Anti-Cheat.

coveredGames.name: Broken Reality 2000
coveredGames.title: Despite some personal nitpicks, "𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐤𝐞𝐧 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝟐𝟎𝟎𝟎" is a fantastic exploration game that offers the player pseudo-nostalgia galore.

coveredGames.name: Arcadia Fallen II
coveredGames.title: The character creator may be lacking and your choice of Magical Discipline doesn't really affect the story, but this VN still proves to be a charming experience with its lovable cast & great artstyle!

coveredGames.name: DRAGON BALL XENOVERSE 3
coveredGames.title: It's finally true after all these years of waiting and memeing. It does feel weird that they're mixing in certain fundamentals of '𝐊𝐚𝐤𝐚𝐫𝐨𝐭' into the series now, but oh well

coveredGames.name: Danganronpa 2x2
coveredGames.title: Alongside its updated visuals and gameplay, this game features the original story of '𝐃𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐚𝐧𝐫𝐨𝐧𝐩𝐚 𝟐' AND an alternate timeline with completely new trials and victims.

coveredGames.name: PANLINE
coveredGames.title: '𝐌𝐢𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐫'𝐬 𝐄𝐝𝐠𝐞' ripoff or not, the foundations used in those games mixed in with the passion of indie developers makes this project rather exciting

coveredGames.name: Drunken Goddess Reflux
coveredGames.title: Think if '𝐁𝐮𝐜𝐤𝐬𝐡𝐨𝐭 𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐞' was a drinking game and you played against an attractive demon waifu. OST done by '𝐀𝐢𝐨𝐛𝐚𝐡𝐧 +𝟖𝟏', and '𝐃𝐄𝐌𝐎𝐍𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐄' sings the theme song.

coveredGames.name: Samson
coveredGames.title: '𝐒𝐚𝐦𝐬𝐨𝐧' possesses an interesting brawling formula and does fairly well with it. However, it currently has many bugs and technical issues, which does make the game a bit of a disappointment...

coveredGames.name: Dino Crisis

coveredGames.name: METAL GEAR SOLID: MASTER COLLECTION Vol.2

coveredGames.name: Little Goody Two Shoes
coveredGames.title: An excellent tale of folkloric horror hidden beneath a cutesy exterior. While not a difficult game, it can be rather mean at times with its trial-and-error...

coveredGames.name: Yomawari: Lost in the Dark
coveredGames.title: The quality of life improvements such as character customization and the freedom of going to any location off the bat make this an excellent title in the series, but not quite our favorite

coveredGames.name: Yomawari: Midnight Shadows
coveredGames.title: A direct upgrade from the previous game, especially in terms of storytelling, atmosphere, gameplay, and scares. Possibly the best game in the series

coveredGames.name: Yomawari: Night Alone
coveredGames.title: A neat little horror game that could have been better if it wasn't for its short length and absurd difficulty spikes. It also crashes a lot, but the link posted here should help with that.

coveredGames.name: Brutal Legend
coveredGames.title: Excellent humor, tons of heavy metal, and surprisingly good RTS gameplay all come together to make '𝐁𝐫𝐮𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐋𝐞𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐝' an outstanding blast from the past.

coveredGames.name: Blue Prince
coveredGames.title: An excellent rougelike with tons of puzzle-solving goodness, yet a lot of stuff is RNG-based and the game gaslights you into thinking it has a time limit when it doesn't.

coveredGames.name: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game
coveredGames.title: Surprisingly, the closed-alpha playtest is very good! We'll be keeping our eyes on this one

coveredGames.name: Persona 4 Revival
coveredGames.title: With this, fans of '𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐚 𝟒' can now finally play the game for the first time

coveredGames.name: Mohrta
coveredGames.title: A rather odd yet intriguing boomer shooter. If you love satisfying movement as well as weapons that are unique and fun to use, then you might enjoy this title

coveredGames.name: Yakuza 0 Director's Cut
coveredGames.title: Getting extra content and visual improvements for one of the best games in the series is very nice. Unfortunately, it doesn't quite justify the download size being almost 4x bigger now...

coveredGames.name: Z.A.T.O. // I Love the World and Everything In It
coveredGames.title: Despite the linear nature of this visual novel, the writing is absolutely phenomenal. The OST, artstyle, and characters are all excellent as well. Why is this game free???

coveredGames.name: Parasite Mutant
coveredGames.title: If you're a fan of '𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐞 𝐄𝐯𝐞' for the PS1, then this up-and-coming title might peak your interest

coveredGames.name: Curse of Resthaven
coveredGames.title: Govern a cursed island by managing trading, upgrading businesses, surviving card-based explorations, and investigating its Lovecraftian secrets. Very nice setting, atmosphere, and style.

coveredGames.name: False Hero
coveredGames.title: Souls-like set in a dark-fantasy world where everyone wakes up wearing masks. As a fighting wizard, use the skills of defeated enemies and bosses, level them up, and be ready to free or murder gods.

coveredGames.name: Chainsaw
coveredGames.title: Play as an insane serial killer with a chainsaw looking for his Apostles in a peculiar JRPG inspired by Omori. With many choices and a set of bizarre characters, the game offers a grim adventure.

coveredGames.name: Mortal Shell II
coveredGames.title: probably one of the most brutal and heavy-metal soulslikes, with a world full of grotesque enemies and deranged cults, where every dungeon is a surprise, often including new mechanics.

coveredGames.name: WUCHANG: Fallen Feathers
coveredGames.title: One of the best "pure" souls-like, mixing a complex and gorgeous level design, hidden lore inspired by Chinese folklore combined with horror-fantasy, and satisfying combat based on martial arts.

coveredGames.name: BLOODLETTER
coveredGames.title: Card game with an incredible art-style inspired by Medieval medical practices. Save villagers from demonic plagues by healing their bodies, spirits, and keeping their trust.

coveredGames.name: Pluto
coveredGames.title: Plastiboo's Vermis as a dungeon-crawler roguelike, with an amazing art-style. As a wizard, manage your fingers to cast spells and wear rings, all while fighting grotesque dark fantasy creatures.

coveredGames.name: Happy Bones: Welcome Home
coveredGames.title: Sort of demonic version of Eartbound set inside a cult-related compound. A colorful journey broken by demons, with many secrets, classes (including Demon Whisperer), and a balanced exploration.

coveredGames.name: Cradle of Nightmare : Flowers to you
coveredGames.title: Dark Souls meets Fear & Hunger in this huge RPGmaker where every room hides tons of secrets. Freedom to explore a dark and deranged world, with great monsters, many items and possible builds.

coveredGames.name: Roots Devour
coveredGames.title: Strategy card game where you play an eldritch plant absorbing blood from living beings. Spread from corpses to animals, improve your powers, and reach cultists to extend the hive-mind.

coveredGames.name: Mind Lure
coveredGames.title: A roguelike deck-builder with Lovecraftian sea abominations. Navigate on your boat to explore uncharted seas, fish, scavenge, and fight monsters in turn-based battles by using cards.

coveredGames.name: Crimson Capes
coveredGames.title: Inspired by Blasphemous and the Witcher, an action-RPG with brutal combat based on precise moves, since few hits means death. Fight abominations as a relentless witch hunter in a gorgeous 2D world.

coveredGames.name: Winnie's Hole
coveredGames.title: Roguelike where you play as a parasite in Winnie's body, controlling his brain in tetris-like puzzles, mutating his body into an eldritch horror, and devouring characters in turn-based battles.

coveredGames.name: Jimmy and the Pulsating Mass
coveredGames.title: Inspired by Earthbound, this is a long and complex JRPG set inside a whimsical world... till grotesque body-horror enemies start to appear. Plus, explore the world by morphing into defeated enemies.

coveredGames.name: NO-SKIN
coveredGames.title: A skinless man cursed you to find his skin while crossing a nightmarish world of mutated friends and cultists in this roguelike with turn-based combat. Full of secrets, lore, and replayability.

coveredGames.name: You Are NOT Bunnygirl
coveredGames.title: A robot-girl wakes up in a hellish dump, managing her feelings to fight and interact with discarded robots. A peculiar JRPG with great art, original battles, and great writing, from comedy to dark.

coveredGames.name: Paracom
coveredGames.title: Military-themed Fear & Hunger, where you control a paranormal SWAT team exploring a "mimic" house. Behind the simple style lies an interesting lore, credible actions, and choices with consequences.

coveredGames.name: Demonschool
coveredGames.title: Inspired by Persona 1-2, spend 10 weeks on a haunted island, join the school, hunt for cursed items, make friends, and fight horrible demons. Strategic puzzle-based battle using chained attacks.

coveredGames.name: Verho - Curse of Faces
coveredGames.title: A world where people wear masks, because seeing another face triggers a deadly curse, is home to a deep RPG inspired by King's Field, featuring deadly dungeons, peculiar characters, and many secrets.

coveredGames.name: Bloodgrounds
coveredGames.title: Build a gladiator school in this deep roguelike set in a dark-fantasy version of ancient Rome. Prepare and train your fighters to survive brutal turn-based battles against humans and monsters.

coveredGames.name: Stray Children
coveredGames.title: From the team behind Rule of Rose, a dark fairytale RPG inspired by Undertale, set in a world where adults became child-eating monsters. Survive bullet-hell battles by attacking or talking to monsters

coveredGames.name: Trench Face
coveredGames.title: Inspired by Fear & Hunger, a short dark JRPG set in a twisted and horror WW1 setting. Explore gas-filled trenches, fight tough puppet soldiers, and select different classes, from sniper to melee.

coveredGames.name: Majogami
coveredGames.title: Reminding of Madoka Magica, this is a 2D action RPG set in a paper world inhabited by twisted and insane witches. Cut through paper monsters and unlock power-ups in a dark world with amazing art-style

coveredGames.name: Enotria: The Last Song
coveredGames.title: It feels like being constantly inside the Windmill Village of Elden Ring, a sun-lit world inspired by Italian theater and folklore where every character is an insane masked actor trapped in their role

coveredGames.name: Mind Control: Bloody Renaissance
coveredGames.title: JRPG set in an insane world inspired by Shin Megami and Killer 7, including turn-based rail-shooter battles, the main characters being disposable puppets of a mysterious entity, and 90+ Achievements.

coveredGames.name: Exorcism Agency
coveredGames.title: Comedy-horror card game based on Taoism with roguelike elements. Exorcise ghosts (often quite sexy...) with talismans and a good deck. Deeper than could look, including a section to share ghost tales.

coveredGames.name: Dice Gambit
coveredGames.title: After a deep character-creation, you are ready to join your family of inquisitors hunting people turning into chromatic monsters. Tactical battles based on managing dices and a complex political city.

coveredGames.name: OFF
coveredGames.title: Updated version of a founding stone for indie JRPG: play as the batter in their holy quest to eradicate spirits. Explore a world of bizarre rules, expand your party, and kill "every" spirit.

coveredGames.name: Stones of Flesh
coveredGames.title: Peculiar JRPG set in a nightmarish world made in claymation. Alone in this dungeon, learn new stop-motion gifts and use them to survive, by throwing flames to "turn the eyeballs all the way around".

coveredGames.name: Dig Night
coveredGames.title: Comedy-dark JRPG where you work as a cleaner in a city where people turn into ghosts. A game full of personality, from old-cartoon ghosts to mini-games and a cinema with short stop-motion movies.

coveredGames.name: Death Ring: Second Impact
coveredGames.title: Build your mech and manage the base waiting the next attack in this post-apocalyptic strategy game. Fight grotesque aliens with many weapons and tactics, from giant swords to a rains of missiles.

coveredGames.name: SkullX: Aibohphobia
coveredGames.title: The battles of Darkest Dungeon but in a modern military-horror setting. Guide and manage your squad, solve puzzles, and make choices that really matter. Plus, great atmosphere and voice acting.

coveredGames.name: Espirito Delusion
coveredGames.title: Short and simple JRPG based on Brazilian folklore set inside a school cursed by a sinful delusion. Use the power of imagination to fight grotesque creatures, level-up with faith, and solve puzzles.

coveredGames.name: NITRO GEN OMEGA

coveredGames.name: Photomaly
coveredGames.title: That was pretty funny. Short and sweet.

coveredGames.name: Valor Mortis
coveredGames.title: 6.5/10 - It was a nice game. I think it dragged out too much. After 5 hours of playing there were no new things, but it went on for another 10 or something. Hitboxes & attack animations are trash too.

coveredGames.name: MOLE
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Cool game, a solid 7. Kind of whatever gameplay, but the story it told was really cool. Really, really cool game. It was fun, super intriguing from the beginning until the end.

coveredGames.name: Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Easy 7/10. It was a nice game. Some of the most gruesome visuals I've ever seen in any game, horror or not. I don't think anything ever came close. It was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up.

coveredGames.name: DreadOut
coveredGames.title: For what it's worth, I think the game was actually pretty good as a horror game. It was just a really bad game, but it was pretty good horror. It was really scuffed on random parts.

coveredGames.name: Hachishakusama | 八尺様がいた夏休み
coveredGames.title: 6/10 - It was fun. Kind of a whatever game, but I thought the concept was fun. Definitely gooner bait too. The woman's a 10.

coveredGames.name: UMIGARI | ウミガリ
coveredGames.title: That was a cool game. That was a really cool game.

coveredGames.name: 日本事故物件監視協会3 -Japan Stigmatized Property-
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Fun in its own way, really creepy. Not really a game. I'd put it at the same level as a walking simulator.

coveredGames.name: 日本事故物件監視協会2 -Japan Stigmatized Property-
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Fun in its own way, really creepy. Not really a game. I'd put it at the same level as a walking simulator.

coveredGames.name: SILENT HILL: Townfall
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Gameplay is a 6, not special at all. Lasts way too long. The story, theme and setting are top tier, like an 8.5 to a 9. I like the puzzles too, the puzzles are fun. Nice to see proper puzzles.

coveredGames.name: Onimusha: Way of the Sword
coveredGames.title: 8.5/10 - Damn, what a game. This was probably one of the best games I played this year. Loved the combat. Levels were whatever, gauntlet backseating was stupid, and lack of hard mode at start was bad.

coveredGames.name: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy
coveredGames.title: 6.5/10 - Overstayed a bit. Pretty game. Music was nice. Was nice, single playthrough. Definitely need to cut down on overused running parts. Art, theme, and background all looked really really good.

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS Zero Company™
coveredGames.title: 6/10 - It was an okay game. Too buggy. Way too buggy.

coveredGames.name: Quasimorph
coveredGames.title: 8/10 - Super fun game, cheap too. Downside is that it has really heavy knowledge checks, a lot of info to take in. Some missions were hard without any warning. Inventory management is also an issue.

coveredGames.name: Dinoblade
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - That was an easy 7 I think. Pretty fun, short and sweet.

coveredGames.name: Palworld
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Early and mid-game is a 8.5/10. Progresses slowly to a 7ish. Great game, and then it goes very average.

coveredGames.name: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition
coveredGames.title: 7.5/10 - I like this game partially. I don't like the amount of units you have to learn, and boring early game. I like the macro, micro, and fighting. The outdated ideas of pulling boars, get me out.

coveredGames.name: Heroes of Might and Magic: Olden Era
coveredGames.title: 8/10 - Early access review. It's a good game, definitely a good game. Plagued by lots and lots of RNG. Lots of things that are completely out of your control.

coveredGames.name: PRAGMATA
coveredGames.title: 8.5/10 - High quality game all the way through. Loved almost every second. Only bad part is the backtracking. It's too easy as well, it's a very easy game.

coveredGames.name: Mewgenics
coveredGames.title: 7/10 – Not super fun, just good. Too much RNG for a tactics game. I like scaling cats & fighting, as well as breeding. Events don't let you choose which cats to use, so negative effects can be random.

coveredGames.name: Crimson Desert Enhanced
coveredGames.title: 8/10 - Gorgeous game, peak combat and exploration. Animations, music, and SFX are on point. Questing is dull, lighting and colors inconsistent, story a mess. Controls are clunky, key mapping shaitan.

coveredGames.name: Slay the Spire 2
coveredGames.title: 8/10 - Early access review. Easy 8. Scaling doesn't go far enough, and MP needs some work.

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Requiem
coveredGames.title: 8.5/10 - It's top tier. Very few things wrong. I would have liked to see more progression. Leon started basically maxed, and Grace never got stronger. Needed more power build up.

coveredGames.name: Quarantine Zone: The Last Check
coveredGames.title: 7.5/10 - That was fun. Nice, short and sweet game. Doesn't overstay. Game crashed, but I guess it is what it is. It was an easy fix, and it stopped crashing.

coveredGames.name: Dispatch
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Solid 7, it was really fun to go through. Not much of a game, but a really fun story. Really should have been a TV series I feel, and not a game.

coveredGames.name: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader
coveredGames.title: 9.5/10 - A near perfect game. I think the story and setting were so cool. It felt like a passion project. Only complaint is that it was too easy. Needed to be 2-3x harder for enemy difficulty.

coveredGames.name: RV There Yet?
coveredGames.title: 8/10 - Easy 8. Easy peasy 8. What a fun co-op game. I would say buggy too, but I think a lot of the bugs made it more funny even.

coveredGames.name: Look Outside
coveredGames.title: 6/10 - It was such an interesting game too, but I'm not going to put myself through trial and error with saves where god knows how long they go back. Okay game for people who can stomach the saves.

coveredGames.name: Japan Stigmatized Property -日本事故物件監視協会-
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - A solid 7.

coveredGames.name: The Outer Worlds 2
coveredGames.title: 6/10 - A lot of perks and flaws, but my character felt the same. I just don't like this game enough. I think it started off really strong, but then fell off a cliff. The story kind of lost me too.

coveredGames.name: Cursed Digicam | 呪われたデジカメ
coveredGames.title: 7.5/10 - It was nice.

coveredGames.name: Escape the Backrooms
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - If this game was single player, it would be a freaking 2, but multiplayer makes it really fun.

coveredGames.name: Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Nice game. Don't like the progression in this, they make you have to replay lower levels too often.

coveredGames.name: BALL x PIT
coveredGames.title: 8/10 - Easy 8/10, really good game. Almost no downsides, other than the encyclopedia, that was awful. I thought it was a bit annoying to discover what combos and what doesn't after you discover it.

coveredGames.name: The Outlast Trials
coveredGames.title: 8/10 - Easy 8/10, what a nice multiplayer experience. It was fun, solid game. Could be scarier, would be main complaint, game could be scarier. Especially after introducing some of the later enemies.

coveredGames.name: Luto
coveredGames.title: 6/10 - It was okay. It started off super strong, but then, I don't know man. It kind of just went off the rails.

coveredGames.name: Cronos: The New Dawn
coveredGames.title: 6/10 - It was okay. Solid 6-6.5/10. Solid gameplay, dragged out a bit. Disappointing ending. I don't like how the story went. It opened up strong, but a lot of what is seen gets sidetracked.

coveredGames.name: MiSide
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - Decent 7, it was a nice game. No real complaints. It was just simply nice.

coveredGames.name: Harvester
coveredGames.title: 7/10 - I actually thought the story and voice acting are just kind of nice in this. Especially for a game from 30 years ago. If you disregard the gameplay it's a solid 7 or an 8. Gameplay is dogwater.

coveredGames.name: The Inn-Sanity
coveredGames.title: 7.5/10 - It was nice. It could have been a little more packed. Maybe a little shorter, despite already being short, as some parts were definitely dragged out.

coveredGames.name: Valkyria Chronicles 4 Complete Edition

coveredGames.name: SYNTHETIK 2
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | Alternate 1985 sci-fi setting listed as part of the fictional universe; no DEI intent documented. Android hero, 10 combat classes; no identity content or statements found. No consultants.

coveredGames.name: Days Gone
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | No consultants, mandates or DEI content statements; no LGBTQ+ characters. Ex-director partly blamed woke reviewers. Publisher Sony Interactive has a DEI strategy and employee networks.

coveredGames.name: ULTRAKILL
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | No in-game LGBTQ+ characters, pride items or identity options documented; wikis tie a secret-level shark joke to Blåhaj. Creator Hakita's own X post says he is bi. No consultants or agenda.

coveredGames.name: Stupid Never Dies
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | Zombie Davy fights to revive frozen Julia; no DEI content, intent statement or consultants documented. Co-publisher SEGA's group lists DEI and ESG programs, incl. DEI expert hires.

coveredGames.name: Phantom Blade Zero
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | Wuxia action RPG, fixed male lead Soul. Critic reviews mention no DEI content. No DEI consultants. Founder said Rainblood plots would change for players' sense of security.

coveredGames.name: Scam With Your Friends
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | Co-op scam call center game set in Kolkata, India, with AI callers. No DEI or ESG elements, statements or consultants documented. Steam forum threads call the premise racist.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | HD-2D version of Brave Exvius Season 1; its original writer rewrote the script. No consultants, statements or DEI content documented; only Square Enix's company-level DEI and ESG pages.

coveredGames.name: Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare® 4
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | A Korea-set war campaign led by a South Korean conscript beside Captain Price. Activision published DEI and ESG material from 2022 to 2024; none of it names this specific game.

coveredGames.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS
coveredGames.title: DEI Subjective | Fans report censorship in the Sonic Generations remaster: Rouge's outfit and Amy/Knuckles scenes. No SEGA statement or consultant on record; some forum replies mock objectors.

coveredGames.name: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse
coveredGames.title: DEI Subjective | Rose Belmont is the locked female lead, with no other playable character described; forum replies shout down critics. Developers cite story reasons. No consultants or LGBTQ+ content.

coveredGames.name: Hood Warfare 2
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | No DEI or ESG element, statement or consultant documented. Press criticizes racial stereotypes and players report "n-word" voice lines in this Chicago gang shooter.

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | No consultants, mandates, or political messaging confirmed. Diverse cast is Star Wars franchise convention. Female VA voices male-pronoun protagonist; cross-gender casting predates DEI.

coveredGames.name: Qliphah in Providence's Shadow
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | Japanese tactical RPG by Arc System Works; no consultants, no queer characters or romance confirmed; low-vote user-applied LGBTQ+ tag on launch day, no supporting content documented.

coveredGames.name: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered
coveredGames.title: DEI Subjective | LGBTQ+ characters from Sapkowski novels unchanged since 2015. CDPR holds formal DEI policy, ESG reporting, and June 2026 pride activism, but no mandate/consultant tied to this title.

coveredGames.name: Minecraft Dungeons II
coveredGames.title: DEI Free | No confirmed in-game DEI content or mandate. Diverse hero roster follows franchise tradition. Publisher Xbox holds DEI framework; no link to specific Dungeons II creative decisions.

coveredGames.name: AION 2
