coveredGames.name: Danchi Days
coveredGames.title: Super cute and cozy, with a lot of heart. Somehow made me nostalgic for a childhood I never had. I loved the art, music, and characters. It gets a bit tedious, but I definitely enjoyed it.

coveredGames.name: We Were Here Tomorrow
coveredGames.title: Unfortunately not as good as the others. The future setting is cool, but the puzzles are way more hit or miss. I still had a good time playing through with a friend.

coveredGames.name: Milki Delivery
coveredGames.title: Super cozy game with beautiful art and music. It boils down to interconnected fetch quests, but there's a great sense of progression and some interesting characters to get to know. I had a good time!

coveredGames.name: Shift At Midnight
coveredGames.title: Really good spin on Papers, Please as a co-op horror game. A few technical issues, but the loop is solid and I love the little details (Norbert my beloved). Very fun with friends.

coveredGames.name: Springs, Eternal
coveredGames.title: Thoughtful, melancholic walking sim with great atmosphere. I like the romance and themes of reflection and acceptance, but wish it explored them more and fleshed out the side characters.

coveredGames.name: The Devil's Due
coveredGames.title: Fairly standard roguelike deckbuilder with some very... interesting art 😅. Not sure I'd recommend it over similar games, but the fun modifiers and challenge types make it worth a look for genre fans.

coveredGames.name: Disaster Arms - Impact Project B.A.H.N.
coveredGames.title: Very fast and fun boss rush / platform shooter. Pretty good weapon variety and fluid movement. Loved the Newgrounds-esque aesthetic/music. Level design is a bit basic, but a fun time overall.

coveredGames.name: Fears to Fathom - Home Alone
coveredGames.title: A short but effective horror game. Oddly nostalgic (in a bad way), like being home alone as a kid, paranoid about every little sound. Did get a jump out of me 😭 Worth a play.

coveredGames.name: Moadra
coveredGames.title: Basically a new Metroid game. Fun combat with varied weapons to unlock, great interconnected exploration, and very nice art. Backtracking is pretty bad even for the genre, but I had fun with it.

coveredGames.name: Car Park Capital
coveredGames.title: Absolutely love the aesthetic of this game, reminiscent of RCT 1/2, some of my fav tycoon games ever. And the gameplay is solid! Very resource management heavy, but fun and wacky.

coveredGames.name: PAPERHEAD
coveredGames.title: Very very fast boomer shooter with some great gameplay, plenty of guns and enemy variety, and cool level design, but some pretty bad performance issues (even on a 5090).

coveredGames.name: Okko The Exiled
coveredGames.title: Exceptional pixel art coupled with some surprisingly fleshed out combat for the genre. Plenty of movement options too, makes the gameplay feel fast and fun.

coveredGames.name: TOEM 2
coveredGames.title: Beautiful follow-up to the original. Absolutely loved the art style, the cute cast of characters, and the simple, yet fun quest-based gameplay.

coveredGames.name: Magical Blush
coveredGames.title: Very cool action-adventure that feels like a combo of Zelda and metroidvania with a neat magic system on top. I liked the spell variety, the level design, and the pixel-3Dish graphics.

coveredGames.name: Wanderburg
coveredGames.title: It's like Vampire Survivors, but with mobile castles! Pretty fun roguelike with some good replayability given all the upgrade enemy types. The UI and overall polish really need some cleaning though.

coveredGames.name: The Children of Clay
coveredGames.title: Weird little archeology horror game. Loved the stop motion animation and the folk/mythology theming, I just wish it was fleshed out a bit more.

coveredGames.name: Blood Dungeon
coveredGames.title: Incredibly addicting roguelike with some excellent music and art, plenty of build variety, and tons to unlock. The movement takes some getting used to, but the gameplay is fluid, fast-paced, and fun.

coveredGames.name: Apidya' Special
coveredGames.title: Absolutely beautiful art/music for this remaster, but the gameplay is pretty standard for the genre and the upgrade system isn't really that exciting. Still a fun play though.

coveredGames.name: Squirrel Stapler
coveredGames.title: Actually scared me more than any other horror game I've played recently. Fun gameplay, even if a bit repetitive, and with an equally interesting, surreal story. It's short, but well worth the play.

coveredGames.name: Elementallis
coveredGames.title: Basically a Zelda-like with a cool magic system. Great art and world design and I liked the puzzles too, but the gameplay can be a bit rough around the edges, especially when it comes to combat.

coveredGames.name: BABBDI
coveredGames.title: Surreal megastructure exploration game with great atmosphere and tons of secrets to find. Loved the movement, the different items you could find, and the overall bleakness.

coveredGames.name: Chop Goblins
coveredGames.title: Very cool game. Simple, yet fun boomer shooter gameplay and I absolutely love the enemy designs. Just a bunch of goblins (and Dracula) running around throwing stuff at you.

coveredGames.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery
coveredGames.title: Super cute story-based puzzle game with gorgeous art and music (I bought the vinyl!) and some simple, yet fun gameplay. I liked the story too, even if it could have been fleshed out more.

coveredGames.name: Rental
coveredGames.title: Spooky scary short indie game with a cute protag and some nice low-poly graphics. I liked the vibe of the game and the simple adventure gameplay, but do wish it had more to offer.

coveredGames.name: PEAK
coveredGames.title: Late to the party, but thoroughly enjoyed this one. Lots of fun with friends and I love just how many little things there are to find. Great item variety, challenging maps, very rewarding gameplay.

coveredGames.name: Subnautica 2
coveredGames.title: Great follow-up to the original with some excellent QOL additions. I had a lot of fun playing through on the new multiplayer mode. Definitely feels a bit empty, but hopefully full release can fix that

coveredGames.name: DEAD OR ALIVE 6 Last Round
coveredGames.title: Minimal upgrade aside and having never played DoA6 before, it's decent. The gameplay flows well, the controls are intuitive, and I loved how over the top a lot of the stages and characters are.

coveredGames.name: The Alters
coveredGames.title: Really fun genre combination, part base building, part survival, but all wrapped up as a narrative adventure. The gameplay loop is solid and rewarding and the game looks great and runs well.

coveredGames.name: MECCHA CHAMELEON
coveredGames.title: Super interesting concept, but oh my god the UI, controls, and overall polish definitely need some work. Still, very fun to play with friends and really tests how creative you can be.

coveredGames.name: Super Battle Golf
coveredGames.title: Very fun game to play with friends. Wish it had some more items/stage variety, but there's a surprising amount of strategy here for what is effectively a game about sabotaging your friends.

coveredGames.name: Echo Isle
coveredGames.title: Super cute little Zelda-like! Simple in its design and not a very long experience, but one I had a great time with. Controls well and has some good pixel art and retro music.

coveredGames.name: ZERO PARADES: Director's Cut
coveredGames.title: Very engaging spy thriller, even if a bit overly dense at times. Loved the art, music, story, and especially the voice acting.

coveredGames.name: Toree's Panic Pack
coveredGames.title: Neat little collection of Toree games. Some better than others (Toree Missions bad), but decent overall.

coveredGames.name: Blippo+
coveredGames.title: Absolutely love the concept and aesthetic here. Probably one of the most unique games I have ever played. That said, not all the content lands and the ending was a bit disappointing. Still enjoyed it!

coveredGames.name: RACCOIN: Coin Pusher Roguelike
coveredGames.title: Very cool twist on a roguelike deckbuilder. Maybe not quite as layered as others in the genre, but it looks great, plays well, and has a great mix of chaos and strategy.

coveredGames.name: Monster Crown: Sin Eater
coveredGames.title: Despite its edgy and weirdly over-philosophical story, I quite enjoyed this one. The creature-collecting mechanics are fun and fusing monsters is an interesting alternative to evolving them.

coveredGames.name: Gamble With Your Friends
coveredGames.title: Very goofy multiplayer roguelike. The core is simple - number must go higher - but it has a lot of charm and a surprising amount of strategy. Lacks replayability, but I had a great time regardless.

coveredGames.name: missed messages.
coveredGames.title: A little bit amateurish with regards to the writing and definitely could use some more depth, but the art is beautiful and the story is both engaging and thoughtful.

coveredGames.name: Dreams of Aether

coveredGames.name: Adventure Honor
coveredGames.title: Roguelike RPG. The only achievement comes pre-unlocked, simply launch the game to sync it to your account. ~1 minute to 100%.

coveredGames.name: 寻真仙侠传
coveredGames.title: Visual novel. Play through four times, doing all top choices, all bottom, 1212, and 12112. Avoid saving, as this regularly crashes the game. ~3 minutes to 100%.

coveredGames.name: The Skull of the Howard Knight
coveredGames.title: Free guided point-and-click. See full review for step-by-step instructions. Turning on skip text recommended. ~2 minutes to 100%.

coveredGames.name: How to Summon a Demon
coveredGames.title: Visual novel with three choice points. Try all possible combinations of choices. Autoclicker recommended. ~4 minutes to 100%.

coveredGames.name: Terraformental
coveredGames.title: Terraformental is a time loop incremental where you try, fail, and try again to survive on a partially terraformed world that wants you dead. Slow, but somehow incredibly enthralling.

coveredGames.name: Timberborn
coveredGames.title: Classic settlement builder, but with a tribe of beavers trying to survive in a hostile, drought-riddled land. The townbuilding is adequate, but the water damming mechanics are immaculate.

coveredGames.name: THYSIASTERY
coveredGames.title: A traditional roguelike dungeon crawler with an impressive amount of party build variety. Can be extremely hard, but overcoming the challenge makes it that much more satisfying.

coveredGames.name: Berry Bury Berry
coveredGames.title: One part incremental game, one part liminal horror; Berry Bury Berry is a short but incredibly satisfying game about tossing absurd amounts of fruit (and gnomes) into a hole.

coveredGames.name: Voidling Bound: Creature Evolution Shooter
coveredGames.title: One of the best "Monster Collection" games I've played in years. The bestiary is small (9 monsters), but branching evolutions, splicing, & catalyst upgrades result in a ton of build variety.

coveredGames.name: Flotsam
coveredGames.title: A short & fairly satisfying mobile settlement builder, set on a flooded world. Very junk punk, where everything you use is salvaged from the dregs of the old world, and yet it's surprisingly hopeful.

coveredGames.name: Holder of Place
coveredGames.title: A grimdark Teambuilder Autobattler Roguelike where you pit a rag-tag group of adventurers against the horrors of a long-fallen kingdom. The build variety is top tier, especially as the moth faction.

coveredGames.name: Anode Heart: Layer Null
coveredGames.title: A fully featured and substantial solo TCG adventure that evokes similar feelings to the original Pokemon TCG gameboy game- but with way, way more content, build variety, & story.

coveredGames.name: Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault
coveredGames.title: A marked improvement on the first game, Moonlighter 2 seriously improves the original formula with better roguelike elements + powerups, and an extremely cool implementation of backpack management.

coveredGames.name: Strange Seed
coveredGames.title: A neat mix of EVO: Search for Eden & Spore, where you cobble a creature together from a variety of parts and solve puzzles, beat bosses, get more parts, and repeat. Short, but very satisfying.

coveredGames.name: Fellowship
coveredGames.title: An MMORPG Dungeon Crawler/Raider, but without the rest of the MMORPG to get in the way. If you loved WoW/Final Fantasy XIV, but don't have the time for a full MMO, you'll probably love this game.

coveredGames.name: BALL x PIT
coveredGames.title: My favorite game of 2025- Ball x Pit takes the best elements of the Bullet Heaven genre and flawlessly fuses them with Breakout/Space Invaders. I could not put this one down until I beat it 100%.

coveredGames.name: Unfair Flips
coveredGames.title: This game is a cruel prank, both against the players and the developer who made it. 10/10, would flip again.

coveredGames.name: Aethermancer
coveredGames.title: The best monster collection roguelite to date (not that there are many) with the fascinating build depth of Monster Sanctuary but with a much higher degree of variety & replay value.

coveredGames.name: ENDLESS Legend™ 2
coveredGames.title: Easily one of the best 4X strategy games ever made, with gorgeous visuals, incredible music, a fascinating setting, and really deep resource & empire-building mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Dice Gambit
coveredGames.title: Dice chucker tactical RPG with a really charming, unhinged energy that's an easy recommendation to Final Fantasy Tactics/Fire Emblem Fans. I recommend playing with Yahtzee mode turned on.

coveredGames.name: The King is Watching
coveredGames.title: Extremely solid Kingdom Builder + Defense roguelite where your citizens only work while you're directly watching them. Has extremely high decision density and really interesting buildcrafting.

coveredGames.name: The Wandering Village
coveredGames.title: An interesting take on the classic townbuilding sandbox formula, as your village truly does wander around the world endlessly, grabbing resources as you pass by them. Very cozy & charming.

coveredGames.name: Yaoling: Mythical Journey
coveredGames.title: An interesting monster collection RPG but with larger teams & auto-battle combat. It can feel a bit empty at times, but the teambuilding is incredibly solid and fun to experiment with.

coveredGames.name: Cyber Knights: Flashpoint
coveredGames.title: An incredible Cyberpunk Crew simulator + Tactical RPG, with a bevy of gear, abilities, & customization options that really let you fine-tune your play style to match your preferences.

coveredGames.name: As We Descend
coveredGames.title: One of the freshest Roguelike Deckbuilders in recent memory that doesn't stray too far from the standard genre formula, but adds squad & city building that seriously broaden your build variety.

coveredGames.name: A Game About Digging A Hole™
coveredGames.title: A short incremental game about, well, digging a hole in your new house's back yard. It's exactly what you'd expect, but also way more compelling than it should be.

coveredGames.name: Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector
coveredGames.title: Citizen Sleeper 2 is a fantastic follow-up to the first, with a larger cast of characters, a whole system to explore, and higher stakes. An absolute must-buy for TTRPG players.

coveredGames.name: Reus 2
coveredGames.title: Chill turn-based civilization/world builder, where you place various flora, fauna, minerals, and other planetary features to fulfill the needs & desires of your people. Very zen and satisfying.

coveredGames.name: SteamWorld Heist II
coveredGames.title: Sidescrolling XCOM in the SteamWorld universe. Has a much greater sense of freedom than the first Heist game, but some of the made-for-Mobile/Console design choices can be frustrating for PC players.

coveredGames.name: Knock on the Coffin Lid
coveredGames.title: A fairly traditional roguelike deckbuilder, but with a fixed map, time loop narrative, and equipment system that makes for a very satisfying (if extremely punishing) experience.

coveredGames.name: Megaloot
coveredGames.title: Endless Dungeon Crawler Roguelike where your equipment is your build. Can get stale after a while, but it's great in small doses or with friends in multiplayer.

coveredGames.name: Wayfinder
coveredGames.title: Highly polished pseudo-MMO that removed its online-only requirement to become a fairly solid co-op RPG. Very grindy, but it's a ton of fun if you've got a group of friends to play with.

coveredGames.name: ZEPHON
coveredGames.title: Streamlined 4X Strategy with a heavy focus on combat and territory control and a lesser focus on resource chains and diplomacy. Easily scratches the Civ itch, but with far less fluff.

coveredGames.name: Talented
coveredGames.title: Short & satisfying Wave Survival Roguelike where you upgrade your character using a massive, randomized talent tree between every wave. The gameplay is basic, but the build-crafting is sublime.

coveredGames.name: Eternal Strands
coveredGames.title: Critically overlooked Action RPG that's easily on-par with the greats from the 2000's and early 2010's.

coveredGames.name: Cataclismo
coveredGames.title: Basebuilding Horde Survival RTS with extensive fortification construction mechanics. You can spend hours fine-tuning your defenses, and it'll only feel like minutes have passed.

coveredGames.name: Blue Prince
coveredGames.title: Puzzle Mansion Roguelite that never seems to end. Great for people who want to lose their mind over obscure puzzles and arcane clues, but can be frustrating for less committed players.

coveredGames.name: Monster Train 2
coveredGames.title: Peerless Roguelike Deckbuilder that practically requires players to create extremely broken builds to win. Superior to the first game in every way, but with greater plot & characterization!

coveredGames.name: Sorry We're Closed
coveredGames.title: Extremely weird survival horror third-person shooter that leans hard on its style and storytelling, rather than gameplay that asks the question: "What if Resident Evil, but very horny?"

coveredGames.name: Tower Wizard
coveredGames.title: Tower Wizard is a short & satisfying incremental archmage simulator, where you balance multiple different resource chains for prestige points, and use those to boost subsequent runs.

coveredGames.name: BLADECHIMERA
coveredGames.title: Extremely solid pixel art Metroidvania with some of the smoothest flowing gameplay of the genre. Despite its relatively short duration, BLADECHIMERA is a surprisingly dense game.

coveredGames.name: ENDER MAGNOLIA: Bloom in the Mist
coveredGames.title: The follow-up game to ENDER LILIES, one of the best Metroidvanias ever made that manages to be even better in every possible way.

coveredGames.name: Heart of the Machine
coveredGames.title: Maximalist 4X AI overlord simulator that dives into every possible trope imaginable, and pulls it off flawlessly. The UI is a nightmare, but you get used to it rather quickly.

coveredGames.name: Look Outside
coveredGames.title: A turn-based survival horror RPG that leans REALLY HARD into body horror. Great for people who love being unsettled and intrigued rather than outright scared.

coveredGames.name: One More Donut
coveredGames.title: A funny little game where you sort thousands of donuts, unlock upgrades and slowly turn chaos into order. Surprisingly satisfying and relaxing, especially with its cozy soundtrack.

coveredGames.name: Gravelord
coveredGames.title: A fast-paced retro boomer shooter. Play as Queedo the Gravedigger, Cause mayhem with powerful weapons, upgrade abilities, and use a Spectral Shovel to decimate enemies and discover secrets.

coveredGames.name: Mekkablood: Quarry Assault
coveredGames.title: Pilot Bill’s mekk in this retro-inspired shooter. Smooth controls, hidden collectibles, and rewarding combat make it a nostalgic yet fresh mech battle against TorxCorp’s schemes.

coveredGames.name: Asfalia: Panic at the Mansion
coveredGames.title: Solve puzzles, collect stickers, and turn emotions like fear into playful companions in this heartwarming journey! Embark on a charming point-and-click adventure in a beautifully hand-painted world.

coveredGames.name: Terrorbytes
coveredGames.title: Survive a chaotic co-op horror where you and friends gather pellets for a mangled arcade villain. Evade twisted enemies and discover the sinister secrets of a corrupted machine. Can you escape alive?

coveredGames.name: Short Trip
coveredGames.title: Relax in a hand-drawn world five years in the making, pick up passengers, and enjoy the tranquil mountainscape. A short, scenic railway adventure where you’re the sole operator of a tram for cats.

coveredGames.name: The Cabin Factory
coveredGames.title: Inspect cabins for signs of paranormal activity and decide whether they are haunted. Report anything unusual and get out immediately.

coveredGames.name: Banebush
coveredGames.title: Banebush is a nonlinear horror visual novel with striking red visuals. Enter Alexey's haunting childhood village, where unsettling fairy tales and dark memories collide. Will you face the nightmare?

coveredGames.name: Fruitbus
coveredGames.title: Customize your food truck, forage fresh ingredients, and cook meals that touch hearts. Explore islands, connect with customers, and spread joy through food! A cozy culinary adventure in a Fruitbus!

coveredGames.name: Lonely Mountains: Snow Riders
coveredGames.title: Tackle icy trails solo or join 2-8 player crossplay multiplayer. Race to the base or join forces to share checkpoints in this thrilling winter ride!

coveredGames.name: Classified: France '44
coveredGames.title: Offers deep turn-based tactics set in WWII. Build a resistance team, balance stealth and combat, and manage morale. Distinctive missions, tools, and multiple endings add replayability.

coveredGames.name: Top Racer Collection
coveredGames.title: Revisit 90s racing nostalgia with Top Racer’s complete series. Enjoy 140 tracks, retro visuals, new cars, multiplayer modes, and strategic gameplay in this quick-paced, arcade-style racing collection.

coveredGames.name: Saviorless
coveredGames.title: A hand-drawn dark fantasy platformer where you explore, fight eerie foes, and unravel secrets as three unique characters. Striking visuals and dynamic gameplay make every moment compelling.

coveredGames.name: Undead Inc.
coveredGames.title: Delivers high-stakes resource management with a sinister twist. Build, expand, and profit from legitimate medicine or Explore illegal bioweapons to appease your corporate overlords.

coveredGames.name: Necrophosis
coveredGames.title: A haunting first-person horror adventure set in a decayed universe. Solve puzzles, explore unsettling landscapes, and discover the poetic mystery behind a curse that turns death into eternal decay.

coveredGames.name: Tennis Manager 2024
coveredGames.title: Enjoy enhanced 3D matches, advanced training, and deep customization options. Prove yourself as the ultimate tennis manager by training talents, managing finances, and leading a national team.

coveredGames.name: Autopsy Simulator
coveredGames.title: Combines realism with horror as you solve cases using anatomically detailed autopsies. Guided by real forensic expertise, discover chilling secrets while unraveling a haunting personal story.

coveredGames.name: Earl vs. the Mutants
coveredGames.title: Blast through mutant swarms as Earl, a pest control pro turned apocalypse hero. Combine chaotic upgrades, drive into chaos, and tackle epic bosses in quick-paced survival roguelite action.

coveredGames.name: Shift 87
coveredGames.title: Memorize environments, spot anomalies, and report deviations in this atmospheric observation horror game. Each shift brings random, unsettling occurrences to test your focus and stave off paranoia.

coveredGames.name: CONSCRIPT: Director’s Cut
coveredGames.title: Find your way through harrowing WW1 trenches in this top-down survival horror. Solve puzzles, manage resources, and fight to find your missing brother amidst the brutal chaos of the Battle of Verdun.

coveredGames.name: Lurch
coveredGames.title: Solve puzzles, evade adaptive demon AI, and escape a sinister mansion. Each playthrough is tense, unpredictable, and packed with chilling surprises. A 4-player co-op horror game where teamwork is key.

coveredGames.name: KitHack Model Club
coveredGames.title: This physics-driven sandbox lets you build, customize, and fly RC vehicles. Create distinctive designs, explore multiplayer chaos, or Explore endless community content!

coveredGames.name: shapez 2 - Factory
coveredGames.title: Streamline geometric production in this top-down factory-builder. Craft multi-layer factories, optimize production, and automate challenges. No enemies, no limits, just pure factory-building bliss!

coveredGames.name: AWAKEN - Astral Blade
coveredGames.title: Explore a dark fairy tale as Tania, a bionic girl searching ancient ruins to discover her fate. Engage in fluid combat, upgrade skills, and shape your journey in this mysterious, perilous world.

coveredGames.name: The Spirit of the Samurai
coveredGames.title: Fight an Oni's undead army in a stop-motion-style 2D action adventure. Play as a samurai, spirit, and warrior cat, mastering combos and legendary weapons to defend your village.

coveredGames.name: Wild Woods
coveredGames.title: Delivers fast-paced couch co-op fun for 1-4 players. Guide brave cat adventurers through a perilous forest, defend their wagon from night-time enemies, and balance risk and reward for big prizes!

coveredGames.name: Few Nights More
coveredGames.title: Reclaim your place as a Vampire Lord in this roguelike turn-based RPG. Build and defend your castle, master distinctive abilities, and conquer territories to fulfill your dark destiny.

coveredGames.name: Airships: Lost Flotilla
coveredGames.title: A strategic airship roguelike with dynamic combat, diverse upgrades, distinctive ships, and demanding enemies. Plan routes, unlock captains, and outsmart enemies in thrilling aerial battles.

coveredGames.name: None Shall Intrude
coveredGames.title: A roguelite deck-builder where you play as a Raid Boss. Master tile-based elemental combat, unlock potent mechanics, and overcome dynamic regions while fending off heroic challengers.

coveredGames.name: Mother Machine
coveredGames.title: Team up as mischievous gremlins, explore alien caves, solve creative challenges, and unlock wild mutations to customize your chaotic gameplay. A chaotic co-op action platformer for up to 4 players.

coveredGames.name: Blacksmith Simulator
coveredGames.title: Enter the forge as a Medieval blacksmith! Master forging mechanics, craft high-quality tools and weapons, mine exotic materials, and manage customers. Upgrade your workshop and grow your business!

coveredGames.name: MISTERY
coveredGames.title: A multiplayer PvPvE game mixing crafting, deception, and monster survival. Scavenge, craft, and expose traitors in this high-pressure, friendship-testing experience!

coveredGames.name: Turbo Dismount® 2
coveredGames.title: Crash, laugh, and create chaos in Turbo Dismount 2, the ultimate physics sandbox. With upgraded visuals, dynamic goals, Steam Workshop support, and amusing characters, the carnage never ends!

coveredGames.name: Streamer Life Simulator 2
coveredGames.title: Rise to streaming stardom in this detailed simulator! Build your career from scratch, upgrade gear, engage your audience, and strategize to grow your channel. Fame, fortune, or chaos, your call!

coveredGames.name: Driving Is Hard
coveredGames.title: Control Jeff, a half-naked hero in a wheeled bathtub, through themed levels in this precision platformer. Collect soaps, master tricky mechanics, and discover a heartfelt tale of self-discovery.

coveredGames.name: Whispers of the Eyeless
coveredGames.title: Serve the Dead Gods in this tactical strategy RPG. Balance ambition and survival in turn-based combat, oversee a growing cult, and expand your Sanctum beneath a corrupted land.

coveredGames.name: Achilles: Survivor
coveredGames.title: Fast-paced bullet heaven set in mythological Greece. Build structures, unlock distinctive heroes, face epic bosses, and grow stronger with every run. Master strategy and destruction!

coveredGames.name: Eternal Strands
coveredGames.title: Blend magic and weapons to battle towering beasts and discover ancient secrets in this fast-paced adventure. Use the environment and dynamic physics to master creative combat and exploration.

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS™: Episode I: Jedi Power Battles™
coveredGames.title: Play iconic Star Wars heroes, tackle droids and assassins, and enjoy couch co-op, classic cheats, and New Game+ surprises! Deflect, defeat, and destroy in this high-energy lightsaber action game.

coveredGames.name: Sniper Elite: Resistance
coveredGames.title: Refined sniping mechanics, stealth, and tactical combat, this fast-paced installment takes players into the heart of occupied France. Experience co-op play, intense kill cams, and Axis Invasions!

coveredGames.name: How to Survive
coveredGames.title: How To Survive was released on Steam and Xbox 360 in 2013. You are shipwrecked on an isolated island and must find food, water, shelter and the components to craft over 100 handmade weapons and tools.

coveredGames.title: Heavy Weapon Deluxe released on Steam in 2006. The Xbox 360 version released in 2007 and was titled Heavy Weapon. It's a classic shoot-'em-up arcade action game by the legendary developer PopCap.

coveredGames.title: Heavy Fire: Shattered Spear released on Xbox 360 in 2013, followed by this Steam version in 2015. It is an on-rails arcade shooter game and the fourth entry in the Heavy Fire series.

coveredGames.name: Haunted House™ (2010)
coveredGames.title: Haunted House released in 2010 on both Xbox 360 and Steam. It pays homage to the original 1980's classic adventure game, with players fighting for their lives across 20 eerie levels in Graves Mansion.

coveredGames.name: Halo: The Master Chief Collection
coveredGames.title: Halo: The Master Chief Collection contains five games in the Halo series that initially released on Xbox 360: Halo 3, Halo 3: ODST, Halo 4, Halo: Reach & Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary.

coveredGames.name: Halo Wars: Definitive Edition
coveredGames.title: Halo Wars released as an Xbox 360 exclusive in 2009. It was later released on Steam in 2017 as Halo Wars: Definitive Edition, an enhanced version with improved graphics and all previous dlc included.

coveredGames.name: Halo: Spartan Assault
coveredGames.title: Halo: Spartan Assault released on Xbox 360 and Steam in 2014, after initially releasing as a Windows 8 Store / Windows Phone 8 exclusive in 2013.

coveredGames.name: BULLET SOUL INFINITE BURST
coveredGames.title: Bullet Soul: Infinite Burst released on Xbox 360 in 2014. The Steam version released in 2017. It adds numerous gameplay enhancements over its predecessor Bullet Soul including refined level design.

coveredGames.name: BULLET SOUL
coveredGames.title: Bullet Soul first released on Xbox 360 in 2011. This Steam version released in 2017. It blends classic shooting game design with a generous dash of modern day bullet-hell and flashy pyrotechnics.

coveredGames.name: Half Minute Hero: Super Mega Neo Climax Ultimate Boy
coveredGames.title: Half-Minute Hero released on Xbox 360 in 2011 as Half-Minute Hero: Super Mega Neo Climax. This Steam version then released in 2012 titled Half Minute Hero: Super Mega Neo Climax Ultimate Boy.

coveredGames.name: Gyromancer
coveredGames.title: Gyromancer released on Steam and Xbox 360 in 2009. It is a fantasy themed puzzle RPG with a new battle system based on Bejeweled Twist, with the ability to learn how to summon dozens of beasts.

coveredGames.name: Guncraft
coveredGames.title: Guncraft was first released on Steam in 2013. An Xbox 360 version titled Guncraft: Blocked And Loaded was released in 2015 and includes a console exclusive split screen co-op feature.

coveredGames.name: GUN™
coveredGames.title: Gun released on Xbox 360 in 2005, then on Steam in 2006. It is a realistic epic action adventure that lets gamers experience the brutality of the lawless West, in an expansive interactive world.

coveredGames.name: GUILTY GEAR XX ACCENT CORE PLUS R
coveredGames.title: Guilty Gear XX Accent Core Plus released on Xbox 360 in 2012. The Steam version released later in 2015. It was reworked and included balance changes, and 'R' was added to the end of the title.

coveredGames.name: GUILTY GEAR 2 -OVERTURE-
coveredGames.title: Guilty Gear 2: Overture was initially released as an Xbox 360 exclusive in 2007. It was eventually ported to Steam many years later in 2016. It's a mix of action, real time strategy and MOBA elements.

coveredGames.name: Guacamelee! Super Turbo Championship Edition
coveredGames.title: Guacamelee! Gold Edition first released on Steam in 2013. Then in 2014 this Super Turbo Championship Edition released on Steam and Xbox 360.

coveredGames.name: Greed Corp
coveredGames.title: Greed Corp released in 2010 on both Xbox 360 and Steam. It is an award winning, innovative turn-based strategy game, set in a rich, fictional world inspired by the industrial revolution.

coveredGames.name: Gray Matter
coveredGames.title: Gray Matter released on Xbox 360 in 2010. The Steam release followed years later in 2014. It was designed by legendary game author Jane Jensen, the creator of the beloved Gabriel Knight series.

coveredGames.name: Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced
coveredGames.title: GTA V released on Xbox 360 in 2013. The original Steam version released in 2015, then in 2025 this Enhanced version released, which if purchased also gives you a separate copy of the original game.

coveredGames.name: Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition
coveredGames.title: Grand Theft Auto IV released on Steam and Xbox 360 in 2008. That original Steam version was delisted in 2020 and replaced with The Complete Edition, with some of the original's licensed songs removed.

coveredGames.name: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas – The Definitive Edition
coveredGames.title: GTA: San Andreas first released for PS2 in 2004. The Xbox 360 version released in 2014. The Steam version released in 2008, was delisted in 2021, then in 2023 this Definitive Edition was released.

coveredGames.name: Goat Simulator: Remastered
coveredGames.title: This remastered version of Goat Simulator was released in 2024. The original version was released on Steam in 2014 and is still available. The Xbox 360 version released in 2015.

coveredGames.name: Goat Simulator
coveredGames.title: Goat Simulator first released on Steam in 2014, then on Xbox 360 in 2015. There is also a remastered version available on Steam that was released in 2024.

coveredGames.name: Ginga Force
coveredGames.title: Ginga Force released as an Xbox 360 exclusive in 2013. It was eventually released on Steam in 2020. It is a vertically scrolling shoot'em up bullet hell game.

coveredGames.name: Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams
coveredGames.title: Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams first released on Steam in 2012, later releasing on Xbox 360 in 2013. It is a challenging platforming game where you morph dynamically between two different dream worlds.

coveredGames.name: Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered
coveredGames.title: Ghostbusters: The Video Game first released on Xbox 360 and Steam in 2009. That original Steam release has since been delisted. A few years later this Remastered version released on Steam in 2019.

coveredGames.name: Geometry Wars™ 3: Dimensions Evolved
coveredGames.title: Geometry Wars 3: Dimensions Evolved released on Xbox 360 and Steam in 2014. Evolved was added to the title when a significant update was released which included new levels, game modes, grids & drones.

coveredGames.name: Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved
coveredGames.title: Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved released on Xbox 360 in 2005, then on Steam in 2007. It is an expanded version of Geometry Wars, a mini game featured in Project Gotham Racing 2 for the original Xbox.

coveredGames.name: Gears of War: Reloaded
coveredGames.title: Gears Of War originally released exclusively on Xbox 360 in 2006. This 2025 Reloaded Steam release is an updated port based on the 2015 Ultimate Edition which never saw a release on Steam.

coveredGames.name: Gatling Gears
coveredGames.title: Gatling Gears released on Steam and Xbox 360 in 2011. It is a twin-stick shooter where you battle evil with a friend by your side, or online through an in-depth campaign spanning many environments.

coveredGames.name: MIMESIS
coveredGames.title: Super trippy and weird. The atmosphere is unsettling and the puzzles will mess with your head. Great if you love surreal indie horror.

coveredGames.name: Cozy Liora
coveredGames.title: Cozy little game to open for a little bit every day to get a chill vibe.

coveredGames.name: No Rest for the Wicked
coveredGames.title: It blends great aspects from very different games, like V-Rising, Dark Souls, Titan Quest...and mix all in it making an awesome experience

coveredGames.name: Necesse
coveredGames.title: Think Terraria meets RimWorld. You explore, fight bosses, and build a settlement where NPCs actually do your chores for you. Super addictive and cheap!

coveredGames.name: Pathologic 3
coveredGames.title: Pathologic 3 is a weird but good game. The Bachelor's time mechanics are brain-melting. Less walking than P2, more timeline fixing. Janky, stressful, but a masterpiece of weird horror.

coveredGames.name: StarRupture
coveredGames.title: Satisfactory with guns and a star that hates you. Building is fun but buggy, combat is intense. Best with friends to manage the chaos. Visually stunning, but Early Access jank is real.

coveredGames.name: MISERY
coveredGames.title: Pure masochism. The Zone is grim and beautiful, but it absolutely hates you. One shot kills, you bleed out fast, and inventory management is hell. Only for hardcore S.T.A.L.K.E.R. fans who love pain.

coveredGames.name: Escape Simulator 2
coveredGames.title: Harder, prettier, and bigger than ES1. Co-op is hilarious chaos, though puzzles can get tricky and stump you. Bring smart friends for the Dracula & Space rooms. Great fun despite minor bugs!

coveredGames.name: MIO: Memories in Orbit
coveredGames.title: Stunning sci-fi Metroidvania. The art is literal eye candy and the movement is buttery smooth (grappling hooks!), the bosses are hard. Basically "Hollow Knight in space." A polished 8/10 gem.

coveredGames.name: Lies of P
coveredGames.title: Pinocchio meets Bloodborne. Crisp combat, sick weapon crafting, and a goth aesthetic. It's tough as nails but fair. Easily the best non-FromSoft Soulslike.

coveredGames.name: Easy Delivery Co.
coveredGames.title: Chill trucking with a cat! Mixes cozy snow driving & lo-fi beats with a hint of mystery. Super relaxing but short & repetitive. Perfect for turning your brain off.

coveredGames.name: Ravenswatch
coveredGames.title: A polished PvE roguelike with satisfying MOBA combat, deep builds, and time-pressure strategy. Crisp animations and addictive gameplay.

coveredGames.name: Light and Shadow - Doppelganger
coveredGames.title: Light and Shadow serves forced encounters and watersports kinks. You guide Nora as a righteous paladin or a dark assassin. You must intentionally lose battles to trigger explicit scenes.

coveredGames.name: Endless Alice
coveredGames.title: Endless Alice caters perfectly to cosplay and outfit fetishes. The developers wrap intense action roguelite mechanics in tight cheongsams, swimsuits, and bunny ears. Will you survive the swarm?

coveredGames.name: Infiltrating Roudille
coveredGames.title: Infiltrating Roudille perfectly serves corruption and prostitution kinks. You play an elite knight forced into disguise as a common ♥♥♥♥♥. Will you fight pure or surrender to total degradation?

coveredGames.name: Echo Tokyo: An Intro
coveredGames.title: Echo Tokyo caters to fans of extreme forced kinks. The first story features brutal sexual assault and partial nudity. The second explores violent mind control. Will you stomach the abuse?

coveredGames.name: Club Life
coveredGames.title: Club Life delivers a fast and energetic dating sim. A strict teacher forces your reclusive protagonist to join school clubs. The colorful art and vibrant soundtrack elevate these lighthearted romantic

coveredGames.name: Aozora Meikyuu
coveredGames.title: The gorgeous anime artwork and clever timed dialogue system elevate this compact romantic comedy. Choosing silence actively shapes the fast narrative. Will you let time expire to win Sora over?

coveredGames.name: CONTROL Resonant
coveredGames.title: Open world structure with filler tasks somewhat dilutes the experience, but main storyline being especially strong in the second half & the creative visual storytelling more than make up for it.

coveredGames.name: Probably Stolen - Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Like Papers, Please, but on drugs. Many different gameplay mechanics intersect to keep your shop-keeping runs varied.

coveredGames.name: Death at Fleming Manor
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] The more scientific, forensic analysis is a nice angle to the puzzling. However, puzzles are often verbose and the clunky UI can get frustrating.

coveredGames.name: SILENT HILL: Townfall
coveredGames.title: Slow-paced and sometimes tedious first half, but nonetheless an enjoyable stealth horror title. Cautious recommend.

coveredGames.name: Legion Was Here
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Very fun & funny - almost like studying for an exam with learning facts about the target (in a good way...!)

coveredGames.name: Disco Elysium - The Final Cut
coveredGames.title: Cream of the crop, wonderfully beautiful prose and a must for story-rich RPG fans. Needs the player to be in the right, patient mood to be receptive of the story though.

coveredGames.name: Forever Ago
coveredGames.title: [Based off first hour] Nice for fans of story-based fans - great cinematography & voice acting. Story is promising but payoff remains to be seen.

coveredGames.name: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy
coveredGames.title: Technically polished and looks great, but storytelling takes a dip compared to the other 2 games. Somewhat overstays welcome with repetitive gameplay.

coveredGames.name: The Sinking City 2
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Genre shift into Resident Evil-esque survival horror will likely be divisive. Either way, it's clearly significantly more polished than the first game & I enjoyed it.

coveredGames.name: Desktop Explorer
coveredGames.title: An unexpectedly layered story on top of all the puzzle solving. Some of it can get tedious to solve but overall had a great time.

coveredGames.name: Lost & Found: A This Bed We Made Story
coveredGames.title: Short but nice addition to the This Bed We Made main story. Looking forward to potentially more down the line!?

coveredGames.name: Road to Empress Ⅱ
coveredGames.title: Not as compact/funny as the first game, but still a great way to learn about a historical figure. NOTE: 98% of game is live-action footage but there's AI usage in minor cutscenes esp towards the end.

coveredGames.name: Schrödinger's Call
coveredGames.title: [Based off first hour] Very atmospheric and cryptic, though pacing is quite slow and took a while to get going. English localization is slightly distracting with a "translated" quality to it.

coveredGames.name: Mina the Hollower
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Very committed to its retro aesthetic. Gameplay took a bit to warm up too but seemed like a good challenge!

coveredGames.name: Luna Abyss
coveredGames.title: [Based off first hour] Bullet hell gameplay is nice but really started enjoyed it when the platforming kicked in. Environments can get a little samey. Cryptic story that seemed promising.

coveredGames.name: 007 First Light
coveredGames.title: Smooth (though not hard) stealth gameplay paired with AAA production values. A few strange bits in the narrative here and there, but overall a very engaging story.

coveredGames.name: Indiana Jones and the Great Circle
coveredGames.title: Neat teasure hunting story with great attention to showcasing different cultures with care. Gameplay is very middling - best to fly though combat sections ASAP to return to the good stuff.

coveredGames.name: Directive 8020
coveredGames.title: A fun B horror movie time if you can overlook the protagonists making inane decisions. Way too many sneaking sections in the gameplay - would've preferred them to mix it up with QTEs.

coveredGames.name: Mixtape
coveredGames.title: Short and sweet with a fantastic curated soundtrack. Helps if you can relate directly to the setting, but not unrelatable to those who can't.

coveredGames.name: People of Note
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] One for the High School Musical/Glee kids. Story is not groundbreaking but enjoyable enough. A little strange the rhythm gameplay is not tied to the in-game music.

coveredGames.name: MOUSE: P.I. For Hire
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Great voice acting & atmosphere. Gunplay seemed basic though - a little unsure the aesthetic alone can carry the entire game through.

coveredGames.name: The Expanse: Osiris Reborn
coveredGames.title: [Based on closed beta] Very reminiscent of Mass Effect and a promising showing. Dialogue writing is shaky though - hopefully it can be improved for release.

coveredGames.name: Look Outside
coveredGames.title: Staggering amount of content for a $10 game. Gameplay is standard RPGmaker turn-based combat. The creepy body horror depictions and companion interactions are highlights.

coveredGames.name: Dosa Divas
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Another fun title full of family drama in the veins of Thirsty Suitors. Combat and cooking mini-games are enjoyable but gathering ingredients can get tedious.

coveredGames.name: REPLACED
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Gorgeous presentation. Gameplay and exploration are basic however and at times feel quite on-rails.

coveredGames.name: Life is Strange: Reunion
coveredGames.title: For Pricefield fans seeking resolution after Double Exposure. Not sure other LIS fans or brand new players will get much out of it.

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Requiem
coveredGames.title: Fantastic gameplay as per usual RE standards, though narrative is middling. Some pacing issues as well in the middle section but overall remains very enjoyable.

coveredGames.name: Cairn
coveredGames.title: How far would you go for your obsessions? Stellar climbing mechanics with a thoughtful story to boot.

coveredGames.name: REANIMAL
coveredGames.title: Enjoyable addition to the horror platforming adventure space of games, though it doesn't deviate far from the Little Nightmares formula.

coveredGames.name: Road to Empress I
coveredGames.title: Production quality far exceeds the game's cost - beautiful sets and costumes. Story is hilarious and the political intrigue ends up being genuinely engaging too. Ends on a cliffhanger TBC in a sequel.

coveredGames.name: Pathologic 3
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] There are glimpses of interesting things but budget constraints are also clear. I found the first hour a little tedious with the high word density.

coveredGames.name: Easy Delivery Co.
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Enjoyed the PS1 aesthetics and the hints of spooky happenings, though I'm not sure if the driving gameplay loop would hold up for many more hours.

coveredGames.name: TR-49
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Intriguing code-breaking puzzle gameplay, though the story is somewhat obfuscated and confusing right off the bat.

coveredGames.name: Earth Must Die
coveredGames.title: [Based on demo] Classic point and click with funny dialogue and great voice acting!

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Village
coveredGames.title: More action thriller than horror, but gameplay & setpieces are fun and varied.

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil 7 Biohazard
coveredGames.title: Absolutely frightening first hour that tapers off the tension to a fun survival action horror. Fun variety of DLCs!

coveredGames.name: Constance
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Cute art & generally plays well, though it feels slower and less responsive coming from Silksong.

coveredGames.name: Skate Story
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Surreal and bizarre (complimentar) story on top of a cool skating game. Be a demon who aims to eat the moon.

coveredGames.name: Vampire: The Masquerade® - Bloodlines™ 2
coveredGames.title: The whodunit story's still interesting if you are willing to put down expectations and look beyond its flaws, but there's no denying it's rough around the edges.

coveredGames.name: SLEEP AWAKE
coveredGames.title: [Based on first hour] Fantastic psychedelic visuals with cryptic worldbuilding. Gameplay is more barebones (akin to a "walking simulator").

coveredGames.name: No, I'm not a Human
coveredGames.title: One of the best narrative driven , atmospheric horror game you can find on steam for now . The artstyle and the soundtracks gives it a whole different vibes . Go try it now

coveredGames.name: Shrine's Legacy
coveredGames.title: This JRPG is heavily inspired and also bit copied from sabotage studios game Sea of Stars. I am not expecting great from it but it looks good ! Can give it a chance if you are into this genre

coveredGames.name: Whisper of the House
coveredGames.title: A Cozy point and click game where you have to organize, clean and arrange items. Cute interactions all over its open world and a good colorful pixel art style that is not overwhelming. Go try it now.

coveredGames.name: Spiral
coveredGames.title: Spiral is a game you definitely must play.Relive your old memories ,find those moments that were precious to you ,You play as Bernard an old man suffering from dementia.Great concept and a great game

coveredGames.name: Menace from the Deep
coveredGames.title: Roguelike game with a dark theme ! Beautiful visuals and clean art style . Good Gameplay with amazing soundtracks what else is your demand? The combat is great .Demand? Go play the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game :D

coveredGames.name: OFF
coveredGames.title: OFF is a great game for those seeking a good story experience and its colorful theme style. This one has been out for a long time but its different and more improved from the original game. Go try it.

coveredGames.name: Ship, Inc.
coveredGames.title: Cozy Job Simulator game ! Ship inc is a best game for those seeking a less stressful clicker game , all you have to do is click ! Thats all? No! Game has a lot to offer , find it on your own Go try it

coveredGames.name: Artis Impact
coveredGames.title: Good narrative driven RPG game offering a cozy and relaxing vibes! Artis impact has some good combat as well ! Pixel art is eye soothing and the story compliments a good experience, Do try this one.

coveredGames.name: KIBORG
coveredGames.title: KIBORG is a perfect example of a good action roguelike game ! This 3D Beat em up title showcases its amazing graphic quality and adrenaline pumping combat . Fan of such titles? Do check this game out.

coveredGames.name: Let Them Trade
coveredGames.title: Good City building game with nice colorful artstyle, and graphics. offering a great relaxing experience! It is quite addictive so be wary ! Try let them trade and you will be a fan of this genre.

coveredGames.name: Demon Hunt
coveredGames.title: Mech vs Monster! or Demons , whatever!! This top down roguelike is worth a shot ! the amazing gameplay will make you hooked to the screen for hours ! it will be your next addiction! Try it out .

coveredGames.name: Cat Detective Albert Wilde
coveredGames.title: Old classic film vibes ! Solve puzzles and mysteries with nice cinematics and visuals ! The key highlights for the game is its amazing story and these character designs! Do check this one out.

coveredGames.name: Ritual of Raven
coveredGames.title: You have got the village and its your duty to make it stable and beautiful? Without hindrance. You need to stabilize the portals .Use magic and dive into the cute and cozy world of ritual of raven.

coveredGames.name: Hell Clock
coveredGames.title: This is an amazing top down action game. One of the main features of hellclock is its vibrant artstyle and graphics. With amazing particle and light quality. Are you ready to dive in the action?

coveredGames.name: Fangtopia
coveredGames.title: Fangtopia challenges you to build your ideal tile-based, spooky landscape for ghouls, goblins and ghasts (oh my!) with the intention of either going your own way and crafting a monstrous world

coveredGames.name: Effulgence RPG
coveredGames.title: Strange special weapons, interesting mechanics and an entire game made only with recoloured ASCII characters make it one of the most memorable and respectable entries into the “solo dev” category

coveredGames.name: Mortal Shell II
coveredGames.title: Mortal Shell 2 oozes soul and creativity in a fresh take on the genre

coveredGames.name: Trailblazers: Into the March
coveredGames.title: Trailblazers: Into the March takes the colony-sim formula into dangerous territory

coveredGames.name: No More Room in Hell 2
coveredGames.title: No More Room in Hell 2 is finally the game it should have been, but it still has a way to go before it’s perfect

coveredGames.name: Chronocracy
coveredGames.title: Chronocracy innovates by bringing the RTS genre into a 2D-plane and dividing its campaign into bitesize, timeline-shifting sections.

coveredGames.name: Keep Driving
coveredGames.title: Keep Driving is a management RPG in which you create a character, and then hit the open road to attend a festival with friends. The road is long and winding, and you will face trials and tribulations

coveredGames.name: Roadlike
coveredGames.title: Run-based, procedurally generated levels and a fun inventory system make Roadlike much more than its Outrun-adjacent appearance might first make you think

coveredGames.name: Order Automatica
coveredGames.title: Order Automatica calls itself a dark tactical roguelite. Those words in that order technically describe what’s happening here, but they do all feel a little grand when you face the reality.

coveredGames.name: Feather's Edge
coveredGames.title: There’s something about a perfectly timed dodge, dash or attack in a 2D platformer, when combined with the right visual effect, that other genres simply can’t manage.

coveredGames.name: Fatekeeper
coveredGames.title: They say the devil is in the details, so, in the case of Fatekeeper, he’s got plenty of places to hide. It’s absolutely drop-dead gorgeous.

coveredGames.name: Security 51
coveredGames.title: Security 51 takes the familiar gameplay of Papers, Please, throws it into a blender with SCP-style horror and then asks you to spend decide which suspicious-looking scientists are allowed into a lift

coveredGames.name: Montabi
coveredGames.title: There are certain pairings that go well in life. Wine and cheese. Milk and cookies. Chocolate and custard creams. With Montabi, Akupara Games brings another pairing to the table. Pokemon and Slay the

coveredGames.name: The Relic: First Guardian
coveredGames.title: Flashy combat skills, permanent world state and narrative-laden boss-rush gameplay is all right up my alley, but there’s just too much wrong with how this game was made, marketed and executed

coveredGames.name: Full Circle
coveredGames.title: While nostalgia is often to blame for blurring over weaknesses and fogs up negatives, Full Circle has leaned heavily on it and for the better.

coveredGames.name: IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator
coveredGames.title: IRON NEST is basically Battleships for people who feel that Battleships didn’t have enough bureaucracy involved.

coveredGames.name: Sesame Street: Friends & Fun
coveredGames.title: In a world where there are tons of messages about games not being child safe, it’s really important that people keep making games like this.

coveredGames.name: Sovereign Tower
coveredGames.title: Like a mix of Dispatch and Reigns, Sovereign Tower sees you manage your knights of the round table and make decisions about your nation(s).

coveredGames.name: Feed the Scorchpot
coveredGames.title: In a nice twist from “videogame genre but roguelike”, new indie darling Feed the Scorchpot is actually “board game genre but roguelike” and this subtle difference carries into every facet of the game.

coveredGames.name: Prophet Margin
coveredGames.title: This intrigued me when I first saw it. It was being spoken about as thought it was a board-game inspired city-builder puzzler. That’s a lot of genres that usually don’t go together, but here it works.

coveredGames.name: Creatures Like Us
coveredGames.title: Creatures Like Us opens strong, with a conversation between friends, having broken into an abandoned building to squat there

coveredGames.name: Moss: The Forgotten Relic
coveredGames.title: Moss: The Forgotten Relic is a brilliant experience, and even if you never got the opportunity like I did on its original VR release, please do yourself a favour and try it now

coveredGames.name: WEGO World War II: Overlord
coveredGames.title: This hex-based wargame recreates the Allied invasion of Western Europe. It includes 14 scenarios, from the landing at Omaha beach to a huge 135-turn campaign covering the entire Normandy campaign

coveredGames.name: Frontline: Assault Corps WW2
coveredGames.title: This iteration of Frontline far surpasses anything they’ve done up to this point. No matter how or who you pick to go to war with, it’s just a freakin’ blast to play

coveredGames.name: Slayblade
coveredGames.title: Slayblade is, in its heart of hearts, a very silly but very endearing attempt to bring the old PS1 style of Beyblade game to the modern era

coveredGames.name: The Sinking City 2
coveredGames.title: Whilst The Sinking City 2 doesn’t feel like a sequel to 2019’s The Sinking City, it’s still a very strong survival horror adventure.

coveredGames.name: Cards On The Table
coveredGames.title: Every run is different and Cards On The Table is extremely addictive. The developer had to tap me and ask me to step aside to let other players have a go – that can only be a good sign

coveredGames.name: Mori Carta
coveredGames.title: Mori Carta is a “handless deckbuilding roguelike”, aiming to set itself apart from the main titan of this specific subgenre by not having a hand of cards

coveredGames.name: HOT WHEELS™ Infinite Rush
coveredGames.title: Whilst it doesn’t quite reach the level of Hot Wheels Unleashed, Hot Wheels Infinite Rush is still a fun racer that’s easily accessible for a younger audience.

coveredGames.name: Frontline: Afrika Korps
coveredGames.title: Frontline: Afrika Korps is an RTS that feels right out of the Golden Age

coveredGames.name: MR. RECORDS
coveredGames.title: Mr. Records takes the familiar, side-scrolling button tapping that we’re used to and wraps it all in a story about an elderly man named George

coveredGames.name: Hell Clock
coveredGames.title: Over the course of a 30+ hour “playthrough” which, in Diablo 2 style, is actually three playthroughs back-to-back, your Hell Clock build is sure to be constantly evolving and adding in fresh ideas

coveredGames.name: Desktop Explorer
coveredGames.title: Probably the most unique game I’ve played so far this year, Desktop Explorer is a puzzling delight that delivers nostalgia in more ways than one.

coveredGames.name: First Class Rescue
coveredGames.title: First Class Rescue comes complete with gorgeous art, fun puzzle mechanics that never felt too over-bearing and adorable hand-drawn art

coveredGames.name: Gemion Function
coveredGames.title: A 2v2 fighter that you use a button to swap targets. Contains a ton of FG and FGC references. Has a gem system to change your unique play style as well as a gem storm. Seriously, look at it. GGPO MP.

coveredGames.name: BreakThrough
coveredGames.title: A four button fighter with a mechanic called Resolve that allows for unique play. Will have to update when I know more. Rollback.

coveredGames.name: HYPERFIGHT 2
coveredGames.title: EARLY ACCESS. A fighter where the goal is to knock your opponent off the side of the screen or have five bars of meter/life. Simple controls with normal attacks, metered, and supers. Rollback.

coveredGames.name: Touhou Dream Duel
coveredGames.title: A spiritual successor to Soku where you create decks to fight. Weather affects the fights like Soku and the game will be very free form in terms of combos if it's a spiritual successor. Rollback.

coveredGames.name: Thumps & Blows
coveredGames.title: A stick figure fighter that is a parody of fighter cliches down to the menus. The game has built-in combos, a dodge, easy specials, and easy super. There's a story mode for SP. Rollback coming soon.

coveredGames.name: NINJA MASTER'S
coveredGames.title: SNK classic. Fighter where you can switch between weapon and hand to hand combat. It's a 4 button fighter like most SNK fighters. Code Mystics port. Rollback netcode.

coveredGames.name: WORLD HEROES PERFECT
coveredGames.title: Mandatory addition for the sake of adding it. Port by Code Mystics. Rollback.

coveredGames.name: Starkheim Tournament
coveredGames.title: EARLY ACCESS - A fighter with a good emphasis on defensive mechanics. Reflect, graze, guard break, and bursts are your defensive options. Attacks can cancel into another based on meter. No online.

coveredGames.name: DEAD OR ALIVE 6 Last Round
coveredGames.title: An updated version of DOA6 that includes a few new costumes and all DLC chars except kula/mai. Doesn't include previous costume DLC. Same delay netcode.

coveredGames.name: Saturday AM: Battle Manga
coveredGames.title: A 2v2 tag fighter with an anime aesthetic similar to ArcSys games. Demo available soon. Rollback netcode.

coveredGames.name: Exploding Judo Federation
coveredGames.title: "Just take the grab!" How about no? The win condition is to grab the other enemy. There's a variety of mechanics to get/avoid the throw. Edition select, plenty of lore, and tourney mode. No online.

coveredGames.name: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game
coveredGames.title: A 1v1 fighter based on the cartoon Avatar with an emphasis on movement. Each character has three variations that changes the properties of their attacks. Rollback netcode and crossplay.

coveredGames.name: KIZUNA ENCOUNTER: SUPER TAG BATTLE
coveredGames.title: A 2v2 tag fighter from SNK. This version was arcade only. Can play up to 4 players at once. Rollback Netcode.

coveredGames.name: REAL BOUT FATAL FURY 2: THE NEWCOMERS
coveredGames.title: It's a port of Fatal Fury 2 with rollback netcode by Code Mystics. This game is the prequel to Garou and still has the line sway system Garou removed. Code Mystics are great, so no worries there.

coveredGames.name: MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls
coveredGames.title: A 4v4 tag fighter from ArcSys with (bias) beautiful cel shading. Unsure of the current state of the game, but combo meter works similar to Granblue. Has an active tag system. Rollback and crossplay.

coveredGames.name: Invincible VS
coveredGames.title: A 3v3 Tag fighter from the creators of KI (2013). Is similar to KI's combo system, encourages active tags to keep combos going, and has defensive mechanics to break .Rollback netcode and crossplay.

coveredGames.name: 9 Kings
coveredGames.title: SP only review. Combo-focused gameplay that is addicting for a while, but the well runs dry quickly due to limited content. Recommended, 7.5/10

coveredGames.name: Kleromancy
coveredGames.title: Plenty of dice forging going on with a solid combat. Could use more polish around some UI elements and boss attack patterns. Recommended, 7.5/10

coveredGames.name: The Zibbo Show
coveredGames.title: Overly simple mechanics with a constrained tactical space and a lot of RNG. Cool visuals, but not for everyone. Mixed recommendation, 6.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Masters of the Universe™: Legends Unite
coveredGames.title: A Masters of the Universe roguelike deckbuilder isn't something I expected to see, but hey it's here.

coveredGames.name: Three Kingdoms: The Blood Moon
coveredGames.title: Tully excellent deckbuilder with unique combat mechanics and excellent deckbuilding opportunities. Royally recommended, 9/10.

coveredGames.name: Sky Settlers
coveredGames.title: Simple building placement game, with light card mechanics with the only goal being high score chasing. Lacks enough depth and not for everyone. Mixed recommendation, 6.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Fruitbearer
coveredGames.title: Solid Dogpile-like gameplay but lacks polish and content to be as engaging. Recommended, 7/10.

coveredGames.name: WildFront
coveredGames.title: Small, but well-made game with innovative minion summoning mechanic. Recommended, 7.5/10

coveredGames.name: Oaken
coveredGames.title: A finely crafted tactical summoner that only gets better at higher difficulties. Could've benefited from having a bit more units and bosses. Highly recommended, 8.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Occlude
coveredGames.title: While deducing game rules within a solitaire format can be fun, some of the puzzles may only appeal to puzzle lovers. Recommended, 7/10.

coveredGames.name: Sagrada
coveredGames.title: Sagrada is a simple, but sufficiently engaging puzzle that's great to play in short bursts. Recommended, 7.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Shards of Order
coveredGames.title: The subpar storytelling doesn't take away from the excellent combat, fueled by an innovative time mechanic. Royally approved, 9/10.

coveredGames.name: MEGAKO☆PUNCH!
coveredGames.title: One of the best Blackjack inspired games, but it's very small and can become repetitive after a few hours. Recommended, 7.5/10

coveredGames.name: Mini Tank Mayhem
coveredGames.title: Very good TD/deckbuilding hybrid that is fun to play but takes a while to unlock enough cards for added variety. Recommended 7.5/10.

coveredGames.name: One Step From Eden
coveredGames.title: Good action/rhythm game with tough learning curve but a weak card game. Requires dedication and you will like or dislike it based on your genre preference. Recommended, 7.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Pirates Outlaws
coveredGames.title: Positives and novelties often come with their negative counterweights. Sitting between a Yarr! and a Yawn, Pirates Outlaws is a slightly above average StS-like experience. Recommended, 7.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Draft of Darkness
coveredGames.title: An amalgamation of horror, RPG and card game that plays reasonably well with fair amount of content. However, the combat is slow-paced and can get repetitive. Recommended 7.5/10

coveredGames.name: Villages & Dungeons
coveredGames.title: An elaborate rock-paper-scissors autobattler with card drafting that's addicting to play, but poor UI, luck dependency and grind bring it down a notch. Recommended, 7/10.

coveredGames.name: Scoundrel's Dungeon
coveredGames.title: (EA) Simple to learn but not without tactical depth. Quick to play but also quick to lose if luck isn't going your way. Recommended, 7/10

coveredGames.name: Magin: The Rat Project Stories
coveredGames.title: Narrative driven game with tactical card combat but struggles with slow pacing and lacks exciting moments in both areas. Recommended, 7/10.

coveredGames.name: Prime Monster
coveredGames.title: Outdebate your opponent or simply kill them in this monstrous political card game.

coveredGames.name: Clonizer
coveredGames.title: Needs a bit more variety, but otherwise Clonizer a refreshing take on deckbuilding with objective based victory conditions and unit management. Recommended, 7.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors
coveredGames.title: Lots of meta upgrades, but very few tactical or interesting choices to make during card play. Still somewhat fun, but gets repetitive fast. Recommended, 7/10.

coveredGames.name: Joker Madness 🃏
coveredGames.title: Some interesting ideas, but requires polish and a stronger gameplay loop to counter the repetition. Probably better with friends. Mixed recommendation, 6.5/10

coveredGames.name: Eternal Dreams: Poker RPG
coveredGames.title: Team-based poker-hand card game with strong mobile roots, that, while polished, just isn't that engaging or strategic. Mixed recommendation, 6.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Reiner Knizia Yellow & Yangtze
coveredGames.title: A good strategic board game with map control that requires sharp decision making and offers quick matches with tactical depth. Recommended, 7.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Golf Peaks
coveredGames.title: If you are fan of compact puzzles (and have a secret love of cards), Golf Peaks is the game for you. Recommended, 7.5/10.

coveredGames.name: Pairs & Perils
coveredGames.title: RLDB based on matching pairs of cards, that somehow plays better than expected. Still, very memory dependent. Recommended, 7/10.

coveredGames.name: Slay the Spire 2
coveredGames.title: (EA) StS 2 gives returning fans exactly what they asked with great new content and familiar gameplay. While those new to the game will find a definite StS experience. Royally approved, 9/10.

coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Drowning Worms" simulator. I spent 30 minutes trying to catch a single carp, only to drop my phone into the pond and hook a boot. 10/10 wet socks.

coveredGames.name: CARNEVALE: Blades in the Crowd
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Paranoid Tourist" simulator. I spent 10 minutes walking in circles trying to act like a brain-dead NPC, only to get stabbed in the neck by my buddy because I walked slightly too fast. 10

coveredGames.name: Axolotl Party!
coveredGames.title: Funny game with funny graphic, only coop. Gj gj

coveredGames.name: MECCHA CHAMELEON
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Body Paint" simulator. I spent 10 minutes painting myself to look exactly like a trash can, only to get found because I posed wrong. 10/10 artistic camouflage.

coveredGames.name: Burglin' Gnomes
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Tiny Kleptomaniac" simulator. I broke in, stole a spoon, and got flattened by a normal-sized human while my buddy built a tiny chair. 10/10 gnome life.

coveredGames.name: Gamble With Your Friends
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Crippling Debt" simulator. We share one bank account, and my buddy blew it all in 5 minutes. Now the loan shark is here for our kneecaps. 10/10 ruin.

coveredGames.name: R.E.P.O.
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Lethal Moving Company" simulator. I dropped a piano on my friend's head while running from a monster, just to satisfy an AI boss. 10/10 physics hazard.

coveredGames.name: Split Fiction
coveredGames.title: A brain-melting puzzle game where I have to exist in two realities at once. I barely manage one in real life. My brain hurts, and I'm stuck on the tutorial. 10/10 existential dread.

coveredGames.name: Panelak
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Depressive Brutalism" simulator. I spent an hour trying to find my flat while listening to my neighbors argue through concrete walls. Czech homies! 10/10 bleak.

coveredGames.name: Brno Transit
coveredGames.title: A "Waiting in the Rain" simulator. I missed my tram, got yelled at by a babka, and ended up in the wrong district. Made by the Czech homies! 10/10 šalina experience.

coveredGames.name: RV There Yet?
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Dad on a Roadtrip" simulator. I spent 40 mins trying to park a house on wheels while virtual kids screamed in my ear. 10/10, I missed the exit again.

coveredGames.name: Half-Life: Alyx
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Panic Reloading" simulator. I spent 20 mins playing virtual piano just to drop my ammo while a headcrab jumped at my actual face. 10/10, Jeff gave me real-life PTSD.

coveredGames.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
coveredGames.title: Henry's back! Now I can miss my sword swings in a bigger city and accidentally shoot myself with a 15th-century boomstick. Czech homies strike again. 10/10, still hungry.

coveredGames.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Peasant Beatdown" simulator. I spent 5 hours picking weeds to buy a sword I can't even swing. Made by the Czech homies! 10/10, Henry is quite hungry.

coveredGames.name: SKIBIDI GYATROOMS
coveredGames.title: Brain rot: The Game. I’m trapped in a fever dream of toilets and memes where the only goal is to lose my last two remaining brain cells. It’s the digital equivalent of eating drywall. 10/10, I hate it

coveredGames.name: SUPERHOT: MIND CONTROL DELETE
coveredGames.title: Time only moves when I do, yet I still managed to get punched by a red guy while standing still. It’s a minimalist murder ballet where I’m the slowest dancer. More levels, more hacks, same 10/10 addic

coveredGames.name: Bulanci
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Napping with AKs" simulator. I’m a murderous pillow in a deathmatch where the only thing softer than the combatants is my survival rate. Made by the Czech homies! 10/10, E.T. phone home.

coveredGames.name: Hatred
coveredGames.title: An edgy "Going Postal" simulator where the main character’s hair has more personality than his motive. I’m just an angry guy in a trench coat fighting the entire world because I hate Mondays. 10/10 ed

coveredGames.name: Rustler (Grand Theft Horse)
coveredGames.title: Grand Theft Horse. I’m a medieval thug beating up knights and drifting a plow while a bard plays live radio hits. It’s historical accuracy for people who think the plague needed more slapstick. 10/10.

coveredGames.name: Portal: Revolution
coveredGames.title: A high-stakes internship where the benefits are "not dying." I’m solving puzzles with a budget portal gun while a robot gaslights me. It’s the free DLC that makes my brain hurt for zero dollars. 11/10

coveredGames.name: Muck
coveredGames.title: Minecraft on a fever dream. I spent the day punching cows and the night running for my life from a giant blue buff guy. It’s free, it’s chaotic, and I still don't know why I’m a bean. 10/10.

coveredGames.name: Super Battle Golf
coveredGames.title: Golf meets a high-speed car crash. I’m trying to putt while a literal tank tries to delete my soul. It's the only sport where the "birdie" is actually an explosive drone. 10/10, I’m bad at sports.

coveredGames.name: Gray Zone Warfare
coveredGames.title: The ultimate "Jungle Trekking" simulator. I spent 40 mins walking just to be one-tapped by a bush. Made by the Czech homies, so it’s 10/10 heatstroke. I love waiting for helicopters.

coveredGames.name: Deadlock
coveredGames.title: It’s like Valve put Dota 2 and Team Fortress 2 in a blender and added 600 vertical miles of zip lines. I’m getting outplayed by a gargoyle and a sentient candle while I try to click on floating souls.

coveredGames.name: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS
coveredGames.title: The world's premier walking simulator. I spent 20 minutes looting a pristine sniper rifle just to be killed by a bush, a car flipping for no reason, or a man with a bulletproof frying pan. 10/10.

coveredGames.name: Mafia: Definitive Edition
coveredGames.title: A 1930s "Career Change" simulator. One day I’m driving a cab, the next I’m wearing a $500 fedora and hiding from the police because I accidentally went 31 mph. That race mission is still a war crime.

coveredGames.name: s&box
coveredGames.title: The spiritual successor to G-Mod that we waited a decade for. It’s a playground where the only limit is your imagination and how many times the Source 2 engine can handle you spawning 500 watermelons.

coveredGames.name: PEAK
coveredGames.title: A cooperative climbing game that tests the absolute limits of my friendships. One wrong move and we’re all falling off a mountain like a bunch of uncoordinated goats. Gravity is the enemy.

coveredGames.name: Liar's Bar
coveredGames.title: I sat at a table with a buffalo and a fox to play Russian Roulette. I’ve never been more stressed about a deck of cards or more suspicious of a domestic pig. High-stakes lying at its finest.

coveredGames.name: Lethal Company
coveredGames.title: My job is to collect trash for a giant monster while my friends scream into the void. It’s a workplace simulator for people who think HR should be replaced by a giant blind dog.

coveredGames.name: Black Mesa
coveredGames.title: Scientific proof that OSHA doesn’t exist in New Mexico. I spent 15 hours jumping over radioactive goop just to get yelled at by a guy in a lab coat. Best disaster simulator ever.

coveredGames.name: Hunt: Showdown 1896
coveredGames.title: A high-stakes walking simulator where I crouch in a bush for 30 minutes only to be killed by a man with a crossbow and a dream. The crows are the real final boss. 11/10 stress.

coveredGames.name: Left 4 Dead 2
coveredGames.title: 15 years later and I’m still hitting zombies with a frying pan. It’s the only game where a fat guy exploding on you is a tactical disaster. Timeless, sweaty, and perfect.

coveredGames.name: Slay the Spire
coveredGames.title: A classic for a reason. A perfect game to pick up for 20 minutes or 5 hours with a first impression that masks an astonishing amount of depth. Give it a try, even if you think you won't like it.

coveredGames.name: THE FINALS
coveredGames.title: A highly kinetic team based FPS that puts its unrivalled destruction technology to good use. Run and gun fans will have a good time if they can pick it up quick enough to keep pace with the community.

coveredGames.name: Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter
coveredGames.title: The adventures of Estelle Bright continue in this fantastic follow up. More of the same for fans who fell in love with the first chapter and both are a must-play for JRPG enthusiasts.

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™
coveredGames.title: A fast and frantic racer infused with a roguelike structure, Galactic Racer feels every bit the spiritual successor to Burnout 3 Takedown, and thus comes highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Veritas Tales: Witch of the Dark Castle
coveredGames.title: A fascinating choose your own adventure book lovingly hand crafted by an auteur. Fans of DnD and practitioners of imagination will especially enjoy what this game has to offer.

coveredGames.name: 007 First Light
coveredGames.title: An honest to goodness blockbuster AAA release just like the good old days of the Xbox 360. A blend of Hitman and Uncharted any fan of action shooters will eat this up and ask for more.

coveredGames.name: inKONBINI: One Store. Many Stories
coveredGames.title: A charming slice of life about running a beat up old convenience store in 90s rural Japan. A delightful and contained experience but possibly too slow for some. For us a solid 7.

coveredGames.name: Mixtape
coveredGames.title: Somewhere between game and movie this prestige tour of teenage life will hit hard for anyone born in the 80s. Great characters and fantastic dialog make this tight 3-4 hour experience well worth it.

coveredGames.name: Ys VIII: Lacrimosa of DANA
coveredGames.title: What if the TV show LOST was also an action RPG from the masters in the genre. Look past the basic graphics and you'll find one of the best ARPGs of the last twenty years. A must play.

coveredGames.name: Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter
coveredGames.title: A sensational RPG with 10/10 combat that starts off slowly and gradually builds to a dramatic finale and a fantastic ciffhanger. Enjoyers of JRPGs will have an excellent time with this one.
