coveredGames.name: Cinema Theater Tycoon
coveredGames.title: A great, although linear tycoon game where you can run and design your own cinemas, buy movies etc., with a big portion of micromanagement.

coveredGames.name: Backlot: Hollywood Studio Tycoon
coveredGames.title: A Hollywood Tycoon game, not similar to The Movies, but to "Hollywood Animal", but in a better way. Offers a lot of stuff to do and a nice soundtrack, yet pretty challenging.

coveredGames.name: Retro Rewind - Video Store Simulator
coveredGames.title: Although a very, very simplistic tycoon game, it offers a lot more than you common job simulator, e.g. seasons and special events and is more focussed on creating a vibe instead of a challenge.

coveredGames.name: Life Is a Dungeon: Lean into It.
coveredGames.title: An slow paced action roguelike where you control one of four characters, each with their own personality, and aim for dungeon completion.

coveredGames.name: Lucky Tower Ultimate
coveredGames.title: A blast from the past where you need to solve puzzles. Work your way to the bottom of the tower, or die trying; most likely dying stupidly and quickly.

coveredGames.name: Ark Defender
coveredGames.title: A real time game where you manage a ship, dealing with what is both going on inside of it, as well as what is going on outside of it. No pause and go gameplay is featured during the arcadey bits.

coveredGames.name: All Who Wander
coveredGames.title: A simple traditional roguelike that sits on a hex grid. Experience is rewarded for traversing zones as opposed to defeating enemies, encouraging stealth and running away.

coveredGames.name: Text Dungeon: The Ring of Life
coveredGames.title: A text based dungeon crawler, it has a guide that is decent enough to get you into the game, but the interface is somewhat clunky. There is a lot of keybinds to remember too.

coveredGames.name: Horn & Dice
coveredGames.title: A dice rolling game where you match up die faces to achieve different actions against enemies. Enemies feature fixed attacked patterns for the player to overcome. Lack of info on what effects do.

coveredGames.name: Crawler 3D
coveredGames.title: A first person 2.5D experience where you run around clobbering enemies for big damage. Slightly simple and not doing anything too new or interesting, yet not doing anything bad either.

coveredGames.name: Warlock: Age of Entropy
coveredGames.title: A very old school feeling traditional roguelike. It has a simple feeling to it, but does feel distinct enough in what it is doing. Also has an over abundance of commands and kinda stupid enemies.

coveredGames.name: Trailblazers: Into the March
coveredGames.title: FTL: Faster Than Light gameplay meets Colony Sim. You'll find a lot of depth with the various mechanics, characters with dialogue and stories, and interesting world dynamics to experience.

coveredGames.name: Skillful Pixel Dungeon
coveredGames.title: One of the many derivatives of Pixel Dungeon, now ported over to Steam. Likely could use a little bit of refinement and explanation on playing it.

coveredGames.name: Shadowlight
coveredGames.title: An interesting sort of tactical assassination style of traditional roguelike, but lacking any real meaningful hook early on to get you really interested in playing.

coveredGames.name: Rogue Elements
coveredGames.title: A tactical roguelike where you have to read the intentions of your enemies and plan ahead of them. It is let down a bit by how poorly the game conveys information to the player.

coveredGames.name: Galdr Inkblade
coveredGames.title: A word game where your actions are derived from the spelling of words. Be quick though, there is a time limit, and no time to check what exactly is going on at any given moment.

coveredGames.name: Dark Dice Dungeon
coveredGames.title: This game has potential to be good, but needs some cleaning up. Gameplay is good, but the pace of play drags on a bit due to animation. Also a little hard to see who enemies are attacking.

coveredGames.name: Rogue Tempo
coveredGames.title: Manage an ensemble of orchestral instruments and coordinate them against various audiences in a Balatro style boss gauntlet. Unlike with other games of this nature, this feels more solitaire.

coveredGames.name: Eye of Khaos
coveredGames.title: A traditional roguelike with a lot of potential; including deep systems, a more 'classical' fantasy theme, and modern controls.

coveredGames.name: Stellar Broadcast
coveredGames.title: A rather information heavy game where you travel the stars, looking for a new home for humanity.

coveredGames.name: Cloudbreaker
coveredGames.title: Definitely feels like this is a survivor like that is trying to be better then the rest. It mixes inventory management into the usual mix of building you up. Minimizes annoying issues too.

coveredGames.name: Spellk
coveredGames.title: A decent enough idea, but could use more enemies that adjust the players playstyle, and make them have to change things up more. Relic system looks well thought out.

coveredGames.name: Pirate Twist
coveredGames.title: An interesting little ship battler where you fight pirates with various cannonshot types in real time. All actions are manual and you have to fire cannons or choose the shot types yourself.

coveredGames.name: Wanderburg
coveredGames.title: A survivor like where you a mobile castle that runs around raiding the countryside. Fight other mobile castles along with basic soldiers, get a game breaking building, etc.

coveredGames.name: Dataminers
coveredGames.title: Minesweeper mixed with roguelike mechanics. Gameplay involves hacking the data'mines', clearing them out of the way so you can climb the tower; keeping ahead of the encroaching firewall below.

coveredGames.name: Guns, Princess and Braves
coveredGames.title: A decent mix of tower defense management gameplay and survival mechanics. The ability to combine items together and link items up on the field for boosting effects was neat.

coveredGames.name: PESKY ORCS!
coveredGames.title: A rather interesting mashup of several ideas: Rogue Legacy, Vampire Survivors, Majesty: The Fantasy Kingdom Simulator, possibly more? Certainly worth checking out for something new an interesting.

coveredGames.name: Synthularity
coveredGames.title: Perhaps a decent way to kill time when you don't have anything specific you want to do. Runs are quick early on, but as you build up upgrades you'll last longer. How long will you persist?

coveredGames.name: Aquest
coveredGames.title: A neat mash up of tower defense gameplay with a survivor-like theme. Some balancing seems needed for defenses and the late game drags, but there is something that could come of this title.

coveredGames.name: PengPong
coveredGames.title: Cuphead artstyle meets arena survivor gameplay. Ricochet your shots to cause mass mayhem all around as you progress through the chaotic stages. Then Gamble your winnings all away if you so choose.

coveredGames.name: Swordcery
coveredGames.title: Features a mix of attacks, challenges, and game systems. Feels more optimized for a controller then for play on keyboard and mouse.

coveredGames.name: MOBU
coveredGames.title: A different take on the survivor-like genre, you play as a superpowered monk that shoots at bouncing enemies. Maybe lacks a little bit in mechanics, but it is a good start for something different.

coveredGames.name: Dunjin
coveredGames.title: A slay the spire clone that is built on poker hands and dice rolls.

coveredGames.name: Double Knight
coveredGames.title: Feels like this could be a decent enough game to buy on sale. Use it to 'kill' time during ones coffee break.

coveredGames.name: Wild Crazy 8s
coveredGames.title: Where there is the roguelike genre, there is something being merged with it. Crazy 8's now joins the club of card games where you look to score big and beat the score needed to continue.

coveredGames.name: biomraid
coveredGames.title: A simple idle game where you manage a single hero and send him on expeditions.

coveredGames.name: DIMENGUARD
coveredGames.title: its a pac-man like roguelike, there isn't much to say beyond that, there are rogue like elements but the base game is pac-man, if that is your thing good, if not then your out of luck

coveredGames.name: Gods of the Grid
coveredGames.title: Feels like when you get going in this one, you become unstoppable. Before then, it is a little bit difficult to start. More luck based then skill based it feels.

coveredGames.name: Endless Tower Survivors
coveredGames.title: A simple time waster where you go as long as possible.

coveredGames.name: Galactic Vault
coveredGames.title: A good solid Rogue FPS game, with large weapon customization and dungeon crawling elements, its fun and combat feels good, it needs more content however, to many same looking foes.

coveredGames.name: Lands of Fury
coveredGames.title: seems to be a standard dungeon crawler, with gameplay like Nuclear Throne somewhat, there are crafting elements and it could be fun, they need to fix intro learning elements of the game.

coveredGames.name: Lucky Shot
coveredGames.title: a target shooter FPS, with rogue like elements, if you like games like duck hunt or the like it could be up your street, the bight colours can be off setting after a while

coveredGames.name: GRIMLOOP
coveredGames.title: Has a neat little gimmick for a survivor-like, but feels like it needs a lot more work done to help it stand out.

coveredGames.name: SILENT HILL: Townfall
coveredGames.title: Recent updates have made this a game I can now recommend, but its still the weakest of the "new generation" of Silent Hill games so far. But not awful.

coveredGames.name: SHOCKFACE
coveredGames.title: A decent Clock Tower clone that is worth playing for fans of the genre

coveredGames.name: A Northern Evil: Tape One
coveredGames.title: A mid tier start to a horror anthology, not awful, not great but okay enough to play

coveredGames.name: Cyan Heart
coveredGames.title: Cyan Heart is an interesting little narrative game with horror elements I recommend for being truly unique.

coveredGames.name: Remothered: Red Nun's Legacy
coveredGames.title: Remothered: Ren Nuns Legacy is a masterpiece and one of the best horror games of all time. Concluding this excellent series in style.

coveredGames.name: Unseasonable Flowering
coveredGames.title: A good tragic horror walking sim with spooky monster designs and an interesting if vague plot

coveredGames.name: The Sinking City 2
coveredGames.title: An excellent Lovecraftian horror adventure that abandons its detective routes for a more traditional survival horror experience

coveredGames.name: Lost & Found: A This Bed We Made Story
coveredGames.title: Lost and Found is an excellent short mystery game that can be completed in one sitting.

coveredGames.name: Twisted Tower
coveredGames.title: Twisted Tower is an excellent Bioshock tribute with excellent slick gunplay and a dark mysterious story.

coveredGames.name: The Skin Stapler
coveredGames.title: Skin Stapler is a decent piece of shlock horror that overstays its welcome a bit but is still fun overall

coveredGames.name: Hariti
coveredGames.title: An excellent single player horror game with great monster design and a surprisingly sweet story and ending

coveredGames.name: Skinwalkers Valley
coveredGames.title: Skinwalker Valley is a decent horror experience about a hunting trip gone wrong. Not amazing. But fine.

coveredGames.name: SLEEP AWAKE
coveredGames.title: Sleep Awake is a masterpiece of horror I must recommend as one of the best I've played this year.

coveredGames.name: Box of Broken Nails
coveredGames.title: Box of broken nails is a tense horror experience where you must nail a door shut to keep something out your home constantly.

coveredGames.name: BORZOI
coveredGames.title: Borzoi is a decent enough Granny-esque game where you must escape from a giant dog and other assorted enemies.

coveredGames.name: Midnight Mazesoba
coveredGames.title: This is a fun little ramen making game, with some spooky side events.

coveredGames.name: Junji Ito Maniac: An Infinite Gaol
coveredGames.title: Junji Ito Maniac is one of the best horror games of the year and brings his iconic creation "Tomie" to life.

coveredGames.name: Flesh Made Fear
coveredGames.title: Flesh Made Fear is a great fun , gory Resident Evil clone

coveredGames.name: Clown Is Hungry
coveredGames.title: Clown Is Hungry is a okay comedy horror game

coveredGames.name: SCULPTURE
coveredGames.title: This is an okay simple horror game

coveredGames.name: Radiolight
coveredGames.title: Radiolight is an excellent time travel horror game with an immersive mystery story

coveredGames.name: Tormented Souls 2
coveredGames.title: Tormented Souls 2 is an excellent modern take on classic survival horror with a steep difficulty curve on normal setting.

coveredGames.name: ENA: Dream BBQ
coveredGames.title: ENA Dream BBQ is a surreal horror experience that is truly unique.

coveredGames.name: My Sleeping Girlfriend
coveredGames.title: My Sleeping Girlfriend is a decent little horror experience.

coveredGames.name: Vampire: The Masquerade® - Bloodlines™ 2
coveredGames.title: Bloodlines 2 is a fun vampire experience that should be judged on it's own merits not the originals.

coveredGames.name: SILENT HILL f
coveredGames.title: Silent Hill F is a masterpiece of modern horror and a game you should all play without delay. The franchise is back now fully!

coveredGames.name: Eclipsium
coveredGames.title: Eclipsium is a surreal masterpiece of horror that is a truly wonderful experience.

coveredGames.name: The Quarry
coveredGames.title: The Quarry is a fun death filled Supermassive movie style romp!

coveredGames.name: Abyss School
coveredGames.title: Another great lewd horror from this dev. Highly recommended.

coveredGames.name: Dead Reset
coveredGames.title: Dead Reset is an excellent horror FMV game with great gore and practical effects

coveredGames.name: Bye Sweet Carole
coveredGames.title: Bye Sweet Carole is a bittersweet return to Clock Tower esque stalker horror, with beautiful Disney style visuals and a decent story.

coveredGames.name: Haunted Room : 205
coveredGames.title: An excellent Chinese horror game with a surprisingly sad and compelling story.

coveredGames.name: Wolf Mate
coveredGames.title: Wolf Mate is a high brow stalker game for the connoisseur of horror games.

coveredGames.name: Sasaeng | 사생
coveredGames.title: Sasaeng is a excellent indie horror game with a gripping story, with an great twist.

coveredGames.name: Bad Cheese
coveredGames.title: Bad Cheese has great aesthetics and while it's a little too short to feel complete story wise, it's still worth a play .

coveredGames.name: Face of Another
coveredGames.title: Face Of Another is a masterpiece of indie horror with excellent writing, gameplay and just very well put together.

coveredGames.name: How to Fish
coveredGames.title: Definitely a SMii7Y-type game. Buy, play with your unpredictable (or overly predictable friends) and laugh. Not a lot of staying power, but for a few YouTube videos or a few nights of fun? Absolutely.

coveredGames.name: ANANTA
coveredGames.title: So close to being a big deal. If they had made this Buy to Play and had an OPTION of an online mode (fully embracing the GTA model) this could've been much bigger. Live Service means inevitable death.

coveredGames.name: Big Walk
coveredGames.title: An interesting game built seemingly explicitly for shenanigan streamers, like SMii7Y and the like. Major sales likely to come from influenced buyers but unlikely to maintain player counts.

coveredGames.name: Aniimo
coveredGames.title: It is just about everything people have wanted out of this genre, then went with a F2P model meaning it will be an inevitable and forever online-only title. Let us buy it and leave us alone.

coveredGames.name: Gales of Nayeli
coveredGames.title: It is a fine game that is just shy of good. Perfect bones to improve upon or follow-up with.

coveredGames.name: Crimson Desert Enhanced
coveredGames.title: There will be things about this game people won't know years after release. It is flooded with mechanics and ways to play.

coveredGames.name: Marvel Rivals
coveredGames.title: I have it on pretty good authority Magik can carry an entire team.

coveredGames.name: Digimon Story Time Stranger
coveredGames.title: This is an amazing $40 game. And you should buy it -- when it is $40. I won't mislead you like everyone else will, this game is NOWHERE NEAR worth $70, much less $120. Still great though.

coveredGames.name: Dispatch
coveredGames.title: What Mass Effect hoped to have achieved in the finale is what this game does, casually.

coveredGames.name: Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon
coveredGames.title: This game has the same indicators Oblivion had, which are precursors to massive success. If they can improve, polish, and add the appropriate new features, the next title could be their own Skyrim.

coveredGames.name: Keysaster
coveredGames.title: You end up being jolted awake in a different dimension, filled with eldritch ladies, and the majority dont have good intentions. Navigate a maze, find 4 keys, and escape to the next floor, repeat.

coveredGames.name: Lingering Torment
coveredGames.title: Explore a little moldy house dungeon crawler style, solve minimal puzzles to get codes for progression. Its short, but a pretty intense experience.

coveredGames.name: T.W.I.R.L.
coveredGames.title: Play as a teenage boy, most probably at the start of puberty, who begins to have an affinity for wearing dresses. Living in a Christian household, this has to be kept secret from family members.

coveredGames.name: BLOOD MALL: RETAPED
coveredGames.title: Theres a dinosaur in the mall, and only one man with his trusty shotgun can end things. Short, fun game, has many references to other indie horror games, and goofy characters to engage with.

coveredGames.name: Anomalous Coffee Machine 2
coveredGames.title: Like the first entry, but this time there is even more, over 500 possible outcomes, which can be applied to two protagonists. Quite the unique and curious designs. Has a NSFW DLC, because why not.

coveredGames.name: Idols of Ash
coveredGames.title: Descend a underground structure, with nothing but a hook. Idols of Ash is simple, and doesnt offer much gameplay wise, but its still a great experience, uses the little there is to its full extent.

coveredGames.name: Dementium: The Ward
coveredGames.title: Awaken in an abandoned hospital, and find your way out. What is even real? Finally a playable Dementium game on PC. Great remake, the atmosphere still holds up. However, a bit too pricey.

coveredGames.name: Banana Blood
coveredGames.title: Vidas has gone bananas! Humorous comedy horror, with too many banana puns. Visit a farm, and figure out its secrets, as you delve into its banana factory. Just like the Timore games, but more yellow!

coveredGames.name: Creature Kitchen
coveredGames.title: Slightly spooky, creative mystery game, where you collect ingredients, and look for recipes. Figure out what the abundance of creatures would like to eat, and how to get them out of hiding.

coveredGames.name: The Wheelchair Man
coveredGames.title: The Steam Frame is coming, and theres a lot of money inside an abandoned apartment complex... but wheelchair man doesnt like VR players. Tense and fun collecting game, quick 10 minute adventure.

coveredGames.name: Poolscape
coveredGames.title: Pretty great collection of poolroom levels, each with their own aesthetic and theme. From classic environments to some more experimental areas. They definitely nail the vibes they are going for.

coveredGames.name: Midnight Hoops
coveredGames.title: You just want to swing some hoops, but teenagers keep disappearing in the neighborhood. We ballin, or are we getting balled? A proper basketball horror game! Quite short, but really fun.

coveredGames.name: White Knuckle
coveredGames.title: Fairly difficult and paranoia inducing climbing roguelike, with a surprising amount of lore. Every round feels fresh. Even the smallest mistakes may end your run, and you arent alone either...

coveredGames.name: [Vladimere Lhore's] Bone Fire Effigy
coveredGames.title: Vladimere strikes again with a bonerfide little entry. Fuel the fire, embrace her love. 30 minutes brimming with style. The first encounter with the chaser is subtle and very well made.

coveredGames.name: A House Inside Me
coveredGames.title: Control a little girl through her house, and other surreal environments, as you watch her story unfold. Bite sized experience, with beautiful hand drawn environments, but quite slow.

coveredGames.name: Birds Watching
coveredGames.title: The whole world burns, except your little mountain retreat. Some bad actors want a slice of that peaceful life. Watch birds, seek their help, and break some noses. Stylish and mysterious adventure.

coveredGames.name: Water Womb World
coveredGames.title: God lives at the bottom of the ocean. Extremely short game, but packed with interesting lore and visuals. Sometimes the truth alters more than just your mind...

coveredGames.name: Angel Engine
coveredGames.title: You have one job, operate. Very stressful but creative simulator, with FNAF elements. Made to expand the lore of the Angel Engine analog horror series. Unlike the source material, it also uses no AI!

coveredGames.name: DYSTHANASIA
coveredGames.title: The Demonophobia developers newest work. You wake up in an unknown facility without any memories, and have to sneak your way around morbid entities that either want to kill or use you as an onahole.

coveredGames.name: SCP – Containment Breach
coveredGames.title: A small malfunction is all it needs to unleash pure terror over the facility. You are the lone survivor in a den of horny monsters, and need to learn their unique behaviors in order to survive.

coveredGames.name: Water Boiling Simulator

coveredGames.name: Eclipsium
coveredGames.title: Eclipsiums style direction and OST compliment each other well, it feels nice simply walking around, as a walking sim should. Stunning environments. You unlock some cool mutations for your hand.

coveredGames.name: Song of Horror: Enhanced Edition
coveredGames.title: I'm a big fan of the flawed but wonderful original Song of Horror, so I'm very curious to see this re-envisioned version come to life and compare the two.

coveredGames.name: Escape From Nightmare Evil Hills
coveredGames.title: Another pretty solid looking over the shoulder survival horror game, and perhaps the option to play in first person based on the trailer? God awful title though...

coveredGames.name: Hollow Galley

coveredGames.name: Dead Turn

coveredGames.name: Dread Omen

coveredGames.name: Birthday
coveredGames.title: A short (10-20min), wholesome little game built around the idea of making someone you care about feel special on their birthday. A heartwarming story with few easygoing puzzles.

coveredGames.name: blockia
coveredGames.title: Blockia is an adorable lego-like, creative, surprisingly feature rich indie gem that offers way much more than its price tag would suggest!

coveredGames.name: Tukoni: Prologue
coveredGames.title: Free to play, short, super sweet and relaxing little prologue. Will maybe take between 15-25 minutes? A point-and-click adventures with just pure wholesome forest magic and LOTS of mushrooms 🍄♡

coveredGames.name: Undusted: Letters from the Past
coveredGames.title: Came for the cozy, satisfying cleaning and stayed for the beautiful, heartfelt story. Such a lovely reminder of why I adore indie games. A tear or two may have escaped... blaming the dust ofc. 🤎

coveredGames.name: Foxy's Potion Shop
coveredGames.title: A tiny, wholesome potion-brewing game with small quests, decorating & lovely autumn vibes. 🍂 Nothing stressful or complicated, just an hour of brain-off cozy time. AND it's free! 🤎

coveredGames.name: Tukoni: Forest Keepers
coveredGames.title: A sweet little point-and-click adventure filled with simple puzzles, cute moments & cozy hand-drawn autumn vibes. 🍂

coveredGames.name: Woodo
coveredGames.title: A lovely little “cozy blanket game” Piece together tiny wooden dioramas while a sweet story unfolds. Calm, gentle, nostalgic & perfect for a rainy autumn day. ☕🍂

coveredGames.name: Lost Little Things
coveredGames.title: A charming little hidden-object adventure. Adorable art, cute creatures, small quests & no timers or stress. A lovely little gem for cozy hidden-object fans! ♡🌿

coveredGames.name: Verde
coveredGames.title: A super cute & chill little city-builder with lovely artsty!e🌿 Unlock new regions, shops & decorations as you build, with plenty of freedom and almost no pressure. Simple, cozy & very enjoyable.♡

coveredGames.name: Find My Frogs: Branches
coveredGames.title: A magical little hidden-object game with 450+ tiny froggos to find! 🐸🌿 Beautiful hand-drawn art, relaxing music, day/night mode & helpful hints. Short, cozy and absolutely adorable! ♡

coveredGames.name: Nonoko: Lofi Days
coveredGames.title: A lovely little idle/helper for your desktop with lofi music, nature sounds, cute companions, unlockable layouts + simple tools like notes, to-do lists and timers. ♡🌿

coveredGames.name: Cozy Night
coveredGames.title: Cozy Night truly lives up to its name. A short, cheap little game where you relax by the campfire, roast some marshmallows, enjoy soothing music, and meet adorable woodland friends! Only cozy vibes.♡

coveredGames.name: 呼~/huuu
coveredGames.title: 🍃 Take a deep breath, let the wind carry you, and treat yourself to one of the most charming free-to-play journeys out there. ♡

coveredGames.name: Whisper of the House
coveredGames.title: If you loved the game Unpacking, and enjoy decorating, organizing, and peaceful, relaxing gameplay… then Whisper of the House might just steal your heart.🌿♡ (Full review linked)

coveredGames.name: Mothkeep
coveredGames.title: If you enjoy cozy games, nature, and/or cute small moths, I can't recommend this one enough. It was very relaxing and so so beautiful! (Full review linket) 🦋❤︎🌿

coveredGames.name: Kernelbay
coveredGames.title: Chirping birds, handcrafted islands, and a lovely calming atmosphere. This cozy idle game is filled with charm, and you can truly feel the love behind it.

coveredGames.name: Puni the Florist
coveredGames.title: Welcome customers to your cozy little flower shop, help with their sweet (and sometimes a little silly) requests, and enjoy the little stories they share. A relaxing game with plenty to unlock.

coveredGames.name: Hidden Pets: 101 Cats in Brussels
coveredGames.title: A very short and simple find-them-all with cats. The game takes around 5-15 minutes, depends on how fast you are. Very easy to complete for all the achievement hunters as well.

coveredGames.name: Midori no Kaori
coveredGames.title: A cozy, relaxing idler. Build your own Japanese shop, welcome customers, or switch to auto-mode and enjoy the calming music and beautiful scenery. 🌸

coveredGames.name: Flibbius McDoogle and the Mysterious Flying Machine
coveredGames.title: A short lovely puzzle adventure game where you meet silly npc's, combine items and solve puzzles. The game take around 2-3 hours to complete. Full controller support + It works on steamdeck.

coveredGames.name: Gnomdom
coveredGames.title: A cozy, charming little puzzle game where you gather twelve adorable gnomes from different mini-games and puzzles to throw a little birthday celebration for their dear friend. 🍰

coveredGames.name: Campoca
coveredGames.title: Free to play short point-and-click adventure, filled with adorable alpacas and tiny woodland critters. Family-friendly, with easy puzzles to solve. A very cozy, comforting and super relaxing game. 🦙

coveredGames.name: FISHERY
coveredGames.title: For someone who has never had an aquarium, Fishery seems to be a realistic aquarium sim where you build and maintain habitats and then enjoy their beauty. That is, if you can keep any fish alive 😭

coveredGames.name: Lofi Haven
coveredGames.title: Design your dream room and your virtual cat to enjoy as an interactive wallpaper as you do other work on your pc. A relaxing set of lofi music, timer and task lists as well as customisable weather.

coveredGames.name: Trinket Bag Maker
coveredGames.title: Trinket Bag Maker is a colorful and cozy decoration game where you design your very own bag. Choose between many cute colors, and bag models, and take the time to be creative without any pressure.

coveredGames.name: Pomelo & Friends: Sevilla
coveredGames.title: A classic hidden object game where you are tasked to find lots and lots dogs in beautiful locations based on the exotic Seville. Includes quirky surprises, photographer pigeons and of course, cats.

coveredGames.name: Sniffin for Bones
coveredGames.title: A straight forward platformer designed to be gentle and relaxing, Sniffin for Bones allows you to explore several environments as a dog searching for hidden bones.

coveredGames.name: The Merry Fairy
coveredGames.title: A beautiful scrapbooking app set in a fairyland scenery. Great soundtrack. Regular updates with new stickers! Very cozy, perfect to stop and think.

coveredGames.name: Ithya: Magic Studies
coveredGames.title: Ithya is a beautiful productivity tool, featuring a mystical hand-drawn environment. It includes useful productivity tools like a timer and a ToDo. There is lots of wonderful music to choose from.

coveredGames.name: CARROT: The First Seed
coveredGames.title: So full of life. Has the two co-mothers from the first Carrot game. It is a prequel, so it also has the two boyfriends, but they are not yet boyfriends, they've just met. (And won't be yet in this.)

coveredGames.name: First Bite
coveredGames.title: Somewhat NSFW. Choose your character's name and a pronoun. Everyone is bi/pan, one says it too. The romanceable characters go by he/him, she/they, and he/they. The vampires are poly-ish (and evil)

coveredGames.name: Dragon Decimator
coveredGames.title: Protagonist uses they/them pronouns. There is limited story, but one of the endings has romance between the main character and a woman. The clicker gameplay is pretty fun. Doesn't take forever either.

coveredGames.name: Later Alligator
coveredGames.title: Player character is not gendered, and can go on a fake date with a (i think?) bisexual man. There is also a non-binary x woman npc couple. Not primarily a queer game, but it's nice

coveredGames.name: The Community Notes Are Wrong
coveredGames.title: Bisexual woman protagonist, out of a long relationship with a woman. She was/is pressured to identify as a lesbian. Bi-erasure is a central theme. One romance route with a woman and another with a man

coveredGames.name: Rectifier: In Bloom
coveredGames.title: Main character is semi-divine and beyond gender (they use they/them), but you get to choose their name and appearance, or to be not visible. Seven romance-ish routes, each with a different man (mlm??)

coveredGames.name: Detective Ridelle
coveredGames.title: It's a wlw game but that isn't obvious for most of its runtime. There is a pride flag and accidental flirting and other's assumptions, but it kinda isn't the main part. Has a [REDACTED] at the end tho

coveredGames.name: In Fair Spirits
coveredGames.title: Ok so. The way Abel talks about women, for example, is pretty bad. Felt horrible. The middle part is super toxic, but there is some bi x gay romance to be read later. Spin-off of The Fairy's Song(wlw)

coveredGames.name: Reborn a Zombie 2: Entwined Hearts
coveredGames.title: They are back! Read first part first (it's free). We still have our trans girl protagonist, and her asexual best friend, but that is explored less. Still not focused on romance. Linear visual novel

coveredGames.name: CARROT: Pancakes and Waffles
coveredGames.title: The main characters do hold hands, but that's about the extent of it. They were boyfriends in the first CARROT game, so they likely still are, but there is no text and limited character interaction

coveredGames.name: The Fairy's Secret
coveredGames.title: Two years after The Fairy's Song (read first), our girlfriends return. They are so nice to each other. "I really am lucky to have you." "That's funny, I was thinking the same thing!" Fully linear vn

coveredGames.name: The Case of the Serialized Killer
coveredGames.title: The main characters are two men who are at least a little gay for each other. Well, one is confirmed to be, other doesn't object. There is also a they/them character, and an aroace spectrum character.

coveredGames.name: The Fairy's Song
coveredGames.title: It takes the novel a bit to get to the queer bits, but the queer bits are pretty sweet. The girls are 16 and 17 of age. Goth girl x medieval out-of-time girl-knight. I do love them. Fully linear vn

coveredGames.name: Autumn's end (Part 1)
coveredGames.title: While it's not like sure that's the case: Main girl has a massive crush on the other girl. Only part 1 out at the time of review. Making all the good choices because this poor girl deserves a break.

coveredGames.name: CARROT
coveredGames.title: Very short (21 minutes for me), but still has that magical spark of life. And the spark of queerness. The main characters are boyfriends, and one of them has a two mothers: a mom and a mama.

coveredGames.name: Reborn A Zombie!
coveredGames.title: Trans girl protagonist (first part of the game has a lot of transphobia). There is kinda some wlw but mostly it's just the power of friendship (affectionate). Also has an important asexual character

coveredGames.name: Dissolution of the Silent Union
coveredGames.title: A sad lonely yearning lesbian. "I wanted to carry you to the stars." All about canon wlw, but it's not that obviously romance. "I'm thinking about you." Already re-played this. Stylish voiced wlw vn

coveredGames.name: Unto the Aurora
coveredGames.title: Only the end is openly queer, and even it leaves some room for interpretation. (But it is confirmed by the dev to be canon wlw.) So escape that witchcraft sentence and look forward to your lesbian arc

coveredGames.name: This Winter of Ours
coveredGames.title: An unfortunate situation for a young merchant's apprentice leads into a top tier wlw opportunity via friendship+ (friendship with hand holding and closeness). Magic exists and it's cool. Linear vn

coveredGames.name: Toxic Yuri
coveredGames.title: Called "Toxic Yuri" for a reason, but there are is a lot of cuteness and sweetness too. Main characters are salarywoman and slime woman, good wlw. Other wlw also, with some polyamory. No detailed NSFW

coveredGames.name: Confluence: An Of Sense and Soul Soliloquy
coveredGames.title: A gay poet's gay thoughts on love, identity, and life. "But the warm weight of his hand in mine as that first train rumbled on away from the only place I had ever known..." Short audio vn full of life

coveredGames.name: Project II: Silent Valley
coveredGames.title: Military setting. I imagined mlm tension which didn't happen, maybe for the better since the imbalance. But there is this wlw love triangle (for some definitions of love), between important characters

coveredGames.name: Life After Magic
coveredGames.title: Ex-magical girls, including bi MC, and a they/them genderqueer person. Silly wlw romance and less silly wlw romance + enby romance. One love interest is a trans woman, and I think one is ace-spec.

coveredGames.name: Drown in Yesterday's Sea
coveredGames.title: Women who love women story, but not exactly what it seems. Still very powerful. From my notes: "Oh... Oh no... Still wlw but very sad wlw. Semi sad. Crushingly sad yet still sweet." Love is beautiful.

coveredGames.name: So May It Be: A Witch Dating Simulator
coveredGames.title: Wlw: witches who love witches. Woman protagonist with three love interests: the other women in her coven. One is likely a trans woman. And one kinda has a boyfriend but don't let that stop you

coveredGames.name: The Day of Revenge
coveredGames.title: Sweet yuri in a mean world. Kinda enemies to friends to lovers, kinda. Complicated feelings, yet also very simple. "Wait... Could it be... I like Carola!" A linear rpg-maker story-game for wlw fans

coveredGames.name: TRUE LOVE'S CURSE
coveredGames.title: Mc is a little unethical but I support enbies' rights AND enbies' wrongs. "It doesn't have to be either-or, does it?" Non-binary protagonist, and possible gay and lesbian characters. Enby x prince ???

coveredGames.name: Taleweavers Alliance Anthology
coveredGames.title: 5 illustrated short stories, all warm. Main queer ones are one about finding and being yourself (and maybe wlw), and one about bodies and making your one yours. And swamp monsters are inherently queer

coveredGames.name: Clear Skye Thinking
coveredGames.title: Starts with the conclusion, and that conclusion is love. Or a crush at the very least. Wlw feelings of two teenage girls slowly (or not so slowly) falling for each other. Linear VN, no choices.

coveredGames.name: Capy Castaway
coveredGames.title: Main character is a capybara who uses they/them pronouns. They can semi-accidentally change their name in the beginning of the game and everyone is so nice about it. Also has a canon gay NPC couple.

coveredGames.name: Good Bones
coveredGames.title: CW: Heavy. Protagonist is a woman who was married to a woman. It was good, they even had a child, but the other woman got sick and died, and main woman has a lot of grief. She tries to move on.

coveredGames.name: Indigo's Dreams
coveredGames.title: The game has no clearly queer characters, but there is a trans pride costume. Maybe the main girl is trans? Celeste? Could make sense. Kind of on the shorter side, but clearly made lots of with love.

coveredGames.name: UNSIGHTED
coveredGames.title: Automata wlw?? Atomata wlw!! A woman looking for a woman she loves. You might have to play the whole game for confirmation, but the girlies are in love. Really in love. Game also has non-binary bots.

coveredGames.name: ALTER EGO
coveredGames.title: Main girl has girlfeelings for another girl. They are in a relationship, but [redacted]. I mean, not necessarily the healthiest relationship, but still. Worth your time, should take like 15 minutes.

coveredGames.name: Misericorde Volume Two: White Wool & Snow
coveredGames.title: Ok so as it turns out my conspiracy was true and pretty much everyone is queer (or at least open to it). "Is it holy?" "I do not care." Mc is still lost, but... *wink*. A little spicy. Vol 1 mandatory

coveredGames.title: Day 1. The city behind us is out of grain and out of kings. We carry barley, three goats and my grandmother's stubbornness. The Sea Peoples took the coast. They didn't take us. Tomorrow we walk.

coveredGames.name: Master of Command
coveredGames.title: Real-time Regimental Line Combat with a very unique army management roguelite system. This is a special game, and I highly recommend checking it out, a labor of love from The Armchair Historian YT

coveredGames.name: GearCity
coveredGames.title: Spreadsheet simulator car car sales tycoon game covering 1900-2000 with a very detailed economic sim behind it. Fantastic if you are into this type of tycoon game. Lots of updates, very solid!

coveredGames.name: Godslayer Arena
coveredGames.title: Master the art of divine combat in this strategic auto-battler. Build your champion's loadout, unleash devastating combinations, and watch your tactics unfold where ARPG depth meets hands-free action.

coveredGames.name: One-Eyed Likho
coveredGames.title: Black and white journey into hell, where talking heads on spider legs and cannibal cyclops roam. A meticulous and disturbing journey connecting Russian folklore and cyclops from different cultures.

coveredGames.name: ERLIK
coveredGames.title: Vampire Survivors-like based on Turkish mythology. Survive 40+ enemies and use 10+ characters in a game that, regardless of AI content, is a product of love and almost a Turkish folklore encyclopedia.

coveredGames.name: Saraab: Beyond The Veil
coveredGames.title: Deep VN with multiple endings touching on psychological and supernatural topics, including sleep paralysis. It is also practically a Djinn encyclopedia, with many entities related to Arabian folklore.

coveredGames.name: Otherside Tapes: Favela
coveredGames.title: Very creepy horror adventure set in a Brazilian favela that becomes a nightmare maze. Following an urban legend, you must solve puzzles between two realities, while avoiding the disturbing residents.

coveredGames.name: MEAT AND FLOWERS
coveredGames.title: Set in Sicily and inspired by the legend of Saint Rosalia, this unique adventure features deadly mutant flowers, precision platforming, abysses not to stare into, and characters as classic paintings.

coveredGames.name: Paper Bride 4 Bound Love
coveredGames.title: With more characters and story than previous entries, join the invitation for a twisted traditional Chinese wedding in a mysterious town, solve complex puzzles, and enjoy the amazing art-style.

coveredGames.name: Paper Bride
coveredGames.title: Getting married was never so creepy. Explore the steps of a traditional Chinese wedding twisted in this puzzle-heavy adventure full of Chinese folklore, from the afterlife to the creepy paper guests.

coveredGames.name: 追曙
coveredGames.title: A gorgeous 2D adventure set in China in the early 2000s. As two protagonists 10 years apart, solve the secret of a mysterious cult and survive nightmares based on twisted Buddhist images.

coveredGames.name: Subversive Memories
coveredGames.title: Profound adventure set in Brazil during the 1964-1985 dictatorship. The game mixes real and fictional events, shaping a survival-horror inspired by classics where light is the only weapon.

coveredGames.name: The Escape to the Afterlife
coveredGames.title: Explore the story of 3 souls looking for the afterlife after their funeral in this short horror adventure. Interesting depiction of Japan in the Showa era, including Yokai and traditional hell.

coveredGames.name: Hungry Horrors
coveredGames.title: Deck-builder based on Irish/British folklore... and cooking! As a princess, cook nice dishes and feed them to Red Caps, Grendels, and even Dullahan. Throw them their fav food to avoid being devoured.

coveredGames.name: The End of the Sun
coveredGames.title: As a fire wizard, explore a time-riddled world inspired by Slavic folklore by using bonfires to unlock memories. Solve puzzles and explore a land rich in legends, beautiful landscapes, and evil beings

coveredGames.name: Jurnal Risa: Dark Destiny
coveredGames.title: VN with multiple-choices from Dreadout's team, following a group of real Indonesian YouTubers. Learn about haunted places, deal with entities from Indonesian folklore, and fend off evil spirits.

coveredGames.name: Real Vampires
coveredGames.title: Peculiar collection of minigames following a real book about vampires in Poland in an almost cursed education game. Fight for day or night, and see minigames changing to eradicate or spread vampirism.

creators.name: BL yaoi games because why not

coveredGames.name: summer haze/glory days
coveredGames.title: VN with a unique layout + storytelling style that follows the MC on tour with their band. It focuses more on the touring experience and band life, making it a great fit for those interested in that.

coveredGames.name: Alaris
coveredGames.title: Very interesting plot + characters. The choices you make affect stats that change how you respond to situations! Overall a really fun experience, though voice acting is sporadic throughout the VN.

coveredGames.name: lovebyte.exe
coveredGames.title: The usual texting/chat-style VN getting to find out others' identities. MC does have the “YN effect”, everyone trusts/likes them for no reason, so it can feel a bit shallow. + Has no skipping feature.

coveredGames.name: Dangerous! TOO SWEET!!
coveredGames.title: Neutral review. It's a cute, short VN. The story is light and contains pretty art, but the ending feels incomplete + there are frequent typos and grammar issues.

coveredGames.name: Our Wonderland
coveredGames.title: Queer horror VN, (already out on itch!!) with really good writing, great ace rep and a very engaging story in general! If you like psychological horror and tons of time loops, keep an eye out this!

coveredGames.name: Paradise: Musubi
coveredGames.title: Sequel to the first game, this VN offers quite a bit of content: multiple routes, after stories for the good endings, and a few reverse routes as well! (Those are scenes from the others' pov).

coveredGames.name: How to Melt a Maiden's Heart
coveredGames.title: A short and sweet kinetic VN with a fun, straightforward story. Follows a cold class president caught crossdressing by his classmate—lighthearted and wholesome with a cute dynamic.

coveredGames.name: start;again
coveredGames.title: Amazing storyline with strong character dynamics that keep you hooked. Mystery-driven with puzzle elements that are well-balanced. The lore is interesting and well-crafted! Very enjoyable short game.

coveredGames.name: Beneath the Bleeding Moon
coveredGames.title: This kinetic VN blends action and romance in a well-paced story. As the main duo travels together, external threats push them closer, turning tension into trust. It contains cute art + smooth writing.

coveredGames.name: My Confounding Cat is Criminally Cute!
coveredGames.title: A short VN with no choices. The story’s predictable but sweet, with cute art and characters. It’s text-heavy at times, but lighthearted + fluffy. Nice if you want something simple and wholesome.

coveredGames.name: Paradise
coveredGames.title: A well-written story with great voice acting and art. The 18+ patch adds crucial lore + context, but also reveals a lot more disturbing content. The game feels more complete with the patch.

creators.name: ackshually this game is a hidden gem

coveredGames.name: TARAE: The Unbound
coveredGames.title: Gamescom trailer started promising, and I'm confident POE players are thrilled to see the gameplay. Chips and parts of the gameplay look fluid, the world gritty and dark. Good start.

coveredGames.name: Mariachi Legends
coveredGames.title: Great idea for settings. Very promising art, including music. The gameplay part is clearly reminiscent of older metroidvanias, not my tempo. The game looks promising if the animations are fluid.

coveredGames.name: Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons
coveredGames.title: While the game artistically looks decent - I believe UE5, clunkiness of the character movement and animations will be the end of any hype around this game.

coveredGames.name: LEGO® Skylines
coveredGames.title: CITIE- LEGO skylines. It's obvious that it's quite literally Cities Skylines, but LEGO spin on it was long overdue, because it's great idea. If they nail audio design of LEGO - full hit.

coveredGames.name: Sea of Remnants
coveredGames.title: Sea of thie- Remnants. The game is bunch of everything thrown together, glued with music and sprinkled with some gacha vibes. The game feels out of place in terms of consistency

coveredGames.name: Heroes of Might and Magic III Remake
coveredGames.title: Olden Era was decent, but the REAL childhood is right here. Nostalgia bait? sure, but if the core is untouched - the game will be great.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY VII REVELATION
coveredGames.title: Smart of them to put the game day one on PC. Exclusivity may be working for the consoles, but not for the games that take short term deals over long term investments. The game will be GOOD.

coveredGames.name: Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember
coveredGames.title: Most surprising reveal to me. I don't think general public enjoyed Wo Long. Hope KT puts more heart into the story of the game, or the amount of finishers, because the first one was lacking there.

coveredGames.name: Vivarium
coveredGames.title: This is the closest we are to jumping right into Ghibli movie. I hope the writers put a lot of work into making the story feel like one too. This is not a game for me, but it is very much needed.

coveredGames.name: Senua
coveredGames.title: I would never expect them to make another one after a glorified walking sequel. This game will always have balance issues when it comes to artistic vision and actual videogame mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Magicians: The Devil's Deal
coveredGames.title: The games art direction is unmatched. It feels like near perfect take on stylized graphics. The gameplay looks fluid and fun. The genre seems to be good 'ol classic. Want to see more.

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Veronica
coveredGames.title: It leaked, people knew, but they needed a date. Capcom is on a roll when it comes to the series and sure works to continue on that. Great games too.

coveredGames.name: Alien: Isolation 2
coveredGames.title: One of the best horror games in terms of pure scare factor. There is no reason to think second will not deliver the same, or maybe even better performance.

coveredGames.name: Guild Wars 3™
coveredGames.title: Guild Wars 2 was not my MMO of choice, but sure was a classic in the genre catalogue, and all the experience should help developers understand the needs of those communities, because not many do so.

coveredGames.name: CLUTCH
coveredGames.title: The traile showcases something promising over what Forza Horizon 5 butchered - city. Seems like the game is more of a story driven experience with open world side content and cruising.

coveredGames.name: The Wolf Among Us 2
coveredGames.title: Another videogame taken away from the greedy hands of Epic Games. We all should enjoy and celebrate the fact that more developers buy out their way out of exclusivity.

coveredGames.name: Alkahest
coveredGames.title: I don't think we've seen a lot of real gameplay footage, and from the pre-rendered footage it obviously looks dynamic and interesting. The game looks like all gameplay, barely any world though.

coveredGames.name: The Expanse: Osiris Reborn
coveredGames.title: I can only comment on the videogame itself, and from the footage we got so far the direction seems very generic, the same way Starfield feels. There is definitely audience for it though.

coveredGames.name: 007 First Light
coveredGames.title: Not a huge fan of both media, but ultimately fun takes the wheel here and determines if something is worth checking out. It looks crisp, plays the way people have enjoyed for years now. A hit for sure

coveredGames.name: Dead as Disco
coveredGames.title: What OSU players think they be lookin like playing. Interesting mix of genres, but we've had that before and it was great. Artstyle looks great, designs are fantastic, the music... obviously.

coveredGames.name: Witchbrook
coveredGames.title: Yeah, those sell, and for a reason. Cozy, cute and immersive life sim with co-op elements are the way to go for a chill experience. This should be no different. Will probably be decently priced too.

coveredGames.name: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
coveredGames.title: I want to feign ignorance and say that I don't know what's the point of this remake, but I know exactly. Old game enhanced graphically, polished mechanically, but ultimately nothing new - for 60 bucks

coveredGames.name: METRO 2039
coveredGames.title: The horrific real world stories will absolutely feed the psychological horror that will be very much present parallel to the more classic horror elements. Quick Q4 2026 release date also.

coveredGames.name: Kena: Scars of Kosmora
coveredGames.title: The first one is universally loved. I know nobody who speaks ill of it, and so the second game will most likely follow its steps. Bigger scale, quite nice art direction & very Disney look to it.

coveredGames.name: Untitled John Wick Game
coveredGames.title: It's the guy from Fortnite. I beg of them to make semi-interactive QTE stylized finishers like in Yakuza, and the rest stealth based with slow-mo mechanics to feel the power of John Wick.

coveredGames.name: SILENT HILL: Townfall
coveredGames.title: Another shot outside of the classic town. Silent Hill f was amazing experience, and I think Townfall will do the same for different reasons - like variety of options gameplay-wise.

coveredGames.name: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse
coveredGames.title: Amazing developers behind the game. Looks like nice balance between platforming and combat. Don't know yet how to feel about the animations & combat feeling, but seems delayed, even if a little bit.

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™
coveredGames.title: I feel like the game can't really do enough inside its universe when it comes to racing to support it for more than a short period of time. It needs to keep balance between fast and clear.

coveredGames.name: YAKOH SHINOBI OPS
coveredGames.title: Normally I wouldn't even look at the game, but age reveals that I yearn for this type of gameplay more and more. It looks decent, plays decent and seems to have fun mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Crimson Moon
coveredGames.title: HELL of a music choice for a trailer I admit. It does not work, it distracts. The lore will have to carry this one, because while art direction is good, the execution of it lacks.

coveredGames.name: DEATH STRANDING 2: ON THE BEACH
coveredGames.title: Someone update Sony and Kojimbovich that PC port of less magical sequel should not be priced as high as it is. Otherwise the game looks great, will play great considering the engine.

coveredGames.name: Forza Horizon 6
coveredGames.title: My prayers worked - Forza finally gets a real city district that's not just a small landmark on the map. The game looks, sound and possibly plays amazing. I hope they don't overdo it.

coveredGames.name: ONTOS
coveredGames.title: It's like Christmas present for the fans of well written and produced horror. Previous works just scream quality and if there's even a chance of another banger - we welcome it.

coveredGames.name: GANG OF DRAGON
coveredGames.title: While RGG misses recently, one of the greats showcases what he's about. Seems like the game is more of a narrative experience rather than borderline sandbox that Yakuzas became. It looks great.

coveredGames.name: CONTROL Resonant
coveredGames.title: Remedy doesn't miss when it comes to art direction. Environments, color palette and overall design is just amazing to look at. The game itself takes different approach it seems from their usual.

coveredGames.name: Armatus
coveredGames.title: A nice mash up of handful of genres. Seems like the game looks comfortably AA. All that matters here is the core roguelike mechanics and the smoothness of gameplay. It looks fluid on trailers.

coveredGames.name: Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors
coveredGames.title: Smart idea to use the genre defining brand and expand to ones that are already established. It will be cheap and it will be great 20-30 hours of big numbers on screen.

coveredGames.name: Steam Machine
coveredGames.title: So... a Steam console. I don't think it is a good idea. The competition is slim, but cemented. The spec's don't look too good either, unless it's a base and will be customizable. Too early to know.

coveredGames.name: Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties
coveredGames.title: Very mixed about this one. Kiwami remakes are amazing, but the changes made are not quite what fans wanted. Additional "Gaiden" for Mine however makes it worth it in my opinion.

coveredGames.name: Kaidan
coveredGames.title: Interesting and unique take on designs. Locations look decent. The game has this passable european style jank that's not really possible to deduce from a trailer itself. Might be great indie.

coveredGames.name: Dragon Age™ Inquisition
coveredGames.title: "Stupid darkspawn ruin everything. We're killing them, right? Because we are. Come on. Let's go plug some arseholes!" - Sera

coveredGames.name: Sea of Thieves: 2026 Edition
coveredGames.title: Yo Ho Ho

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles
coveredGames.title: One of the best games ever made.

coveredGames.name: Deep Rock Galactic
coveredGames.title: For Rock and Stone!

coveredGames.name: Zombies Aren't Real
coveredGames.title: If you like tower defense, military strategy, and simulation games, Zombies Aren't Real is definitely worth keeping an eye on – even if it's still in development.

coveredGames.name: Last Train Home
coveredGames.title: If you prefer strategy games with both tactical battles and extensive management, Last Train Home is definitely worth a try.

coveredGames.name: Lessaria: Fantasy Kingdom Sim
coveredGames.title: A solid fantasy strategy game that particularly succeeds with its idea of ​​a kingdom where the heroes act independently.

coveredGames.name: CONTROL Resonant
coveredGames.title: Provides a more dynamic combat system, larger areas, better traversal, and a hugely creative world. If you liked Control mix of act action, mystery this is highly recommended.

coveredGames.name: Transport Fever 3
coveredGames.title: If you love Transport Fever 2, Workers & Resources, Cities: Skylines or other complex management games, there's a lot to pick up here.

coveredGames.name: SILENT HILL: Townfall
coveredGames.title: If you particularly enjoyed Silent Hill 2 Remake, this is worth checking out.

coveredGames.name: Park Beyond
coveredGames.title: Creative and entertaining park building game, but with a management system that doesn't quite live up to its ambitions.

coveredGames.name: Empire of Sin
coveredGames.title: One of the most interesting mafia strategy games on the market. It sets in an atmospheric version of Prohibition-era Chicago] and combines city-building, economics, and turn-based combat.

coveredGames.name: The Sinking City 2
coveredGames.title: Looks substantially more modern than its predecessor. Arkham has a convincing combination of period architecture, decay and supernatural corruption. The creature design is particularly strong.

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS Zero Company™
coveredGames.title: The combat is satisfying, squad management is deep, the characters are memorable and the presentation is excellent. One of the best Star Wars games in years

coveredGames.name: Spacebase Startopia
coveredGames.title: Its underlying concept is still good, and there is fun to be had in constructing and operating your bizarre alien resort. But it feels much more like an attractive modernised interpretation.

coveredGames.name: Nobody Wants to Die
coveredGames.title: Atmosphere is outstanding: rain, neon, towering architecture, smoky interiors and retro-noir influences give the game a very distinctive identity.

coveredGames.name: Warhounds
coveredGames.title: Positioning, cover and line-of-sight matter in a way that makes firefights feel more physically grounded. The mercenary management and base layer provide enough strategic depth.

coveredGames.name: Corsair Cove
coveredGames.title: Successfully blends pirate fantasy with deep strategic management, making it one of the strongest releases in the genre this year.

coveredGames.name: Ghost Master: Resurrection
coveredGames.title: Game design never truly dies. Despite its imperfections, it successfully resurrects a cult classic and delivers hours of clever supernatural strategy.

coveredGames.name: City States: Medieval
coveredGames.title: Distinguishes itself from many modern city builders by emphasizing politics, economics, and social management alongside traditional construction mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Nightmare Frontier
coveredGames.title: Combines tactical RPG combat with the high-stakes tension of extraction games, creating a formula that feels surprisingly original.

coveredGames.name: The Necromancer's Tale
coveredGames.title: The Necromancer's Tale is one of the most distinctive narrative CRPGs in recent years. It feels closer to an interactive gothic novel than a traditional dungeon-crawling RPG.

coveredGames.name: Clanfolk
coveredGames.title: Requires patience to master, the rewarding progression and thoughtful design make it an excellent choice for strategy and simulation enthusiasts.

coveredGames.name: ENDLESS Legend™ 2
coveredGames.title: It delivers the "one more turn" feeling that defines the best 4X experiences while carving out its own identity through an evolving world and remarkably diverse factions.

coveredGames.name: FATAL FRAME II: Crimson Butterfly REMAKE
coveredGames.title: Fans of atmospheric supernatural horror should not miss this unforgettable journey into one of gaming's most haunting villages.

coveredGames.name: Esports Manager 2026
coveredGames.title: Fans of strategy and sports management games will find dozens of hours of rewarding gameplay as they chase championship glory.

coveredGames.name: Sintopia
coveredGames.title: It stands as one of the more inventive management games in recent years, successfully balancing complexity with personality.

coveredGames.name: Republic of Pirates
coveredGames.title: The greatest strength is its economic system. You establish settlements across multiple islands, manage production chains, and expand their pirate republic through careful resource management.

coveredGames.name: Atomfall
coveredGames.title: You should find plenty to enjoy, particularly if you value exploration and atmosphere over action-heavy gameplay.

coveredGames.name: DEATH STRANDING 2: ON THE BEACH
coveredGames.title: It refines the original's bold ideas rather than replacing them, delivering a more polished, more emotional, and more entertaining experience from beginning to end.

coveredGames.name: Frostpunk 2
coveredGames.title: Players seeking deep strategy, meaningful decision-making, and a richly atmospheric setting will find one of the strongest city-building games of recent years.

coveredGames.name: Terrinoth®: Heroes of Descent

coveredGames.name: Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss
coveredGames.title: It succeeds as a detective-driven cosmic horror experience thanks to its oppressive atmosphere, compelling mystery, and strong investigative mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Stray
coveredGames.title: Whether you're a cat lover, a fan of cyberpunk worlds, or simply someone who enjoys well-crafted storytelling, this is a journey worth taking.

coveredGames.name: Life is Strange: True Colors
coveredGames.title: For fans of narrative-driven games, character-focused storytelling, and emotionally intimate adventures, it is one of the strongest entries in the series.

coveredGames.name: Cronos: The New Dawn
coveredGames.title: What ultimately makes Cronos: The New Dawn interesting is that it feels authored rather than focus-tested.

coveredGames.name: Laysara: Summit Kingdom
coveredGames.title: A fresh and highly atmospheric city builder that transforms mountain survival into a rewarding strategic challenge.

coveredGames.name: Star Trek: Voyager - Across the Unknown
coveredGames.title: A faithful and atmospheric return to Voyager.

coveredGames.name: ZERO PARADES: Director's Cut
coveredGames.title: For players who love dialogue-heavy RPGs, ideological storytelling, and psychologically driven roleplaying, this game is essential.

coveredGames.name: Sudden Strike 5

coveredGames.name: Directive 8020
coveredGames.title: For fans of narrative-driven horror and classic sci-fi paranoia, this is an easy recommendation.

coveredGames.name: Until Dawn™

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Requiem

coveredGames.name: Age of Wonders 4

coveredGames.name: Paradigm

coveredGames.name: Domino Sky

coveredGames.name: Big Klondike - Classic Solitaire

coveredGames.name: Automachef

coveredGames.title: Old-school first person point and click puzzles with a pulp-novel writing style. Presented with a story of personal loss and mild psychological horror.

coveredGames.name: Tropico 7
coveredGames.title: With only the teaser trailer revealed ~ this is an early hype review comment just to say the updates and additions look like a good direction for the series ~ this review will be updated over time.

coveredGames.name: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse
coveredGames.title: Definitely have a love-hate relationship with Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. There are aspects it does well in, some aspects that could have improved, and I cycled between being annoyed and having fun.

coveredGames.name: Duck Side of the Moon
coveredGames.title: An overall alright game where you play as a duck in space helping out sentient geodes and fixing his ship. It’s cute, cozy, and enjoyable, but has some downsides, bugs, and annoyances.

coveredGames.name: The Witch's Bakery
coveredGames.title: Despite the rough start and many small negatives, The Witch’s Bakery is definitely a game that gets better the more you play as I came to really enjoy my time with it. Definitely recommend.

coveredGames.name: Click&Fix
coveredGames.title: I’m pretty neutral on Click&Fix. I did like Story mode and the incremental gameplay, but mixed on Unscrewing Ace mode and the roguelite element.

coveredGames.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope
coveredGames.title: I loved Little Hope and it’s my favorite DPA game. It has its issues, but it has the best prologue, I liked all of the characters, I liked the twist, and I didn’t get bored when doing Curator’s Cut.

coveredGames.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Man of Medan
coveredGames.title: Honestly was the first DPA game (played this after DiM and HoA) that didn’t bore me in the beginning and I didn’t hate the characters from the start. Not to mention this was surprisingly scary.

coveredGames.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes
coveredGames.title: Has a slow start, most characters are unlikeable, and it being more action packed means it’s not as scary, but I did end up liking it by the end and it still was tense.

coveredGames.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: The Devil in Me
coveredGames.title: It does have a slow start and items aren’t as important as they probably should be, but honestly it’s engaging and kept me hooked until the end.

coveredGames.name: Mewgenics
coveredGames.title: If you really like tactical turn-based combat, don’t mind the various aspects that comes with the roguelite genre, and don’t mind this being a slowburn, you can’t go wrong with Mewgenics.

coveredGames.name: Bloody Service
coveredGames.title: A short, but sweet horror visual novel. Only a few choices mattered and some points in the story were confusing, but it has interesting visuals and a crazy story you can’t look away from.

coveredGames.name: Atelier Shallie: Alchemists of the Dusk Sea DX
coveredGames.title: Atelier Shallie is an enjoyable, but average, game. There is a lot that brings this game down, like the inconsistent voice acting and writing, but I did enjoy most of my time with the game.

coveredGames.name: Woodo
coveredGames.title: Woodo is such a delightful and cozy little game. Playing with anything but a mouse isn't ideal, but I still had an enjoyable time with the story and the coloring book-hidden object hybrid gameplay.

coveredGames.name: Crime Scene Cleaner
coveredGames.title: I haven’t liked any other cleaning games in the same vein, but I absolutely loved Crime Scene Cleaner. The theming, storyline, and carefully crafted levels definitely puts this a step above the others

coveredGames.name: Shift At Midnight
coveredGames.title: Despite my little snafu with the music box, I honestly enjoyed Shift at Midnight. I love the analog horror vibes it gave me, I enjoyed the gameplay, and man is it so much scarier playing solo.

coveredGames.name: Ledgerbound
coveredGames.title: Ledgerbound might not be for everyone but if it is you’ll have a really hilarious and wild ride in store as you help Rayna and her ragtag team of non-Heroes save Heroes United Li- I mean save Eldarra!

coveredGames.name: Contrast
coveredGames.title: Finally coming around to playing Contrast, I ended up liking the shadow mechanic and the story of Didi and Dawn. However, it could have benefitted from being more fleshed out.

coveredGames.name: even if TEMPEST
coveredGames.title: I can't believe it took me so long to play even if TEMPEST. I ended up really enjoying my time with this otome VN with its interesting story, intriguing mysteries, and great writing and visuals.

coveredGames.name: Denshattack!
coveredGames.title: Denshattack may be a game that starts out strong and loses steam towards the end, but man is it worth it for the gameplay alone. It’s a really approachable and addicting game that is so fun to play.

coveredGames.name: Teeto
coveredGames.title: Teeto ended up being a really fun and charming 3D platformer that kept surprising me in various ways. This is an easy game to recommend to anyone that enjoys 3D platformers.

coveredGames.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami
coveredGames.title: Duck Detective does have its narrative and gameplay problems, but it’s honestly a really cute and interesting short detective game. I really hope we get another game as I did really enjoy the game.

coveredGames.name: Deathbulge: Battle of the Bands
coveredGames.title: I absolutely loved Deathbulge. This game is so funny and enjoyable that I couldn’t stop playing. You can feel the amount of love, care, and hard work was put into every aspect. This is a must play.

coveredGames.name: Schrödinger's Call
coveredGames.title: A must play visual novel that takes the Schrodinger's Cat thought experiment to the next level. This is such an emotional and impactful story that I'm so grateful I was able to experience.

coveredGames.name: Miss Rosen's Wowtastic! Marching Band
coveredGames.title: A delightfully weird and silly game that I can’t help but recommend. It’s a really charming short but sweet game that was so fun to play through and I really hope we get another game from these devs.

coveredGames.name: Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced
coveredGames.title: While Story Mode could have been better and more immersive, I honestly had a lot of fun with GTA 5 and loved the characters. Makes it even more disappointing the Story DLCS were cancelled for Online.

coveredGames.name: All Hail the Orb
coveredGames.title: All Hail The Orb is a silly little clicker incremental game that blends the best of both genres, making a really satisfying and enjoyable game.

coveredGames.name: MOUSE: P.I. For Hire
coveredGames.title: I’m so glad I decided to play MOUSE: P.I. despite not liking other games in its genre. I ended up really enjoying my time with the game, from the fun and satisfying gameplay to the wonderful visuals.

coveredGames.name: Cupid Parasite
coveredGames.title: Cupid Parasite is one of my favorite Otome VNs. I absolutely loved my time with the game as it was a lot of fun reading through, Lynette is a wonderful protagonist, and all the LIs are great.

coveredGames.name: Spooky Monster
coveredGames.title: An alright otome VN where you’re dragged into the monster world during Spooky Moon. The premise is interesting and the artwork is pretty, but translation is subpar and I didn’t like the execution.

coveredGames.name: Gecko Gods
coveredGames.title: A chill and cozy puzzle adventure game where you play a cute gecko doing puzzles and challenges placed around the archipelago. It’s nothing too complicated, but it’s a pretty enjoyable experience.

coveredGames.name: Dosa Divas
coveredGames.title: Dosa Divas is a delightful turn-based RPG that definitely hit my flavor weaknesses. If you find the story that focuses on food and family interesting and enjoyed Thirsty Suitors, you’ll like this.

coveredGames.name: Devil Jam
coveredGames.title: A decent bullet heaven set in Hell where you get the help of the Seven Deadly Sins (+the Devil) to defeat Death and gain back your soul. Not quite my jam (heh), but it could be others.

coveredGames.name: Etrange Overlord
coveredGames.title: I’m really glad I picked up this game as Etrange Overlord honestly made me so happy and laugh so much. This game does nearly everything perfectly and is definitely a must play game.

coveredGames.name: Trash Goblin
coveredGames.title: Trash Goblin is a great cozy game with a good gameplay loop and lovely character writing where you're a goblin who totally doesn't clean trinkets that were thrown away and sells them back to you.

coveredGames.name: Alba: A Wildlife Adventure
coveredGames.title: A cute short but sweet game where you play as a little girl taking pictures of the island wildlife and saving a nature reserve to stop plans for a luxury hotel. Worth buying but when it’s discounted.

coveredGames.name: Cat President: 3rd-Rate Candidate
coveredGames.title: I ended up liking Cat President 3 more than I thought I would. It’s pretty funny, the writing is well done, and I had a great time going through all the routes. This is an easy recommendation.

coveredGames.name: Edgar Allan Poe's Interactive Horror: 1995 Edition
coveredGames.title: The Dark Eye is a great game that adapts Poe’s stories in an interesting way while also meaningfully adding to them. This re-release is a great way to experience this game and it still holds up today.

coveredGames.name: Death Match Love Comedy!
coveredGames.title: DMLC might have had a bit of a rough patch during the beginning, but by the end it turned out to be such an amazing visual novel that does so many things well. It’s definitely a must play VN.

coveredGames.name: SOPA - Tale of the Stolen Potato
coveredGames.title: It's a short and cute game, but I'm neutral on Sopa. I leaned just enough to liking it to finish the game. If the story interests you, pick it up on sale.

coveredGames.name: Crisol: Theater of Idols
coveredGames.title: I absolutely loved Crisol: Theater of Idols. It’s a near perfect survival horror game that nails its atmosphere, immersion, & has a unique mechanic where you use blood as ammo against animated statues

coveredGames.name: My Sweet! Housemate
coveredGames.title: My Sweet! Housemate is a great short, but sweet VN that blends horror and comedy together well as you find yourself suddenly living with a (surprisingly charming) cannibal. Definitely recommend.

coveredGames.name: Dead Garden Zero

coveredGames.name: Red Vanilla 2
coveredGames.title: A simple but sweet arcade style shooter, while the goal is straight forward the warping mechanic makes it refreshing. Thought he primary colour choice of red started to strain my eyes after a bit

coveredGames.name: Extra Extra Poison

coveredGames.name: A Happy Place
coveredGames.title: A happy place is a fun game, though needs a bit more polish to be great. Its N64 visuals really sells it nicely but some info panels are more confusing than helpful. Apart from that its a good game <3

coveredGames.name: End's Reach
coveredGames.title: End's Reach is a promising story filled action adventure game with PSX visuals and good world building. With a bit more love to this game and it will be gold, aside from that have fun!

coveredGames.name: Arctic Eggs

coveredGames.name: Lunacid

coveredGames.title: Collect stickers to solve a murder in this ~1hr fill-in-the-blank style detective game. Cute, quirky, and unabashedly queer, it's perfect for busy weeknights; BUT the UI can be a tad cumbersome.

coveredGames.name: Home Safety Hotline
coveredGames.title: Windows 95 meets folklore in this clever, cozy-creepy ~3hr reading comprehension exam. Ideal for lore and art nerds (included artbook is amazing!), BUT no story and gameplay is 99% reading/recall.
