coveredGames.title: Easy | 4 hours | Keeps the improvements and gameplay options introduced by the previous game and adds new artworks more somber and fantasy themed puzzles that fans of the franchise will enjoy solving

coveredGames.name: RoboCop: Rogue City
coveredGames.title: Easy | <15 hours | Fun to play FPS and a great homage to the classic films, but might be too slow and janky if you’re not a fan of the franchise. For me, it was a great experience for its price.

coveredGames.name: Whimsical Heroes
coveredGames.title: Easy | < 2 hours | Interesting Turn Based Tactics game with cute characters and a beautiful visual style but it’s still missing a lot of content that hopefully will be added in the following updates

coveredGames.name: Hades II
coveredGames.title: Medium | 80 hours | Great roguelite game, as good as the first one but with a lot more content and even more different approaches to combat with the new abilities, upgrades and weapons.

coveredGames.name: Mars Attracts
coveredGames.title: Easy | 10 hours | Fun theme park building game with some new interesting mechanics and flavor but with some room to grow, because, at this moment, it’s easy to complete and there isn’t much content.

coveredGames.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip
coveredGames.title: Easy | 7 hours | Fun indie game full of weird characters, missions and side missions, where you also play minigames and can drive around in a small city, but getting 100% requires some time and effort

coveredGames.name: Snakebird Primer
coveredGames.title: Easy | 2 hours | Interesting indie puzzle game where most levels can be solved easily and where the graphics are pleasant, bright and colorful, but targeted mostly at children.

coveredGames.name: Overdrawn
coveredGames.title: Easy | 2-3 Hours | Fun but short on content indie, roguelike deckbuilder that fans of Balatro will probably enjoy, but looks and is played differently, relying most on luck and not on math

coveredGames.name: Jusant
coveredGames.title: Easy | 8 Hours | Jusant is a game about a world that has seen water vanish. You play as a character climbing a hill in search of answers. It is a lovely game with charming graphics and storyline.

coveredGames.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees
coveredGames.title: Hard* | 7 Hours | You play as a Gibbon trying to survive against deforestation. This is a wonderful game with a difficult achievement that requires a certain map to be generated on weekly challenge.

coveredGames.name: There Is No Game: Wrong Dimension
coveredGames.title: Medium | 9 Hours | "There is No Game" is a puzzle based game which has a variety of different styles for each level. It is very enjoyable but will require a bit of back tracking for achievements.

coveredGames.name: A Short Hike
coveredGames.title: Easy | 6 hours | A Short Hike is a nice, soothing game with a good storyline. The graphic style is unique and the achievements are fun to get and not too difficult.

coveredGames.name: Far Cry 3
coveredGames.title: Medium | 28 Hours | Far Cry 3 is a classic FPS with a fantastic storyline, ground-breaking (at the time) FPS mechanics and a giant map to explore.

coveredGames.name: Garden Story
coveredGames.title: Easy | 12 hours | A fun, top down pixel adventure game with light combat and loot and fetch based missions. You play as a fruit and have to save "The Grove" from the dreaded "Rot".

coveredGames.name: Glass Masquerade 3: Honeylines
coveredGames.title: Easy* | 7 hours | Interesting classic indie puzzle game that fans of the genre will enjoy, now with “lighter” and more hopeful imagery and more puzzle modes and piece shapes like hexagons.

coveredGames.name: Cat Quest III
coveredGames.title: Easy | 10 hours | Fun to play indie action game that is more enjoyable with two players. The characters are cute, the world looks fantastic and the graphics have improved a lot since the last game

coveredGames.name: Balatro
coveredGames.title: Hard | 300+ hours | One-of-a-kind, genre defining deckbuilding game with lots of strategies and content to keep you engaged for a long time but getting 100% requires a lot of persistence and some luck

coveredGames.name: Superflight
coveredGames.title: Easy | 1,5 hours* | Interesting wingsuit simulator where you feel the speed as you dive and avoid the obstacles and it’s immersive despite the simple voxel graphics. Atm it only costs 59 cents.

coveredGames.name: Dungeon and Puzzles
coveredGames.title: Easy w/guide | < 14 hours | interesting Sokoban-style game, but the limited number of weapons, the total number of puzzles, and the difficulty level of some of them make the game a bit repetitive.

coveredGames.name: 9 Kings
coveredGames.title: 9 Kings is an extremely challenging roguelite deckbuilder that simultaneously lets you go out of hand like there's no tomorrow by using its intentionally exploitable mechanics. It's so much FUN.

coveredGames.name: Void War
coveredGames.title: So, let's make more FTL and make it metal, they said, then went full 40k power fantasy with it and did both worlds justice. I'll call my firstborn Giant Necrophage.

coveredGames.name: You Are Empty: Absolute Edition
coveredGames.title: Slavjank+

coveredGames.name: Galactic Glitch
coveredGames.title: If you want a solid roguelite SHMUP with strong enemy design, juicy looks, variety, and accessible difficulty, then you can't go wrong with Galactic Glitch.

coveredGames.name: Disfigure
coveredGames.title: The game is generous, challenging, it just clicks. And it's Crimsonland-adjacent.

coveredGames.name: Silver Pines
coveredGames.title: Looking at the trailers, I expected a stylish, non-substantial cinematic experience. What I got was fully-fledged survival horror magnum opus of great impact.

coveredGames.name: Iron Blight
coveredGames.title: Cry of Fear 2 ain't happening, not during this wave. I didn't hope for it, although, Iron Blight has broken the upsetting combo of mediocrity using an offbeat approach.

coveredGames.name: Pathogenic
coveredGames.title: A great roguelite doesn't just demoralise when it kills you, this one swiftly replaces the sprouts of sadness with anticipation for the next run where anything could happen. It's brilliant, simple as.

coveredGames.name: INCISION
coveredGames.title: The closest parallels gameplay-wise would be DUSK and HROT if you infused them with the period blood of a Strogg juiced on anabolics and hepatitis.

coveredGames.name: Aliens vs. Predator™
coveredGames.title: Ever wondered how a Xeno would react if you catch its inner mouth like a cat's tongue? Here you go, for honour or whatnot.

coveredGames.name: Beneath Oresa
coveredGames.title: So, why do I recommend Oresa despite all? It's a gratifying spectacle spun around a smart system. I'm not saying the game is an academic study, but I can't fault something so clever and elegant.

coveredGames.name: ROUTINE
coveredGames.title: Look, it isn't perfect. Solemn, slow, confusing, it outstays its welcome. But great things are allowed to have flaws. Besides, it's beautiful and the monster is caked up alright.

coveredGames.name: Quake
coveredGames.title: It felt like Quake reciprocated, like it was glad I returned, happily assaulting me with a vicious smile on its square mug and a jagged hard-on in hand.

coveredGames.name: DOOM
coveredGames.title: I keep it short and sweet this time. Okay, maybe a bit bitter.

coveredGames.name: Returnal™
coveredGames.title: Returnal is a roguelite bullet hell arena shooter with metroidvania elements. Every run a speedrun, every frame a painting! Finnish gamedev is cooking with plasma.

coveredGames.name: Dragon Front: Adventures
coveredGames.title: It's an addictive roguelite deckbuilder that focuses on tactical unit placement. It's synergetic, snappy, transparent with its information... and utterly underrated.

coveredGames.name: Heavy Metal Death Can
coveredGames.title: Das Boot horror with fixed camera angles is all I ever wanted. It feels fresh yet comfortably familiar, a dependable survival horror loop is as potent as it ever was.

coveredGames.name: For The King II
coveredGames.title: I know "organic" and "emergent" are buzzwords, but they accurately describe this TTRPG roguelite extravaganza.

coveredGames.name: Skewer Squad
coveredGames.title: I didn't make a single food pun and I'm proud of it. Anyway, it's a Brotato-like roguelite, clever and cute.

coveredGames.name: Tyranny
coveredGames.title: It's a tiny stub of a review that I brushed up to fit in, but Tyranny must be here as a sobering lesson in the unapproachable reality of raw power. One of my faves.

coveredGames.name: Lucky Tower Ultimate
coveredGames.title: Your death is the main attraction here. Abrupt and painful, it takes many gruesome forms, typically hilarious, which is Lucky Tower's bedrock.

coveredGames.name: Banquet for Fools
coveredGames.title: I'm uncertain what it evokes. Nox? Dungeon Siege? Morrowind? "We don't follow a canon, manifesting like it's the first game ever made" - is how I imagine the thought process behind its defiant design.

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil 7 Biohazard
coveredGames.title: No worries, I'm cooking a huge gem of a game this month, just wanted to restore justice and add a tiny little review on my favourite newer Rezzy. The most viscerally terrifying one, that's for sure!

coveredGames.name: Esoteric Ebb
coveredGames.title: What a strange game! So well-built it punches far above its weight. On paper, it's something only a seasoned industry veteran like Brian Fargo could produce.

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Requiem
coveredGames.title: What kind of a devil has such favourable soul exchange rate? We'll never know. But it worked! So does the game, huge and operating smoothly from day one, which is no small feat.

coveredGames.name: Mewgenics
coveredGames.title: A cluster♥♥♥♥ of good ideas.

coveredGames.name: Cronos: The New Dawn
coveredGames.title: Like a Christmas dream, I see Dead Space entering SOMA and The Thing breeding all 12 Monkeys at once!

coveredGames.name: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin
coveredGames.title: A culture that fosters inclusivity desperately needs its mean-spirited, obnoxious outliers to remind us that art doesn't need to appease. It can crap the bed... and get away with.

coveredGames.name: BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER 3: I OPENED A PORTAL TO HELL IN THE FAVELA TRYING TO REVIVE MIT AIA I NEED TO CLOSE IT
coveredGames.title: Wait, I removed this one? My mistake (what a coward). It's crazy and it's Quake. Out of Early Access, so it's about time.

coveredGames.name: The Last of Us™ Part I
coveredGames.title: There were points when I was close to crying without the sad piano to manipulate my emotions. It kept me in a chokehold.

coveredGames.name: BioMenace Remastered
coveredGames.title: I was hyped for a game and it exceeded my expectations. Mind-blowing. BioMenace already was a cut above the rest, but this remaster broke all sorts of grounds. Deadass.

coveredGames.name: Blood: Refreshed Supply™
coveredGames.title: The way they treated Fresh Supply owners was disgraceful and I don't endorse it. To boot, FS got delisted, bonking my review off the curator page. Sorry for reposting, but I want for it to be here.

coveredGames.name: Dungeon Rats
coveredGames.title: Just don't expect much charity, this cruel mistress won't kneel. It's minmax or bust. The game was designed to be studied, mastered, exploited - not to simply be beaten.

coveredGames.name: The Lacerator
coveredGames.title: This thing is only playing dumb. Its uniquely eccentric gameplay deserves to be experienced, its branching narrative - pieced together. It's a cult hit, is all.

coveredGames.name: Gears of War: Reloaded
coveredGames.title: This isn't a perfect reload by a mile. But half of the players are upset with the multiplayer, which I never tackle. The campaign alone was worth it for me, but it would be wise to wait for the fixes.

coveredGames.name: Heretic + Hexen
coveredGames.title: A classic Nightdive remaster, woo! They really did a number on Hexen.

coveredGames.name: Hands of Necromancy II
coveredGames.title: A solid Heretic-like. It won't blow your mind, especially if you already played the original, but this is how you make a conservative sequel. Which is a pretty damn oldschool practice in itself.

coveredGames.name: Skogdal
coveredGames.title: A MEGA-COOL punk-ass Black Metal deckbuilder.

coveredGames.name: CONSCRIPT: Director’s Cut
coveredGames.title: Rezzy got reanimated once again for our rotten pleasure. I loved its highs and wasn't bothered by the lows. Great War wasn't so great, but as a game's setting it's one of the tastiest corpse soups.

coveredGames.name: Forgive Me Father 2
coveredGames.title: Trust me, I'm no less of a wretch than before, so the sequel was subjected to the same amount of scrutiny. FMF2 is just so disarmingly good.

coveredGames.name: My Name is Mayo: Remayo
coveredGames.title: A remake of My name is Mayo? Take my money. You will understand.

coveredGames.name: Deadly Days: Roadtrip
coveredGames.title: I admit I didn't play this voluntarily at first (gamescom, iykyk), but I loved it from the spot, and I had a lot of fun so far with my partner. Can recommend for coop, even in early access state.

coveredGames.name: office chair curling
coveredGames.title: A fun little game that was originally developed for Playdate, but it also works great on Steamdeck. Hurl chairs along hallways, glide over greasy stains and land some points!

coveredGames.name: The Alters
coveredGames.title: Creating a clone that helps you with your daily tasks? Yes, that is a real necessity if you are in a survival game. Jan Dolski must create Alters of himself, but behind that is a question of morale.

coveredGames.name: Cast n Chill
coveredGames.title: Relaxed fishing? Yes, please. You can play it actively, but also in passive mode. Collect (rare) fishes, upgrade your gear and enjoy beautiful pixelated landscapes.

coveredGames.name: The Diary
coveredGames.title: A puzzler revolving around several diaries that lets you peek into the lives of people's lives. It is an interactive story told via the written word - a bit like Florence, according to the Devs.

coveredGames.name: Date Everything!
coveredGames.title: You can date... everyTHING! Yes, your bed, your trashcan, your whatever, about 100 characters and it looks hilarious. I need this sandbox dating simulator baaad.

coveredGames.name: Tiny Aquarium: Social Fishkeeping
coveredGames.title: This is the kind of game that popped up again in 2025: a small window on your desktop that kind of plays itself. I love the idea though. And it looks great.

coveredGames.name: The Drifter
coveredGames.title: I love point&clicks that try to defy genre rules and so I was captivated by The Drifter that feels like a playable pixelart movie. There is no screen searching here, but action and a grim touch.

coveredGames.name: Is This Seat Taken?
coveredGames.title: Place little people in an arrangement of chairs, but behold! They have specific wishes and dislikes to honour. Sp pay attention. Cute and relaxing, just what I need :D

coveredGames.name: Star Birds
coveredGames.title: From the creators of Kurzgesagt comes a - strategy game? Yes. Still in early access, this game brings the known art style and satisfying ressource management on tiny asteroids.

coveredGames.name: Mind Diver
coveredGames.title: This looks like a cinematic point&click with a huge portion of detective game. As a mind diver, you search in the subconscious of Lina and try to restore her memory.

coveredGames.name: Dispatch
coveredGames.title: This is the superhero game we needed, period. After you've played this, there is no going back to normal. I think I might be in love with the comics, the gameplay and the cast. Oh, and the music.

coveredGames.name: The Séance of Blake Manor
coveredGames.title: A detective game with a touch - okay, a load of mystery is just my jam. The developers of Darkside Detective and the publisher Raw Fury promise a lot with this one!

coveredGames.name: The Berlin Apartment
coveredGames.title: This is history, lived through. Not a feelgood-game, but I guess an important one. Experience Germany at the time of the DDR and the Mauer.

coveredGames.name: My Wife Threw Out My Card Collection (So I Bought a Dump to Find Them All) ⭐
coveredGames.title: This caught my eye immediately - I am a collector at heart and so the game mechanic (sorting through trash, redeeming your lost cards) resonated with me.

coveredGames.name: The Darkside Detective: Backside of the Moon
coveredGames.title: You heard it here first: this cannot be bad. I always loved the humour of the darkside detective games, classic Point & click combined with absurd conversations and some monsters and references.

coveredGames.name: The First Mine
coveredGames.title: In the aftermath of Dorfromantik, many games were developed that had a similar mechanic. This one as well, but it has some interesting tweaks that create a satisfying loop. I really enjoyed playing.

coveredGames.name: ISLANDERS: New Shores
coveredGames.title: A follow-up title to Islanders. This feels more intuitive, more organic and more beautiful without losing its core mechanic. I can only recommend playing it if you liked the first one.

coveredGames.name: SUMMERHOUSE
coveredGames.title: This chill game lets you design your perfect holiday location in a bright pixelart look that makes me feel the sun on my skin. Without highscores, there is just your perfectionism to beat.

coveredGames.name: Trinket Bag Maker
coveredGames.title: If you want a cute game with pretty aesthetics that feels like a nostalgic trip to the early-2000’s, I highly recommend Trinket Bag Maker.

coveredGames.name: Alba: A Wildlife Adventure
coveredGames.title: Featured on Her Cozy Gaming blog - Easy games for first-time gamers

coveredGames.name: Warhammer Survivors
coveredGames.title: Yes!

coveredGames.name: Cronos: The New Dawn
coveredGames.title: Wishlist and follow!

coveredGames.name: STARCULT Night Twisted Age
coveredGames.title: Visual novel with a sci-fantasy setting where you're a young noblewoman investigating the murder of her husband. The emotions system adds an cool twist to the standard VN gameplay. Has demo!

coveredGames.name: Cross Country Case
coveredGames.title: Upcoming detective game with pixel-art visuals where you'll track down a killer throughout the Italian countryside.

coveredGames.name: The Wolf Among Us Remastered
coveredGames.title: Remaster of narrative game where you'll explore the seedy underbelly of a community of fairy tale refugees. Peak example of Telltale's "Your choices (don't actually) matter" model, for good and ill.

coveredGames.name: Cognition: An Erica Reed Thriller
coveredGames.title: [Haven't played] Adventure game where you're an FBI agent on the trail of a serial killer. Standard point-and-click gameplay, though fans of the genre might find the QTE-like challenges frustrating.

coveredGames.name: Heaven Does Not Respond 2
coveredGames.title: Upcoming sequel to analog horror/fake OS game. This time you'll have to delve in the depths of a retro computer in search of your missing memories.

coveredGames.name: The Apothecary Diaries: The False Imperial Brother
coveredGames.title: Upcoming 3d adventure game where you play as everyone's favorite poison gremlin, solving cases in the imperial palace through observation and interrogation. Pretty steep price tag.

coveredGames.name: The Archives of Trevosa
coveredGames.title: Upcoming remake of a browser-based deduction game where you'll pour over letters and documents to untangle the family tree of a royal dynasty. Loved the original, and this one promises bonus content!

coveredGames.name: Alex Hill: Whispers at White Oak Inn
coveredGames.title: [Haven't played] Mystery point-and-click where you'll investigate a haunting. Part of the recent trend of Nancy Drew-likes, along with "Penelope Pendrick and the Art of Deceit". Has demo!

coveredGames.name: Dreadline Express
coveredGames.title: Psychological horror game with mystery and point-and-click elements where you find yourself aboard the last train on earth. The vibes are truly rancid, in the best sense. Has demo!

coveredGames.name: Surradia: An Art Retrospective
coveredGames.title: Upcoming deduction game with fill-the-blanks gameplay a la Golden Idol, where you'll unveil the drama behind an art movement / magic cult based on their works and documents.

coveredGames.name: Zaehbet, Draad
coveredGames.title: Upcoming visual novel with language deciphering elements, where you wake up in a hospital to a nurse speaking a language you don't understand. Make sense of her words, one by one, and.... Has demo!

coveredGames.name: The Polar Darkness
coveredGames.title: Upcoming funky-looking mystery game where you'll investigate the disappearance of a child preacher in 1980s rural Finland.

coveredGames.name: Wren Falls
coveredGames.title: [Received key] A couple is found murdered at their farmhouse, their son the only witness. Look after him for a week as you try to solve the case. Bit rough around the edges, but a solid story!

coveredGames.name: Alien Morgue
coveredGames.title: [Played demo] Determine the cause of death of various strange alien species. It's essentially a series of logic puzzles, but has a cool vibe. Could there be something linking these deaths together...?

coveredGames.name: Uplink
coveredGames.title: Haven't played this old hacking sim so I can't vouch for how mystery-ish it gets, but you can definitely use it to live out all your "[mashes keyboard randomly] I'm in" fantasies.

coveredGames.name: Grégoire Lefèbvre Investigations : The Vow of Hate
coveredGames.title: [Received key] Game set in 1799 France, where you'll investigate the murder of an unpopular town priest. 3D point-and-click gameplay. Too much jank and pixel hunting to recommend, but decent story.

coveredGames.name: Where is Starlingdive
coveredGames.title: Upcoming Roottrees-like investigation game. Search through various archives, documents and zines to solve a missing person case at a local college.

coveredGames.name: This Is Not For You
coveredGames.title: Upcoming dreamlike horror game inspired by fiction such as "House of Leaves". Map out an impossible lighthouse and burn it all down.

coveredGames.name: The Deed
coveredGames.title: Short little game that's not a whodunnit but a how-get-away-with-it. Plan the murder of a relative and pin the blame on someone else. Visuals are rough, but not bad for what it is. Multiple endings.

coveredGames.name: Hill Agency: PURITYdecay
coveredGames.title: [Haven't played] Point-and-click game where you play as a private investigator in an indigenous-inspired futuristic noir setting.

coveredGames.name: The Reluctant Redemption of Verity Lux
coveredGames.title: [Played demo] Visual novel with a sci-fi setting where you play as a journalist investigating a celebrity disappearance. Some investigation elements.

coveredGames.name: Private Psychic
coveredGames.title: Upcoming point-and-click adventure where you'll play as a psychic who's just opened a paranormal detective agency.

coveredGames.name: Lenrual
coveredGames.title: [Received key] A surreal, laid-back puzzle game where you find yourself in a strange city. Not exactly mystery-ish, but very cool dreamlike setting.

coveredGames.name: Truth Scrapper
coveredGames.title: Upcoming Visual Novel from the dev of In Stars and Time, where you must crack the case of a mysterious attacker, while your memory resets every night. Has demo!

coveredGames.name: Broken Sword - Shadow of the Templars: Reforged
coveredGames.title: Even in its remade form, Broken Sword retains some of the known pains of old-school point and click adventures, but it remains a great option if you're in the mood for a globetrotting caper.

coveredGames.name: French Crime Detective Game
coveredGames.title: [Haven't played] Detective game including 9 bite-sized murder mysteries with FMV visuals. Seems to require a separate account and permanent online connection, which I'm not thrilled about.

coveredGames.name: Tearoom of Terror
coveredGames.title: Upcoming mystery game where you inherit a teahouse frequented by weirdos and you'll have to alternate between serving treats and solving murders.

coveredGames.name: Psycho-Sleuth
coveredGames.title: Upcoming visual novel where people with special abilities are locked in a deadly game. Death games aren't really my genre at all, but it might appeal to you if you enjoyed Danganronpa. Has demo!

coveredGames.name: A Night at Moka Efti: A Babylon Berlin Story
coveredGames.title: (Free!) noir adventure game based in the book and TV series, where you play as a journalist investigating the seedy underbelly of Weimar-era Berlin. Plot's all over the place, but very stylish!

coveredGames.name: SOKO 1977: Anti-Terror Task Force
coveredGames.title: Upcoming investigation game by the devs of The Darkest Files, set during the German Autumn, with deduction and rogue-like elements.

coveredGames.name: Obsidian Moon

coveredGames.title: I enjoyed this game. Some of the obstacles made me want to smash my head through the monitor but but overall the humorous parts of the game kept me enjoying it all the way through.

coveredGames.name: BrokenLore: UNFOLLOW
coveredGames.title: The story was a bit strange at times but the chase scenes were super intense. Also, that mom was hot.

coveredGames.name: 日本事故物件監視協会2 -Japan Stigmatized Property-
coveredGames.title: Second installment to the series. Its an "observation duty" like game. However, apparently the screens are real camera footage. If you like these type of games then you will definitely like this!

coveredGames.name: ROUTINE
coveredGames.title: The most visually realistic horror game I have seen. The devs give ho hints. So learning anything is all on your own. I find myself frustrated at times but i still can't stop playing this.

coveredGames.name: A.I.L.A
coveredGames.title: A true hidden gem. I am not sure why its not as popular as it is. It has all the elements that make horror games fun. Great story, great visuals, great jumpscares. One of my favorites of the year!

coveredGames.name: Fever Meme
coveredGames.title: THIS GAME IS TOXIC, UNFAIR, AND I CAN'T STOP PLAYING IT. I WILL BEAT THE BOSS EVEN IF IT TAKES ME 100 HOURS. 10/10.

coveredGames.name: Species: Unknown
coveredGames.title: How is this game not viral?! This is easily my favorite multiplayer horror of the year! 1. mission based game. 2. Each monster has its own "personality". 3. Its gorgeous, challenging and scary!

coveredGames.name: Last Term
coveredGames.title: "Exit 8 like game." I love when they add an actual story with multiple endings. Fun concept to the genra.

coveredGames.name: Dead Reset
coveredGames.title: This is the best FMV game I have ever played BY FAR. Its also the only FMV game that I have played multiple times for different endings.

coveredGames.name: PIGFACE
coveredGames.title: Old school graphics. Super violent. Bad guys are vulgar. Combat can be chaos and funny. All in all. Great game.

coveredGames.name: CloverPit
coveredGames.title: This is only horror gambling game I have ever liked. I cant stop playing this. Maybe because that what gambling does to you. But in this game "being horror" you gamble with your life.

coveredGames.name: The Lightkeeper
coveredGames.title: It's a really well done horror game. A really dark story. While typically "lighthouse" games are lovecraftian i feel this is more its own thing. but why ai voices? Also, this game is beautiful.

coveredGames.name: Cronos: The New Dawn
coveredGames.title: Its not Indie, but I had to add this. Its my personal favorite of the year. It's "deadspace gameplay" with a Mandalorian type story. Also, the story keeps you guessing to the end. LOVE THIS GAME !!!

coveredGames.name: No, I'm not a Human
coveredGames.title: Absolute fantastic game. This is so fun to play with friends especially. Every day is a debate. And every playthrough is different. Visitors are randomized to so you can't Meta it. Loved it !

coveredGames.name: Japan Stigmatized Property -日本事故物件監視協会-
coveredGames.title: Another refreshing take on the "spot the anomaly" genre. This one uses real life camera footage. I really enjoyed that the changes were not only creepy but were challenging too!

coveredGames.name: Tales Beyond The Tomb - Route 86
coveredGames.title: Another great one by 616 Games. This is arguably the best story so far. Much more gruesome than the others too.

coveredGames.name: School 666
coveredGames.title: Another great anomaly based multiplayer game from this dev. I like that it's more silly than scary. its a must for people that love anomaly games!

coveredGames.name: Lost Luminosity
coveredGames.title: I enjoyed this game. The jump scares were more dialed in than most games i've played. Story wasn't bad either. This game won't change your life but for 3 dollars its definitely worth it.

coveredGames.name: Luto
coveredGames.title: Beautiful game. Beautiful story. Some of the puzzles can be a little confusing. controller preferred over mouse and keyboard. Consider this one of the best horror games of the year.

coveredGames.name: Who's at the door?
coveredGames.title: One of the most fun anomaly (exit 8 like) games of the year. The graphics and story is wild. 100% for streamers or gaming with friends.

coveredGames.name: Dread Flats
coveredGames.title: YES! This is a fantastic walking sim! Lots of creepy and uncomfortable vibes with great jump scares! My favorite walking sim I have played in a while!

coveredGames.name: Last Report
coveredGames.title: Wow. What a great story. I did two playthroughs to make sure I didn't miss any endings (not trying to spoil). Its, definitely one of the most enjoyable games I have played as of late!

coveredGames.name: Don't Mess With Bober
coveredGames.title: Its a short silly horror game. Its fun for a laugh with friends or stream. My only complaint would be the AI voices which were so bad it was ruining the humor. Buy on a discount.

coveredGames.name: Infected Dawn
coveredGames.title: I loved the concept (use the limited time you have to prepare for a zombie attack). The animations are so bad that its fun to watch. This game is fun with friends or for stream! Buy on a discount.

coveredGames.name: The Echo Paradox
coveredGames.title: Fun game. Alien | Portal vibes. Horror mixed with humor. The game is worth a playthrough if its on sale.

coveredGames.name: SUBMERSIBLE
coveredGames.title: I am addicted to this game. You are in a submarine, you dive, you land on and search anomalies (ocean floor, submarines, underwater stations), collect loot. shoot monsters. survive! It has story! Win!

coveredGames.title: A tactical, turn-based RPG where you can control the game either from your PC or your phone. A hex-based world where you can play co-op. Has a playable Jerboa character called the Vanguard.

coveredGames.name: Brewhaha
coveredGames.title: A deckbuilding co-op game where whatever you draw is played immediately! Randomness is emphasized, and either rewarded or punished!

coveredGames.name: Wanderling

coveredGames.name: Missi
coveredGames.title: A charming hand drawn point and click game where to guide the titular mouse Missi on her quest to gather special items and herbs for her sick son.

coveredGames.name: Kneedle Knight
coveredGames.title: A 3D platformer where you play as a small mouse knight, who must solve puzzles and fight candle enemies in order to defeat the Fabric Witch!

coveredGames.name: Winter Burrow
coveredGames.title: A cozy survival game where you, a little mouse, return home to find much work needing to be done. Craft clothes and items, meet friendly neighbors, and build a warm cozy home to shelter in.

coveredGames.name: Danger Mouse
coveredGames.title: Play as the eponymous Danger Mouse or his sidekick Penfold through 15 levels in this side-scrolling beat'em up.

coveredGames.name: RatScum
coveredGames.title: Play as a lost rat trying to find his way home. Befriend other rats, solve puzzles, and explore the mysterious underground in an atmospheric and story-rich world.

coveredGames.name: Morsels
coveredGames.title: As a small mouse you find yourself trapped in the sewer. But fear not! a magical fatberg grants you the magical ability to change your form in a variety of ways to battle killer cats.

coveredGames.name: Draggin'
coveredGames.title: Slay dragons by dragging your mouse (LITERALLY!) in this charming spell-based game. Unlock new spells for your mouse witch to use and turn up the heat on the dragons!

coveredGames.name: Slay or Fall
coveredGames.title: Play as a dark lord defending his dungeon from venturing heroes. A text-based management game where you must summon and command your minions to fight humans. Has ratfolk units you can control.

coveredGames.name: Mousebusters
coveredGames.title: After moving into your new apartment you're suddenly cursed and turn into a mouse! Now what? You hunt ghosts that's what! The only way to undo the curse is to help your neighbors with their hauntings.

coveredGames.name: Rocket Rats
coveredGames.title: Play as an Astronaut rat and defeat waves of cheese-based aliens. The more cheese you acquire, the more you can upgrade and customize your gear, as well as unlock new characters.

coveredGames.name: Wires And Whiskers
coveredGames.title: A co-op platformer where a Laboratory Gerbil and his mechanical companion must traverse dangerous levels, combat mutated enemies, and overcome obstacles in a post-apocalyptic world.

coveredGames.name: GAT RAT
coveredGames.title: Use twenty different guns, multiple spells, and other items to blast your way across different realms as a gun wielding rat/mouse in this side-scrolling shooter.

coveredGames.name: Mouse Curser
coveredGames.title: Use your mouse cursor to play as a mouse curser. All movement, actions, etc are controlled by moving your computer mouse. Cast spells, defeat enemies, and be the best curser you can be!

coveredGames.name: MouseVentures
coveredGames.title: Play as Pipo, a plush mouse, as he enters storybooks and aids characters with their various stories in this charming game with a cute paper-cutout design.

coveredGames.name: Restaurats
coveredGames.title: Open a medieval tavern either solo or with your friends, and cook delicious meals as a rat. As chef, cook and serve meals to a variety of costumers, and get into bagu fights with your friends.

coveredGames.name: Maze Mice
coveredGames.title: A roguelike where time only moves when you do. Play as cute mice evading cats, collecting dots, and getting upgrades.

coveredGames.name: Squeakross: Home Squeak Home
coveredGames.title: Solve puzzles to decorate your new home as a little mouse. Unlock new items and customize your little rodent in this cozy game.

coveredGames.name: Tour de France 2025
coveredGames.title: Lacks a pissing mechanic. Unrealistic. What's the point if I can't be at the front of the pack to piss all over myself and the other riders? I'm not going to the back when I'm winning.

coveredGames.name: Blood: Refreshed Supply™
coveredGames.title: Better and harder than any of your mum's FPS games. One of the best, from gameplay to level design. However, the price is way too high (thanks WB and Atari, you bastards). Wait for it to go on sale.

coveredGames.name: HYPNOSYNC
coveredGames.title: You mind control customers by syncing up with the rhythm game mechanics, and the game mind controls you with gacha mechanics. Hypnosis fetishists get manipulated, news at 11.

coveredGames.name: Frogatto & Friends
coveredGames.title: It's more accurately "Frogatto, His Neighbours, the Town Usurer, and a Bunch of Dudes He Doesn't Know," but that doesn't roll off the tongue quite so well, nor does it please the ear like its OST.

coveredGames.name: Scam With Your Friends
coveredGames.title: You and your friends become one with the Infinity Indians in their scam call centres, and recite ancient Hindu mantras into your microphones to earn infinity wealth from baby boomers.

coveredGames.name: Family Time
coveredGames.title: You were raped by a wolf girl and cast out of society, so now you have to wrangle, feed, and shelter dozens of fluffy children. The kids are cute, but Holo would have made the superior wife.

coveredGames.name: Rideshare "Stimulator"
coveredGames.title: Believe it or not, it isn't a western h-game: it's a glorified benchmark program from Unigine about driving your car through town and having non-sexually stimulating conversations with passengers.

coveredGames.name: Poke ALL Toads
coveredGames.title: Poke All Toads Has Toad-Poking Fairies Who All Poke Toads But Toads Poke All Fairies With Long Sticky Tongues For Poking All Toads And Swallow Them Up So Fairies Work Together To Safely Poke All Toads

coveredGames.name: Unclean Water
coveredGames.title: The second sewerslut game after Peripeteia, Unclean Water has you fight scantily-clad women while wading through human waste in a medieval sewer.

coveredGames.name: Monster Girl Therapy
coveredGames.title: There's a lot of talking and rare minigames, just like therapy in real life. Unlike real therapy (unless you're schizo), you're also trying to rescue annoyed monster girl NPCs from a dying MMO server.

coveredGames.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie
coveredGames.title: It's a fanservice followup to Katamari Damacy. You walk around, find fictitious fans of the original game, and try your best to satisfy their weird-ass requests for the sequel.

coveredGames.name: Katamari Damacy REROLL
coveredGames.title: 塊 魂 is Japanese for "clump spirit," which is a pretty good name for a game about a little dude who rolls up objects onto a big adhesive ball.

coveredGames.name: Rez Infinite
coveredGames.title: The director & producer have both given different meanings for Rez's name. Resolve? Resolute? Tron's de-rezzing? All depends on who and when you ask. What's certain: the devs hope you enjoy it forever

coveredGames.name: Too Many F*cking Nazis
coveredGames.title: After years of being called Hitler for everything, no one cares in-universe when time traveling Nazis take over the world. Jonathan Pageau warned you.

coveredGames.name: Raise the Colours
coveredGames.title: It's a co-op game where you and your buds scramble to raise britbong flags (hence the King's English spelling) all over the level while local council members hunt you down.

coveredGames.name: Text To Speech
coveredGames.title: It is indeed a text to speech program. More accurately, it's a paid GUI frontend to a free TTS engine. Maybe it's decent, but I doubt it'll do well in the arms race of free programs vs paid ones.

coveredGames.name: Ctesiphon
coveredGames.title: Ctesiphon was originally named after the ancient Persian capital back when it was a desert-themed FPS, and the name stuck even after it was shifted to a tropical resort planet. Have fun pronouncing it

coveredGames.name: Muse Dash
coveredGames.title: Does violently jerking your muses up and down to whack enemies in time to music count as dashing? Debatable. I'll let the scholastics figure that one out.

coveredGames.name: Hyper Chess
coveredGames.title: This isn't fetish chess: it's realtime chess with no turns and a dancing anime girl.

coveredGames.name: The Police Mystery
coveredGames.title: It is no mystery why someone made a Lorn's Lure clone about tiny police officers climbing a giant policewoman, or why it has so many ways for your little dudes to get eaten.

coveredGames.name: Studio System : Guardian Angel Soundtrack
coveredGames.title: It is my duty as a non-vegetarian and a Steam Curator to share this video with you:

coveredGames.name: Guns and Nuns: Storming Hell
coveredGames.title: An anime nun re-enacts the Harrowing of Hell with firearms. It's less effective than the regular monastic life, and her outfit isn't accurate (sadly), but it's still a step in the right direction.

coveredGames.name: Rules & Rodents
coveredGames.title: Here he comes now, the Big Rat that makes all the rules. Whatever his rules touch turns to pawns in his clutch. He's too much. You're Mr. Mouse. Whatever you touch molds the rules of his clutch. 2much

coveredGames.name: BENBOWARS

coveredGames.name: Croc Legend of the Gobbos

coveredGames.name: Escape From Duckov
coveredGames.title: It's an overhead survival RPG built and named around ducks for a punny name to line Bilibili's pockets.

coveredGames.name: MOTORSLICE

coveredGames.name: Bubsy in: The Purrfect Collection
coveredGames.title: It's a collection of every Bubsy game up till Bubsy 3D. I hesitate to call this purrfect, but if it were dirt cheap you could treat it like the new Bad Rats and curse your friends' steam libraries.

coveredGames.name: HIROTONFA’s American Revolution Smuggler

coveredGames.name: The Leverage Game

coveredGames.name: NECRONOMICAT

coveredGames.title: Dead Space is both enjoyable and horrifying with both monsters and atmosphere. Good powers and combat to fight diverse enemies with limited resources creates a sense of dread.

coveredGames.name: BALL x PIT
coveredGames.title: Ball X Pit is a shmup where your projectiles bounce off the wall combine with a brick breaker that progresses forward. Engaging and interesting. Good game loop and time well spent. Random power-ups.

coveredGames.name: Super Meat Boy 3D
coveredGames.title: Super Meat Boy 3D is brutal platformer with brief levels. Great looking, no control of the camera. Lots of wall jumps, long jumps, and dives to get through. Very intense from start and doesn't let up.

coveredGames.name: Mortal Kombat 1
coveredGames.title: Mortal Kombat 1 is still the premier fighting game with a 6 hour story, introducing a new kameo system for bonus hits. Story is reset and retold again. Characters look like COSplayers in beautifulgame

coveredGames.name: Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors
coveredGames.title: Vampire Crawlers is surprisingly addictive and deep card game dungeon crawler. Upgrades and unlocks keep you going for the next play, even after a 20 minute failure. Dozens of foes per battle.

coveredGames.name: Aphelion
coveredGames.title: Aphelion is ledge climbing: the game, set on a frozen planet. Easy to play, doesn't require much effort, always one path forward. Great visuals, story is cringe when it focuses on the relationship.

coveredGames.name: Minishoot' Adventures
coveredGames.title: SHMUP Zelda is a great experience. Fluid, easy to play, great exploration, fresh ideas, engaging bosses, clean aesthetic in a 6 hour package. Not just for SHMUP fans.

coveredGames.name: Mixtape
coveredGames.title: Mixtape is 3 hour experience of a high production that incorporates movie magic into a simple story of 3 friends memories heading into a party. Sprinkled in with 20 silly mini games over 25 chapters.

coveredGames.name: A Game About Digging A Hole™
coveredGames.title: Digging a Hole is just that. Shovel energy depletes, you explode. Find ore, sell it, to buy upgrades for digging, energy, inventory, and jet pack to get out of hole. Looks good, yet a chore.

coveredGames.name: RAGE 2
coveredGames.title: Rage 2 is a modern Doom, open world FPS, but a vast departure from the original. 99% of combat is done outside in a drivable desert. Game is overly colorful, neon enemies, gangs don't feel different.

coveredGames.name: RAGE
coveredGames.title: Post apocalyptic, brown desert FPS that jumps to mediocre vehicle combat too often. Tough to get excited about the wasteland and sewers punctuated by a pair of settlements. Good FPS, with a lot of meh

coveredGames.name: Owyn's Adventure
coveredGames.title: Owyn's Adventure is a brief, basic platforming quest that holds the GameBoy aesthetic, but plays closer to a modern game. Find toy train cars, keys and reach doors. Still enjoyable.

coveredGames.name: The Myth of a Godslayer
coveredGames.title: Myth of the Godslayer is a great overhead adventure with good combat, good battles, quality puzzles, and RPG tweaks to make it your own. Art style really holds it back from being a star.

coveredGames.name: Mouthwashing
coveredGames.title: Mouthwashing is a very engaging and creepy horror game whose gameplay is akin to a walking simulator. Tough not to get through this atmospheric creepshow of 5 crew trapped in a small space freighter.

coveredGames.name: Gear.Club Unlimited 2 - Ultimate Edition
coveredGames.title: Gear.Club 2 is a paint-by-numbers, vanilla, easy, and yet fun racer. No frills, no nitros, or boosts. Just car upgrades and purchases. Its all a satisfying formula. Many races, lacks course diversity.

coveredGames.name: Bulb Boy
coveredGames.title: Bulb Boy is a blend of oddity, grotesque, and horror in a point & click game. It pits you as an infant in a house where grotesque is the norm. Gameplay is simple, hints available, mainstream avoided.

coveredGames.name: The Walking Dead: The Final Season
coveredGames.title: Final Season becomes a single teen mother simulator in a zombie apocalypse with a cast of troubled youth. One of the best in the series. Choices, more gameplay vs zombies, danger, and emotion.

coveredGames.name: The Walking Dead: A New Frontier
coveredGames.title: A New Frontier is a great story game that doesn't waste time with things like exploration. Make choices, build relationships, see how it plays out against zombies and mankind. Easy, breezy at 7 hours.

coveredGames.name: Scooby Doo! & Looney Tunes Cartoon Universe: Adventure
coveredGames.title: Cartoon Universe is a very bland, basic, and generic isometric maze with some platforming elements. Looney Tunes are in dialog scenes and you play as your own generic character outside dialog sections

coveredGames.name: Quarion
coveredGames.title: Quarion is a basic, fun, and engaging adventure through a world of challenging platforming. Boss fights help add spice to what is otherwise by the numbers, yet done so well.

coveredGames.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection
coveredGames.title: CastleVania: Dominus Collection is three big games from the DS with a unique remake of the original arcade game. These are top tier adventures that manage to keep the Vania fresh after years.

coveredGames.name: Asphalt Legends
coveredGames.title: Asphalt Legends is mobile's finest racing game. Arcade fun for the 1 minute that the races last. Very menu heavy. Beautiful, slick, jump, boost. Took 20 minutes before hitting the free game paywall.

coveredGames.name: The Plucky Squire
coveredGames.title: Plucky Squire is a fantasticly creative, fun, and easy overhead slasher that's full of charm and imagination. It takes place inside a colorful story book, until it broadens. Words to solve puzzles.

coveredGames.name: Wolfenstein: The Old Blood
coveredGames.title: Old Blood is still the great FPS the New Wolfenstein brought. Lots of grey, stealth, good weapons, and gameplay. Less story. Gets supernatural and mech piloting by the end. Highly enjoyable.

coveredGames.name: Downwell
coveredGames.title: Downwell is a quick, arcade-ish game that turns platformers and overhead shooters on their head. You shoot down, can hop on enemies in brief, generated levels. Good, quick action and thought process.

coveredGames.name: Princess Remedy in a World of Hurt
coveredGames.title: World of Hurt is a fresh blend of RPG overworld and shmup battles to cure patients in a game that consists of a single button. Enjoyable, easy enough, engaging, engrossing, and wrapped in basic art.

coveredGames.name: Wolfenstein: The New Order
coveredGames.title: Wolfenstein: The New Order is a fresh and alternate timeline FPS. Great, intense combat with stealth or big guns. Really enjoyable. Alternate history world is a shining point to stand out.

coveredGames.name: Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap
coveredGames.title: The Dragon's Trap is a great looking, beautiful side-scrolling adventure remake of the Master System game. Each part of the world has you play as a different creature with unique abilities.

coveredGames.name: Pikuniku
coveredGames.title: Pikuniku is a 2D bland scavenger hunt platformer in a quirky world. Movement is quirky. Dull, but chill. Scouring everywhere again and again with sparse offshoots of traditional platformer.

coveredGames.name: Restore Your Island
coveredGames.title: A few achievements are bugged or unobtainable. Check the discussions for more info.

coveredGames.name: Spellstone
coveredGames.title: The game has 4 Broken Achievements!

coveredGames.name: Blast Beam Bang
coveredGames.title: not bad at all for $7. it's no Vampire Survivors, but it does a fine job at offering a unique experience similar to VampS or Crimsonland. Recommended for enjoyers of Crimsonland for sure.

coveredGames.name: Skyformer
coveredGames.title: good stuff. i last played the game during EA but even at that time, the game was not half bad: https://youtube.com/live/ns9aJFbvnE4

coveredGames.name: Beyond the Map
coveredGames.title: has the potential to be very good with more development time: here's my full written review: https://steamcommunity.com/id/lfpg/recommended/2896380

coveredGames.name: Enshrouded
coveredGames.title: very good. here's my full written review: https://steamcommunity.com/id/lfpg/recommended/1203620

coveredGames.name: Desynced
coveredGames.title: very good. I need to play the game more now that the game has a 1.0 release, but with about 20hours in EA and 30hours+ on the 1.0 release, I can say the game is certainly worth the asking price.

coveredGames.name: Len's Island
coveredGames.title: Lacking in content, but not bad for €25... here's my full written review: https://steamcommunity.com/id/lfpg/recommended/1335830

coveredGames.name: Vapor World: Over The Mind
coveredGames.title: i did a short exposé showing all of the removed AI cutscenes https://youtu.be/ASbolyByjqE

coveredGames.name: DDoD
coveredGames.title: The world map is massive. Combat is satisfying. The zombie variety is nice (and zombies even do interesting things like dodge-rolling). Dismembering zombies is fun. But is misses some QoL features

coveredGames.name: Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon
coveredGames.title: Great. Not as great as Skyrim, but it's very close honestly. The only thing the devs can do to make the game better now is add more fantastic DLCs like Sarras, and add more content/spells/zones/etc.

coveredGames.name: Northwind
coveredGames.title: Very good right now, even during EA. The can only expand and improve the game in the future, and it'll be a banger. Watch my video review below and skip to the end if you want the summary.

coveredGames.name: Everwind
coveredGames.title: Fantastic. It's like if Minecraft and Forever Skies had a baby. I hope they fix the small handful of issues currently in EA, but honestly, it can only go up from here (pun intended)

coveredGames.name: Monster Crown: Sin Eater
coveredGames.title: Very good. This game does everything that the OG pokemon games did, and so much more. The fusion+breeding system is a revelation. Well worth the money.

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™
coveredGames.title: Fantastic racer that's playable on Steam Deck at 30 FPS with FSR Balanced, High textures/AA and the rest Low. Works offline. It's so fast though that it feels way better at 60 on stronger hardware.

coveredGames.name: BALL x PIT
coveredGames.title: A brick breaker crossed with a survivor roguelite crossed with a base builder, and somehow it works. Runs at max settings on the Steam Deck with no drops. Around 4:30 battery on OLED at a 90 FPS cap,

coveredGames.name: Mortal Shell II
coveredGames.title: Medium settings with Global Illumination and Post Processing on low gets you 30-45 FPS with FSR 4.1 Performance. Worth capping at 30 for consistency.

coveredGames.name: Lootbound
coveredGames.title: Turn based roguelite where the loot is your build, not just a reward. Full controller support, 656MB, plays offline and 7.5 hours on the OLED at 60 FPS. Staying installed on my Deck permanently.

coveredGames.name: Duskfade
coveredGames.title: Steam Deck preset with a 45 FPS cap is the way to play. Not locked, but a good experience and 2:45 battery on OLED. Settings are limited to preset, shadows and upscaler.

coveredGames.name: DragonSword : Awakening
coveredGames.title: Runs better than expected on Deck. 70-90fps on low, 40-60 on medium, dips in cities and big fights. Lossless Scaling gets you 90. Battery is 2.5h. Korean audio only, English subs. Recommended.

coveredGames.name: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
coveredGames.title: Runs at 35-45 FPS on Medium Preset. 2:30h Battery life on OLED. 1:30h on LCD. Absolutely earns the Verified Badge. This is a great experience on the Deck. Can be played fully offline!

coveredGames.name: Voidling Bound: Creature Evolution Shooter
coveredGames.title: Medium + 80% res scale = stable 45fps. No upscaling, res slider only. Aiming feels snappy for a shooter. Small evolution UI text isn't fixed by accessibility settings. Recommended.

coveredGames.name: Arms of God
coveredGames.title: Bullet heaven that runs well on Deck. Low + Low AA + 90% res scale = stable 60 most of the time. Drops hit during chaos, but that's the genre. Under €10. Recommended.

coveredGames.name: Solarpunk™
coveredGames.title: Cozy base builder that runs well on Deck. Full controller support, cloud saves, no anticheat issues. High settings at 45fps cap or medium at 60fps - both work. Recommended.

coveredGames.name: 007 First Light
coveredGames.title: 30fps cap, low/medium settings - runs great on Deck. ~2h45m battery, fully offline capable. I think it's an amazing experience on the Steam Deck!

coveredGames.name: Luna Abyss
coveredGames.title: Excellent first person bullet hell - Returnal meets Metroid. Runs well on Deck but add SteamDeck=0 %command% to unlock video settings. Medium + Lossless Scaling = 90fps at ~3hrs battery.

coveredGames.name: Deep Rock Galactic: Rogue Core
coveredGames.title: 45 FPS cap is your target. FSR 3 on, built-in frame gen off. Drops below 40 in heavy encounters even on low settings. Lossless Scaling for 60. Battery ~2h 30m. Game itself is a good time - solid Early

coveredGames.name: ZERO PARADES: Director's Cut
coveredGames.title: Runs well on Steam Deck. High preset throughout, 45 FPS cap recommended. 2h45m battery at 45FPS, 4h30m at 30FPS. Strong recommend if narrative RPGs are your thing.

coveredGames.name: Blades of Fire
coveredGames.title: Runs well on Steam Deck with some tweaking. Stable 45fps is achievable using frame gen for a smooth experience, or cap at 30fps if you need the extra battery life. Worth picking up. 2:45h battery life

coveredGames.name: The Lord of the Rings: Return to Moria™
coveredGames.title: Playable but inconsistent. Low preset with FSR Balanced gets you ~60fps early, but bigger spaces and combat drag it down hard. Limited settings mean no way to fight back. Better on PC.

coveredGames.name: Forza Horizon 6
coveredGames.title: Playable and enjoyable at 30fps with tuned settings, but city races drop below 30 even on Very Low. Use the Deck limiter over the in-game cap. Always-online, Xbox account required. 2:30h Battery Life

coveredGames.name: Directive 8020
coveredGames.title: Playable on Steam Deck. Lowest settings, shadows and textures on medium, TSR Balanced upscaling. Later sections dip below 30fps. Skip built-in frame gen. 2:30h battery life, great controller support!

coveredGames.name: Conan Exiles Enhanced
coveredGames.title: Free UE5 upgrade with merged maps. On Steam Deck OLED, lowest preset hits near 60 FPS with 2.5hr battery. Medium preset with some tweaks + LSFG for best results. Solid survival sandbox. Recommended.

coveredGames.name: Far Far West
coveredGames.title: Runs at almost stable 60 FPS on medium settings. If played with 4 players it can drop below that. Battery life is 2:30 hours, controls are good and aim assist helps. Pretty fun game on the Deck!

coveredGames.name: Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors
coveredGames.title: Runs great on Steam Deck OLED: locked 60 FPS with ~5h battery. Cap to 30 FPS for up to 6.5h. Excellent controller support and smooth gameplay. Easy pick for handheld sessions.

coveredGames.name: Tides of Tomorrow 🌊
coveredGames.title: Tides of Tomorrow locks down settings on Steam Deck and originally it struggled hitting 30 FPS. IT has since got patched and while it's still pretty locked down it now runs a lot better.

coveredGames.name: MOUSE: P.I. For Hire
coveredGames.title: Mouse: P.I. For Hire runs great on Steam Deck. Medium settings hit 60-85 FPS with some dips. Excellent controller options, strong battery life, and a fun, stylish FPS. I recommend it!

coveredGames.name: iRacing Arcade
coveredGames.title: Runs great on Steam Deck (up to 90 FPS). Arcade-style racer, not a sim, but fun and perfect for quick sessions. Best at Medium - 60 FPS with tweaks. Limited multiplayer, but solid handheld experience.

coveredGames.name: Soulmask
coveredGames.title: Runs at ~ 40 FPS with tweaks, 2:30 hours OLED battery, but poor UI, tiny text, and clunky controller support make it hard to enjoy on Steam Deck. Playable, but not well suited for handheld right now.

coveredGames.name: Monster Hunter: World
coveredGames.title: Runs well on Steam Deck. Low settings push high FPS but look rough without anti-aliasing. Medium with a 45 FPS cap offers the best balance. Stable performance, good battery life, and a lot of content!

coveredGames.name: Screamer
coveredGames.title: Runs well on Deck with tuning. 80-90 FPS possible on low but looks rough. Best experience is ~40 FPS + 2x lossless scaling for smooth 60. Medium settings drop to ~45 FPS.

coveredGames.name: Darwin's Paradox!
coveredGames.title: Unique octopus platformer with movement that actually works. The Steam Deck preset holds 30 FPS better than manual tweaks. Battery life: 2:30 hours! Pretty Great on the Deck!

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS Jedi: Survivor™
coveredGames.title: Runs around 30-40 FPS on Steam Deck at low settings with FSR, but can drop below that. “May the Performance Be With You” mod improves performance and can reach ~45 FPS. Battery life around 2:30 hours

coveredGames.name: Dying Light 2 Stay Human: Reloaded Edition
coveredGames.title: Runs well on Steam Deck OLED with a custom settings mix. Skip the built-in frame gen, it's broken. Use Lossless Scaling instead and you're looking at 60 FPS and 3.5 hours of battery life.

coveredGames.name: Filthium Zero
coveredGames.title: Addictive survivor-style roguelite with great movement and a unique Filthium extraction mechanic. Runs around 30-60 FPS on Steam Deck and works great for quick handheld runs.

coveredGames.name: Tom Clancy’s The Division™
coveredGames.title: Still one of the most atmospheric open worlds in gaming. Snowy New York feels incredible to explore and the Steam Deck handles the game surprisingly well at around 45 FPS!

coveredGames.name: Carmageddon: Rogue Shift
coveredGames.title: Classic Carmageddon chaos with roguelite progression. Steam Deck performance ranges from 60 FPS to around 30 FPS in heavy moments. Best experience: disable upscalers and use 80% resolution scale.

coveredGames.name: Slay the Spire 2
coveredGames.title: Runs perfectly on Steam Deck. Only 1.71GB, full controller support, and excellent battery life. Around 8 hours on OLED. Works offline or online, and multiplayer runs great!

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Requiem
coveredGames.title: Runs surprisingly well on Steam Deck. Low textures + FSR 3 Balanced + 40 FPS cap = stable combat and ~3h battery on OLED. Impressive scaling for a new RE title.

coveredGames.name: Insider Trading
coveredGames.title: A smart and highly addictive market-based deckbuilder. Deep card synergies, satisfying system mastery, and excellent performance on Steam Deck. 10 hours of battery life at 30 FPS! Easy Recommendation!

coveredGames.name: Touhou: Lost Branch of Legend

coveredGames.name: A Clockwork Ley-Line: Flowers Falling in the Morning Mist

coveredGames.name: Touhou Hero of Ice Fairy

coveredGames.name: Labyrinth of Refrain: Coven of Dusk

coveredGames.name: A Clockwork Ley-Line: Daybreak of Remnants Shadow

coveredGames.name: WitchSpring R
coveredGames.title: Equal parts melancholic and heartwarming, this unique JRPG with Princess Maker elements leans on grinding, but the story, characters, and strategic gameplay make this game worth your while.

coveredGames.name: Touhou Mystia's Izakaya

coveredGames.name: Rabi-Ribi
coveredGames.title: Cute metroidvania platformer starring a bunny girl and her friends. Explore a colorful world hiding a surprising depth of gameplay and story, with white-knuckle bullet-hell boss fights galore.

coveredGames.name: Astral Party
coveredGames.title: Astral Party is a cute anime-style party game, similar to Mario Party with a twist. It mixes board game chaos with card battles. Roll, fight, and scheme using unique abilities to outplay your friends.

coveredGames.name: Etrian Odyssey HD

coveredGames.name: Aokana - Four Rhythms Across the Blue
coveredGames.title: A heartfelt sports drama set in the skies. Lovable heroines, breathtaking art, and thrilling competition come together beautifully in this comfy VN. Sweet slice of life moments are the highlights.

coveredGames.name: Recettear: An Item Shop's Tale
coveredGames.title: A sweet and cozy game where you manage a fantasy world item shop to save your deadbeat dad from loan sharks. Great gameplay loop, plenty of side content, memorable characters, highly recommended.

coveredGames.name: ATRI -My Dear Moments-
coveredGames.title: A gorgeous sci-fi visual novel. Explores themes of impermanence and the long-lasting effect that fleeting moments have on a lifetime. Short, sweet, and touching.

coveredGames.name: BLACK SOULS II
coveredGames.title: The sequel and heart to Black Souls, this RPGMaker game expands on the original. Your search for Alice will lead deep in the rabbit hole, a Wonderland of horrors and depravity. I'm going to Alice.

coveredGames.name: Chrono Ark
coveredGames.title: Cute anime-style roguelike deckbuilder. Manage your team, deck synergies, and tactical turn-based combat through a story that unfolds across multiple time loops. Replayable and strategically deep.

coveredGames.name: Mary Skelter: Nightmares
coveredGames.title: Dungeon-crawling RPG with cute anime waifus, where you navigate twisted labyrinths and battle grotesque, nightmarish enemies. Recommended for fans of Etrian Odyssey-style games or DRPGs.

coveredGames.name: Dolls Nest
coveredGames.title: One part Dark Souls, one part Armored Core, combined with a subdued anime art style. Combat can feel clunky but an enjoyable experience overall.

coveredGames.name: Little Noah: Scion of Paradise

coveredGames.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

coveredGames.name: BLACK SOULS

coveredGames.name: The Song of Saya
coveredGames.title: A tragic, otherworldly love story with a beautifully haunting soundtrack. A short read packed with emotion that you won't soon forget.

coveredGames.name: Blue Archive
coveredGames.title: Adorably cute characters and charming stories. Bubbly visuals with impossible to resist gacha mechanics. A delight to play.

coveredGames.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless
coveredGames.title: Charming tactical RPG. Side quests, skill leveling, and strategy keep progression engaging. Vibrant anime style and upbeat soundtrack shine.

coveredGames.name: Disgaea 6 Complete
coveredGames.title: A whimsical tactical RPG. Over-the-top combat and skill upgrades make every fight fun. Colorful anime art and cheerful music delight. Performance is solid.

coveredGames.name: Disgaea 5 Complete
coveredGames.title: Playful and tactical RPG. Turn-based battles, side quests, and skill customization keep it fresh. Bright anime visuals and catchy music. Smooth and fun.

coveredGames.name: Disgaea 4 Complete+
coveredGames.title: Adorably cute and tactical turn-based RPG. Vibrant anime art with endearing, fun characters. Zany story. Catchy soundtrack. Seriously funny.

coveredGames.name: Escape from Tarkov
coveredGames.title: A great game, but has a lot of QOL features missing and lots of bugs. Sure can be fun with friends, though. Especially the PVE mode. Highly enjoyable despite the issues. Don't expect any hand holding.

coveredGames.name: ZEPHON
coveredGames.title: A well made 4x strategy game that is great for a slow paced and enjoyable experience. Graphics, sounds, lore, and gameplay are all very good and it keeps getting updates and patches!

coveredGames.name: Jump Space

coveredGames.name: Whisper Mountain Outbreak

coveredGames.name: Desktop Defender
coveredGames.title: Actually quite entertaining to have going in the background while working. Grabbed this to support a fellow indie dev and keep me sane while working on my own game projects on Steam.

coveredGames.name: Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition
coveredGames.title: An excellent upgrade over the original.

coveredGames.name: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2
coveredGames.title: A good, fast-paced coop game to play with friends. Lots of customization options. Great graphics. Smooth gameplay. Enjoyable combat.

coveredGames.name: System Shock
coveredGames.title: An extremely well made remaster. Great game with a ton to do and explore. Absolutely outstanding. Using this as inspiration for my game, Chaos Chain.

coveredGames.name: Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon
coveredGames.title: Excellent roleplaying game. Honestly, this gives Oblivion, Skyrim, and the other major open world RPGs a run for their money.

coveredGames.name: Put Back Stuff
coveredGames.title: Just fun to sort out all the chaos! Huge bonus being this is set in beautiful Australia, maybe even Victoria specifically? Love to see it

coveredGames.name: Tidy Up the Flower Shop
coveredGames.title: This was really cute and charming, and if you love sorting out chaos you'll love this!

coveredGames.name: Adorable Adventures
coveredGames.title: Stoooop, these lil piggies are too cute!!! OMG! Just a fun adventure and it's enjoyable to track down all the unique smells in the world

coveredGames.name: TOEM 2
coveredGames.title: I've been waiting ages for TOEM 2 and it's been worth the wait! Just as charming as TOEM, just as cute, just as fun. I loved finding all of the outfits and the costume references were so fun!

coveredGames.name: Dressmaker
coveredGames.title: I loooove dress up games, and it's a woefully underserved genre of game. Dressmaker delivers on a great gameplay loop, endless options to design, and beautifully drawn characters. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Woodo
coveredGames.title: I played the demo and loved this, but getting to experience the entire game was so rewarding! Absolutely adorable and fun to build these cute dioramas.

coveredGames.name: Cat Me If You Can

coveredGames.name: Gamble With Your Friends
coveredGames.title: Just good ole fun for the whole family! (gamble responsibly friendos)

coveredGames.name: Wax Heads

coveredGames.name: ReStory: Chill Electronics Repairs
coveredGames.title: So much fun to figure out how these gadgets come apart! Relaxing and chill, easy to lose a few hours in!

coveredGames.name: The Sorting Bureau

coveredGames.name: Infinity Nikki
coveredGames.title: If you ignore the microtransactions around every corner, this is another fun entry in the Nikki series. It's a blast exploring and the outfits are so pretty. Genuinely a pretty fun time!

coveredGames.name: The Mermaid Mask
coveredGames.title: Ahh it's so good to be back with Detective Grimoire. Another wonderfully fun narrative mystery with challenging puzzles sprinkled throughout. And the characters--oh my goodness, they are beautiful!!

coveredGames.name: Big Walk
coveredGames.title: Fun puzzles, lots of space to wander around, and you get to be a cute lil ant. Perfection

coveredGames.name: Camper Van: Make it Home

coveredGames.name: Cats in Pixels by Louisselle

coveredGames.name: Wormies

coveredGames.name: The Looker

coveredGames.name: Glimvale : My Mini Overworld

coveredGames.name: Trinket Bag Maker

coveredGames.name: Hidden Dogs

coveredGames.name: Cats & Pandas

coveredGames.name: I Eat Paintings When Guards Aren't Looking
coveredGames.title: YES. YES WE DO EAT PAINTINGS AND NO YOU CANNOT SHAME US

coveredGames.name: Esoteric Ebb
