coveredGames.title: Smesh

coveredGames.name: METAL EDEN
coveredGames.title: Smesh!

coveredGames.name: Deep Rock Galactic: Rogue Core
coveredGames.title: Smesh

coveredGames.name: Cronos: The New Dawn
coveredGames.title: When you see your opponent wants to fight .. you fight. I want to fight right now

coveredGames.name: ILL
coveredGames.title: SMESH!

coveredGames.name: Nate Hand Gesture
coveredGames.title: Demo review. This is a neat demo. Excellent use of the medium and the monster lady is really cute. I don't know if I was getting lucky or what, but using real RPS psychology got me a lot of wins.

coveredGames.name: Rain98
coveredGames.title: Demo review. Nice vibes, but narratively, it's not gripping me and I'm not really into the whole "everything sucks" doomer schtick. Might be your cup of tea, can't really say it's looking like mine.

coveredGames.name: Laica
coveredGames.title: I've seen a lot of people comparing this to Saya no Uta. Those people don't know what the ♥♥♥♥ they're talking about and should never share their opinions about games ever again. This looks neat tho.

coveredGames.name: Magic: The Gathering Arena
coveredGames.title: Couldn't get into Magic until the Commander boom hit, then it clicked. Brawl is as close as it gets to Commander on Arena. Personally, I'd use other tools to play Magic online, but this is fine too.

coveredGames.name: Aestheta
coveredGames.title: I don't play Clash Royale, but my buddy that does claims it's damn near 1:1 when it comes to unit archetypes. Personally, this isn't my cup of tea for gameplay. I do enjoy the art direction, though.

coveredGames.name: KOTAMON: My Sis Found A Super-Rare Card In Her Cereal Box, So I Became A Garbage Man To Find The Entire Collection And Earn $1,000,000
coveredGames.title: If this looks familiar, this is indeed a reskin of "My Wife Threw Out My Card Collection". I would play more chore simulators if more of them had this kind of art direction. Excellent fanservice.

coveredGames.name: Family Time
coveredGames.title: Sgthale's on a bit of a roll, this looks like it'll be even better than his last game, MyRobot. I stand by his work and I think this will be his big break. ♥♥♥♥ anti-natalists, families are awesome.

coveredGames.name: Happy Wheels
coveredGames.title: This is a Flash-era classic and I'm glad to see it come to Steam, even if I think it should have happened much sooner. A relic of a better, freer, less enshittified internet. ♥♥♥♥, I'm feeling old.

coveredGames.name: Class of '09: Puzzle Showdown
coveredGames.title: This is as good as any of the other Class of '09 sequels in terms of charm and character appeal. The puzzle gameplay is a bit flawed, but it's fun enough when you get a flow going. Over-hated as hell.

coveredGames.name: Class of '09: The Flip Side
coveredGames.title: This one is almost as good as the first two. The only reason it's a weaker entry is because of how limited its scope is. It's the same old Class of '09. Like Re-Up, this should have been an expansion.

coveredGames.name: Class of '09: The Re-Up
coveredGames.title: If you liked the original Class of '09, this is more of that. It's much more limited in scope and probably would have been better as an expansion rather than a standalone, but it's great nonetheless.

coveredGames.name: Class of '09
coveredGames.title: Remember when cartoon sitcoms were actually funny? This is a lot like that. I would prefer if it had a few more features that were standard to VNs, like backlogs and auto-advance toggle. It's good.

coveredGames.name: Girlfailure Art Club
coveredGames.title: I don't think that's what it's called in the original Japanese, but this looks neat. These are great character designs and everyone else should be taking notes. Why can't we romance the mob-faced one?

coveredGames.name: Endacopia
coveredGames.title: So far, a great point-and-click adventure game. The visuals are neat, the horror elements are effective, the puzzles are fun. Everything is as it ought to be. Captivating.

coveredGames.name: Swords & Slippers
coveredGames.title: A flashy character action game seeking to bring back fanservice. They told the woke puritards to kick rocks, so I'm obliged to support these devs in their noble pursuit. Looks like fun, should be good

coveredGames.name: Duskfade
coveredGames.title: I played the demo. This is undoubtedly inspired by Kingdom Hearts and seems to want to be like it in terms of gameplay. I think that it falls quite a bit short. Maybe next time they'll get it right.

coveredGames.name: Viva
coveredGames.title: I'm old enough to remember when this was called Shinobu Project. I also remember the gameplay being smoother and less janky in clips I had seen of it. Sgthale went on to make MyRobot, which isn't bad.

coveredGames.name: Snowbreak: Containment Zone
coveredGames.title: Their noble attempt to go all in on waifus was ultimately thwarted by the CCP. I'll admit, I didn't much care for this game, but they didn't deserve to go out like this. Hopefully they break free.

coveredGames.name: The Song of Saya
coveredGames.title: Played the Director's Cut on GOG. Everything about this VN sickens and disturbs me and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. By that, I mean that this is an exemplary horror title. Actually psychological

coveredGames.name: Muse Dash 2
coveredGames.title: If this doesn't have the a pass that gets you all current and future DLC like the first game, this is gonna be a big flop. Rhythm games live and die by their monetization. Looks snazzy though.

coveredGames.name: MECCHA CHAMELEON
coveredGames.title: Lives up to the hype. If you're into prop hunt styled gamemodes, you'll love this. I'm not a fan of the Unreal lighting and antialiasing that leaves ghosting artifacts, but the game runs well.

coveredGames.name: Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair
coveredGames.title: The minigames are much more refined this time around, but it's still not as good of an adventure game as the worst Ace Attorney games. The mysteries are much better this time around too, less obvious.

coveredGames.name: Persona 6
coveredGames.title: Get ready for a new generation of LARP. So many tourists are gonna latch onto this like ticks and you won't hear the end of it for at least ten years.

coveredGames.name: Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc
coveredGames.title: Ace Attorney, but mechanically ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Just let me cross-examine the debates like Ace Attorney and delete the tempo tap ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and it'd be SO much better. I still enjoy it, though.

coveredGames.name: AION 2
coveredGames.title: So far, I'm having a good time. If you're into Black Desert or PSO2, you might enjoy this more than if you're a fan of FFXIV or WoW. Character creation is great, game looks great, doesn't feel too bad

coveredGames.name: Battle Queen
coveredGames.title: Upcoming fighting game with rollback netcode from a Korean solo dev. They're all in on fanservice and sex appeal. I've followed the development for a long time. I think it'll be pretty good.

coveredGames.name: DRAGON BALL XENOVERSE 3
coveredGames.title: So, now that Toriyama's dead, we're just not doing the whole themed name thing anymore? Why do the original characters have 4kids-ass Woolseyist names? Hopefully the game is alright.

coveredGames.name: ENA: Dream BBQ
coveredGames.title: A playable installment in Joel G's ENA series. The bulk of the gameplay involves wandering around surreal zones that are something between edutainment shareware and fever dreams. Great if you love ENA

coveredGames.name: Yume Nikki
coveredGames.title: One of your favorite indie cult classic's favorite indie cult classics. Yume Nikki is a game about exploring a surreal dreamscape that tells a story through abstract visual metaphors. Inimitable.

coveredGames.name: Bejeweled 2 Deluxe
coveredGames.title: A very nostalgic title for me and it's exactly how I remember it. It's nothing more than just a match-three puzzle game. The backdrop renders are showing their age, but that ♥♥♥♥ still goes hard.

coveredGames.name: Dead Island 2
coveredGames.title: STEEP discount only, wait till it's 5 USD. A sequel to Dead Island in name only, clearly the old team is gone. Poorly written, but still kinda fun. Would be insufferable solo, play with a friend.

coveredGames.name: Demon Street
coveredGames.title: I have no interest in reviewing VR titles at this time. Looks cool though.

coveredGames.name: BRAVELY DEFAULT FLYING FAIRY HD Remaster
coveredGames.title: I can only speak for my experience with the original 3DS release, but the Bravely Default I played was great. Doesn't reinvent the wheel, but it's really solid. Incredible music and art direction.

coveredGames.name: Pickmos
coveredGames.title: I sincerely thought this was a Palworld rebrand or something. This looks so damn sloppy, but I would be lying if I said I wasn't interested in seeing how this plays out, if at all. Likely Chinese.

coveredGames.name: MyRobot
coveredGames.title: I'm a backer for this game and the playtest is pretty neat. I think the game's a bit clunky, but there's something here that could be special. Not sure the AI adds too much here.

coveredGames.name: DNF Duel
coveredGames.title: This is one of the more slept-on ArcSys titles. DFO is already niche and making it a FG didn't help. It's good though. It's definitely a post-Strive game, but it's a really accessible title. Stylish.

coveredGames.name: OMORI
coveredGames.title: Mogs the ♥♥♥♥ out of all other Earthbound derivative slop. It's sincere and surprisingly unpretentious. Despite being simple and mostly traditional, the turn-based combat is very fun. This is lovely.

coveredGames.name: Iron Lung
coveredGames.title: Fascinating game, very mysterious. I haven't seen Markiplier's movie based on it yet, but I have heard only good things.

coveredGames.name: BOOST VECTOR EX
coveredGames.title: Formerly a ROBLOX game. The demo is nice, very stylish. I'm looking forward to seeing where this goes.

coveredGames.name: Horripilant
coveredGames.title: I used an autoclicker in the demo, getting a gut feeling that this is the type of game to jumpscare you and crash the game for doing that. My instincts were right on. Neat game though.

coveredGames.name: Arithmetic Arena
coveredGames.title: ELO ranking and an immersive lobby with detailed characters make it addictive, but a steep high-tier curve, decimal-only answers, and repetitive presentation limit variety.

coveredGames.name: Incremental RTS
coveredGames.title: A fun incremental auto battler with a deep upgrade tree and automated macro RTS commands, but the campaign is too short, late-game clicking feels tedious, and QoL automation is missing.

coveredGames.name: Lucky Scoop
coveredGames.title: A cozy, cute, and entertaining experience that is fun at first, but missing colors break orders and limited item variety and stock make the repetitive, soulless gameplay wear thin.

coveredGames.name: Fleshborn
coveredGames.title: An interesting story and fun incremental roguelite make this short experience satisfying, but repetitive grinding, forced death-loop progression, and low replayability leave it feeling too brief.

coveredGames.name: Fish It!: Sort the Aquarium Shop
coveredGames.title: A charming, relaxing aquarium sim with varied fish, engaging movement, and quality music, though its repetitive loop and abilities lacking synergy limit long-term appeal.

coveredGames.name: Arctic Drive
coveredGames.title: The Arctic survival setting and fun solo gameplay shine, but persistent bugs, glitches, stuttering, and repetitive design hold it back.

coveredGames.name: Cucumber
coveredGames.title: An addictive, meditative cucumber-themed jumper with impressive visuals and humor, though AI-generated content claims and murky upgrade progression frustrate.

coveredGames.name: Pixel Gun 2
coveredGames.title: Visually pleasing with fun destructible environments and a fair free-to-play option, but aggressive pay-to-win monetization, generic gameplay, and poor weapon balance and hit detection hold it back.

coveredGames.name: Reshine
coveredGames.title: A relaxing, calming restoration game with stunning visuals and intuitive controls, though its short length, thin content, and fiddly painting and color customization hold it back.

coveredGames.name: Traymon World: Taskbar Monster RPG
coveredGames.title: Responsive devs and cute pixel art make this idle fun, but weak anti-cheat, marketplace pay-to-win issues, and severe server lag and stuttering hold it back.

coveredGames.name: Pinata Smash: Incremental Circus
coveredGames.title: A fun, visually stylish core with satisfying upgrades is undermined by grindy, repetitive gameplay and a forced coin-flip progression system.

coveredGames.name: Net Worthless
coveredGames.title: An engaging life sim with good humor and references, but it lacks depth and content, grows repetitive late on, and costs too much for what it offers.

coveredGames.name: KICKSLAUGHT: Football Idle
coveredGames.title: Charming retro pixel art and a satisfying idle progression loop make this self-playing game relaxing, but minimal interaction, no real difficulty or meaning, and slow pacing leave it shallow.

coveredGames.name: My Dirty Little Lake
coveredGames.title: A cozy, relaxing pixel-art game with enjoyable music, but it is too short, repetitive, and lacks enough content to justify the price.

coveredGames.name: When Chests Rain Tons of Loot
coveredGames.title: Addictive, fun gameplay with satisfying progression and appealing pixel art, but it's short on content, the survival mode is poorly designed, and the AI-generated writing is obvious.

coveredGames.name: Rekindled: Cozy Tavern Life
coveredGames.title: A cozy, relaxing cooking game with creative plating and rewarding gathering, but its empty unfinished world, unpolished movement, and ineffective helper AI drag it down.

coveredGames.name: One Last Cast
coveredGames.title: Charming pixel art, relaxing idle fishing, and a rich fish collection are undermined by material shortages that block progression, weak idle mechanics, and shallow upgrades.

coveredGames.name: A Thousand Cloys
coveredGames.title: Exploration-driven progression and a satisfying loop make this funny corporate satire a top incremental, but repetitive grinding, slow pacing, and late-game performance issues hold it back.

coveredGames.name: HelloLove2:Binary
coveredGames.title: Excellent cast performances and a novel AI-companion hook enliven this Hello-series FMV sequel, but cheap-looking AI visuals and a short, content-light runtime undercut it.

coveredGames.name: BORE
coveredGames.title: Fun co-op tension horror with strong atmosphere and sound, but frequent bugs, poor guidance that leaves players lost, and soulless AI-generated assets hold it back.

coveredGames.name: Business Simulator
coveredGames.title: Fun, addictive gameplay and promising ideas are undermined by frequent severe bugs, persistent technical issues, and an unfinished, unpolished experience.

coveredGames.name: Chinese-Style Exams
coveredGames.title: A nostalgic trip through varied subjects and detailed exam papers, though repetitive grinding, steep difficulty spikes in later grades, and a grading-screen freeze can frustrate.

coveredGames.name: Mirklurk: Every Step Matters
coveredGames.title: Its enjoyable survival loop and innovative grid-based health system stand out, but poor UI and controls, excessive micromanagement, and a weak tutorial make the learning curve frustrating.

coveredGames.name: Kaetram
coveredGames.title: Fun gameplay and a welcoming community backed by responsive developers are undermined by bugs, clunky UI, and server lag that causes high ping.

coveredGames.name: Double Whammy
coveredGames.title: A fun guitar shop simulator with extensive modding and real guitar connectivity, though it's limited to standard guitars, lacks tablature and functionality, and suffers from input latency.

coveredGames.name: Astario
coveredGames.title: A promising space sim with impressive scope, atmosphere, and Newtonian orbital mechanics, but an incomplete tutorial, janky unfinished feel, and awkward, unscalable UI hold it back.

coveredGames.name: NebulArena
coveredGames.title: Engaging, strategic buildcrafting and an addictive autobattler loop pair with polished pixel art, but severe balance issues, missing tutorials, and frequent bugs and lag hold it back.

coveredGames.name: On The Train
coveredGames.title: Its unique train-survival concept and responsive devs make co-op fun with friends, but buggy overpowered zombies, frequent instability and thin progression hold it back.

coveredGames.name: Nullnest
coveredGames.title: An addictive and satisfying power-fantasy loop with great pixel art, though poor build diversity, monotonous repetition, and an unreasonably difficult late game hold it back.

coveredGames.name: PC Store Together
coveredGames.title: An addictive co-op PC-building and repair loop with satisfying shop management depth is engaging, though performance and optimization issues plus bugs and crashes can mar the experience.

coveredGames.name: DecoGear Dimensions
coveredGames.title: Excellent enemy and boss design, top-tier beat 'em up mechanics, and outstanding practice tools are undermined by steep frontloaded difficulty, enemies ignoring attacks, and sluggish movement.

coveredGames.name: Terminus: Day Zero
coveredGames.title: An intense apocalyptic atmosphere, appealing child protagonist, and worthwhile free demo are undermined by an unfinished, short experience with clunky controls and inconsistent, exploitable zombie AI.

coveredGames.name: Internet Cafe 98
coveredGames.title: A fun, relaxing, well-crafted idle game with engaging mini-games, but slow research, poor balance and pacing make it boring over time.

coveredGames.name: No Asteroids
coveredGames.title: Fun, addictive asteroid mining and destruction keep the progression loop engaging, but late-game bottlenecks, bugs, and an unbalanced economy soon get in the way.

coveredGames.name: C.L.T.
coveredGames.title: A nostalgic GTA-style open world with smooth, engaging freedom and a strong Brazilian identity, though poor optimization, FPS drops, and an unfinished, unpolished feel hold it back.

coveredGames.name: Sintopia
coveredGames.title: Sintopia offers great vibes, solid humor, and a cool concept. Mistakes are heavily punished, but if you enjoy a challenging management sim, you’ll love the atmosphere. It's a fun management game.

coveredGames.name: Coridden
coveredGames.title: Despite weak narrative and dull writing,, Coridden brings fresh energy with its unique creature-transformation mechanics, satisfying progression, and rich skill customization options.

coveredGames.name: BARDA: Backpack Roguelike
coveredGames.title: Loved the unique concept and gorgeous art! Understanding the mechanics at the start was tricky, but it's a solid roguelike overall. Really cool experience once you get past the visual curve.

coveredGames.name: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
coveredGames.title: With its dark and fascinating artistic direction, Clair Obscur won me over with its captivating storyline and a well-executed hybrid gameplay that blends turn-based and real-time elements. A real gem!

coveredGames.name: IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator
coveredGames.title: It's a totally immersive experience—the dark atmosphere is incredible, and the turret simulation is truly gripping. It's intense, realistic, and very satisfying to play. A great experience!

coveredGames.name: PRIM
coveredGames.title: With its neat hand-drawn art and dark humor, PRIM captures the essence of Monkey Island and Maniac Mansion. A great Point & Click homage. A total success. Don't miss it!

coveredGames.name: Tavern Master
coveredGames.title: Loved the relaxing and cozy atmosphere of Tavern Master. Customizing the layout and adding decorations is super addictive. It's the ultimate chill cozy game to play after a long day.

coveredGames.name: The Planet Crafter
coveredGames.title: I really love this! It's such a pleasure to watch the world evolve over time. Between the cozy vibes, the beautiful artwork and how addictive collecting resources is, it's impossible to stop playing.

coveredGames.name: Worms Armageddon
coveredGames.title: Worms Armageddon is an absolute gem. It's a wildly addictive and hilarious game that I spent countless hours playing when I was younger. It's pure nostalgia—a timeless masterpiece!

coveredGames.name: DEATH STRANDING DIRECTOR'S CUT
coveredGames.title: A contemplative masterpiece. The hypnotic atmosphere builds on a sublime art direction and a brilliant soundtrack. Exploration feels visceral, led by a top-tier Hollywood cast.

coveredGames.name: King of Dragon Pass
coveredGames.title: Combines management with a exciting story, reminding me of one of my favorite “Choose-your-own-adventure” books. It's a real nostalgic treasure, but it's a shame it hasn't been translated into French.

coveredGames.name: Escape From Mystwood Mansion
coveredGames.title: Escape From Mystwood Mansion offers an accessible and decent puzzle experience. The puzzles are simple, and the atmosphere does the trick, but the game as a whole lacks originality. A decent game.

coveredGames.name: Martha Is Dead
coveredGames.title: A nice drama. Martha Is Dead is a true atmospheric masterpiece. Visually beautiful and with a captivating story, the game immerses you in a disturbing and unforgettable atmosphere. A great experience!

coveredGames.name: MIO: Memories in Orbit
coveredGames.title: A wonderful Metroidvania! The hand-drawn art style and the atmosphere of the spaceship are incredible. A true visual masterpiece, a real treat for the eyes.

coveredGames.name: Samorost 2
coveredGames.title: Samorost 2 remains a timeless masterpiece of the genre. Its enchanting art style, magical soundtrack, and intuitive puzzles make this short cosmic rescue mission a pure delight for gamers.

coveredGames.name: 嗜血印 Bloody Spell
coveredGames.title: Not a bad game, but Bloody Spell isn't anything special. It quickly feels too easy, but makes up for it with pretty cool, polished graphics. Perfect if you're looking for a casual action-RPG.

coveredGames.name: SteamWorld Build
coveredGames.title: An clever fusion of city management and mining exploration. Steamworld Build is a highly accessible and enjoyable game, though fans of the genre will likely find it lacks a serious strategic challenge

coveredGames.name: Mewgenics
coveredGames.title: An addictive gem! With its dark humour, deep strategic mechanics, and massive replay value, you’ll never want to put it down. A must-have for fans of unique challenges and genetically modified cats :)

coveredGames.name: Neo Cab
coveredGames.title: Neo Cab charms me with its intimate cyberpunk atmosphere. With clever dialogue, the game catch me with its diverse and complex cast of passengers. A touching and memorable overnight journey.

coveredGames.name: Kill The Crows
coveredGames.title: A great “Die & Retry” game based on instant-death mechanic—one hit and you're out. Very addictive; there's no break between sessions—you start over right away. Perfect for those with quick reflexes.

coveredGames.name: Horizon Forbidden West™ Complete Edition
coveredGames.title: A truly beautiful sequel, even if the charm of discovering the first game remains unmatched. A brilliant exploration of a sumptuous world and gameplay that’s more satisfying than in Zero Dawn.

coveredGames.name: Herdling
coveredGames.title: A wonderful escape game, Herdling tells a touching story without a single word. Its heart lies in the affection for the herd. A majestic soundtrack enhances this short, sweet and unforgettable journey

coveredGames.name: Eyes Of The ElderWood
coveredGames.title: "A retro early 2000s style folk horror adventure rooted in Kashubian myths. Dual wield a revolver and hand drawn magic against demons while managing your sanity in eerie forests and forgotten villages

coveredGames.name: Caput Mortum
coveredGames.title: "A tense first-person horror dungeon crawler with retro King's Field controls and survival horror dread. Descend a macabre alchemist's tower, solve eldritch puzzles, and watch your scarce healing item

coveredGames.name: Peripeteia
coveredGames.title: "A gritty cyberpunk immersive sim in post-Soviet Poland with classic Deus Ex DNA. Explore massive open levels with no quest markers, manage physical ammo, and solve problems your way in a bleak world.

coveredGames.name: Bonehold
coveredGames.title: "A 3D roguelike dungeon crawler with ARPG and hack and slash elements, blending pixel art textures with hand painted style. Pick from 10 classes, hunt procedural loot, and conquer an ancient fortress.

coveredGames.name: FlyKnight Enhanced Edition
coveredGames.title: "A retro first person dungeon crawler with pure King's Field DNA, tactical limb chopping combat, and up to 4 player co-op. Explore hand crafted dungeons, fish for buffs, and earn your knighthood!"

coveredGames.name: ELDERBORN
coveredGames.title: "A heavy metal first-person slasher that blends Dark Messiah melee combat with Souls-like progression. Explore a dark, hand-crafted fantasy city of doom in this brutal, retro-inspired action RPG."

coveredGames.name: SKINFACE
coveredGames.title: A grim, nightmarish horror thriller set in brutalist Soviet era with dark stealth and Hitman like infiltration. Piece together gruesome face disguises to fool targets in a twisted nightmare.

coveredGames.name: The King's Surveyor
coveredGames.title: A solo-dev retro first-person dungeon crawler with pure King's Field and Shadow Tower DNA. Explore a dark forgotten valley with no XP bar, managing your torchlight and mapping secrets by hand.

coveredGames.name: Goldenheart
coveredGames.title: Goldenheart brings classic old-school action RPG vibes with no map or quest log to hold your hand. Explore a surreal, lore-rich world with real-time tactical combat and environmental puzzles.

coveredGames.name: Dungeons & Darkness
coveredGames.title: Dungeons & Darkness is a poorly optimized game, a bit of a mess, but still very charming and has a lot of KF inspiration - AfroRyan

coveredGames.name: SHA BEAST DRESSAGE
coveredGames.title: A bizarre and dark occult fusion of horse simulation and retro dungeon crawler. Escape a cycle of reincarnation by training deadly beasts for a murderous dressage competition.

coveredGames.name: Ex Libris
coveredGames.title: Ex Libris becomes the third Sword of Moonlight game to release on Steam, and the first SoM game of 2026!!! - @verditecat

coveredGames.name: Crimson Rest
coveredGames.title: This retro-style dungeon crawler has elements of King's Field and Elder Scrolls 2 with how one travels and the combat looks.

coveredGames.name: Dungeons of Blood and Dream
coveredGames.title: Another Indi Kings's like game with a retro look and feel with quality of life mechanics . Play as a a blood Wizard trying to escape a death loop.

coveredGames.name: Queen's Domain
coveredGames.title: This game looks to be a fusion both Fromsofts both games the King's Field game and Dark souls with the atmosphere, mechanics and even the world itself. the game is coming soon but looks promising.

coveredGames.name: Necrofane
coveredGames.title: The game itself is still in early access but looks simple to play with a simple story. Now the simplicity doesn't take it away as Most king's field games are like that and its your job to explore.

coveredGames.name: Witchfire
coveredGames.title: While i would call this FPS a King's scroll game due to many of its similarities it has its own unique feel and game play mixing magic and gun play. An interesting game in a interesting world.

coveredGames.name: Darkblade Ascent
coveredGames.title: Roguelike RPG King's Scroll like game which looks like a high impact, high action indi-game. from available material this game looks simple yet tactical a interest product for all kinds of players.

coveredGames.name: Dreamspring
coveredGames.title: Dreamspring Is a King's Scrolls like game in a dark fantasy in a dying kingdom. despite its simple UI and low-poly graphics its ambitious game. Give this Indi-game a try.

coveredGames.name: TANUKI: Pon's Summer
coveredGames.title: This game knows exactly what it wants to be and who it wants to be a game made for, and you can imagine how much the developers were smiling [...] [A] treat for the eyes, ears and your paws [...]

coveredGames.name: Warota: I Live Next to The Demon King's Castle LOL
coveredGames.title: Warota: I Live Next to The Demon King’s Castle LOL is a lot of fun, but it’s difficult to outright recommend in its current state. Poor balance, iffy localization, and little content for the price.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE
coveredGames.title: The long-awaited HD-2D Final Fantasy game absolutely delivered.

coveredGames.name: Monkeys!¡
coveredGames.title: With a crossdressing delinquent protagonist, absurd comedy, and sometimes serious themes, it stands out for more than its eye-catching visual style.

coveredGames.name: ANOMALITH
coveredGames.title: A fine, albeit predictable, experience for fans of liminal horror and anime.

coveredGames.name: TORAWASE: The Girl in the Mirror
coveredGames.title: TORAWASE: The Girl in the Mirror is a nukige that uses the genderbender concept to deliver a uniquely exciting experience for readers of the genre.

coveredGames.name: Muchi Muchi Pork! & PinkSweets Boosted
coveredGames.title: Muchi Muchi Pork! & Pink Sweets Boosted is very much a niche package aimed at hardcore Danmaku fans who want access to as many CAVE titles as possible.

coveredGames.name: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered
coveredGames.title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is an excellent budget title for fans of Godzilla, both new and old.

coveredGames.name: Psycho-Sleuth
coveredGames.title: Underneath its weak spots and the sense of pastiche with its inspirations lies a clear passion and love for this genre.

coveredGames.name: Azure Striker Gunvolt Trilogy Enhanced
coveredGames.title: A stunning suite of great games brought to their definitive forms

coveredGames.name: Village in the Shade
coveredGames.title: Village in the Shade delivers a far more in-depth and engaging narrative than most would expect from a farming simulator.

coveredGames.name: Forever Ago
coveredGames.title: A journey well worth taking

coveredGames.name: Stupid Never Dies
coveredGames.title: tupid Never Dies reminds me strongly of a late-PS2 era AA title or mid-360 era titles like Neverdead or Splatterhouse. It has a strong heart, but it is just missing a few things

coveredGames.name: Silver Pines
coveredGames.title: Silver Pines is an excellent addition to the horror genre and a great choice for Halloween 2026

coveredGames.name: Alien Breed 35th Anniversary Collection
coveredGames.title: With some great additions and a few baffling omissions, I can ultimately recommend Alien Breed 35th Anniversary Collection for retro enthusiasts.

coveredGames.name: CONTROL Resonant
coveredGames.title: Control Resonant is an exceptional reminder that Remedy are the masters of their craft.

coveredGames.name: Triple Pairing
coveredGames.title: Triple Pairing doesn’t really lean into its love triangle theme as much as you might expect from the premise, but it’s still a good time

coveredGames.name: SiN Reloaded
coveredGames.title: If you’re a long-time follower of SiNTEK or just a curious bystander caught up in the war on drugs and corporate conspiracy, SiN Reloaded is the best way to experience this underdog collection

coveredGames.name: BIRDCAGE
coveredGames.title: From the moment I started Birdcage, I knew there was something special about it.

coveredGames.name: Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko's Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD-
coveredGames.title: I would not say that this is essential for anyone other than diehards, but I definitely had fun experiencing the ups and downs, the trials and errors, and the great sense of victory

coveredGames.name: Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter
coveredGames.title: Like 1st Chapter, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a remake made by a team that clearly shows love and reverence for the original game, and genuinely enjoyed making it.

coveredGames.name: Onimusha: Way of the Sword
coveredGames.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword is a home run for Capcom.

coveredGames.name: COCORO
coveredGames.title: Cocoro the robot girl is plenty lovable, but I found the COCORO the visual novel unambitious and overly sentimental

coveredGames.name: HimaNatsu: Of Churches, Sunflowers, and Long Summers
coveredGames.title: HimaNatsu is a feel-good romance story you should definitely give a try. Who knows, maybe you’ll be able to rediscover yourself through them this summer as well.

coveredGames.name: Fuyukuru. - Winter winds, adieu? -
coveredGames.title: Fuyukuru. – Winter winds, adieu? – is an at times bizarre visual novel, but an incredibly interesting one that works perfectly within the framework of its own world’s logic.

coveredGames.name: Apidya' Special
coveredGames.title: ​I don’t think it’s going to attract much of a new crowd given how niche a title it is, but for you retro enthusiasts out there, Apidya’ Special is absolutely worth it.

coveredGames.name: The Sinking City 2
coveredGames.title: ​The Sinking City 2 is a solid survival horror and a great way to lead into the spooky season of gaming.

coveredGames.name: Angeline Era
coveredGames.title: Angeline Era doesn’t really serve as a kind of shining example that does the bump combat system as well as I would like.

coveredGames.name: Koikata: How Our Love Grows
coveredGames.title: Koikata: How Our Love Grows stands out for its striking art and cute heroines, if not it's plot.

coveredGames.name: LABYRINTHOS: The Depths Want You
coveredGames.title: For people who are keen on reading consistently interesting dialogue, this one might not be for you. Between the lackluster gameplay and the buffet of honey pots, there are too many stopping points...

coveredGames.name: My (♂) Life as a Vampire's Maid (♀)
coveredGames.title: My (♂) Life as a Vampire’s Maid (♀) offers a very specific combination of tropes, but even as someone who enjoys many of them, I found the game to be ultimately forgettable.

coveredGames.name: Sister Other Paranoia
coveredGames.title: Although relatively simplistic and straightforward in terms of the storyline, Hasuya’s own journey makes for a memorable experience

coveredGames.name: STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT
coveredGames.title: By drawing inspiration from the charm of the traditional visual novel format and the updated flow in STEINS;GATE ELITE, it brings its well-loved time travel story to 2026 for old fans to relive...

coveredGames.name: Staffer Retro : A Supernatural Mystery Quest
coveredGames.title: Staffer Retro: A Supernatural Mystery Quest is a worthy follow-up to Staffer Case that expands and enriches the Staffer universe.

coveredGames.name: BLUE REFLECTION Quartet
coveredGames.title: In the end, Blue Reflection: Second Light is the star of this collection, and it brings with it all the titles that lead up to it and the context and character introductions they bring.

coveredGames.name: 70s-style Robot Anime Geppy-X
coveredGames.title: 70s-style Robot Anime Geppy-X isn’t going to quite match the shmup genre’s elites, but it is absolutely a quirky, unique, and fun experience with an average, if janky, shmup attached to it.

coveredGames.name: Truxton Extreme
coveredGames.title: Much like the original Truxton, I have no doubt this game will garner a cult-like following, and I feel this title is strongly aimed towards them while trying to bring in the wider shmup demographic

coveredGames.name: WAGAMAMA HIGH SPEC OC
coveredGames.title: There’s plenty of meat on the bone here, so if you like Wagamama High Spec already it’s well worth the purchase, especially given its lower price point

coveredGames.name: WAGAMAMA HIGH SPEC
coveredGames.title: Although more than a decade old by now, Wagamama High Spec is still a decent enough moege for what it is.

coveredGames.name: Advent: Dawn
coveredGames.title: With an exciting story and enjoyable characters, Advent: Dawn is a solid entry into the annals of mystery visual novels. It might not blow your mind, but it’s well worth a read.

coveredGames.name: Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 1+2 Dual Collection
coveredGames.title: ​Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 1+2 Dual Collection is a double dose of some of Inti Creates’ most considered games to date.

coveredGames.name: XNemesis
coveredGames.title: A now FREE shooter game creator with a bunch of pre-made levels. Not perfect, but nice to try out to design your own first shmup.

coveredGames.name: Neon Breaker: Endless Arcade
coveredGames.title: Defeat enemy wave after wave in this wraparound Defender clone with twin-stick controls. Find power-ups, score combos, 2 pilots, 2 difficulties, roguelite and local/online co-op mode.

coveredGames.name: Aircraft Evolution
coveredGames.title: Level up and evolve your fictional aircrafts in this 2D action game. Play through 40 missions - destroy cannons, buildings or planes. Mobile port. Not realistic - but can be fun.

coveredGames.name: Alastrius: Star-Fighter
coveredGames.title: Help to restore the Republic while you fly your starfighter in this on-rails shooter. Different ships, a branching storyline, bosses, fully voiced.

coveredGames.name: Alien Attack
coveredGames.title: Fight for your survival in this tiny but fast and challenging twin-stick Asteroids score-chaser. One hit and you are dead. Diffferent weapons, online leaderboard, local 2-player mode.
Challenging FREE retro Galaga clone with nods to some more arcade classics. 3 game modes, power-ups, leaderboards.

coveredGames.name: Space Defender: Frontier Squadron
coveredGames.title: Be a pilot in the dangerous frontier region in this story-heavy twin-stick shooter. Complete missions, upgrade your ships, recruit wingmen, follow the story through 4 acts, co-op mode.

coveredGames.name: Razor Squadron
coveredGames.title: Take part in a large war in this vertical shmup. Shift power between machine guns, lasers, and missiles, rescue wingmen in battle, command other ships. Graze mechanics, 3 difficulties and 6 stages.

coveredGames.name: Void Revenant
coveredGames.title: Blast through 20 sectors in a slow-going pixel-art vertical shoot ’em up. Fire/Bomb, collect coins and buy upgrades for your ship from the merchant Vesk.

coveredGames.name: Exo-Calibre
coveredGames.title: Vertical fantasy bullet hell shmup. 6 (unlockable) pilots, various shot and melee weapons. Story, arcade, boss rush and time attack modes, online leaderboards.

coveredGames.name: Iridium
coveredGames.title: Interesting retro-styled shmup with multi-directional controls – fight your way through 24 levels to complete the mission objectives. Upgrade your ship, use your missiles, defeat massive enemies.

coveredGames.name: XELAN FORCE
coveredGames.title: Challenging vertical shmup in 8-bit style. 2 ships, 3 difficulties, caravan mode.

coveredGames.name: Sektori
coveredGames.title: Survive relentless attacks from all sides in this frantic twin-stick arena shooter. Campaign mode, various challenges. Upgrade and survive!

coveredGames.name: Witchcraft: Candy Hunt
coveredGames.title: FREE horizontal shmup. 3 difficulties, different weapons, cats as drones, creepy bosses - quite easy, an ideal shmup for kids.

coveredGames.name: Bit Blaster XL
coveredGames.title: Collect loot, shoot nasties and stay alive in this simple yet fun score-chaser arena shooter.

coveredGames.name: Beyond Solar
coveredGames.title: Switch between normal/turtle/assault modes of your ship in this vertical shmup with ship/drone upgrades, room building, unaudible speech und unreadable font, 1v1 pvp mode.

coveredGames.name: Bladestar
coveredGames.title: Defend the frontier and collect proto-energy to advance in this vertical shmup with 50 procedurally generated waves. 3 weapons, power-ups, paint schemes, cool speech.

coveredGames.name: Warspace
coveredGames.title: FREE Galaga inspired wave based score chaser. Quite basic, but no monetarization. Earn cash and buy a few upgrades between the rounds.

coveredGames.name: tz mini stg collection
coveredGames.title: 4 tiny game jam shmups from Tamazusa. Not really spectacular, but the compilation is for FREE.

coveredGames.name: AWA
coveredGames.title: Below average vertical shmup. 9 stages, power-ups, 8 (unlockable) jets, 3 difficulties, TATE mode.

coveredGames.name: Atria Valkyrie
coveredGames.title: Purely mouse driven vertical shmup. Absorb bullets to protect your cruiser and charge your gun. 5 episodes, 2 difficulties, 4 pilots, arcade, skirmish and endless modes.

coveredGames.name: AstroWings: Space War
coveredGames.title: Fight through 22 stages in this vertical shmup. Turn your ship left or right. 6 ships, grind to perma upgrade 6 systems of your ship, mobile port.

coveredGames.name: ASTROLANCER
coveredGames.title: Great retro hybrid of run and gun and vertical shmup. Cool 8-bit visuals and gameplay.

coveredGames.name: The Art Of Flight
coveredGames.title: Control a whole squadron of ships in this unusual vertical shmup. Collect power-ups, change the formation. Up to 4 local players. Randomized enemy waves, 60 stages, online leaderboards.

coveredGames.name: Astro Fighters 2
coveredGames.title: Vertical bullet hell shmup, with time slowdown, bombs, graze mechanics, 2 difficulties, local co-op. Similar, but even more options than in the first part.

coveredGames.name: Astro Fighters
coveredGames.title: Full screen vertical bullet hell shmup with grazing mechanics, time slowdown, screen clearing bombs, spread attacks, 4 difficulties, an endless mode, online leaderboards, local co-op.

coveredGames.name: ASCENXION
coveredGames.title: Interesting mix of twin-stick shmup with metroidvania mechanics. Unlock new areas with skills and items that you obtain through exploration. Big difficulty spikes during later game.

coveredGames.name: RANDOMAX
coveredGames.title: Cute roguelite vertical shmup with 70 randomized weapons, 6+3 stages, 3 ships, 5 difficulties, a colorful presentation and a risk reward scoring system.

coveredGames.name: ARMED SEVEN
coveredGames.title: Great horizontal mecha shmup - fly your mech armed with main/sub/charge weapons through 7 stages. 4 difficulties, online leaderboards.

coveredGames.name: Astebreed: Definitive Edition
coveredGames.title: Fantastic horizontal/vertical/3D mech shoot 'em up with 2 difficulties, bullet canceling and lots of Japanese speech. Shoot, regenerate health, melee attack, dash, use lock-on mechanics.

coveredGames.title: Ambitious horizontal/vertical shmup. 5 ships, 4 long operations, optional auto-aim.

coveredGames.title: Cute horizontal bullet hell shmup with 5 stages, focus (slow) move, shield, graze mechanics, 3 characters and 5 difficulties. Story or arcade (+pacifist) modes, online leaderboards.

coveredGames.title: A simple and fun gathering game.

coveredGames.name: KLETKA

coveredGames.name: My Card Is Better Than Your Card!
coveredGames.title: A delightfully unique card game.

coveredGames.title: A quaint, well structured strategy game.

coveredGames.name: ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN
coveredGames.title: A thrilling cooperative experience, lively and impactful.

coveredGames.name: Lords of the Fallen
coveredGames.title: A fun, action-packed roleplaying experience; although it has some flaws the overall experience is quite nice.

coveredGames.name: LIMSCAPE : THE LIMINAL SPACE EXPLORER
coveredGames.title: An amusing funhouse of random occurrences, however that entertainment factor does detract from the overall sense of atmosphere. Thus the game is fun, but not especially profound.

coveredGames.name: PEAK
coveredGames.title: A compelling gauntlet of platforming, resource management and decision making.

coveredGames.name: Monster Train 2
coveredGames.title: A compelling, well-rounded and very replayable rogue-lite experience.

coveredGames.name: CONTROL Resonant
coveredGames.title: A great sequel to CONTROL, more fantastic visuals and a really interesting story and world to explore. The combat took a while to get going but overall if you enjoyed CONTROL this is a must play!

coveredGames.name: Normal Golf Game
coveredGames.title: Absolute banger of a golf game, it's got a steep learning curve but learning and mastering the mechanics is so incredibly satisfying. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS Zero Company™
coveredGames.title: A solid entry point into the squad tactics genre, lacks some of the depth compared to games like X-COM but makes up for it with a strong story and heavier focus on characters. Solid recommend!

coveredGames.name: The Blood of Dawnwalker
coveredGames.title: A really good vampire RPG, and a rare example of a game that focuses on choices and succeeds. An engaging story, likeable characters, enjoyable combat and a fun world to explore. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Escape from Ever After
coveredGames.title: An excellent little RPG in the vein of the Paper Mario games. Charming characters, consistently funny writing and just overall a really fun experience. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Mina the Hollower
coveredGames.title: A really enjoyable retro-styled top-down adventure. The first area is a little rough, but after that the game really opens up and becomes an absolute gem. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Esoteric Ebb
coveredGames.title: Absolutely outstanding. That this was (mostly) done by one man is unbelievable. If you're a fan of Disco Elysium, D&D or narrative RPG's in general this is a must play!

coveredGames.name: Vault of the Void
coveredGames.title: Absolutely phenomenal deckbuilder. It's got a huge amount of variety and each character feels extremely distinct. My favourite deckbuilder by a good amount. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Pipistrello and the Cursed Yoyo
coveredGames.title: An enjoyable top down metroidvania that oozes charm from every pore. If you enjoyed the GBA zelda games this is a must play. Solid recommend!

coveredGames.name: Dogpile
coveredGames.title: A wacky and fun suika game/deckbuilder mashup that works really well. It's charming, very energetic and just a good time. If it looks interesting to you it's well worth trying out. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: ASTLIBRA Revision
coveredGames.title: A very weird RPG with a interesting systems and progression but it's mostly carried by it's utterly insane story. Has way too much fan service but if you can look past that it's well worth your time!

coveredGames.name: CrossCode
coveredGames.title: A real gem of a game. Enjoyable combat, well crafted puzzles and an enormous world to explore and get lost in. Add in great music and a fantastic story and I highly recommend it!

coveredGames.name: Isles of Sea and Sky
coveredGames.title: Excellent sokoban puzzler. A well paced difficulty curve and a beautiful 2D world of puzzles to explore. If you enjoy sokoban puzzlers this is well worth your time and money.

coveredGames.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance
coveredGames.title: One of the best open worlds out there, a grounded and highly immersive experience. The combat is a little clunky to get used to, but the story and characters easily make up for it. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: The Last of Us™ Part I
coveredGames.title: A beloved game that fully deserves the reputation. A heartfelt story with excellent characters combined with a beautifully realised world. One of the best AAA games on steam, I highly recommend it!

coveredGames.name: Deathbulge: Battle of the Bands
coveredGames.title: An absolute gem of an RPG with great writing, a banger soundtrack and a unique battle system. A real shame that this didn't get the attention it deserves. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: CIPHER ZERO
coveredGames.title: A minimalist but very polished logic puzzler. Struck a good balance of being tricky to grasp the rules initially, but never getting overly frustrating. If you enjoy logic puzzles it's worth playing!

coveredGames.name: Öoo
coveredGames.title: A short and sweet puzzle-platformer with some incredibly good puzzle design. It's extremely polished and well hour or so it'll take to beat the game and the bonus puzzles. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood
coveredGames.title: A dark and gritty metroidvania with a heart-wrenching story and phenomenal visuals and soundtrack. The controls are tricky at first but very rewarding to master. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: The First Berserker: Khazan
coveredGames.title: A soulslike that does more than enough to stand out in a crowded genre. Fast paced parry-centric combat with a decent story and truly excellent bosses. If you enjoyed Nioh this is a must play

coveredGames.name: Out Of Hands
coveredGames.title: A truly surreal adventure with a well written story about loss and grief. Interesting card-based combat and overall just a very well crafted experience. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: SANABI
coveredGames.title: Hands down one of the best stories I've experienced in a platformer. Fun movement and grappling focused gameplay, but the game really shines in its gorgeous presentation and story. Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective
coveredGames.title: A wonderfully fun and unique adventure. An insane but thoroughly engaging plot with some incredibly well written characters. Very highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Deep Frost
coveredGames.title: Great social deduction/ investigation game. Had me hooked pretty fast. Can seem daunting at first but don't let that fool you. Had me at the edge of my seat not to make a mistake. I didn't 😎😎💜🧩

coveredGames.name: PRAGMATA
coveredGames.title: ...And then all the pedos accused it of being pedo content.... maybe pedos need to STOP PROJECTING. If this is a pedo game, then freaking prove it. It's easy, but nobody proves it, thus they're liars.

coveredGames.name: Trials of Mana
coveredGames.title: An imperfect but amazing rework of the original SNES game. Odd, as far as aesthetics go, but where the Mana franchise has mostly failed, this succeeds. Thumbs up.

coveredGames.name: Death's Gambit: Afterlife
coveredGames.title: Probably the best 2D action platformer I've ever experienced. No exaggeration. Stellar gameplay, epic adventure, and a soundtrack that can challenge the legends. Thumbs all the way up.

coveredGames.name: DARK SOULS™: REMASTERED
coveredGames.title: I was there when this game descended into the mortal world, not fully formed because they cut out the whole Prepare To Die content to make it DLC. Great game, great remaster, with full DLC. Thumbs up.

coveredGames.name: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin
coveredGames.title: Dark Souls 2 is disliked for good reason. The first one hit hard, but this one hit unfairly, and certain mechanics wreck the experience at times. Good? Not as great as 1 or 3. Thumbs up.

coveredGames.name: DARK SOULS™ III
coveredGames.title: Ah, the Dark Souls of Dark Souls. It's good, clunky, and hard to go back to after Elden Ring. Thumbs up.

coveredGames.name: Devil May Cry HD Collection
coveredGames.title: Classic awesomeness. 1 and 3 still hold up after all these years. 2 was always hated, but you can just play that once and forget about it. Timeline of games is screwy, 3 > 1 > 2 > 4 > 5, I think.

coveredGames.name: Devil May Cry 5
coveredGames.title: Devil May Cry is back, baby. It's crazy awesome good combat to the max, with style. Killing demons is fun. Thumbs up.

coveredGames.name: ENDER MAGNOLIA: Bloom in the Mist
coveredGames.title: The sequel to Ender Lilies. Same as previous review. Platformer soulslike with female protag and also zero smut and zero political drama. Thumbs up.

coveredGames.name: ENDER LILIES: Quietus of the Knights
coveredGames.title: An disturbed platformer soulslike with a female protag that isn't pervy smut and doesn't constantly preach shame men. Save the good guys who were monsterized, and save the world. Thumbs up.

coveredGames.name: Hollow Knight
coveredGames.title: Not projecting, a great game, but definitely also overhyped at times. Imagine if Zelda II was a well made dark fantasy game, then you'd have Hollow Knight.

coveredGames.name: Super Time Force Ultra
coveredGames.title: It's super dumb, super fun, and Super Time Force Ultra. Thumbs up.

coveredGames.name: From the Depths
coveredGames.title: Don't believe the negative reviews about weeb skins. You can make the things you send into strategy battle, and there is tons of details. Awesome.

coveredGames.name: Underkeep
coveredGames.title: If you loved Lands of Lore as much as I did, this game should hit the spot. Fun exploration and battling and tons of things to find. Good puzzles too.

coveredGames.name: Silver Pines
coveredGames.title: It's Silent Hill, except it's a side-scroller and a metroidvania, so it's better. Great atmosphere, amazing exploration. Every item you get lets you explore this haunting town more.

coveredGames.name: The Incident at Galley House
coveredGames.title: A clever interface and intriguing concept makes this a good puzzle game to sink your teeth into. Find out who is who, why no one remembers anything and what is going on.

coveredGames.name: Well Dweller
coveredGames.title: Another winner from Kyle Thompson. This is a delightful game that combines dark fantasy with friendly critters. Fun, almost never frustrating. Quality of life features are superb, feels good to play.

coveredGames.name: Before I Go
coveredGames.title: A must play for fans of platforming. It frequently requires pixel perfect movement, but the controls are super smooth. Movement feels great.

coveredGames.name: Esoteric Ebb
coveredGames.title: Brilliant narrative roleplaying game that combines the mechanics of Disco Elysium with the setting of Planescape Torment and adds a lot of silly comedy while still being earnest.

coveredGames.name: Dead In Vinland
coveredGames.title: A survival/management game, mixed with RPG and adventure elements, about a Viking family trying their best to survive on a mysterious island. Probably my least fav of the series, but still enjoyable.

coveredGames.name: Dead in Antares
coveredGames.title: This one may be my favorite of the Dead In... series. Exploring a mysterious planet, gods and other beings, managing relationship and skilling up characters. A glorious spreadsheet game.

coveredGames.name: UNSIGHTED
coveredGames.title: Combines great exploration, story, and a time limit (yay) with interesting combat and abilities. Something a bit different in the genre.

coveredGames.name: Minishoot' Adventures
coveredGames.title: A new take on the genre, combing an interconnected overworld map and dungeons. Lots of upgrades to find and things to discover.

coveredGames.name: Crypt Custodian

coveredGames.name: Aeterna Noctis

coveredGames.name: Dreambound
coveredGames.title: 15-20+hrs, Dreambound is a LGBTQ+ VN with 3 routes and 9 endings. Play as Noah, a painter who's lost his passion and has isolated himself since his boyfriends death several years ago. Excellent!!!

coveredGames.name: Etrian Odyssey HD
coveredGames.title: 50-70+hrs, an incredible Dungeon Crawler with Grid based movement, manual mapping, and multiple party members, classes and abilities. Delve deep into the Labyrinth of Yggdrasil!

coveredGames.name: Tavern Master
coveredGames.title: 16-30+hrs, Tavern Master is a building and management sim with three maps, you build your own tavern that eventually, partially becomes an inn. Lots of decorations, wall and floor types, and events!

coveredGames.name: Shelves and Sorcery: Tidy Up the Enchanted Shop
coveredGames.title: 10-30+hrs, Shelves and Sorcery is a great Tidy Up game with three levels and four game modes. Use magic to organize enchanted shops - there will be multiplayer in a future update!

coveredGames.name: Chants of Sennaar
coveredGames.title: 10-15+hrs, Chants of Sennar is essentially a giant language based logic puzzle. While the story was lost on me, it's a solid game loosely based off the Tower of Babel, and not too complicated.

coveredGames.name: Planet Zoo
coveredGames.title: 35-100+hrs, Planet Zoo is probably the most realistic and creative Zoo management and building sim you will ever play. While it's kinda buggy, it's fun enough that it's worth putting up with.

coveredGames.name: Gone Home
coveredGames.title: 2–5+hrs, Gone Home is a walking sim with no monsters or horror. Explore an old family home as Kaitlin searches for clues to uncover what happened while she was away. Dev commentary mode included!

coveredGames.name: Salvation:Immortale
coveredGames.title: 2-5+hrs, Salvation:Immortale is a Linear VN with one ending and full voice acting. Follow Detective Mei Qu as she investigates a fifteen year old cold case in the beautiful city of Florence.

coveredGames.name: Inua - A Story in Ice and Time
coveredGames.title: 2-3+hrs, Inua is a narrative adventure about the famously doomed ships, The Terror and the Erebus. Manipulate time to connect your three protagonists together and change the course of history.

coveredGames.name: Amber Isle
coveredGames.title: 35-50+hrs, Amber Isle is a cozy shopkeeping and island restoration sim where you collect materials, craft items, run a store, and work to bring new life back to a prehistoric island.

coveredGames.name: Petit Island
coveredGames.title: 7-9+hrs, Petit Island is a cute/casual exploration game about a cat named Lily exploring her Grandpaw's childhood island to meet up with his old friends and restore his journal. Fairly solid.

coveredGames.name: Ropuka's Idle Island
coveredGames.title: 200-300+hrs, Ropuka's Idle Island is a True Idle game with minimal interaction. Ropuka is a companion frog that will sit on your desktop and cut grass with scissors, with some island decoration.

coveredGames.name: Duck Detective: The Ghost of Glamping
coveredGames.title: 2-3+hrs, Ghost of Glamping is a sequel to The Secret Salami, this time with assistant Freddy, go on a vacation to the (potentially) haunted and abandoned Sunny Lake Sanatorium!

coveredGames.name: LOST EMBER: Rekindled Edition
coveredGames.title: 5-16+hrs, Lost Ember: Rekindled is the newly updated 2025 version of the original from 2019. Play as a Wolf, an Earthbound Spirit traveling with a human soul through their now collapsed civilization.

coveredGames.name: Stars In The Trash
coveredGames.title: 1-3+hrs, Enjoy a completely handmade, watercolor-painted, hand-animated adventure where you play as spoiled housecat Moka, who has escaped to the great outdoors for an unexpected journey!

coveredGames.name: Sonic Frontiers
coveredGames.title: 20-26+hrs, Play as Sonic in an open world exploring the Starfall Islands. Rescue your allies from the Digital Dimension, and discover an ancient civilization that faced a catastrophic end.

coveredGames.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami
coveredGames.title: 2-3+hrs, mystery/detective. Play as Duck Detective investigating a lunchbox theft and it's elusive culprit, The Salami Bandit! Surprisingly fun + well made, with full voice acting and a quack button.

coveredGames.name: The Stanley Parable
coveredGames.title: 1-9+ hrs - 5yrs to complete, The Stanley Parable is an absolutely delightful narrative driven experience about Stanley, who was left unsupervised in their office. Multiple endings! Highly recommended!

coveredGames.name: Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library!
coveredGames.title: 4-22+hrs, Librarian is a simple, mindless and entertaining game about re-shelving and sorting magical books after a minor disaster. Highly recommended.

coveredGames.name: Hidden in my Paradise
coveredGames.title: 3-5+hrs, a cute HOG game that has 4 areas and 25+ levels to explore; you can even create and share your own maps with friends and other players. Overall it's fun, adorable, and well designed.

coveredGames.name: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
coveredGames.title: 40-70+hrs, Clair Obscur is a fantasy turn-based game with a lovely and rewarding world to explore and has one of the most interesting and unexpected storylines I've ever read. Highly recommended.

coveredGames.name: Webbed
coveredGames.title: 4-8+hrs, Webbed is a fun physics based platformer where you play as a female peacock spider rescuing her boyfriend from a Bowerbird, who has mistaken him for a lovely blue rock. Recommended!

coveredGames.name: Cats in the Forbidden City
coveredGames.title: 10-30+ minutes, Cats in the Forbidden City is a hidden object game where you look for 200 cats on the 1761 silk painting “Ten Thousand Nations Coming to Pay Tribute” (299 × 207cm.) Very cute!

coveredGames.name: Smushi Come Home
coveredGames.title: 5-7+hrs, Smushi Come Home is a super chill mushroom themed exploration game with light platforming, puzzles, character customization, and questlines.

coveredGames.name: Kabuto Park
coveredGames.title: 2-3hr+ Kabuto Park is a hand-drawn casual bug collecting and battling RPG! Hana and her friend Midori collect various beetles, mantises, and dragonflies to compete with the local kids in a Tournament.

coveredGames.name: Fish to Dish: Idle Sushi
coveredGames.title: 100-200+hrs. Fish to Dish: Idle Sushi is a cute pixel art desktop game. Collect fish and turn them into sushi for your restaurant; a dog and/or cat can accompany your tiny adventure.

coveredGames.name: planetarian: Snow Globe
coveredGames.title: 1-2+hrs. A slice-of-life KN following a Planetarium supervisor and their companion robot/employee, Yumemi. A prequel to Planetarian, but should be read as a sequel for maximum emotional damage.

coveredGames.name: Sophia the Traveler
coveredGames.title: 3-4+hrs, Hidden Object game with ten fully colored, illustrated, and mostly animated maps. Follow Sophie and her dog Max as they travel through the scenic and historical City of Water, Venice.

coveredGames.name: Fallstreak 2: Traum
coveredGames.title: 8-15+hrs, Fallstreak 2: Traum continues the journey of our heroine Adelise as she journeys beyond the mist that cradled her home, Socotrine, into the dangerous and lovely home of the fae.

coveredGames.name: Escape From Mystwood Mansion
coveredGames.title: 2-5+ hrs, Escape from Mystwood is a clever escape room simulator. Two endings, some puzzles can be solved in various ways, with a bit of a storyline and environmental storytelling. Recommended!

coveredGames.name: Fallstreak
coveredGames.title: 6-8+hrs, Fallstreak is a dark fantasy VN about the people of Socotrine, a closed off city still recovering ten years later after a catastrophic disaster. An excellent story, but it's not for everyone.

coveredGames.name: Doors: Paradox
coveredGames.title: 5-12+hrs, Doors: Paradox is a point and click casual puzzle game with three chapters, and 58 themed doors to try and open! Pretty enjoyable, with many varying themes and clever mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Cyberpunk 2077
coveredGames.title: 30-200+hrs, Cyberpunk 2077 Is a fantastic RPG about a merc living in a glittering dystopia. Branching story paths, incredible characters, skilled writing, and a city as beautiful as it is rotten.

coveredGames.name: Deliver Us The Moon
coveredGames.title: 5-8+ hrs, explore a hastily abandoned colony on the moon in an attempt to restore an Energy source that Earth desperately needs. Solid mystery sci-fi game with a fantastic ending.

coveredGames.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg
coveredGames.title: 15-30+ hrs, Dungeons of Hinterberg is a fun mix between vacation and dungeon crawler. Fight monsters, solve puzzles, then unwind at the end of the day in a magical tourist town.

coveredGames.name: Angeline Era
coveredGames.title: Angeline Era most prominently features a very rewarding type of overworld exploration that ties together it's sometimes abstract and always entertaining levels with a sense of constant progression.

coveredGames.name: In Stars And Time
coveredGames.title: Trapped in a time-loop, this deeply story-driven RPG makes you go through the ups and downs of having to relive the same points in time again and again. Extremely well written and worth a play!

coveredGames.name: Once Upon A KATAMARI
coveredGames.title: Roll around an ever-growing ball and make everything in your way stick to it. This one has a fun twist of rolling through levels in various iconic time periods, like during the Stone or Ice Age. Fun!

coveredGames.name: Stray Children
coveredGames.title: A wildly obscure non-traditional RPG with a great cast of characters and a ton of secrets. The combat features some elements from Undertale, but puts a twist in the form of semi-cryptic puzzles on it.

coveredGames.name: Corn Kidz 64
coveredGames.title: A very much N64-inspired collectathon platformer that combines the strengths of the best genre-giants from the Golden Age of 3D Platformers with a unique and satisfying movement system! Great fun!

coveredGames.name: Look Outside
coveredGames.title: An incredibly atmospheric horror RPG that mixes creepy and weird to a height that I've rarely seen and never seen executed so perfectly. Especially Earthbound-fans should take a look (outside)!

coveredGames.name: The Wee Pier
coveredGames.title: One fisherman, endless fish in the sea, and a surprisingly addictive upgrade loop. This relaxing idle game offers satisfying progression, automation, and just enough grind to keep things hooked.

coveredGames.name: KICKDOWN: Highway Traffic Racing
coveredGames.title: Repetitive arcade racer with simple gameplay, limited track variety, and frustrating police chases. Decent car customization and upgrades add some fun, but the overall experience feels shallow.

coveredGames.name: Very Very RARE
coveredGames.title: Idle tower defense built around random turret forging, upgrades, and loot collection. Progression is initially engaging, but quickly runs out of depth, leaving an unnecessarily long endgame.

coveredGames.name: Intergalactic Burger Joint
coveredGames.title: "Falling shape" puzzle game with random ingredient placement, 120 stages, and minor chapter mechanics. Cosmetic chefs and unlockables provide some incentive, mainly through Endless Mode.

coveredGames.name: Sardoinky
coveredGames.title: Opening fish cans, selling loot, and unlocking upgrades make for a quirky incremental game with fun surprises, but repetitive clicking and achievement grinding make it less enjoyable toward the end.

coveredGames.name: Flag Fiasco: Tidy Up
coveredGames.title: Educational flag-collecting game with a simple premise, but limited skills, occasional bugs, and a cluttered map make the experience increasingly frustrating over time.

coveredGames.name: Rhythm Roll
coveredGames.title: Challenge is modest, the presentation is pleasant, and the soundtrack is probably its biggest selling point. However, once you've played all the stages, there's little reason to return.

coveredGames.name: THE NOM MUST BE FED
coveredGames.title: Starts with promising ideas and the potential for something more, but ultimately turns into a disappointing grind with little to no meaningful rewards.

coveredGames.name: Pool of Madness
coveredGames.title: Surprisingly addictive mix of pool and roguelite mechanics, with fast rounds, random events, challenging obstacles and permanent upgrades that make every run worth another try.

coveredGames.name: Dark Rail
coveredGames.title: Promising mix of dark fantasy, dice-based combat, and resource management. Runs end quick, but permanent boosts might let survive a few days more on your next try.

coveredGames.name: Corridor 13
coveredGames.title: Creepy, detailed anomaly-hunting experience with fun scares, but repeating anomalies and no tracker make full completion unnecessarily frustrating.

coveredGames.name: The Great Ebony Clock
coveredGames.title: Short point-and-click adventure with an interesting time mechanic, but limited exploration, only one logical puzzle, and hidden endings that are worth exploring at a discount.

coveredGames.name: Arcane Dash - A Pixel Adventure
coveredGames.title: Nostalgic arcade platformer with fast gameplay, but limited enemy variety, frustrating moving platforms, and a tedious but optional ascension system that overstays its welcome.

coveredGames.name: Dino Slug
coveredGames.title: It might not offer an enormous amount of content, character variety, or mechanical complexity, but the core gameplay loop is solid.

coveredGames.name: Grégoire Lefèbvre Investigations : The Vow of Hate
coveredGames.title: Straightforward novel-like game centered entirely on storytelling and dialogue, with minimal inventory management and virtually no puzzles to solve.

coveredGames.name: Constellations
coveredGames.title: Relaxing star-connecting game featuring all 88 constellations, with visual clues, discovery facts, ambient effects, unlockable space elements, and an atlas for revisiting completed constellations.

coveredGames.name: We Have a Sheep Problem
coveredGames.title: Casual sheep-sorting game with over 30 themed stalls, helpful tracking abilities, simple mechanics, and generous upgrades, though some special skills feel largely unnecessary.

coveredGames.name: Knuckleball: Free Kick Football
coveredGames.title: Easy-to-play free-kick game with little content and no tutorials for advanced moves. Fun briefly, but offers almost no reason to keep playing after a short career and challenge modes.

coveredGames.name: Space Builder Idle
coveredGames.title: Incremental game with satisfying automation and prestige progression, but repetitive grinding and increasingly slow resource production make much of the experience feel passive.

coveredGames.name: Reality Drift
coveredGames.title: Entertaining and somewhat luck-dependent roguelite racer, where random upgrades and cards can ruin an otherwise good run, or let you gain an incredible lead.

coveredGames.name: Dark Alley
coveredGames.title: Predictable, paper-thin detective story with minimal investigation, trivial puzzles, and no twists. More of a short visual novel than an actual adventure game.

coveredGames.name: FIRE AND ASHES
coveredGames.title: Short but enjoyable horror experience with a few bugs and clunky combat, yet its nice atmosphere, interesting microphone mechanics, and story make it worth playing.

coveredGames.name: HO HO HO SOKOBAN
coveredGames.title: Basic Christmas-themed Sokoban game with 50 challenging stages, but no variety or extra content.

coveredGames.name: Tiny Knight and the Corrupted Crystal
coveredGames.title: Mix of action and incremental mechanics makes progression addictive, but repetitive combat, escalating upgrade costs, and the need to grind can slow things down, especially in the later stages.

coveredGames.name: False Hero
coveredGames.title: Scholar in a dying world must master combat through a mysterious mask, learning enemy skills, overcoming brutal bosses, and making choices that shape the fate of the gods.

coveredGames.name: Train Survivor
coveredGames.title: Survivor game with interesting train-based mechanics, but severely lacking in content, challenge, and replayability. Only worth considering at a steep discount.

coveredGames.name: ESCAPE: The Cabin
coveredGames.title: Puzzle adventure with clever challenges, random clues and solutions, and a time limit that adds tension, though automatically closing drawers and doors can be annoying.

coveredGames.name: Clairvoyage: The Lighthouse
coveredGames.title: Interesting premise built around time loops and tight time limit, though the lack of content and brief experience leave the asking price feeling a little steep.

coveredGames.name: Way Too Many Eggs
coveredGames.title: Idle game built around repetitive egg collection, chicken upgrades, and prestige progression. Workers eventually take over, making active gameplay largely unnecessary.

coveredGames.name: Manus Sors
coveredGames.title: Short adventure featuring simple puzzles, exploration for clues around small locations, and using camera filters to take care of anomalies.

coveredGames.name: The Angry Zoo: The Animals Hate You
coveredGames.title: Silly but challenging game full of unpredictable animal encounters, some cheap deaths, and no saving. Fun for a while, but lacking depth and replay value.

coveredGames.name: Slots & Skulls
coveredGames.title: Roguelite built around fast-paced slot machine combat, where symbol selection, permanent upgrades, and a bit of luck determine how far you can progress.

coveredGames.name: Studs Up! Win Ugly
coveredGames.title: Fun but unbalanced mix of soccer and violence that quickly becomes repetitive. Worth a look at half price, but difficult to recommend at full price.

coveredGames.name: Good Children Say Grace
coveredGames.title: Surreal first-person narrative game where characters, branching storylines, and bizarre imagery create an unsettling experience.

coveredGames.name: Wildixir
coveredGames.title: Accessible survivor-style game with clear objectives, straightforward mechanics, and generous progression. Ideal for newcomers.

coveredGames.name: Untold Cases - Stillwater Lake
coveredGames.title: Atmospheric visuals and solid flashlight mechanics, but repetitive and short gameplay, meaningless dialogue choices, and an abrupt ending. There's room for improvement in future episodes.

coveredGames.name: Gold Miner: Return to Glory
coveredGames.title: Simple game offering a few minutes of casual fun by clicking a single button, but the basic gameplay and lack of depth leave little reason to keep playing.

coveredGames.name: Blastlane Racers
coveredGames.title: Chaotic combat racer with several cars, weapons, and upgrades, but unforgiving AI and relentless attacks make even the easiest races a challenge.

coveredGames.name: ERLIK
coveredGames.title: Promising survivors game with a fresh Turkish mythology setting, fast and rewarding gameplay, satisfying progression, and plenty of potential.

coveredGames.name: Silicon Sprint: Data Center Incremental
coveredGames.title: Repetitive gameplay and no big surprises make the game tedious over time, but low cost makes up for it.

coveredGames.name: Milki Delivery
coveredGames.title: cute game held back by the Pokemon level resource grind after the first upgrades, the pace plummets into a mindless repetition of actions that could be relaxing but are lacking after its great start

coveredGames.name: A Case of Fraud
coveredGames.title: Great afternoon sized document exploring deduction game where you solve and murder and unearth some juicy office drama. I'm always up for both of those. Also, cute pets! Do it for Plum!

coveredGames.name: No Murders in Grimwick
coveredGames.title: a truly bite sized point and click murder mystery that would have benefited from having more depth. is nonetheless a charming little thing to spend one lunch break with!

coveredGames.name: CryptidCam
coveredGames.title: Short and sweet critter photography game with a handful of nice challenges to provide a tad of replayability, go get the best photo possible of the cutest cryptids on this side of the forest.

coveredGames.name: The Last Campfire
coveredGames.title: a sweet storybook-in-tone adjacent puzzley romp about loss and being lost, masterfully and oh so sweetly executed.

coveredGames.name: Dressmaker
coveredGames.title: the best dressmaking game there is, and it's not even close. a true canvas that challenges you by giving you a dress shaped canvas for your art, so why not burlap? burlap. it's burlap time.

coveredGames.name: Florence
coveredGames.title: Cute and well implemented storybook game that ends in a metaphorical saccharine car crash that left me seething. Worth it because of the minigames and their ludonarrative resonance. And nothing more.

coveredGames.name: Vampyr
coveredGames.title: Play on story mode. As good as the story and dilemmas, the setting and characters are, and I loved them quite a lot, it doesn't justify that atrocious thing we call combat. Decent vampire attempt too.

coveredGames.name: Super Candle World
