coveredGames.title: 8/10. Delightfully simple puzzle platformer: run, jump, and collect the trinkets, but how? Masterclass exercising simple mechanics to great effect; puzzles nontrivial but never unduly hard.

coveredGames.name: Discolored
coveredGames.title: 4/10. Color themed puzzle game with very pretty environments but almost entirely random puzzles that defy logic or explanation. Somebody confused obtuse/random with good/challenging. Still, Pretty.

coveredGames.name: AMEN 11 11
coveredGames.title: 8/10. hidden object game; clearly runs on the same foundation as the developer’s Hidden cat games, but trades that collection’s charm and cuteness for something much darker and more mature (SFW).

coveredGames.name: Tokiros
coveredGames.title: 6/10. puzzle platformer built around a small set of simple abilities. Surprisingly for the genre, it's also a bit of a precision platformer/mild rage quit game. Might appeal to some, but not me.

coveredGames.name: Die Young: Prologue
coveredGames.title: 7/10. Alternates between being an adventure game, FPS-shooter, and FPS-stealth. All set in a world that is often quite open compared to typical FPS corridor-based shooters. Short/Free/worth it.

coveredGames.name: A Color Theory
coveredGames.title: 7/10. Answers the question, “what if Baba is You was a 2D platformer, and used color instead of code blocks for all of its rules (although much to the same effect?)”. +++ novelty, ++ fun, - gfx.

coveredGames.name: Fluffy Horde
coveredGames.title: 6/10. This game is hard to classify. But the experience is a bit like playing those old Angry Birds games, with a surprising amount of physics for a so-called tower-defense game + similar randomness.

coveredGames.name: Alien Cartographer
coveredGames.title: 7/10. Minesweeper-ish game with several mine types and highly constraining rules about adjacency. Feels very novel, and fairly challenging. Presentation is quite spartan but UI is good.

coveredGames.name: Roboggled Sokoban Game
coveredGames.title: 7/10. Sokoban with a bunch of extras: ice levels, lasers, or simultaneously moving pushers. While there’s nothing truly novel, it’s a good mix + new mechanics are introduced at just the right rate.

coveredGames.name: FAITH: The Unholy Trinity
coveredGames.title: 5/10. Two Game mechanics: Untimed wandering around maze-like environment and reading above-average storyline (good) + Careful memorization of movement patterns of one-hit-kill monsters (lame).

coveredGames.name: Directory Dungeon - File Explorer Dungeon Crawler
coveredGames.title: 5/10. This game really is played completely from the Windows Explorer File Manager. A gimmick, but also intriguing, and makes this game worth trying, but only if you are into that kind of CS-weirdness

coveredGames.name: Kingsgrave
coveredGames.title: 9/10. Equal parts Twin stick A-RPG / Metroidvania / puzzle game. No single element dominates over the others, although it is definitely more action heavy than puzzle heavy. Super fun!

coveredGames.name: Ratico Puzzle Adventure
coveredGames.title: 5/10. Sokoban, but viewed from a 3D perspective. It also has minor gameplay elaborations such as obstacles that you clear by eating them (just walking through them, really). Ok but ultra-bland.

coveredGames.name: Nomad Survival
coveredGames.title: 8/10. A very earnest clone of Vampire Survivors; just enough new to be mildly fresh, but enough faithfully copied to be very fun. Unless you crave novelty, check it out.

coveredGames.name: Felix The Reaper
coveredGames.title: 5/10. Grid puzzler; pick up “boxes” and drop them wherever, either to cast shadows, activate switches, or win. Step into the sun and die. Great A/V/S, poor Gameplay. Waste of polish.

coveredGames.name: Mega Maze
coveredGames.title: FREE; 5/10. This is a very simplistic first-person 3D maze game. The hook is that the walls are transparent so you don’t have to wander around completely lost, but that's not really enough novelty.

coveredGames.name: Block in the Lock
coveredGames.title: FREE. 8/10. A sokoban‑adjacent puzzler. Instead of pushing crates you move all the crates simultaneously in the same direction. Simple graphics, interesting ideas. Gets too hard after ~2 hours.

coveredGames.name: Sparklite
coveredGames.title: 6/10. A Top-down Zelda-alike w/ Good combat/movement, BUT: heavy emphasis on level-up grind to make bosses manageable. Pseudo-random levels failed at keeping it fresh enough to hold my attention.

coveredGames.name: Caravan SandWitch
coveredGames.title: 8/10. Modern reimagining of collectathon; story-heavy 3D explorathon with heavy emphasis on finding + collecting to upgrade abilities and unlock full story. Easy platforming, mild puzzles. Open world.

coveredGames.name: Rondoku
coveredGames.title: 6/10. Interesting+novel variant on Sudoku BUT I think would be more fun to play with pencil and paper than using a computer, where there's no good way to keep notes on what you've tried.

coveredGames.name: A Demon's Game - Episode 1
coveredGames.title: 4/10 A highly repetitive horror game, where you navigate a claustrophobic sewer system, avoiding a monster by sneaking around in the dark and finding clues and key objects in order to unlock the exit.

coveredGames.name: Cats vs Zombies III
coveredGames.title: 7/10. Absurdly short hidden object game feature cats and zombies in an unlikely but amusing mashup. The art is clearly hand drawn, although there's some significant Photoshop work.

coveredGames.name: MR. ELEVATOR
coveredGames.title: 8/10. Adventure game / escape room featuring logic puzzles and semi-frequent auditory cues. Unusual UI, but fun and novel puzzle design. Interesting retro / highly stylized GFX. Good Music.

coveredGames.name: There Will Be No Turkey This Christmas
coveredGames.title: 4/10. This is just a simple stealth game; despite the puzzle tag there is absolutely nothing puzzling. At most, the levels are a bit of a maze, but it's really just a reflex test / arcade game.

coveredGames.name: Axiom Verge
coveredGames.title: 10/10. One of the best Metroid-alike games on PC. Great action, fun weapons and exploration, good QoL + Storyline. SciFi + horror vibes, great pixel art styled between NES and SNES.

coveredGames.name: Lenrual
coveredGames.title: 5...8/10. Sci-fi themed 3D puzzle game where the goal and even what you can do is itself a puzzle: zero hand-holding. Recommend ONLY if you like being lost and experimenting a lot. Nice visuals.

coveredGames.name: Cats vs Zombies II
coveredGames.title: 8/10. FREE but super short hidden object game featuring cat+zombies. Art is real cute and all the quality of life features are included. BUT: only 8-10 minutes of play time.

coveredGames.name: Mai: Child of Ages
coveredGames.title: 8/10 3D action adventure that mixes 75% of Zelda with 25% of Mario mechanics. Cute & pleasant looking, with cartoony, Wii era look. Definitely worth a look.

coveredGames.name: Neverout
coveredGames.title: 5/10. An ultra-casual 3D puzzle game, played inside a cube. When you reach a wall you can keep on moving, which rotates gravity, making that wall the new floor. Many puzzles are over-trivial.

coveredGames.name: Puzzle - LINES AND KNOTS
coveredGames.title: 7.5/10. A connect-all-the-paths puzzler vaguely reminiscent of Pipe Dream, but secretly it’s a jigsaw puzzle. Difficulty is one step above casual - sometimes you have to think ahead.

coveredGames.name: Puzzle - LINES AND KNOTS 3
coveredGames.title: 8/10. A connect-all-the-paths puzzler vaguely reminiscent of Pipe Dream, but secretly it’s a jigsaw puzzle. Difficulty is one step above ultra-casual, but never trivial.

coveredGames.name: Ever Forward
coveredGames.title: 6.5/10. A very pretty 3D puzzle game. Puzzles are demanding in terms of reflexes, intellect, and observation. They mostly consist of avoiding cameras (ie stealth); not really a platformer.

coveredGames.name: Backrooms Open World

coveredGames.name: Warp to Sector One

coveredGames.name: Annum Crossroads

coveredGames.name: Engagement
coveredGames.title: The perfect answer to "what if I wanted capital ship dogfighting in a bullet heaven roguelite scenario?" Entirely better than expected and the fact that it's co-op just slaps

coveredGames.name: Soul Snake 3D
coveredGames.title: 3D snake and a bullet heaven roguelite with a coat of crunchy, lofi goodness. It's good for the soul.

coveredGames.name: Hot Wax
coveredGames.title: One of the most unique takes on the falling block puzzle game I've seen.

coveredGames.name: Solar Voltage
coveredGames.title: An isometric puzzle platforming adventure with a nice cast of characters and surprisingly tight controls.

coveredGames.name: Bad Trip
coveredGames.title: A rather promising horror title that managed to actually hit me in the feels pretty early.

coveredGames.name: Playable Archive
coveredGames.title: Short, but solid. Wild to think we were getting a Paranormal Activity game

coveredGames.name: Last Round at the End of the World
coveredGames.title: Macabre occult deduction with beautifully weird presentation. We don't have enough games with the picture cutout style like this.

coveredGames.name: School Labyrinth
coveredGames.title: A solid co-op horror experience. Good atmosphere, neat designs inspired by yokai and other supernatural legends of Japan.

coveredGames.name: They Die Tomorrow
coveredGames.title: I know it's not technically ghost hunting, but it's in the vein and it's honestly kind of neat. I just had to give it a couple gos.

coveredGames.name: Escape from the Black Monolith
coveredGames.title: For something that started as a game jam entry, it's rather solid. Just how tall is this monolith?!

coveredGames.name: Wreck Below
coveredGames.title: Dev's very receptive to feedback, and the core game is a lot of fun. Great for thalassophobes.

coveredGames.name: Oh!Ware
coveredGames.title: I love weird roguelike/lite combos. Never expected to see Mancala as a base for one. Works well.

coveredGames.name: The Loopler
coveredGames.title: Generally not the biggest fan of slightly more idle games like this, but it's a surprisingly satisfying number-go-up dopamine factory.

coveredGames.name: ICEwall
coveredGames.title: Like your classic shmups like Space Invaders? Enjoy roguelites? Then enjoy ICEwall.

coveredGames.name: Tech Support: Error Unknown

coveredGames.name: Forsworn

coveredGames.name: Ignite the Depths
coveredGames.title: Based on the playtest, this will be a hardcore co-op experience I'm going to enjoy a lot.

coveredGames.name: Blue Wyrm

coveredGames.name: Kyubu Kyubu Dice

coveredGames.name: Dorts : A Darts Roguelike

coveredGames.name: Stonewards
coveredGames.title: Top notch co-op base defense. You're a dwarf. You dig. You fight. You drink. Do it with friends. Win. Lots of long term progression is rather nice, too.

coveredGames.name: One Stroke Hunter
coveredGames.title: An interesting concept that's definitely a more thinking-man's kinda roguelike. Strategy is key, and I am not the greatest strategist. Still, a fun time and solid presentation.

coveredGames.name: Nazi Zombies

coveredGames.name: The Blackwood Project

coveredGames.name: Battlefleet Gothic: Armada (Classic)
coveredGames.title: A simultaneously deep, yet incredibly frustrating tactics game. It's got some very rewarding mechanics, but the main campaign drags with some god-awful RNG objectives and missions. Worth giving a try.

coveredGames.name: R.U.S.E.™
coveredGames.title: After being delisted for too long, it's back with all DLC. Very scripted single player experience (story is cliché) but still absurdly enjoyable, especially in multiplayer. Macro-RTS fun!

coveredGames.name: Subnautica
coveredGames.title: A pretty compelling survival game with some sandbox and exploration elements. Really fun, extremely immersive.

coveredGames.name: CHRONO TRIGGER®
coveredGames.title: A Square RPG with snappy combat that won't take 100 hours to finish. This port is probably the best yet with the QoL improvements of the DS version but in HD. It's really great, but you knew that!

coveredGames.name: Company of Heroes: Opposing Fronts
coveredGames.title: A fantastic expansion that showcases two additional factions. One of the better (arguably best) campaign pair in the franchise, though there are some frustrations with the British one.

coveredGames.name: Borderlands 2
coveredGames.title: This is a decent ARPG (albeit a bit shallow) that has unfortunately been given the moniker of "co-op game". There is co-op, but it's not fleshed out at all. Otherwise, HUGE improvement over the OG.

coveredGames.name: Gears of War: Reloaded
coveredGames.title: I haven't checked out the SECOND remaster (jesus christ), but the original Gears is not only a fun game, it's unlike the rest of the trilogy with its use of horror elements. Still fun, a little dated.

coveredGames.name: Assassin's Creed 2
coveredGames.title: It went from thought-provoking discussions of free will (AC 1) to loud Italians. Still, an improvement over the original's gameplay, though it continues the repetition. Strong protagonist.

coveredGames.name: Chronicles of the Wolf
coveredGames.title: Great horizontal Metroidvania and ARPG, a true successor to Simon's Quest that isn't terrible. Has some very frustrating, instant-death story traps where you could tell the developer was trolling.

coveredGames.name: DYNASTY WARRIORS: ORIGINS
coveredGames.title: Lots of mixed feelings so far, but I will recommend it if you can get it cheap. This should not be $70. Feels like the overworld and narrative direction cut into map and mission development. Lacking.

coveredGames.name: No Mortal Space
coveredGames.title: An okay mix of open world survival/crafting/sandbox & some cultivation. Combat, though a bit shallow, has some level of personal expression through art modifiers. Surprisingly fun for a demo.

coveredGames.name: 真夜的居所 - Chanye's Home
coveredGames.title: 1x1 kinetic novel, high sweetness, ~3h. Super fluffy, cozy & charming. Deep about loving oneself, personal freedom, trust & equality. Tons of really cute art & Shenzhen's landmarks in pixel-art.

coveredGames.name: Tied by your Red
coveredGames.title: 1x1 linear plot, high sweetness, ~2.5h. A classic fairy-tale style story, funny & wholesome, with a boyish-looking heroine & a bit of mystery. Other perspectives unlocked after reaching TE.

coveredGames.name: 天香与小百合 - Tinheung & Sayuri
coveredGames.title: 1x1 kinetic novel, high sweetness, ~30m. Sweet, funny, and heartfelt. Bite-sized story about a bored Chinese recent graduate and a lonely Japanese businesswoman. A little age gap included.

coveredGames.name: Double Date - Yuri Visual Novel
coveredGames.title: 1x1 kinetic novel, high sweetness, ~2h. Fluffy, simple, drama-free story. Funny idea with sentient pets. Death Becomes You characters in an alternate universe. Pretty art, 4 CGs.

coveredGames.name: Beyond the Sunset 斜阳下的彼岸
coveredGames.title: 1x1 linear plot / 4 endings, medium sweetness, ~3h. An unremarkable writer and her mirror opposite from the twilight realm. Simple but touching and very atmospheric story set in a fantasy world.

coveredGames.name: 流光易逝的夏末 - Fleeting Summer's End
coveredGames.title: 1x1 kinetic novel, ~1.5h. Cute and heartfelt story, on the realistic and bittersweet side, with philosophy and self-discovery. Real Chinese countryside is faithfully represented in pixel art.

coveredGames.name: The Final Prize is Soup
coveredGames.title: 2 routes / 2 major endings, medium-high sweetness, ~6h. Death game, Chinese legends, light horror elements. Beautiful story, rich and emotional. Interesting, cute, and well written characters.

coveredGames.name: Flowering Across 樱下花期
coveredGames.title: 1x1 branching plot / 4 endings, very high sweetness, ~1h. Super adorable chibi yuri about an introverted uni student and a sakura spirit. Waterside Chirping characters, but in a different world.

coveredGames.name: Waterside Chirping 水畔空蝉
coveredGames.title: 1x1 linear plot / 2 endings, medium sweetness, ~1.5h. A quiet village girl reunites with the lover of her past life. A story with witchcraft and mystery, on the emotional and atmospheric side.

coveredGames.name: Desert Blossom
coveredGames.title: 1x2 linear plot / 5 endings, medium sweetness, ~10h or more. Cute, funny, lighthearted, colorful yuri JRPG. So many couples!! Lots of references to yuri media. No grinding, VN player friendly.

coveredGames.name: Adult Life Yuri Bundle by Team ANPIM
coveredGames.title: 4-pack of 1x1 kinetic novels, medium sweetness, ~2h each. Fluffy, light and grounded, very nice short stories. Slice of life, comedy, a bit of drama. Mostly sweet, Moon Star is bittersweet.

coveredGames.name: 茜色
coveredGames.title: 1x1 linear plot, ~20h. Dreamy, sincere, emotional. 20 years of life and love painted with great passion and love for yuri. A deep plot of mystery and mutual support. Grab the DLC for desserts!

coveredGames.name: The Fruitless Flower 雾雨中的徒花
coveredGames.title: 1x1 linear plot / 4 endings, ~7h. Dark and sweet, emotional adventure spanning many years from childhood friends to inseparable lovers. Beautiful atmosphere, music, maps, day and night scenes.

coveredGames.name: The Light at the End of the Ocean
coveredGames.title: 1x1 linear plot / 3 endings, ~3h. Amnesia mystery & greek mythology. Beautiful atmosphere, lots of melancholy, and unforgettable story. Friendship themed (very beginning of a romance).

coveredGames.name: Lachesis or Atropos
coveredGames.title: 2 routes / 4 major endings, medium sweetness, ~4h. Mystery, mythology, and horror. Complex lore and story (but a bit fast-paced). Great atmosphere, quite spooky. Interesting and cute characters.

coveredGames.name: Amelie
coveredGames.title: 1x1 mostly linear plot / 1 true ending, medium sweetness, ~2h. Mystery and psychological horror. Nice plot, emotional line and soundtrack. Actually creepy atmosphere. No on-screen violence.

coveredGames.name: Rose Seed Replica
coveredGames.title: 1x1 branching plot / 1 ending, high sweetness, ~6h or more. Point & click adventure, very cute, lots of ways to "shape" your romance (high replayability), engaging plot, lots of rainbows!

coveredGames.name: optimal conditions for a sacrifice
coveredGames.title: 1x1 linear plot / 3 endings, ~30m. Cute and fun, surreal narrative about the meaning and value of love. Pretty and colorful artworks. Even a minor sidecouple.

coveredGames.name: Kiss the Demiurge
coveredGames.title: 1 choice / 3 routes, medium-low sweetness, ~15h. Mystery and an emotional roller coaster. Nice plot and emotional descriptions. The art isn't professional, but the CGs are very pretty!

coveredGames.name: The Fairy's Secret
coveredGames.title: 1x1 kinetic novel, medium-high sweetness, ~6h. A sequel to The Fairy's Song. Less interesting than the prequel, but it's a rare story starting with an existing couple!

coveredGames.name: The Fairy's Song
coveredGames.title: 1x1 kinetic novel, medium-high sweetness, ~6h. A fairy tale about Cute goth and Curious medieval knight set in a remote village and forest. Nice plot, soundtrack and atmosphere.

coveredGames.name: A Field of Flowers and Stars
coveredGames.title: 1x1 kinetic novel, voice acting, high sweetness, ~3h. Grump human x Sunshine alien + AI friend. Star Wars style "science" fiction. The story is nothing too deep, but it's really cute and sweet.

coveredGames.name: Monster Fantasy
coveredGames.title: Looks interesting, has online co-op.

coveredGames.name: Crimson Moon
coveredGames.title: Looks interesting, has online co-op.

coveredGames.name: Bioneers
coveredGames.title: Craft your organism one cell by cell.

coveredGames.name: Substrate: Emergence
coveredGames.title: Game in devloment about single cell evovlivng in petri dishes simulation

coveredGames.name: Planetary Life
coveredGames.title: Spiritual successor of Spore, but with more advance evolution and "natural" selection.

coveredGames.name: Primordialis
coveredGames.title: Rogue like Microorganism builder. Similar to spore cellular phase but with more modularity and engineering. No evolution here

coveredGames.name: Intelligent Design: An Evolutionary Sandbox
coveredGames.title: Evolve alien plants on a planet. Conceptual but with some cool mechanics.

coveredGames.name: PolyPine
coveredGames.title: Simulation of a forest ecosystem. No evolution or DNA, but an agent based system.

coveredGames.name: Plague Inc: Evolved
coveredGames.title: Simulation of pandemics with gamified evolution.

coveredGames.name: Equilinox
coveredGames.title: No genetic and evolution, but an educational light introduction on ecosystem.

coveredGames.name: Artificial Life Simulator
coveredGames.title: A classic and beautiful particle simulator.

coveredGames.name: Thrive
coveredGames.title: An ongoing open source game with the goal to simulate evolution from single cell to galatical empire. The development recently reached multicellularity stage. Biology is as accurate as possible.

coveredGames.name: Rain World
coveredGames.title: You play a little slugcat prey and need to survive an hostile simulated ecosystem. Each creature have its own agency with or without you around, and can adapt to your behavior.

coveredGames.name: Species: Artificial Life, Real Evolution
coveredGames.title: Classic morphology genetic evolution. The devlopment has stopped but this is still a good reference.

coveredGames.name: Ecosystem
coveredGames.title: Marine evolution of morphology/locomotion and neural network.

coveredGames.name: ANLIFE: Motion-Learning Life Evolution
coveredGames.title: Cute game where 3D creatures evolve to walk. 3D physics-based locomotion and neural network.

coveredGames.name: Horsey Game
coveredGames.title: Breed horse and more to win the race. You can use CRIPSR to edit your "horse" genome and use computer to optimise their gene for the race. The genes determine the morphology and behaviour.

coveredGames.name: The Bibites: Digital Life
coveredGames.title: God games where you follow the genetic evolution of little creature, the bibites. Each bibite has neural network and specific biological parameters.

coveredGames.name: Sandboxels
coveredGames.title: Charming life sim that plays like living sand art. You choose the ingredients you are dropping into the simulation and then they may or may not interact. Life and mutations occur all very naturally.

coveredGames.name: Wormies
coveredGames.title: Cute game where you can breed wormies. Wormies breed by themselves with the option to put them in boxes for more specific pairings.

coveredGames.name: Cauldron
coveredGames.title: This game has a set of roguelike mini games. I have spent 4 hours playing ONE of them. Needless to say, even if you only like one of them, it's worth it, I'm pretty sure there's turn based combat too.

coveredGames.name: Heidi's Legacy: Mountains Calling
coveredGames.title: What a breath of fresh air. It has that cozy feel of stardew and it's like, but is entirely it's own thing. Unique mechanics, interesting characters, and a charming art style that work well together.

coveredGames.name: The Witch's Bakery
coveredGames.title: Lovely little game about helping people heal by feeling their feels. Also with bread. And a little magic. Very cute, fun to play, lovely artistic style.

coveredGames.name: Squeakross: Home Squeak Home
coveredGames.title: Lovely little picross game, teaches you as you go, giving you tips. I can't get over the ratty eye boggling, it's so cute.

coveredGames.name: Penelope Pendrick and the Art of Deceit
coveredGames.title: I feel like I'm playing Nancy Drew all over again, if you're a fan of those, you'll likely enjoy this. Can get a bit challenging and require some paper, even on easy mode, but fun all the same.

coveredGames.name: Alabaster Dawn
coveredGames.title: I suck at combos, but they; while for me it was a bit futzy; were pretty easy to learn. Love the pixel art style while still having that 3D feeling to the movements. Was an pleasant surprise.

coveredGames.name: The Skin Stapler
coveredGames.title: A nice mix horror and comedy, with the two even managing to enhance each other at certain moments. Can sometimes be hard to find where to go though.

coveredGames.name: Strange Seed
coveredGames.title: Bit of a rough start, but I'm glad I powered through. Fight and eat creature, steal their parts as upgrades, like a tactical SPORE with a focus on combat and puzzles.

coveredGames.name: Ardenfall
coveredGames.title: Something about this game gave me the feeling of playing Oblivion for the first time despite being quite dissimilar. I think it was that childlike wonder of exploring a new world for the first time.

coveredGames.name: Voidling Bound: Creature Evolution Shooter
coveredGames.title: Loved this game! Creature collector/fighting/skill management game with weird lil critters to help retake the galaxy! Good soundtrack, good visuals, fun gameplay all round. Love collecting stuff!

coveredGames.name: Townseek
coveredGames.title: Demo: I found myself surprisingly addicted to this game. Trade between towns, complete quests, plant, dig, mine, and so much more. I'm glad I didn't look over this one.

coveredGames.name: Tears of Metal
coveredGames.title: Demo: This was a blast to play, combining your usual roguelike with army management. Music is to die for and I did in fact, die a lot.

coveredGames.name: Demon Tides
coveredGames.title: Demo: Gives massive Jak and Daxter vibes in the best way, while still having rather unique mechanics and having its own great energy to it. This game shines with it's platforming mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Void Jump VR
coveredGames.title: Lovely game atmosphere. A fun game with creative mechanics that unfortunately didn't work smoothly on my outdated device. Thankfully there's a demo! Go give it a shot. I see this being a huge hit!

coveredGames.name: Cave Crave VR
coveredGames.title: Absolutely stunning game. I have trouble getting into VR games, but this had me COMPLETELY hooked. Such an interesting story, lets you explore IRL caves, has some horror caves, fantastic.

coveredGames.name: VEIN
coveredGames.title: Is this game perfect? No. But for a game with only 2 developers? It's fun, it works (mostly), it's constantly updated, and it has a free demo. I see great things for this game as it develops.

coveredGames.name: Stoneshard
coveredGames.title: There's something special about beating a boss that's been giving you trouble with only 2 health remaining. Excited to play more, big fan of the vibes, just the right amount of luck involved.

coveredGames.name: Eclipsium
coveredGames.title: I hated(loved) this so much, it was dark, it was claustrophobic, it was uncomfortable in all the best ways for a game like this. A walking sim with such a great new mechanic to keep things fresh.

coveredGames.name: Fine Work: Act I
coveredGames.title: Such a neat way to do the rhythm portion of the game! Takes getting used to, but it's a fun new way to spruce up a timeless genre. Give the demo a shot!

coveredGames.name: Hozy
coveredGames.title: Cozy, satisfying, fun little game I had the pleasure of play-testing. Please do read the full linked review, this game is such a gem already and I fear it will be all I play once it's out.

coveredGames.name: Baby Steps
coveredGames.title: Honestly? This game is quite fun. Demo has a lot of personality, controls arn't difficult, but I can see where it could start to get harder as you progress. Story; whatever it is, quite funny so far.

coveredGames.name: Pool of Madness
coveredGames.title: Not my personal cup'o tea, but a very unique, interesting new way to play pool. Interesting mechanics, spooky vibes, and you get a gun. Beware falling fish. Give the demo a shot!

coveredGames.name: SherloCAT Nonogram Rio
coveredGames.title: Recommend full review, but here's the spark notes. Game is fun, has same feature I loved in the first game. But I have learned it uses generative AI. Not a deal breaker for everyone, so informational.

coveredGames.name: Letters to Arralla
coveredGames.title: It was a bit of a slow start, but once I started meeting people who had things to say and places to send me and so forth, I was quite sucked in. Cute mailing game with a whole lotta booty jigglin.

coveredGames.name: Woodo
coveredGames.title: Absolutely adorable. Simple gameplay, match the objects to the scene your in. But the story? Beautifully narrated, about a girl obsessed with tech being sent to a low tech village.

coveredGames.name: The RPG
coveredGames.title: Funny little take on the RPG genre. If you like poking fun at the Elder Scrolls, this will be a great time.

coveredGames.name: Gecko Gods
coveredGames.title: Such a cute little game, be a gecko, solve puzzles, eat bugs, be happy.

coveredGames.name: Teller's Duty
coveredGames.title: Fun little game about being a bank teller in hard times. Very "Papers, Please" or "That's Not My Neighbor" like gameplay.

coveredGames.name: Rekindled Trails
coveredGames.title: A joyful inventory management game with a lot of fun versions of the classic mechanic. Read my full review for details!

coveredGames.name: Beyond The Board
coveredGames.title: Honestly this demo felt like a full (though short) game. I'm excited to see what else they include moving forward! PS, you don't need to know how to play chess (or at the very least it gives hints)

coveredGames.name: ChromaGun 2: Dye Hard
coveredGames.title: Fantastic demo, big portal vibes, using color theory, interesting puzzle mechanics, and multidimensional nonsense! Puzzles get really hard, be warned.

coveredGames.name: Slip 'n Slime
coveredGames.title: Cute little puzzle game, lot of fun, not too complicated. Give the demo a try!

coveredGames.name: How Old is James?
coveredGames.title: Excellent game! It's a nice balance of challenging and rewarding. A lot of adapting as you switch between modes, interesting game play, some familiar and some newer to me. All good!

coveredGames.name: The Art of Reflection
coveredGames.title: A breath of fresh air! The vibes remind me a bit of Portal but calmer. It can get difficult at times, especially with how unique the mechanics are, but I'd at least try the demo out to get a feel.

coveredGames.name: Trifolium: The Adventures of Gary Pretzelneck
coveredGames.title: Not my personal cup of tea, but the game is very unique. A fun time for those with a sharper mind (or less tired) than mine.

coveredGames.name: Mind Diver
coveredGames.title: A unique puzzle game with investigation at its forefront, work to rebuild memories and get to the bottom of what really happened.

creators.name: Games that disclose they used AI

coveredGames.name: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
coveredGames.title: Placeholder art, undisclosed but later removed

coveredGames.name: The Alters
coveredGames.title: Removed AI "placeholder" art, but it was originally undisclosed

coveredGames.name: The Roottrees are Dead
coveredGames.title: AI art assets replaced with real art

coveredGames.name: Working Daily
coveredGames.title: NSFW puzzle game. Complete all puzzle levels (hints can be used at no cost) and deliver to all map locations. Deliver 3x to the purple map locations. ~5 minutes to 100%.

coveredGames.name: Nekopedia: Find Her Tail
coveredGames.title: NSFW hidden cat game with 13 levels. NSFW+Artbook DLCs required. Zooming out is needed for some cats. Hints available on a timer. Saving is buggy, try to complete in one session. ~30 minutes to 100%.

coveredGames.name: Family Time
coveredGames.title: This is like Pikmin but for obese ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and why is my ♥♥♥♥ hard

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY XIV Online
coveredGames.title: I opened up the game and as soon as I agreed to the EULA they molested me.

coveredGames.name: Fate/stay night REMASTERED
coveredGames.title: The critically acclaimed light novel-turned hentai game-turned visual novel-turned anime-turned manga-turned video game-turned gacha game-turned movie-turned back into hentai.

coveredGames.name: MECCHA CHAMELEON
coveredGames.title: Behold the latest friend slop, perfect to enjoy while watching video essays of why your step-dad is like Hitler and the devs are basically Captain America.

coveredGames.name: Mahjong Soul
coveredGames.title: james 1v1 me again i promise i wont sweat bro

coveredGames.name: Umamusume: Pretty Derby
coveredGames.title: They call me Mr. Hands out here

coveredGames.name: Zombie Assault: Resurgence
coveredGames.title: Ninja Kiwi remembered they make games that aren't just about monkeys and balloons after 11 years. I can't wait for this game to get gutted and replaced with a horrible mobile version!!!

coveredGames.name: Five Nights at Cobson's
coveredGames.title: Nature is healing.

coveredGames.name: Bongo Cat
coveredGames.title: Getting molested by a purple monkey wasn't enough. Now we have a cat on steam to bang while Gabe Newell counts your hours in the cuck chair.

coveredGames.name: Tenebris Somnia
coveredGames.title: An incredible journey into a dark and twisted lore-filled realm! Mixed with 2D 8-bit graphics and live-action cutscenes with a rich story. My absolute favorite indie game of 2026! 10/10

coveredGames.name: Graveyard Keeper 2
coveredGames.title: The best chill, cozy, and creepy game out there! Not just manage a glorious graveyard, but also build up relationships, trade, fish, build a zombie army, run zombie logistics, and more! 9/10

coveredGames.name: The Skin Stapler
coveredGames.title: I freakin' love this game! PS1 graphics, hilarious dialogue, outrageous voice acting, all within a dark aesthetic. I can't recommend this game enough who are into bizarre games! 10/10

coveredGames.name: Funnel Runners
coveredGames.title: A fun game to play with friends. Audio is a bit weird and actually messed with my computer. A small simple map, fun mechanics, the tornadoes are really cool. Needs work but worth a play. 7/10

coveredGames.name: The Mound: Omen of Cthulhu
coveredGames.title: Amazing graphics with an awesome premise! Solo was okay, playing with friends is where the game shines. After a few levels the difficulty scales too fast and there is no character progression. 8/10

coveredGames.name: Photomaly
coveredGames.title: A fun quick horror game. Classic playstation graphics with a fun premise of owning a photo studio, but your customers are not what they seem. Jump scares and spooks a' plenty. 8/10

coveredGames.name: Shift At Midnight
coveredGames.title: So much fun! I absolutely love the classic Playstation graphics and horror vibe. Gameplay is simple and fun. Don't let Dopplegangers leave the gas station, or else you'll be hunted. Go play it! 9/10

coveredGames.name: Subnautica 2
coveredGames.title: The best Subnautica yet! Made in Unreal Engine 5. Gorgeous graphics, rich lore, engaging gameplay. And the leviathans are EPIC! If your system can handle it, play this game! 9/10

coveredGames.name: Subnautica: Below Zero
coveredGames.title: A great addition to the Subnautica franchise. Excellent gameplay, beautiful biomes, and many more amazing creatures. Story arch is flat but picks up eventually. A must-play of any Subnautica fan! 8/10

coveredGames.name: Subnautica
coveredGames.title: A truly magnificent survival game! Even with thalassophobia, I am still truly amazed by the depth of gameplay, building, crafting, and awe moments this game has. Embrace the depths! 9/10

coveredGames.name: Retro Rewind - Video Store Simulator
coveredGames.title: An incredible nostalgic trip and one of my most favorite simulators. Run your own VHS rental store, expand, grow, and chuckle at the silly movie names. Highly recommended for any sim lover! 10/10

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Requiem
coveredGames.title: Incredible! RE7 horror mixed with action from RE5. Survive as Grace, sneaking and dodging zombies and take out zombie hordes as action-hero Leon. Amazing story. Awesome creatures! Top-tier! 10/10

coveredGames.name: REPLACED
coveredGames.title: My most anticipated indie game of 2026! This Bladerunneresque, pixel art game is taking 2.5D combat and storytelling to a whole new level! Smooth combat animations with cyberpunk tunes. Love it! 10/10

coveredGames.name: UMIGARI | ウミガリ
coveredGames.title: Bizarre yet amazing! Travel around with your boat, catching fish and helping those who need it. But something is off. And the fish are looking stranger... also there's a bit of horror. 8/10

coveredGames.name: The Last Caretaker
coveredGames.title: Surviving as a robot on a post-apocalyptic water world has never been this much fun! Travel around by boat visiting locations and salvaging what you can. Great gameplay, awesome concept. 9/10

coveredGames.name: Flotsam
coveredGames.title: A refreshing, chill post-apocalyptic water world survival game. Build up your floating town, mobile by boat while saving survivors all across a large map. A great game after a long day. 8/10

coveredGames.name: SILENT HILL f
coveredGames.title: Stunning graphics in the macabre world of Silent Hill in 1960's Japan. Excellent storytelling, creepy creatures, fun game mechanics. Definitely a must-play for any horror fanatic. 9/10

coveredGames.name: Waterpark Simulator
coveredGames.title: It's an absolute blast! The game to play if you ever wanted to run a waterpark. And in a game that doesn't take itself too seriously. Upgrade, build, and manage while saving customers. 8/10

coveredGames.name: Cronos: The New Dawn
coveredGames.title: The survival horror game of 2025! Cronos is both challenging and fun. The world is alive and the graphics are amazing. Bloober Team is killing it and I'm here for it. 9/10

coveredGames.name: Who's at the door?
coveredGames.title: Such a great anomaly game where you're paying close attention to changes in your apartment. Is any of it real? Maybe the person knocking on your door knows... 9/10

coveredGames.name: ORDER 13
coveredGames.title: Ever wanted to ship packages, dodge monsters, all so that your kitty can live its' best life? Well now you can. This game is awesome you should totally play it. 8/10

coveredGames.name: ILL
coveredGames.title: Can't wait to play it! Will be streaming it at www.twitch.tv/anarxix!

coveredGames.name: The Classrooms
coveredGames.title: Truly a wild and fun time! So many great moments while playing this game and escaping the creatures. And even when you beat it there is a custom mode to take things up a notch. 8/10

coveredGames.name: I SHALL NAME THE DEAD
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Hauntingly beautiful Brazilian interactive fiction rooted in folklore. Speak with the dead to uncover the secrets of their bones, as the Worm tries to influence and take over.

coveredGames.name: Deep Snow Delivery
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Death Stranding to its core, in a tiny tank piloted by two courier siblings, hauling supplies across a frozen valley to forge connections and push toward the towers beyond.

coveredGames.name: Diviner
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Messy but tons of fun. Tile-based buildcrafting and custom movesets riff on Mega Man Battle Network and Slay the Spire, even if rough edges elsewhere show. Worth playing.

coveredGames.name: DERELIKT
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Retro first-person survival horror that truly gets System Shock, Dead Space, and Alien: dim corridors, vent crawls, hacking, scarce resources, and perfectly paced tension.

coveredGames.name: The Hollowing
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - From the makers of Lorn’s Lure: a narrative horror flight sim in a brutalist megastructure, flying between comms towers to unravel what killed past technicians. Great voice acting.

coveredGames.name: Kero Quest 64
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Super Mario 64, full stop: triple jumps, backflips, and wahoos at a sunny seaside resort, with its own flavor from modern controls, lovely music, and a tongue for wild new moves.

coveredGames.name: The Secret of Weepstone
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - A hand-drawn love letter to AD&D. A weak party of misfits braves a trap-filled keep where one hit can mean permanent death and a +1 sword feels like Excalibur.

coveredGames.name: TRIP
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - From the maker of Carimara, TRIP is another gorgeous, compact game, this time about loops, packed with quirky characters and an uneasy mystery just beneath the surface. Instant buy.

coveredGames.name: Green Mist over Portland
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - A true puzzle sicko game. Green Mist Over Portland has you search databases, build timelines, and crack codes with pen and paper to trail a vanished MI6 agent and a deadly plot.

coveredGames.name: Inkblood
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - In the vein of Golden Idol, Inkblood has you scan crime scenes with a magnifying glass that sees into the past, solve puzzles from your carriage, and unravel an occult mystery.

coveredGames.name: Guns of Eschaton
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Guns of Eschaton is a first-person souls-like in an eldritch western where every shot counts: hit weak spots to stagger foes and customize each bullet in slow-to-reload chambers.

coveredGames.name: Militsioner
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - A giant cop watches your every move. Militsioner blends Deathloop-style looping days with immersive sim freedom, letting you find creative ways to escape your looming trial.

coveredGames.name: Radio the Universe
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Radio the Universe is jaw-droppingly gorgeous: dreamlike pixel art with light-touch instruction. You learn its world and systems by watching and tinkering, with fantastic gamefeel.

coveredGames.name: At Fate's End
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - From the makers of Spiritfarer, At Fate’s End pairs gorgeous animation and sharp family drama with twin-stick melee combat that lets you aim strikes past enemy defenses.

coveredGames.name: Ballistic.exe
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Like Cairn or Normal Golf Game, Ballistic.exe revels in real minutiae, trading shooter arenas for fussy ranges where hand placement, bullet drop, and ammo types all matter.

coveredGames.name: The Telwynium
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Retro point and click, 16 colors, zero hand-holding. Feels like a lost fantasy novel from the Wheel of Time shelf. From the Drifter writer.

coveredGames.name: Divine Frequency
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - GZDoom cosmic survival horror with a VHS filter and challenging boss fight duels. Nails the RE tension-to-action pipeline in its own grimy way.

coveredGames.name: IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - One-man artillery sim with fully diegetic controls. Ticker tape orders, paper maps, blast radius math. Most immersive war game with zero infantry.

coveredGames.name: 4x4 in a Furniture Store
coveredGames.title: Demo Impressions - Exactly what it says. Jeep. Ikea. Physics. Fun and silly Challenges. Like Baby Steps but with a winch.

coveredGames.name: Flame, Forest & Flood
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - a fun strategy puzzle game to play against friends. We are having such a great time with it. PLUS you get to build your own garden to show off to others.

coveredGames.name: Tom the Postgirl
coveredGames.title: Well Well Well...that was one wild ride. The humor is funny, the story is...interesting, but the gameplay felt lackluster. I was expecting a point-and-click puzzle game, but there are no real puzzles.

coveredGames.name: Pibcremental
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - a cute wholesome incremental, but I'm not 100% sure what we are working towards other than growing the tree.

coveredGames.name: Honeycomb: The World Beyond
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - The keys and mechanics are not very intuitive, and it feels a little unfair to be attacked without any type of defense. But the story is good and the world is beautiful.

coveredGames.name: Phonopolis
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - the world is beautiful and the story keeps you captivated, but the puzzles don't necessarily feel like puzzles. You are mostly just moving things till they click without reference

coveredGames.name: Ten Bells
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - enjoyed it so much, we decided to keep playing until we got all of the anomalies. The story is tragically horrific and the game definitely gets you on jump scares.

coveredGames.name: 7 Nights with Vroombi
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - ever dream of playing as a roomba? Now is your chance! Help keep the house clean of debris, dust, blood, ...and ritual circles? Oh and don't let the monster catch you.

coveredGames.name: Remnant: From the Ashes
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - not sure I am fully understanding the story and the game keeps kicking me from the host party - BUT the gameplay loop is fun and challenging.

coveredGames.name: All Eyes on Me
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - a great game for those who enjoy cozy games but are looking for something a little more creepy. The game loop is fun and keeps you on your toes. Recommend!

coveredGames.name: Helix: Descent N Ascent
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - a logic puzzle game set in a beautiful world. I am really enjoying my time with this game and it is interesting to combine different abilities and find where they are applicable

coveredGames.name: The Mortuary Assistant
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - Full Review to Follow: Creepy, eerie, scary. All with an interesting story that makes you want to replay it for each ending. It has me interested in a career shift.

coveredGames.name: Carnaval Marbles
coveredGames.title: Just buzzing along - Full Review to Follow: an interesting take on a deckbuilder roguelike. Slow to start, but satisfying when you see the combos light up the table.

coveredGames.name: Woodo
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - a cozy wholesome game about taking sometime away from our electronics and enjoying the country side. It's incredibly satisfying finding each piece and returning color to the world

coveredGames.name: Paranoia Place: Escape Together
coveredGames.title: Just buzzing along - an interesting gameplay loop that relies on working together, knowing where you are and making little noise. Will probably only playthrough each area once, but I still recommend.

coveredGames.name: Fofumia
coveredGames.title: Just Buzzing Along - full review to follow. If you enjoy cozy games, with cute cat like creatures, with a hidden object/organization gameplay - this is the game for you. Highly recommend!

coveredGames.name: Photomaly
coveredGames.title: Just buzzing along - full review to follow. Owning your own photography shop has never been so fear inducing. The jump scares got me, the story was strange, but there was something missing.

coveredGames.name: Monk Took Book
coveredGames.title: Just buzzing along - really enjoying this cozy organization game with my player two! Highly recommend so far!

coveredGames.name: Ori and the Blind Forest
coveredGames.title: Took me awhile to get used the the controls, but overall I enjoyed the gameplay and the story. The world is absolutely beautiful!

coveredGames.name: over the hill
coveredGames.title: Just buzzing along - I cannot recommend this one enough, especially with a friend(s). This game is a cozy, open world exploration, designed for you to take your time and enjoy the game. Recommend!

coveredGames.name: Where the Veil Thins
coveredGames.title: On the Hive's Watchlist - Demo Approved! The card battling was fun and you'll be able to choose a card to add to your deck after each battle. The overall game, however, needs some polish.

coveredGames.name: Fear Tall Grass
coveredGames.title: On the Hive's Watchlist - Demo Approved! Beautiful art style and creature collector. Plays like a board game, an auto-battler, and creature collector. Feels well balanced. Recommend!

coveredGames.name: Nippets: A Hidden Object Game
coveredGames.title: A cozy wholesome hidden object game where each object found and each puzzle completed tells a short story. Highly recommend picking this one up for any hidden object or puzzle lover!

coveredGames.name: Light of Atlantis
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation - Demo Approved! The world is unique and the dialogue is punny. I enjoyed the puzzles, it definitely feels like it will be a more linear metroidvania. Worth it to wishlist!

coveredGames.name: Feather's Edge
coveredGames.title: On the Hive's Watchlist - Demo Approved! I wish you had free movement in the overworld and the puzzles were a little more lenient. But it is still an interesting and unique metroidvania.

coveredGames.name: Spirits of Baciu
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation - Demo Approved! The art style, the music, the world just pull you in. I wasn't expecting such a puzzle heavy game, but I really enjoyed it. Highly recommend.

coveredGames.name: Buckshot Roulette
coveredGames.title: A uniquely fun roulette game to be played with friends. The lobbies aren't the greatest and playing with two gets boring rather quickly. Still a fun game!

coveredGames.name: The Dark Queen of Mortholme
coveredGames.title: Absolutely loved this short story. I just wanted more. More combat, more of her story. Which I am chalking up to a good thing. Highly recommend checking it out!

coveredGames.name: DORONKO WANKO
coveredGames.title: An adorably cozy, short and sweet game that is well worth the free price and an hour of your time.

coveredGames.name: Mirealle
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation - Demo Approved! I am ready for this game to crush me. Beautiful atmosphere and art, interesting story, and thoughtful puzzles. The controls and mechanics could be improved.

coveredGames.name: Bad Magpie
coveredGames.title: On the Hive's Watchlist - Demo Approved! If you loved Untitled Goose Game, you'll love Bad Magpie. I am ready for the story to make me feel all the emotions.

coveredGames.name: Inkblood
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation-Demo Approved! I can't begin to tell you how much I loved this game. The art, the mechanics, the story, the atmosphere, everything was *chef's kiss*. Highly highly recommend!

coveredGames.name: Apple Crumble
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation-Demo Approved! I love Happy Broccoli Games - the voice acting, the art, both great but I have no idea what the story is and the POV camera is a little too intense. Zoom out?

coveredGames.name: Aberrate Inc.
coveredGames.title: On the Hive's Watchlist - Demo Approved! What looks to be a cute cozy puzzle game, quickly turns into a puzzle heavy thinking game. The later levels offered some real challenge.

coveredGames.name: Militsioner
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation - Demo Approved! Do I know what I'm doing? No. But am I enjoying the journey? Yes. Art style and graphics are gorgeous, the story wants me coming back for more.

coveredGames.name: Hillthorn
coveredGames.title: On the Hive's Watchlist - Demo Approved! A game that combines murder mystery and a card game. I was confused at first, but the more you play, the more hooked you become when things click into place.

coveredGames.name: Hellmate - Chess Deck Builder
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation - Demo Approved! This felt like a really great take on both chess and deckbuilders. I found myself incredibly locked in - however, I do hope it offers more of a challenge.

coveredGames.name: FLASK
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation-Demo Approved! I'm not the biggest fan of auto-battlers. Flask might have changed that for me. The art style is beautiful and you can tell how much care went into the game.

coveredGames.name: Talystro
coveredGames.title: Buzzing with Anticipation - Demo Approved! I don't like math. Math does not like me. And yet, Talystro joined us together in holy matrimony. This isn't casual play, you'll have to use your brain.

coveredGames.name: Hypnospace Outlaw
coveredGames.title: It tries to hook your nostalgia by providing content on what the internet in the early 2000s looks like. It feels like you are still part of the world with their updates and storytelling.

coveredGames.name: Crashout Crew
coveredGames.title: Crashout Crew is an addictive co-op game that can also be played solo. It gives you an adrenaline rush from finishing orders within a time limit, with difficulty increasing as you play.

coveredGames.name: Police Stories
coveredGames.title: It's a good game if you expect it to be a game where you have to be patient and not kill anyone. It's short enough not to make you feel bored, and the smaller rooms make it easier to beat the level.

coveredGames.name: You And I
coveredGames.title: You And I might give a nice experience if you played it once or twice and got the "good" endings, although you might be disappointed if you end up with the subpar one, which is far more common.

coveredGames.name: Cat Over Here!
coveredGames.title: Finding the cats is not too stressful since there are some "hints" on their whereabouts, and you can always use catnip to lure them out.

coveredGames.name: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School
coveredGames.title: The puzzles are at the right difficulty, and there are plenty to keep you entertained. The new additions of the explorable map make way for collectible and side quest hunting, which was fun to do.

coveredGames.name: Reaplaced
coveredGames.title: It's a perfect Halloween game for those who enjoy reading murder mysteries and don't want to be spooked for the occasion.

coveredGames.name: Finding Cats
coveredGames.title: The cats' placement makes them easy to spot, although the large map makes it harder to find. The quality isn't the best, but the quantity alone makes up for it.

coveredGames.name: CONTROL Ultimate Edition
coveredGames.title: As someone who likes SCP, I naturally come to like the setting. It's all mysterious and spooky; the conversation sometimes doesn't make sense, but the curiosity keeps me going.

coveredGames.name: Wavekin
coveredGames.title: It feels like a mini Metroidvania with very little progression and a small map, although you'll find it fun just to explore the area and find the collectibles.

coveredGames.name: Froggonit: Prologue
coveredGames.title: What captivates me when playing this game is the sense of accomplishment of exploring everything that the map has to offer, including the collectibles and secret areas.

coveredGames.name: Lysfanga: The Time Shift Warrior
coveredGames.title: It does a good job mixing hack-and-slash with puzzle. The variety offers a lot of flexibility to solve the level, and the puzzle itself has a lot of leeway for non-hardcore players to finish.

coveredGames.name: Curious Paws: hidden objects
coveredGames.title: The images look sharp, and they still stay that way even after being zoomed in. The objects blend well into the background and are drawn in the same style as the background, making them harder to find

coveredGames.name: Socrates Jones: Pro Philosopher
coveredGames.title: As a game that tries to mimic Ace Attorney series, this game gives a similar feeling to it. There is no exploring the map, and the debate was made simpler.

coveredGames.name: Geometric Sniper
coveredGames.title: Geometric Sniper does a fresh take on the hidden object genre. You need to find a target through your sniper scope to kill them instead of finding numerous objects on the screen.

coveredGames.name: It Takes Two
coveredGames.title: It Takes Two is a high-quality game that can only be played with 2 people. The scenery looks great, and the quality is top-notch.

coveredGames.name: PlateUp!
coveredGames.title: PlateUp! is a chaotic restaurant simulation game that can be played with up to 4 people. Its gameplay becomes vastly different when played singleplayer and co-op.

coveredGames.name: Beyond: Two Souls
coveredGames.title: Beyond Two Souls is a nice narrative game with a darker story. You'll switch controls between Jodie and the invisible entity, Aiden, from time to time depending on the situation.

coveredGames.name: The Bookwalker: Thief of Tales
coveredGames.title: The Bookwalker is a game for those who enjoy reading a story and exploring the world. It's fun figuring out the connection while trying to min-max everything.

coveredGames.name: Polterguys: Possession Party
coveredGames.title: A fun PvP game where you cause mischief to everyone while trying to survive.

coveredGames.name: Cats of the Song Dynasty
coveredGames.title: The decision to use a real-life painting makes the art in Cats of the Song Dynasty unique while still offering an enjoyable hidden cats game.

coveredGames.name: Wavetale
coveredGames.title: Exploring the world in Wavetale while listening to the music is really nice. There are times when I feel bored, but the game's short length makes me tolerate it.

coveredGames.name: Gurumin: A Monstrous Adventure
coveredGames.title: It's nice if you play it on the lower difficulties. Enemies are scaled down, and you can cheese most of the gameplay without worry. However, the game becomes too hardcore at the greatest difficulty.

coveredGames.name: Monument Valley
coveredGames.title: It's not a game that you enjoy because of the difficulty, but rather due to the game mechanics.

coveredGames.name: Hidden Folks
coveredGames.title: Hidden Folks is an enjoyable hidden object game, provided that you have the right mindset to enjoy playing it instead of rushing it.

coveredGames.name: BubbleBeast DigiDungeon
coveredGames.title: The music is pleasing to hear, and the gameplay was alright. It can be hard to find out how to improve your score and get a higher grade in each level, but you just need to survive to finish the game.

coveredGames.name: United heist
coveredGames.title: As a puzzle game, there might be times when you need to use your brain to solve the puzzles, but they are usually not that difficult to solve as long as you communicate the clues properly.

coveredGames.name: Along the Edge
coveredGames.title: Along the Edge is a mediocre visual novel, one where your choice matters. Its visuals look great—they have so many unique cutscenes that differ almost at every dialogue and every state.

coveredGames.name: Balatro
coveredGames.title: Balatro can be a hit or miss for some people. Those who like cards and maths will like it, while those who hate repetitiveness will hate it.

coveredGames.name: Tukoni: Prologue
coveredGames.title: Tukoni: Prologue is a game that you play to see its visuals rather than its puzzles. The environment looks nice with the various plants drawn on the background.

coveredGames.name: In Sink: A Co-Op Escape Prologue
coveredGames.title: While puzzles are on the easier side, they are designed in a way that makes it easy to pick up the clues and figure out what you are supposed to do without giving away the answer.

coveredGames.name: Life After Magic
coveredGames.title: Life After Magic is a romantic visual novel with mainly slice-of-life content. Since the pairs are mostly female, it caters mostly to those who are content with this kind of content.

coveredGames.name: Illusion Carnival
coveredGames.title: Illusion Carnival is a game that is best played for the experience. Its flashing and bright light might not be suitable for some people, but if you can get past that, you'll be able to enjoy it.

coveredGames.name: Cryptmaster
coveredGames.title: Everything that it offers feels fresh, and the riddles will leave you thinking. It's a perfect game for those who like riddles, even more so if they prefer the harder ones.

coveredGames.name: FIND ALL: Halloween
coveredGames.title: FIND ALL: Halloween might be short, but its increased difficulty adds more challenge to the game. Moreover, the hint system will help you in case you are stuck, further reducing the difficulty.

coveredGames.name: Mars Power Industries Deluxe
coveredGames.title: Although the puzzles might be brain-numbing sometimes, they are still enjoyable. Not for those who seek challenging puzzles, but casual gamers who prefer an easier one will enjoy it just fine.

coveredGames.name: Project Starship
coveredGames.title: It was fun and was designed to be replayed several times. The numerous bullets might be difficult to dodge for non-skilled gamers, but some upgrades can help to mitigate the difficulty to some extent.

coveredGames.name: Unboxing the Cryptic Killer
coveredGames.title: It requires you to communicate well with each other and have the thinking skills to put two and two together. If this sounds interesting to you, you'll surely enjoy this game.

coveredGames.name: Silktrails 2: Cats in the grove
coveredGames.title: It can look rough around the edges, but it still gives the same enjoyment as other hidden object games. It's for those who want to be more overwhelmed with clicking objects rather than finding them.

coveredGames.name: Silktrails: Cats in the grove
coveredGames.title: Silktrails: Cats in the Grove might be short, but the gameplay is similar to other hidden object games. It looks rough around the edges, though.
