coveredGames.title: FMV choice-and-escape about a teen sent to an internet-addiction camp, based on real cases. Branching paths, QTEs, and investigation hit as social drama more than puzzles. Steam score is Very Positive

coveredGames.name: Buckshot Roulette
coveredGames.title: A tense round of shotgun Russian roulette against a demonic dealer, later against other players. Items twist the odds each round, and the dread is the hook. Steam score is Overwhelmingly Positive.

coveredGames.name: House Flipper
coveredGames.title: A first-person renovation sim: clean filth, knock walls, paint, and furnish wrecked homes until they feel new. The cleanup loop is repetitive, messy, and oddly soothing. Steam score is Very Positive.

coveredGames.name: Pile Up!
coveredGames.title: Chill strategy-builder: stack card-like buildings on tiny islands to grow population—until a risky placement blows it all up. Cute and replayable, with a sandbox mode. Steam score is Mostly Positive.

coveredGames.name: Empires of the Undergrowth
coveredGames.title: Ant RTS meets nest-building: dig tunnels, manage workers, and steer swarms with pheromones against rival colonies and giant insects. Deeper than a typical bug sim, too. Steam score is Very Positive.

coveredGames.name: Cities: Skylines II
coveredGames.title: City-builder sequel that goes deeper on traffic, economy, and scale than the first Skylines. Overall Steam score is still Mixed from a rough launch, but recent reviews are Mostly Positive after patche

coveredGames.name: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege
coveredGames.title: Tactical 5v5 shooter: breach walls, gadget ops, one-shot tension each round. Steam Very Positive (~82%). Peak with a squad and patience for the curve; skip if toxic lobbies and live seasons burn you o

coveredGames.name: Street Fighter™ 6
coveredGames.title: Modern fighting game: Modern/Classic controls, World Tour, and a deep ranked scene. Steam Very Positive (~82%). Best on-ramp into competitive FGs; skip if DLC roster grind and season swings annoy you.

coveredGames.name: HELLDIVERS™ Dive Harder Edition
coveredGames.title: Top-down twin-stick co-op: friendly fire, stratagems, and brutal Democracy drops. Steam Very Positive (~90%). Classic roots of Helldivers 2; skip if you want modern 3D spectacle or a busy player base.

coveredGames.name: HELLDIVERS™ 2
coveredGames.title: Satirical 4-player co-op shooter: drop in, call stratagems, die for Democracy. Steam Mostly Positive (~75%). Peak with friends who love chaos; skip if live-service swings and review drama turn you off

coveredGames.name: Broken Arrow
coveredGames.title: Modern real-time tactics: deck-build armies, 5v5 multiplayer, deep unit customization. Steam Mixed (~54%). Great for Warno/Wargame fans who tolerate rough edges; skip if cheats and jank kill your mood

coveredGames.name: Subnautica 2
coveredGames.title: Underwater survival sequel (EA): new ocean, 4-player co-op, bases and craft still growing. Steam Very Positive (~91%). Jump in if you love Subnautica vibes unfinished; wait if you need a complete stor

coveredGames.name: Subnautica: Below Zero
coveredGames.title: Arctic ocean survival sequel: dive icy biomes with more story and landside bases. Steam Very Positive (~90%). Solid for Subnautica fans chasing more; skip if you want the original awe and scale.

coveredGames.name: Subnautica
coveredGames.title: Alien ocean survival: craft, dive, and base-build while wonder flips into dread. Steam Overwhelmingly Positive (~97%). Must-play for explorers; skip if deep-water fear or sparse guidance will wreck yo

coveredGames.name: PlateUp!
coveredGames.title: Co-op restaurant roguelike: cook, seat, layout, and automate kitchens across runs. Steam Very Positive (~95%). Overcooked fans craving deeper strategy will love it; skip if short party chaos is enough

coveredGames.name: Overcooked! All You Can Eat
coveredGames.title: Remastered co-op cooking anthology: Overcooked 1+2 plus extras, 4K polish. Steam Mostly Positive (~73%). Great couch buffet; skip online-first play—connection complaints still drag the score.

coveredGames.name: Overcooked! 2
coveredGames.title: Chaotic co-op cooking sequel: kitchen mayhem with online play and wilder levels. Steam Very Positive (~90%). Best party upgrade over Overcooked; skip if yelling-over-orders already burned you out.

coveredGames.name: Overcooked
coveredGames.title: Chaotic couch co-op cooking: chop, plate, serve under ticking timers as kitchens go haywire. Steam Very Positive (~90%). Peak friendship stress-test; skip if you want polished online co-op or calm sol

coveredGames.name: It Takes Two
coveredGames.title: Co-op adventure (GOTY vibes): two players team up through wild, shifting levels and gags. Steam Overwhelmingly Positive (~95%). Ideal couch/online date night; skip if you hate forced co-op or want sol

coveredGames.name: Football Manager 27
coveredGames.title: Football management sim: club control, tactics, rebuild after FM26. No full Steam score yet (launches Nov 10). Promising rebound for series fans; wait if UI/match-engine gripes still worry you.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE
coveredGames.title: Pixel FF evolved: turn-based break/resonance combat, Vision crystals of past heroes. Overwhelmingly Positive (~97%). Must-play for classic FF fans; skip if you dislike turn-based or HD-2D style.

coveredGames.name: Minecraft Dungeons II
coveredGames.title: Sequel dungeon crawler: new Sift dimension, tougher fights, co-op loot runs. Mixed (~67%). Fine with friends if you liked the first; skip if more of the same or launch roughness bugs you.

coveredGames.name: Minecraft Dungeons
coveredGames.title: Minecraft dungeon crawler: co-op loot runs, simple Diablo-lite combat, cute blocky vibes. Very Positive (~90%). Great casual fun with friends; skip if you want deep builds or hardcore challenge.

coveredGames.name: NARAKA: BLADEPOINT
coveredGames.title: Melee battle royale: parries, hero skills, grappling-hook parkour across a wuxia arena. Mostly Positive (~73%). Best if you love close-range skill fights; skip if cheaters or long queues put you off.

coveredGames.name: Apex Legends™
coveredGames.title: Hero battle royale: slick movement, legend abilities, tight squad play. Mixed (~68%). Still excellent gunfeel if you like BR; skip if cheaters, balance churn, or grind fatigue wear you down.

coveredGames.name: Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced
coveredGames.title: Open-world crime sandbox: sharp story, Los Santos chaos, endless Online grind. Very Positive (~88%). Still a classic for story and freedom; Online can feel toxic and grind-heavy if that puts you off.

coveredGames.name: Phantom Blade Zero
coveredGames.title: Dark wuxia action RPG: kung-fu punk style, flashy combat, 30+ weapons, cinematic bosses. Very Positive (~93% CN). Must-play for stylish melee fans; skip if floaty hits or heavy PC demands bother you.

coveredGames.name: Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six® Extraction
coveredGames.title: Tactical co-op PvE shooter: Siege operators vs alien Archaeans, extract or die. Mixed (~66%), very quiet lobbies now. Fun with a fixed squad if you like tense PvE; skip if you need lively matchmaking.

coveredGames.name: Green Hell
coveredGames.title: Amazon survival sim: parasites, infection, nutrition, story mode plus co-op. Very Positive (~85%). Deep and tense if you love hardcore survival; skip if co-op bugs or motion sickness put you off.

coveredGames.name: Black Myth: Wukong
coveredGames.title: Mythic action RPG: staff combat, boss gauntlets, stunning folklore spectacle. Overwhelmingly Positive (~96%). Must-play for bosses and visuals; skip if linear levels or thin builds bug you.

coveredGames.name: Neighbors: Suburban Warfare
coveredGames.title: Chaotic party brawler: smash rival houses, trap yours, frying pans and seagull bombs. Early Access, Mixed (~65%). Best with friends for loud laughs; skip solo or if EA roughness bugs you.

coveredGames.name: Golden Light
coveredGames.title: Horror FPS roguelike: eat weird weapons in a meaty prop-hunt hellscape. Procedural spooks, dark comedy. Very Positive (~91%). Great for weird indie horror fans; skip if gore-absurdism turns you off.

coveredGames.name: Pyramid Game
coveredGames.title: Odd social-sim satire: grind math/vocab jobs, then dice/roulette up a live wealth ladder. Mixed (~50%, tiny sample). Clever class experiment; thin if you want real game systems.

coveredGames.name: Wild Terra 2: New Lands
coveredGames.title: Medieval sandbox MMO: no fixed classes, deep crafting, pets, PvE/PvP risk zones. Mixed (~62%). Great for slow hardcore life-skill grind; skip if you want polished modern combat or a busy player base.

coveredGames.name: Spin Hero
coveredGames.title: Pixel roguelike: slot spins decide fights while you craft icon synergies. Mostly Positive (~73%). Fun if you like high-RNG Lucky Landlord vibes; skip if uneven balance or gambling combat bugs you.

coveredGames.name: Nocturnal
coveredGames.title: Flame-sword 2D action through dark fog: light paths, puzzles, foes. Stylish, ~2-3h, Chinese support. Clever fire-light loop, thin combat. Solid short mood piece.

coveredGames.name: Ball Bugz
coveredGames.title: I'm not a fan of most incremental games, but this felt pretty decent for those that are into that.

coveredGames.name: Rogue Monster Rush
coveredGames.title: Pretty fun, grindy roguelite TD. Overstays its welcome eventually due to the grindy and repetitive nature of it. While it has some different monsters to obtain, I felt dettered from experimenting.

coveredGames.name: Acid Planet
coveredGames.title: Abandoned in EA. Actually very fun. In the vein of Deep Among the Swarm and Thronefall. Poor level variety. Long-term progression is over too fast - I lost interest after a few hours.

coveredGames.name: Spires of Morosith: Gossamer Sundered
coveredGames.title: Decent mazer with a fair bit of complexity. Later stages sort of devolve into hard puzzles though. Pretty repetitive (after a few hours, you've seen the show). Still, I had some fun with it.

coveredGames.name: Gnomes
coveredGames.title: Narrowly recommended. It's a decent mazing tower defense however every wave means repositioning your entire defense. While it seems like there are many options in a run, the variety exhausts quickly

coveredGames.name: Rats, Bats, and Bones
coveredGames.title: Excellent clone of Dungeon Warfare (2D version of Orcs Must Die! -minus controlling a hero). Banger synthwave soundtrack. A quality release that will forever live in Dungeon Warfare's shadow.

coveredGames.name: X-Morph: Defense
coveredGames.title: Brilliant! Tower Defense with a bit of Shmup thrown in. Both aspects are handled well. Mazing is also possible. Has co-op too!

coveredGames.name: Warstone TD
coveredGames.title: Excellent standard tower defense and the first one to pop up on Steam that could rival Fieldrunners 2.

coveredGames.name: Unstoppable Gorg
coveredGames.title: Very narrowly recommended. Perhaps I just have a soft spot for this one because of its wonderful thematic presentation. It's quite difficult trial & error and could allow for more player freedom.

coveredGames.name: Tower Tactics: Liberation
coveredGames.title: This is a nice roguelike + deckbuilder + Tower Defense mashup. A single terrible music loop requires muting though.

coveredGames.name: Tiny Tactics
coveredGames.title: Decent mazer. If you miss placing heroes as towers (like Warcraft 3 custom games) which all come with their own unique skills and synergies, this is for you. Permanent upgrade system could be better.

coveredGames.name: Thronefall
coveredGames.title: In some ways this is an easier, less strict Bad North. Primarily a TD but you run around during waves fighting with your hero. Pretty interesting game. 7/10.

coveredGames.name: Stronghold Defenders
coveredGames.title: Quite novel yet very straightforward to understand and play. It's short and I have some caveats, but overall I enjoyed this.

coveredGames.name: Spirits of the Hellements - TD
coveredGames.title: Fun, intricate mazer.

coveredGames.name: Revenge of the Titans
coveredGames.title: Extremely hectic TD with a simple yet charming art style. It feels like defending a base in an RTS game.

coveredGames.name: Refactor
coveredGames.title: Far from a favourite, but it's quite interesting to engage with. Worth a try.

coveredGames.name: Prime World: Defenders
coveredGames.title: Very grindy. Levelling up cards/towers is part of the draw. If you don't like the sound of that then avoid this.

coveredGames.name: Orcs Must Die! 3
coveredGames.title: The orcs must fly! Another solid entry in a fantastic series. This one includes a rogue-like mode which is quite fun (but could use more variety).

coveredGames.name: Orcs Must Die! 2
coveredGames.title: Same great formula with small improvements. This time with co-op! Highly recommended.

coveredGames.name: Orcs Must Die!
coveredGames.title: This series is excellent. Third person shooter + Tower Defense. Highly recommended. The sequels have a good co-op implementation but this one is single player.

coveredGames.name: Kingdom Rush  - Tower Defense
coveredGames.title: Decent mobile game that feels pretty overrated if judged as a PC game. It's alright.

coveredGames.name: Hexguardian
coveredGames.title: This roguelike tile-laying TD was a lot of fun. Eventually I concluded that it could be better balanced and tweaked, but the journey to that conclusion was an enjoyable one.

coveredGames.name: Heretic's Fork
coveredGames.title: Excellent if you enjoy Survivor Roguelites. It combines this with tower defense and deckbuilding. Nice variety of easy listening metal music and cool dark 90's internet theme.

coveredGames.name: GROSS
coveredGames.title: A short mazer TD + First Person Shooter. In no way comparable to greats like Orcs Must Die! but still a fun time.

coveredGames.name: Fieldrunners 2
coveredGames.title: For the longest time this was the best standard Tower Defense game on Steam. A lot of variety on the levels (some mazing, some puzzle, some standard). Tries to dupe you into spending money for unlocks

coveredGames.name: Dungeon Warfare 2
coveredGames.title: I was disappointed with the changes in the games systems compared with the first game. Even despite that, it blows most other tower defense games away.

coveredGames.name: Dungeon Warfare
coveredGames.title: Orcs Must Die! as a standard top-down tower defense game. Excellent!

coveredGames.name: Dungeon of the ENDLESS™
coveredGames.title: Unique roguelike defense game which incorporates resource management you might experience in tabletop euro games. Very difficult.

coveredGames.name: Digs TD
coveredGames.title: It's a fun mazer. Some drawbacks though: lack of enemy variety. A single music loop. Progression could be more interesting.

coveredGames.name: Defender's Quest: Valley of the Forgotten (DX edition)
coveredGames.title: Simple but interesting. I enjoyed this raw indie.

coveredGames.name: Deep Among the Swarm
coveredGames.title: A bit like Creeper World. It's fantastic! held my interest for around 40 hours. Eventually the path to the endgame got a bit too samey and repetitive. The rogue-like aspect could be improved though.

coveredGames.name: Creeper World 3: Arc Eternal
coveredGames.title: Unique take on tower defense. You're trying to contain the flood of liquid. You build nodes everywhere to power turrets and fight for area control, salami slicing your way to victory.

coveredGames.name: ReStory: Chill Electronics Repairs
coveredGames.title: (Soft rec) An awesome chill electronics repair simulator with an interesting cast of characters and an intriguing overarching storyline. Only cons atm are poor achievements and game breaking bugs.

coveredGames.name: Minami Lane
coveredGames.title: (Soft rec) A wonderful little street management game, very cute, very wholesome, very chill.

coveredGames.name: Unfair Flips
coveredGames.title: (Soft rec) Despite the unfairness of the gameplay loop, the game is really chill and easy to just sit and increment while listening to something else.

coveredGames.name: Sticky Business
coveredGames.title: (Soft rec) A cute wholesome game about running a sticker store. Sticker making system doesn't allow full customization, but does allow for creative creations despite some limitations.

coveredGames.name: Spray Paint Simulator
coveredGames.title: (Soft rec) Does a lot of what powerwash simulator does well, adds paper and tape to make spray painting make sense, but adds a little exploration to the world, though it could've been leveraged more.

coveredGames.name: PowerWash Simulator 2
coveredGames.title: (Solid rec) They've done it again, with a fantastic chill simulator game with a new story line and hundreds of hours of content to clean and surely more to come.

coveredGames.name: SuchArt: Genius Artist Simulator
coveredGames.title: (Soft rec) A have it your way art simulator where you can truly do no wrong. Fun gameplay, interesting tales and characters, very chill.

coveredGames.name: Stray
coveredGames.title: (Solid rec) An absolutely amazing heartfelt story about a cat navigating a post apocalyptic world full of robots.

coveredGames.name: Spirit of the North
coveredGames.title: (Soft rec) A beautiful game with an expansive world, but the ambiguous story plays out with limited aim winds up with recurring aimless wandering.

coveredGames.name: A Short Hike
coveredGames.title: (Solid rec) A fantastic mountain adventure where you explore and interact with a varied cast of characters, the only noteworthy downside is the lack of an in-game map.

coveredGames.name: TOEM: A Photo Adventure
coveredGames.title: (Solid rec) A fantastic photography adventure game that plays out with quests and quirky characters.

coveredGames.name: Alba: A Wildlife Adventure
coveredGames.title: (Solid rec) A fantastic island adventure where you capture photos of animals and save a village with your friends.

coveredGames.name: Little Kitty, Big City
coveredGames.title: (Solid rec) A fantastic city adventure game where you wander around as a cat looking for their way back home.

coveredGames.name: Alpaca Stacka
coveredGames.title: (Soft rec) Cute and short little island adventure game where you collect Alpaca and bring them home to mom.

coveredGames.name: Dispatch
coveredGames.title: Really great choice-based game. Every single episode is peak and I never got bored once. The voice cast is absolutely stacked too, making the characters so good. Highly recommend playing it!

coveredGames.name: Among Us
coveredGames.title: With a full squad, this game never gets boring in my opinion. Plus, when you start modding, it gets so much more fun. It is easily one of the best games to play with your friends.

coveredGames.name: Poppy Playtime
coveredGames.title: First 3 chapters are so good! But 4 and 5 feel like boring filler, except for the cool endings. Devs haven't added achievements since February. Only buy chapters 1 to 3, the rest aren't worth it.

coveredGames.name: My Friendly Neighborhood
coveredGames.title: Super underrated! One of the best mascot horror games ever. It is like Sesame Street but the puppets got evil. I beat the game multiple times and am definitely looking to replay it again.

coveredGames.name: Escape the Backrooms
coveredGames.title: About 60% through and loving it. Low replayability, but levels are super interesting. Friends and I got totally skill-issued on the hardest diff, but if you want a story Backrooms game, this is it!

coveredGames.name: Cyberpunk 2077
coveredGames.title: Honestly didn't expect to enjoy Cyberpunk this much. Thought I'd get bored but got totally hooked. The story is easily in my top 3, and I'm planning to 100% complete the game. Highly recommend!

coveredGames.name: Dead as Disco
coveredGames.title: 6 hours in between the demo and main game just playing Infinite Disco! This game is incredibly underrated. No regrets buying this at all, especially knowing I'll get to the story mode eventually.

coveredGames.name: Little Nightmares
coveredGames.title: I get a yearly obsession with Little Nightmares. The world is so good and easily in my top 3 games. The atmosphere and DLC are incredible. It tells a masterclass story without any dialogue.

coveredGames.name: Outlast
coveredGames.title: There's something about Outlast 1. I keep coming back to it, tried speedrunning and now going for 100% on Insane. The story is incredible and the game still holds up 13 years later. Must play.

coveredGames.name: Outlast 2
coveredGames.title: Crazy game, beat it in one sitting! Definitely harder than Outlast 1 and the achievements are tough, but I still want to 100% it. The story is so good and the religious horror vibe is amazing.

coveredGames.name: Big Walk
coveredGames.title: Easy GOTY contender, worth a play through with any friend group, and there are discords to get groups together if you don't have a group to get with.

coveredGames.name: REPLACED
coveredGames.title: Pretty fun game and the pixel art work is gorgeous. It feels like it goes just a bit too long but it's still a good game and story overall, I recommend.

coveredGames.name: Lovish
coveredGames.title: Cute tongue-in-cheek platformer that pokes fun at NES type games and stories. A decent and fun platformer all around with a ton of secrets.

coveredGames.name: Gravity Circuit
coveredGames.title: Fantastic Mega Man inspired game where you punch instead of shoot, easy recommend for anyone looking to play something in that vein!

coveredGames.name: Future Knight
coveredGames.title: Really well done platformer/shooter. The old art style really adds a lot and the music is also immaculate. Underrated gem

coveredGames.name: Halo: Campaign Evolved
coveredGames.title: Halo: CE is a masterpiece in itself, so this is only about the new additions. The graphics are pretty and some new interesting skulls have been added. The new levels are aight. Just needs multiplayer!

coveredGames.name: Mashina
coveredGames.title: Chill stop-motion game that is pretty to like at. Everything was made by hand and all the animations and characters are super cute. Extremely relaxing game about digging.

coveredGames.name: Denshattack!
coveredGames.title: Tony Hawk Pro Skater made by anime nerds. Bright and fun art, banging soundtrack, and fast-paced gameplay. As everyone favorite website Polygon says "This is the best 3D Sonic game ever made."

coveredGames.name: You are Peter Shorts
coveredGames.title: You play as Peter Smash Bros and you fight other Peter Smash Bros in this metroidvania style game. I give it a Peter out of 10.

coveredGames.name: TR-49
coveredGames.title: A super unique puzzle game with a cool sci-fi narritive. Piercing together the story as you uncover more documents gripped me more than I thought it would.

coveredGames.name: PRAGMATA
coveredGames.title: In what seems to be a rarity nowadays, a AAA company created a new IP that has a good story AND good gameplay? The hacking to shooting game flow is perfect.

coveredGames.name: Absolum
coveredGames.title: Beat-em-up and roguelite hybrid that has some beautiful artwork, animations, and music. Each of the different characters is unique and fun to play, and the game is co-op as well!

coveredGames.name: Agent 64: Spies Never Die
coveredGames.title: A wonderful continuation of classic N64 shooters, it wears its influences on it's sleeves for better or for worse. The visuals and gunplay feel amazing, but some of the levela can drag on a bit.

coveredGames.name: METAL GEAR SOLID - Master Collection Version
coveredGames.title: What else there to be said about this game, it's a classic that popularized the modern stealth-action game. Sail the seven seas if you hate Konami, it's a must play.

coveredGames.name: Fugaz
coveredGames.title: A puzzle-metroidvania hybrid with some simple puzzles and plenty that will give you some "oooohhhh" moments. Make sure to play in windowed mode!

coveredGames.name: CICADAMATA"
coveredGames.title: Neon White with modern Marathon asthetic. Great movement, great soundtrack, great game Tear flesh from bone.

coveredGames.name: BABBDI
coveredGames.title: Fascinating little art game that takes place in near-empty butalist style city. Unsettling and disturbing, play it if you are looking for something quick or a world to get lost in. And it's free!

coveredGames.name: How Many Dudes?
coveredGames.title: [b]Love this![/b] A great light weight game that can be run along side AI I2V or anything else for that matter. intricate details for micro managers/BIS runs, Zany naming and ideas.

coveredGames.name: Deck of Haunts
coveredGames.title: Dungeon Keeper meets MTG. Simple to get the hang of. Diverse complex strategies. Huge replayability. High potential for expansions. A must on my list, regardless of the reasonable price.

coveredGames.name: Amberspire
coveredGames.title: A thoughtful and meditative game on the nature of cities, growth, and community. I've had a wonderful time on Amber and will visit again from time to time. Full review at the link.

coveredGames.name: Hades II
coveredGames.title: A game that builds on the structure of the original while polishing, smoothing, and expanding the core of that experience. Enjoyed it a lot. Check out my review on the site.

coveredGames.name: StarVaders
coveredGames.title: A fascinating and compelling blend of deckbuilding, turn based tactics, and space invaders. Absolutley brill. Check out my full review on my site.

coveredGames.title: Great with friends, but I wish there were more maps and tougher ghosts. It isn't really too scary but it is fun

coveredGames.name: Heartopia
coveredGames.title: I do really like the game, i would describe it as mix of animal crossing and sims. It is quite slow paced to progress so if you like fast progress it's not for you. calm, relaxing fun with friends

coveredGames.name: Ryse: Son of Rome
coveredGames.title: While I was not a fan of the writing, I did really enjoy the combat and execution system. Not to mention, this game is gorgeous for an early 2010s game. Recommend if you’ve got an afternoon.

coveredGames.name: NINJA GAIDEN 3: Razor's Edge [NINJA GAIDEN: Master Collection]
coveredGames.title: This might be sacrilegious but I really enjoy NG3RE for what it is, does it fall short in some areas yeah but to outright hate this game is disingenuous. NG3RE is definitely a game you should play :D

coveredGames.name: DRAGON BALL GEKISHIN SQUADRA
coveredGames.title: Its a moba-lite but honestly I find myself enjoying the experience pretty darn well. The characters variety is enough to keep you engaged and have fun...beware this is partly a gacha :D

coveredGames.name: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin
coveredGames.title: Is it crazy to say this for me is the best Fromsoft has ever done....No because this game is fantastic. All ds2 haters are not real people, and I bet they use Celsius instead of Fahrenheit :D

coveredGames.name: MELTY BLOOD: TYPE LUMINA
coveredGames.title: Melty Blood is easy to pick up but so so so hard to master....all the time spent in the lab is worth every moment of time that slips away. Any fighting game fan would enjoy some Melty, scrubs included

coveredGames.name: Borderlands 2
coveredGames.title: Probably the most mid shooter looter I've ever played....I don't really fw most weapons and the characters are just okay personality wise. B2 is the most 7/10 low enjoyment i've ever had :/

coveredGames.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS
coveredGames.title: They really managed to make the boost kind of formula really fun and free again......well the Shadow levels at least. Switching engines totally wrecked the Sonic portion of the game...unfortunate :(

coveredGames.name: Sonic Adventure 2
coveredGames.title: This is Sonic at his peak and sadly SEGA will never truly recognize the love people including myself have for this entry in the series. Please get the mod manager, this game is infinite fun and joy :D

coveredGames.name: AI LIMIT
coveredGames.title: This game is pretty fun and has some pretty crazy weapons to try out.....the enemies and bosses can be meh at times and a lil jank but that does not take away from the enjoyment I had while playing :D

coveredGames.name: Blood Vial
coveredGames.title: Such a great game. I'm highly looking forward to seeing some content updates and possibly even co-op. The small amount of content is insanely addictive and has very satisfying movement.

coveredGames.name: Serious Sam II
coveredGames.title: Go into this one completely blind, it's great. IYKYK. Combat is standard here, the focus is much more on the visual design and overall fever dream world building. Still great fun.

coveredGames.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem
coveredGames.title: A love letter to fans of the original games and an apology for Serious Sam 3, this game delivers on both fronts. Highly recommended if you love blowing ♥♥♥♥ up.

coveredGames.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Conviction™
coveredGames.title: This game gets a lot of hate, much like Hitman Absolution, but I can't help but love the black sheep of a franchise. Overall, this game nails the dark, edgy vibe and has smooth combat.

coveredGames.name: Romestead
coveredGames.title: Not a huge fan of this genre, to be honest, but I love the aesthetics of this game, and I love the clever ways that the developers have found to negate the usual monotony of building tasks.

coveredGames.name: Cargo Hunters
coveredGames.title: I really find this game super fun and find myself saying just one more after each run until its 7 hours later and I can barely keep my eyes open. Beware this is really addicting, play this game.

coveredGames.name: Sniper Killer
coveredGames.title: One of the best indie titles I have ever played, there is so much to love here it completely towers over the questionable ending. If you're looking for something original, play this.

coveredGames.name: Dead Rising 2: Off the Record
coveredGames.title: One of those games I could play endlessly. Incredible soundtrack, amazing design and co-op, plus enough charisma to carry the entire series' writing on its back.

coveredGames.name: DOOM 64
coveredGames.title: While I haven't finished it yet, I've found it to be really well designed and a refreshing take on the original that stands alongside the official id titles. I'd honestly say I prefer it to DOOM.

coveredGames.name: Serious Sam HD: The First Encounter
coveredGames.title: Some of the best co-op I’ve experienced in a long time. Please play this if you haven’t — it’s one of the greats, and it’s beyond hilarious. 𝘈𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏, 𝘈𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏𝘏 𝘺𝘰𝘶𝘳𝘴𝘦𝘭𝘧.

coveredGames.name: The Wolf Among Us
coveredGames.title: Honestly, I’m conflicted. The game starts well-written and tightly paced, but Episode 3 onward buries the main plot under subplots and random hype moments. Overall it's meh.

coveredGames.name: Fallout: New Vegas
coveredGames.title: Arguably one of the greatest action RPGs ever made, with near-infinite replayability thanks to its massive mod scene, fantastic music, incredible writing, and a level of quality still untouched today.

coveredGames.name: STAR WARS™ Empire at War - Gold Pack
coveredGames.title: RTS games usually overwhelm me, but this one just clicks. The atmosphere is great, the economy system really stands out, and there are plenty of mods to choose from.

coveredGames.name: (the) Gnorp Apologue
coveredGames.title: This is the standard of what an incremental upgrade game should be. Cute little gnorps working toward a simple goal, smash the rock until it breaks open! Good choice making needed to beat.

coveredGames.name: White Knuckle
coveredGames.title: A very "speed runner" type game requiring a high skill cap to beat, not for everyone! Knows what it wants to be and does it well. Climb quickly. Great aesthetics, great movement, rewards good play.

coveredGames.name: Megabonk
coveredGames.title: Abandoned by Developer fun but flawed 3D take on vampire survivors. Meme heavy, lots to unlock, and feels great. unfinished and still buggy, left unbalanced. Custom soundtrack is great!

coveredGames.name: 9 Kings
coveredGames.title: Currently in Early Access auto battling rogue-like card based army building. Requires strategy. Great for a quick game here and there. Very addictive. Well made. I heap my praise on this.

coveredGames.name: Cthulhu Saves the World
coveredGames.title: A forgotten RPGmaker game. Basic? Yes. But the spritework, music, and dialogue are all charming and well done. Humorous and wacky. Help Cthulhu and his friends save the world!

coveredGames.name: Vital Shell
coveredGames.title: Robots Playstation aesthetics Dreamy Drum&Bass music Arena Style arcade roguelike autoattacking shooter. Think "asteroids" with bosses, unique characters and upgrades. Short but brilliant game.

coveredGames.name: Phucker in the Ashes
coveredGames.title: 11/10 The best game ever made. EVER. Only the enlightened would understand. Ryukaze Terra is an inspirational American HERO! Best absurdist humor. Clever writing. Visual Novel for the ages.

coveredGames.name: Secret Agent Wizard Boy
coveredGames.title: Harry Potter AND 007 James bond? Yes! This game lovingly made by a family developer team, recreates those early harry potter games vibe. Wacky sandbox physics are fun, explore and unlock fun secrets!

coveredGames.name: Nubby's Number Factory
coveredGames.title: Numbers are powerful. Launch nubby, the eponymous hero of the game, and use him to make big numbers. This rogue-like peggle inspired game hits that late 90's - early 2000's CG wacky computer game vibe

coveredGames.name: LEGO® Batman™ 3: Beyond Gotham
coveredGames.title: It's pretty awesome! So far I think it's the best one out of the trilogy. -character list and voice acting is amazing -the story is great 9/10

coveredGames.name: LEGO® Batman™ 2: DC Super Heroes
coveredGames.title: Overall, it’s a pretty fun ride! -The open world hub is a nice step and can be a lot of fun. -Story, sound and visuals is pretty solid and make for a well rounded outing. 7/10

coveredGames.name: LEGO® Batman™: The Videogame
coveredGames.title: basic tale of villains escaping Arkham Asylum. - great visuals and is stunning to look at. - great to see the film joke about Batman’s expensive lifestyle using Lego pieces. - ton of villains 8/10

coveredGames.name: Don't Escape Trilogy
coveredGames.title: Instead of fleeing danger, you’re setting traps, securing rooms, rationing supplies, and making decisions that can change the ending. It’s refreshing and makes every choice feel meaningful. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Buckshot Roulette
coveredGames.title: sitting in a dark room at 3 AM trying to calculate probabilities like some dude with a gambling addiction. 10/10 experience.

coveredGames.name: Papers, Please
coveredGames.title: This has definitely been an entertaining and weird game as the story keeps you playing and the game loop is beautifully done with morally complex but simple tasks that keep you engaged. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Celeste
coveredGames.title: An outstanding 2D platformer where you help a young girl named "Madeline" survive her inner demons while she's on her way to the top of Celeste Mountain. It's a surprise masterpiece! 10/10

coveredGames.name: Until Then
coveredGames.title: Until Then is a 2-D interactive Visual Novel with a compelling coming of age story that is both strange and relatable, it's definitely worth a playthrough. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Dead as Disco
coveredGames.title: An absolute banger! It's Harmonious features will leave you in awe and it's custom mode allows you to fight the bad guys to your own imported music. A Masterpiece indeed. 10/10

coveredGames.name: ANTONBLAST
coveredGames.title: Pure action with high humor and big explosions! Its a cartoonish Wario-Land Inspired game that is extremely charming as it is fast-paced. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Hades II
coveredGames.title: A definite upgrade from Hades 1 as the art is even more breathtaking, its characters are captivating, and the combat is fast and fun. Hades 2 is one of the best roguelite experiences ever. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Hades
coveredGames.title: Hades is an addicting action roguelike with remarkable varied combat and progression. It has incredible characters and story from start to finish. 9/10

coveredGames.name: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus!
coveredGames.title: Absolutely incredible visual novel with twist and turns that will leave you captivated and it doesn't just excel in one area; it delivers on every single level! 10/10

coveredGames.name: Death's Door
coveredGames.title: Its a solid mix of Zelda-style puzzles and for those looking to scratch that itch with classic dungeon combat, it has an essence of Dark Souls level designs. 9/10

coveredGames.name: BALL x PIT
coveredGames.title: Ball x Pit is pure addictive genius and the core activity is an arcade-style brick-breaking mode that just pulls you in and keeps you there while time fly's by. 10/10

coveredGames.name: The Binding of Isaac
coveredGames.title: The times I've played the game have shown me a some thrill of the unexpected. Mostly, it's due to the dozens upon dozens of ridiculous items that you're able to use. Fantastic arcade shooter 9/10

coveredGames.name: Path of Exile 2
coveredGames.title: I was never a fan of Path of Exile as its overly complex systems always scared me off but I gave it a shot with Path of Exile 2 and happy to say it's quite enjoyable and looks stunning! 9/10

coveredGames.name: KINGDOM HEARTS III + Re Mind (DLC)
coveredGames.title: The story has it's highs and low's but It still has the heart and Disney magic that I’ve come to love from the series. It was a joy to return and the world's were great and interesting to play. 10/10

coveredGames.name: KINGDOM HEARTS HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue
coveredGames.title: Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter features three solid entries into the Kingdom Hearts series and although there’s plenty of setup for the future, what’s here is mostly fantastic. 10/10

coveredGames.name: KINGDOM HEARTS -HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX-
coveredGames.title: Kingdom Hearts 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX is a beautiful collection of 6 titles. There's 4 full games and a collection of cutscenes that retell the game events from the games 358 days and Re: Coded. 10/10

coveredGames.name: METAL GEAR SOLID - Master Collection Version
coveredGames.title: The Master Collection gives you a chance to appreciate the series evolution going from MGS 1 that was on the PS1 to MGS 2 that was on PS2. It's packed with content and also comes with MGS 3! 9/10

coveredGames.name: MOUSE: P.I. For Hire
coveredGames.title: It's a delightful adventure through a cartoon, noir-fueled type environment. It has hand drawn levels with rubber hose animations and It's definitely worth playing just for the vibes alone. 9/10

coveredGames.name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
coveredGames.title: Are you ready to waste another fifty hours of your life killing dragons and stealing cutlery from strangers? Skyrim draws you into a finely crafted fictional pace that's packed with content. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Scritchy Scratchy
coveredGames.title: Honestly, I didn’t expect to fall for a game that simulates buying scratch cards, but Scritchy Scratchy made me both laugh and grab my mouse like I'm a slot-machine addict. It's a fun pick-up. 9/10

coveredGames.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley
coveredGames.title: I’ve been playing it for almost 2 years and can genuinely say that I never get bored. The mechanics are fun and there's tons of Disney characters and quest related stuff to do in the game. 10/10

coveredGames.name: One Finger Death Punch 2
coveredGames.title: If you are looking for a game to play in short bursts or just to have a little bit of fun, definitely get One Finger Death Punch 2. It's simplicity at its finest with fighting stick figures. 10/10

coveredGames.name: One Finger Death Punch
coveredGames.title: It's a game where stick figures beat each other up with their bare hands, or a mix of different weapons that includes a lightsaber. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Cult of the Lamb
coveredGames.title: you’re a lamb sacrificed to four gods but upon death, you find a locked fifth god and they grant you a second lease on life; all you need to do to obtain it is start a cult in their name. 9/10

coveredGames.name: Gears 5
coveredGames.title: It hits that sweet spot between brutality and cinamatic momentum. The Lancer still shreds and is beautiful and the encounters are designed to keep you moving instead of turtling everywhere. 9/10

coveredGames.name: DAVE THE DIVER
coveredGames.title: Dave the Diver is a gorgeous underwater adventure RPG experience that has you diving into the depths of the ocean while also maintaining/managing a sushi restaurant. -works great on Steam Deck 10/10

coveredGames.name: Dead Cells
coveredGames.title: Dead Cells is a very well-done roguelike. It always has something to work toward whether you're unlocking items, skills or progressing further into the game. -Works great on Steam Deck 10/10

coveredGames.name: Rogue Legacy 2
coveredGames.title: Rogue Legacy 2 is basically Rogue Legacy 1, except it's also a tiny bit better in every single way! It is an excellent sequel! -works great on steam deck 9/10

coveredGames.name: Sleeping Dogs: Definitive Edition
coveredGames.title: Sleeping Dogs provides a very fun open-world type of gameplay experience and has a 10+ hour campaign (with additional time for side missions). works wonderful on the steamdeck. 10/10

coveredGames.name: Escape From Duckov
coveredGames.title: This is an Escape from Tarkov parody, except it's completely offline and you replace the scary mercenaries with little ducks. Your general goal is to complete missions, kill, loot and extract. 9/10

coveredGames.name: Mega Man Star Force Legacy Collection
coveredGames.title: This collection contains the entire Star Force trilogy, seven games when you add up all their different versions that fans and first-timers to enjoy. 8/10

coveredGames.name: R.U.S.E.™
coveredGames.title: The story is a lot more deep and interesting than I would expect from a game like this. It's a wartime RTS at it's core and deception and intelligence are the tools you need to pull off a win. 9/10

coveredGames.name: High On Life
coveredGames.title: It's that Rick and Morty type humor style High on Life is more about jokes and weird vibes than deep combat. The gunplay is fine, the levels are fun, but the talking is constant. 8/10

coveredGames.name: Forza Horizon 6
coveredGames.title: "Forza Horizon 6 has not skipped a beat, and it runs like a titan. Aesthetically, it’s the best-looking and best-sounding game Playground has produced to date." Works great on steamdeck! 10/10

coveredGames.name: 007 First Light
coveredGames.title: James Bond's video game return is a delight from start to finish. It's quite literally the best Bond has been since GoldenEye! -works on steam deck with low/medium settings 9.5/10

coveredGames.name: LEGO® Batman™: Legacy of the Dark Knight
coveredGames.title: Legacy of the Dark Knight embraces its Lego building blocks more than any other game in the series. There's charm overload at every turn, with cutscenes that are often hilarious as silliness. 10/10

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY VII
coveredGames.title: FF7 wrestles with Cloud's fractured sense of self, loss & sacrifice, though the Lifestream leans pantheistic. Corneo/Wall Market's sleaze is clearly framed as villainous, not endorsed. Worth playing.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY III
coveredGames.title: FF3's Warriors of Light restore balance to a world threatened by darkness & void, echoing Scripture's light vs. darkness imagery. Classic, clean, and free of romance or crude content. Recommended.

coveredGames.name: Welcome To Everdell
coveredGames.title: Everdell is a charming, peaceful game of building community among woodland critters. Beautifully wholesome, family-friendly, and totally free of crude or objectionable content. Highly recommended.

coveredGames.name: FANTASY LIFE i: The Girl Who Steals Time
coveredGames.title: Wholesome, cozy fun - crafting, friendship & light adventure across a charming island. No romance or crude content to worry about. Relaxing, family-friendly, and easy to recommend and super fun co-op.

coveredGames.name: Sunderfolk
coveredGames.title: Sunderfolk's heroes selflessly defend their village from corruption, fostering real community & cooperation with friends. Wholesome, family-friendly, free of crude content. Great for the whole family.

coveredGames.name: KINGDOM HEARTS -HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX-
coveredGames.title: KH 1.5+2.5 delivers the series' finest arc: Sora's journey of friendship, identity & light overcoming darkness. Emotional, wholesome, and free of crude content. A must-play. Highly recommended.

coveredGames.name: Satisfactory
coveredGames.title: Echoes Genesis' call to steward creation & subdue the earth through diligent work. Relatively peaceful, family-friendly, free of romance or overly crude content. Wholesome and recommended.

coveredGames.name: Enshrouded
coveredGames.title: Enshrouded shows humanity's greed for power corrupting the world, birthing the Shroud. As Flameborn, your light pushes back darkness & rebuilds what's lost. No romance, no crude content. Recommended.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY II
coveredGames.title: FF2's Emperor forges a pact with Hell for power, a warning against pride and tyranny. Themes of sacrifice and rebellion against evil ring true. No romance or crude content. Recommended.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY
coveredGames.title: FF1's light vs. darkness echoes Scripture (John 1:5). Four Warriors of Light restore hope to a broken world—no romance, no crude content. Clean, classic, and easy to recommend.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles
coveredGames.title: FFT bravely critiques corrupt religious power while still affirming truth, integrity & sacrifice through Ramza. A mature, thought-provoking story—recommended for discerning Christians.

coveredGames.name: FINAL FANTASY XIV Online
coveredGames.title: As a Protestant Christian, I love how FFXIV's story centers on self-sacrifice and hope, not romance/sex. Some lewd community chatter exists but is easily ignored. Highly recommend!

coveredGames.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
coveredGames.title: Medieval Bohemia so real you smell the mud and blood. A brutal sim-RPG where every swing, meal, and misstep matters. Punishing by design, gloriously so. An 87 earned. Live filthy, die honest.

coveredGames.name: Solo Leveling: ARISE OVERDRIVE
coveredGames.title: They ripped out the gacha and let it breathe. Watch Jinwoo evolve into a walking nightmare—no slot machine bolted on. Not flawless, but the version that finally respects fans. Level up.

coveredGames.name: Granblue Fantasy: Relink
coveredGames.title: Gorgeous action-RPG with a charming story, a roster to drown in, and an endgame that refuses to die. Flashy, satisfying, endlessly deep. Assemble your party and don't come up for air.

coveredGames.name: Resident Evil Requiem
coveredGames.title: The best Resident Evil since RE4—an 88 and 2026's highest-rated game. Enough action to race your pulse, enough horror to dread every door. Grotesquely beautiful. Play it in the dark.

coveredGames.name: Red Dead Redemption 2
coveredGames.title: A slow, mean, gorgeous elegy for the outlaw age. Arthur Morgan is gaming's finest tragic corpse. Deliberate to a fault, stronger for it. It doesn't end—it haunts you. Non-negotiable.

coveredGames.name: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
coveredGames.title: They resurrected the best Assassin's Creed and it still floats like a dream. New visuals, same salt-and-blood pirate soul. An 84 on Metacritic, earned. Hoist the black flag.

coveredGames.name: 007 First Light
coveredGames.title: Young Bond before the smugness set in. Smooth-talk, bluff, or break a jaw—it respects all three. Goes genuinely dark. Not spotless, but a spy fantasy with real teeth. Slip in, slip out.

coveredGames.name: Gothic 1 Remake
coveredGames.title: They stitched a 2001 corpse back together in UE5 and it lives. Grim, harsh, unbothered by your comfort—just like the original. Newcomers beware; veterans, welcome back to the colony.

coveredGames.name: Tears of Metal
coveredGames.title: Musou carnage meets roguelite addiction. Grab 3 friends, a Scottish battalion, turn hordes into red mist. A little repetitive solo, an absolute bloodbath in co-op. Early Access, already vicious.

coveredGames.name: Forsaken Realms: Vahrin's Call
coveredGames.title: 7 devs, 12 years, zero AI—and you feel the love in every handcrafted inch. A classless RPG where you build any monster you want. Rough in spots, gorgeous in soul. Bury a weekend in it.

coveredGames.title: A unique space sim with deep character customization and a cool world to explore. The learning curve is steep and it barely holds your hand, but sim fans who enjoy space themes may find plenty to like

coveredGames.name: Once Human
coveredGames.title: A solid pick if you enjoy PvP, grinding, and seasonal progression. The PvP is a highlight, and while there are optional gacha-style cosmetics, they never got in the way of the experience. YES WMT!

coveredGames.name: Arena Breakout: Infinite
coveredGames.title: More than a Tarkov clone—Arena Breakout Infinite has its own arcadey identity. Great gunplay, easy to pick up, highly replayable, and packed with tense fights and rewarding extracts. YES WMT!

coveredGames.name: ARC Raiders
coveredGames.title: ARC Raiders completely pulled me back into gaming. The gunplay, atmosphere, and constant tension are ridiculously addictive. I haven’t been this hooked on a game in a long time. YES WMT!

coveredGames.name: Pax Autocratica
coveredGames.title: Like Helldivers, Battlefield, Palworld and SimCity rolled into one. Surprisingly polished for Early Access, runs great, looks fantastic, and already has a ton of potential. YES WMT!

coveredGames.name: MECCHA CHAMELEON
coveredGames.title: One of the best buys of 2026, it should be winning game of the year. I love this game, and jumping into playing it, is my biggest thing for most games, is being able to jump in when i don't have time.

coveredGames.name: Balatro
coveredGames.title: Game I've been playing to jump into a game quick and wanna play a random-slop kind of game, Have it on mobile, and steam. Love me a good roguelike game, this is on the top, if not the TOP for me.

coveredGames.name: Left 4 Dead 2
coveredGames.title: Yet another old game, that I've had amazing time playing on the steam deck. It was weird a first, but got the hang of it, and i can still use the workshop modding easily as well. 9/10 game

coveredGames.name: Tales of Symphonia
coveredGames.title: Childhood game, been playing it a bunch on the steam deck, amazing game great story. Most likely my start into most RPG/Solo Games of the like!

coveredGames.name: Trove
coveredGames.title: Amazing game, great events while still maintaining the base game of where to go and how to play, love jumping back into the game for hours, being able to pick it up whenever i want and start playing!

coveredGames.name: Sonic Adventure 2
coveredGames.title: Amazing game, with a great port to PC, worth putting hours into for the transformation fun-ness, almost like an idle game you can play to "Upgrade" your chao's and things of that nature!

coveredGames.name: Devil May Cry 5
coveredGames.title: Been an amazing games so far, Ive owned it for upwards of 5~ years, and only got around to playing it because of how good it runs on the steam deck, i haven't played such a good game on the Steam deck

coveredGames.name: Schedule I
coveredGames.title: Playing it a few times with friends, just being able to do whatever i want like a true Dru6 Deala. Fun all around and replayable while still being updated!

coveredGames.name: Raft
coveredGames.title: 100% MUST play the story is amazing, solo or with others, raft is Definity a pick up and play a few times, one of my favorite survival type games, I should do a playthrough on it, haha

coveredGames.name: Palworld
coveredGames.title: I've been playing this before the 1.0, But after being able to play at my own speed with friends, the game feels much better paced. Glad i touched bases with it again, because a new favo game!

coveredGames.name: Tall Trails
coveredGames.title: The perfect game to take and play, good controls, soothing visuals, really relaxing.

coveredGames.name: BALL x PIT
coveredGames.title: Ball x Pit blends arcade challenge with strategic progression, rewarding experimentation and learning through failure. Its striking visuals and engaging loop shine despite unclear mechanics, UI bugs,

coveredGames.name: Kenshi
coveredGames.title: Don't really respect your time ; however I'm too much attracted by the universe to not recommend it. Nothing really compares to it today. Full of bugs, too.

coveredGames.name: Kabuto Park
coveredGames.title: Kabuto Park captures childhood wonder through bug hunting, candy trading and playful battles. Its coherent design and nostalgic charm shine, despite a short campaign and weak controller support.

coveredGames.name: Promise Mascot Agency
coveredGames.title: It gets a bit trivial after the beginning learning priorities to make money, and a tad repetitive, but the originality of the world more than makes up for it.

coveredGames.name: The Roottrees are Dead
coveredGames.title: A mystery game with a nostalgic feel that will draw you in without holding your hand. Excellent tutorial, you'll think about this game between your runs.

coveredGames.name: Mewgenics
coveredGames.title: A bit dark, but a must have for all the strategy players out there. The mix between genetics and roguelike is a successfull one.

coveredGames.name: Rain World
coveredGames.title: A successful metrovania that manages to deliver a unique experience through its gameplay and game design.

coveredGames.name: Void War
coveredGames.title: A game that doesn't reinvent the wheel, following directly in the footsteps of the FTL series with a Warhammer-style aesthetic. Excellent.

coveredGames.name: RimWorld
coveredGames.title: More than ten years after its early access release, the game has stood the test of time. A classic that pioneered the colony-building genre.

coveredGames.name: Slay the Spire 2
coveredGames.title: The same as the first one, but overhauled.

coveredGames.name: The Isle Tide Hotel
coveredGames.title: The Isle Tide Hotel — Strong performances & cinematic presentation create a creepy and memorable FMV experience. While the gameplay can feel repetitive and linear at times, there are multiple endings.

coveredGames.name: Erica
coveredGames.title: Great acting, filmography, imagery, and music. If you have the patience you may enjoy the interactivity of choosing things. I found it tedious so watched it as a movie on YouTube.

coveredGames.name: Luminary
coveredGames.title: Beautiful fantasy adventure with impressive visuals, music, and satisfying combat. Battles feel skill-driven and rewarding, making player decisions matter more than chance.

coveredGames.name: Zombieville USA 3D
coveredGames.title: Fast-paced and addictive zombie action with stylish cartoony gore and rewarding upgrades. Difficulty ramps up quickly, making every run feel tense and satisfying.

coveredGames.name: State of Decay 2: Juggernaut Edition
coveredGames.title: Strong survival atmosphere and base-building mechanics, though the emotional attachment to characters makes every loss hit hard. Still an engaging zombie survival experience.

coveredGames.name: RoboCop: Rogue City
coveredGames.title: Once the upgrade system clicks, the game becomes a satisfying action-heavy power fantasy. While some encounters allow subtlety, charging in with overwhelming firepower is far more fun.

coveredGames.name: Kind Words (lo fi chill beats to write to)
coveredGames.title: Amazingly chill and positive experience centered around relaxing in your room, listening to lo-fi music, and exchanging supportive letters with other players.

coveredGames.name: Horizon Zero Dawn™ Complete Edition
coveredGames.title: Engaging adventure with a unique world, rewarding progression system, and meaningful side quests that expand the lore and atmosphere of the setting.

coveredGames.name: Her Story
coveredGames.title: Strong mystery driven by a clever video-search investigation system. Organizing interview clips into a coherent story is engaging, though interaction can feel confusing at times.

coveredGames.name: Gauntlet™ Slayer Edition
coveredGames.title: Fun modern take on the classic with satisfying character progression and distinct playstyles. Great for quick action sessions when there’s not enough time for a longer game.

coveredGames.name: Firewatch
coveredGames.title: Beautiful and distinctive visual style paired with relaxing exploration and strong environmental storytelling. The emotional finale leaves a lasting and haunting impression.

coveredGames.name: Dungeon Keeper™ 2
coveredGames.title: Creative dungeon-building and strategic base management still hold up well. Older graphics and interface limitations can occasionally make interaction frustrating.

coveredGames.name: Dear Esther: Landmark Edition
coveredGames.title: Visually beautiful and haunting exploration adventure that tells its story through the environment. Progression can occasionally feel unclear, but the atmosphere is exceptional.

coveredGames.name: Cibele
coveredGames.title: Creative blend of live-action video, laptop interaction, and an in-game MMO used to tell a personal and emotional story. Uncomfortable at times, but memorable and distinctive.

coveredGames.name: Arcade Paradise
coveredGames.title: Stylish atmosphere and enjoyable arcade mini-games create a great overall vibe. Progression through the laundromat management can feel grind-heavy, but the arcade payoff is satisfying.

coveredGames.name: AI Roguelite 2D
coveredGames.title: Interesting early experiment in AI-driven procedural game generation. The system produced creative results, though some generated imagery became unsettling and the gameplay lacked long-term engagement

coveredGames.name: Carcassonne - Tiles & Tactics
coveredGames.title: Excellent digital adaptation of the board game with strong strategy and endless replayability. Challenging AI encourages experimentation until you’re ready for multiplayer matches.

coveredGames.name: Bloodshore
coveredGames.title: Enjoyable FMV presentation with strong movie-like moments. Gameplay is limited, but players looking primarily for an interactive film experience may still enjoy it.

coveredGames.name: Sid Meier’s Civilization® VI
coveredGames.title: Rewarding strategic depth once the systems begin to click. Large-scale coordinated offensives and late-game nuclear warfare make progression especially engaging.

coveredGames.name: ACE COMBAT™ 7: SKIES UNKNOWN
coveredGames.title: Impressive visuals and a large variety of aircraft. The depth of the flight combat systems may be especially rewarding for players willing to invest time mastering them.

coveredGames.name: Cyberpunk 2077
coveredGames.title: Strong exploration, satisfying combat, and outstanding cinematic presentation after the major patches. More explorable interiors would have made the world feel even richer.

coveredGames.name: Rebel Inc: Escalation
coveredGames.title: Took a few levels to fully click, but the balance of resource allocation and military strategy became highly engaging. Some repetition, though insurgent combat stayed compelling.

coveredGames.name: Jessika
coveredGames.title: Strong interface built around the perspective of using a laptop. Interesting mystery and atmosphere, though the beginning can feel confusing and overall progress can be difficult to track. Originally

coveredGames.name: They Are Billions
coveredGames.title: Excellent freedom for defensive layouts, base building, and offensive strategy. A unique twist on resource-management games, though progression can feel punishing even on easy difficulty.

coveredGames.name: Godot Engine
coveredGames.title: My favorite open source game engine. Functional, powerful and without bloat. Also there are no predatory pricing practises. You own your code. You own your game. If you can, make a donation to Godot!

coveredGames.name: Aseprite
coveredGames.title: I honestly love this program. It's fast, small in size yet very powerful. I use it for everything from pixel art, to simple edits, to format conversions. It's very well designed and thought through.

coveredGames.name: RPG Maker MZ
coveredGames.title: Similar to RPG Maker MV with QoL updates but lacks innovation. Like in MV, I dislike that MZ still uses Chromium Electron instead of being native. Buy this if you don't own MV.

coveredGames.name: RPG Maker MV
coveredGames.title: A lot of great games were made in this engine. It is "battle tested" and has ton of community resources to help you make your dream RPG. Very easy to grasp too. I highly recommend it to anyone!

coveredGames.name: GameMaker
coveredGames.title: Their new pricing model is great. All features are available to use in the free version. I recommend GameMaker if you want an easy yet powerful 2D game engine that includes all tools you'll need.

coveredGames.name: Clickteam Fusion 2.5
coveredGames.title: The easiest engine to make games and applications without writing code. I made tons of tools and games using Clickteam. Without it I would never delve into programming. Highly recommended to everyone!

coveredGames.name: RPG Maker 2003
coveredGames.title: Try RPG Maker 2003 or RPG Maker 2000 before newer releases. It includes all basic features without incomprehensible extras, making it the perfect way to learn the basics without feeling overwhelmed.

coveredGames.name: RPG Maker 2000
coveredGames.title: I recommend trying RPG Maker 2000 before newer releases. It includes all basic features without incomprehensible extras, making it the perfect way to learn the basics without feeling overwhelmed.
